### Allegro browser extensions

**Verdict:** SKIP · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 5 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Two unrelated Chrome extensions. (1) 'Cenowskaz Allegro' (English store name 'Allegro Price Guide'), v1.0.7, official, by Allegro. It recognises the product you view on one of 36 listed Polish online shops, asks Allegro for a matching offer, and shows a notification linking to Allegro only when the Allegro offer is cheaper. Role: one-way price comparison and redirect to Allegro. (2) 'Allegro Price Tracker & History - Sledzenie Cen i Okazji', v1.0.0, a third-party hobby extension by an individual developer. It reads the price from Allegro offer and product pages you visit and stores it in your browser to build up to a 30-day price chart. Role: local price tracker. Reference alternative for the same job: 'AlleRadar: Allegro Helper' (third-party, alleradar.pl), with price-history charts, price alerts and filters on allegro.pl.

**vendor and ownership**

Cenowskaz: Allegro sp. z o.o., ul. Wierzbiecice 1B, 61-569 Poznan (KRS 0000635012). The Chrome Web Store marks it as a 'Trader' (D-U-N-S 366369944, support cenowskaz@allegro.com). The extension terms give afiliacja@allegro.com, Allegro's affiliate team, as the contact. Not neutral: it is the marketplace's own tool for pulling buyers away from 36 competing shops. Price Tracker & History: offered by 'Parsa.Rezaei.2014', an individual developer in Lodz, PL, with a gmail contact. The store marks it as a 'Non-trader', so EU consumer rights do not apply to the contract with the developer. It is not affiliated with Allegro despite the name. AlleRadar: third-party, 'not connected with Allegro.pl in any way', non-trader, verified owner of alleradar.pl.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

Cenowskaz: launched publicly at the end of Aug 2026 and promoted by Allegro emails and an Allegro Share points promotion (200 points for installing plus 100 for a survey, until 29.09) (Antyweb 2026-10-08; Pepper). ⚠ *(unverified)* Store metadata carries a first timestamp of 2026-05-11, which may be an earlier unlisted publication. Terms effective 2026-10-01. Version 1.0.7 updated 2026-10-09. 7,000 users, 4.0 stars from 40 ratings on 2026-10-15. Active development. Price Tracker & History: version 1.0.0 published and updated 2025-12-10, with no update in 10 months; 149 users and no ratings on 2026-10-15; extscope.org shows a 'declining' trend (146 installs). Effectively unmaintained. AlleRadar: v3.9.11 updated 2026-10-09, 2,000 users, 3.9 stars from 51 ratings. Verified 2026-10-15 on the Chrome Web Store (primary).

**cost model**

All three are free (Cenowskaz terms section 3.2; store pages). Cenowskaz pays users in Allegro Share points for installing and using it (landing page: 'use Cenowskaz and collect extra points in Allegro Share'). Seen 2026-10-15.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Cenowskaz: works only on the 36 Polish shop domains in Annex 1 of its terms; requires an Allegro login; links to allegro.pl. Price Tracker: allegro.pl offer and product pages only, Polish UI. AlleRadar: allegro.pl only (not allegro.cz).
- **EU**: Cenowskaz store listing is translated into English, Polish, Czech and Ukrainian, but the shop list is Polish only. ⚠ *(unverified)* No Czech, Slovak or Hungarian shop coverage was found. Price Tracker: not for allegro.cz, .sk or .hu (host permission is allegro.pl only).
- **US**: N/A.
- **platform**: Chrome desktop only. Cenowskaz FAQ and terms: Google Chrome on a computer, 'not available on phones or tablets'. ⚠ *(unverified)* Firefox or Edge versions of the two extensions were not checked; AlleRadar has a Firefox add-on (addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/filtr-ofert-dla-allegro).
- **language**: Cenowskaz UI in Polish, listing in 4 languages; Price Tracker in Polish.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

None. Cenowskaz matches the product you are viewing to an Allegro offer. Its own FAQ warns that 'the product match is not always unambiguous', and section 5 of its terms says it does not guarantee 'the lowest price' or 'an exact or complete comparison'. Price Tracker does no matching or spec work.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Cenowskaz compares one way only (external shop to Allegro) across 36 shops listed in its terms (Annex 1, effective 2026-10-01). Electronics (6): mediaexpert.pl, mediamarkt.pl, euro.com.pl, komputronik.pl, morele.net, x-kom.pl. Home and garden (9): agatameble.pl, bricoman.pl, obi.pl, castorama.pl, dlaroslin.pl, BRW.pl, lazienkaplus.pl, leroymerlin.pl, tim.pl. Automotive (6): autodoc.pl, intercars.pl, iparts.pl, oponeo.pl, strefakierowcy.pl, ucando.pl. Health and beauty (5): superpharm.pl, rossmann.pl, gemini.pl, doz.pl, sfd.pl. Supermarket (4): carrefour.pl, kaufland.pl, frisco.pl, zakupy.auchan.pl. Other (6): bee.pl, empik.com, lego.com, smyk.com, taniaksiazka.pl, korob.pl. It stays silent when the shop is cheaper or equal, so it can never tell you to stay in the shop. Not covered: Decathlon.pl, Amazon.pl and .de, Ceneo, brand stores. Price Tracker does no cross-shop comparison.

**price history and omnibus**

Cenowskaz: none. Price Tracker: records the price each time you open an allegro.pl/oferta/* or /produkt/* page (content-script matches in its manifest) and keeps up to 30 days locally, shown as a chart. History exists only for pages you have already visited, with no backfill and no crowd data, and it does not derive or flag the Omnibus 30-day lowest price. AlleRadar (alternative): shows price history 'if available', which is more likely for popular offers, so it pools data beyond your own visits, and it checks favourite offers once a day for alerts.

**total landed cost**

No. Cenowskaz compares item prices; a store reviewer (2026-09-16) notes you still have to compare the total including shipping yourself. Price Tracker records the displayed price only.

**⚠ review and seller verification**

None. Cenowskaz links to one Allegro offer without showing the seller's rating or type in the notification. ⚠ *(unverified)* The notification content was not observed directly. Price Tracker: none. AlleRadar can hide sellers below a rating threshold, hide business or private accounts, and keep a seller blacklist.

**safety and compliance checks**

None in any of the three.

**independent test coverage**

N/A.

**alerts and monitoring**

Cenowskaz: an in-page notification only while you view a product on a listed shop, with no alerts. Price Tracker: no notifications; it has only 'storage' permission and no alarms or notifications. AlleRadar: target-price alerts in the extension and as optional system notifications, checked once a day for favourite offers.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

None. Cenowskaz's notification opens the Allegro offer; buying is the normal manual Allegro checkout. Price Tracker has no purchase function.

**after sales and resale**

N/A.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Cenowskaz reads product identifiers from the shop page and queries Allegro's systems in real time on each page view (terms section 3.1; FAQ). Prices in the notification may change and depend on data availability (terms section 5). Price Tracker reads the price from the Allegro page DOM at visit time and stores it in chrome.storage, so it is only as fresh as your last visit. Neither tool provides a citable snapshot.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

None. No API, CLI or MCP. They are manual tools in the user's own Chrome. The Claude built-in browser cannot open the Chrome Web Store and so cannot install extensions (checked 2026-10-15). ⚠ *(unverified)* An agent driving the user's own Chrome (Claude in Chrome) might see a Cenowskaz notification if the user installed it; not tested. Grade: none. To get Allegro price history into Claude Code, take your own periodic snapshots of the offer page via a browser agent.

**protocol support**

N/A (browser extensions).

**open source and licence**

Closed for both, with no public repositories. Price Tracker is 8.83 KiB and Cenowskaz 43.13 KiB, so both are small enough to audit from the CRX, but neither publishes source. AlleRadar is closed (734 KiB).

**account linking and data access**

Cenowskaz manifest v1.0.7 (embedded in the store page, read 2026-10-15): permissions 'identity', 'storage', 'activeTab'; content script injected on '<all_urls>' (every site, not only the 36 shops; the script decides where to act); web_accessible_resources on <all_urls>. It requires logging in to an Allegro account (terms section 3.3). Chrome Web Store privacy disclosure: handles 'Authentication information' and 'Website content'. Terms section 7: Allegro is the data controller and processes 'data or identifiers that may constitute personal data' for operation, abuse prevention, improvement, and 'analytics and measurement of activity and use of the extension, including analytics of traffic passing through the extension', from install until removal, with cookies; it states users are 'not profiled'. The marketing claim on the landing page, 'does not collect any data about you', conflicts with the terms' analytics clause and with requiring an Allegro login. A user review (2026-09-16) reports the 'Nie jestes zalogowany' prompt appearing on all sites, including allegro.pl, which fits the <all_urls> injection. Price Tracker manifest v1.0.0: permission 'storage' only; host permission https://allegro.pl/*; content scripts only on allegro.pl/oferta/* and /produkt/*. No other hosts, so a 'no data sent' claim is plausible but not code-audited. The store disclosure says it collects no data. AlleRadar: storage, unlimitedStorage, alarms, contextMenus, scripting, declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess; host allegro.pl only; optional notifications.

**automation legal risk**

Low for personal use. Cenowskaz is Allegro's own product (licence terms in section 4 forbid decompiling or modifying it). Price Tracker reads pages you open yourself, at no added traffic. The Allegro terms (art. 10.10) ban scraping for business reuse, but local personal price notes are not that. Using a non-trader extension removes consumer-law recourse against its developer.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Cenowskaz exists to move purchases from 36 competing shops to Allegro. It is run by Allegro's affiliate team (contact afiliacja@allegro.com) and pays users in Allegro Share points. The terms reserve 'analytics of traffic passing through the extension'. It is structurally biased: it fires only when Allegro looks cheaper and never confirms the external shop is the better deal. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether its links carry Allegro Share or affiliate tracking parameters, and whether it overrides cashback portals' attribution (a question raised by Pepper commenters), was not observed because the extension was not installed. Price Tracker: no monetisation disclosed. AlleRadar openly says it 'may occasionally use affiliate links on Allegro'.

**ranking transparency**

Low. Cenowskaz shows one Allegro offer without explaining how it was picked (cheapest item price? delivery included? which seller?) and states no criteria beyond 'cheaper offer'. Price Tracker: N/A, since it ranks nothing.

**run to run consistency**

N/A. Not generative AI. Cenowskaz output depends on live Allegro offers and on whether the product is recognised.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Not applicable to prompt injection. Risks: Cenowskaz can match a similar but different product, which its FAQ admits; Price Tracker shows seller price games only if you happened to visit at the right times. Neither checks seller trust.

**known failures**

Cenowskaz store reviews (Polish, 2026-09-16 to 2026-10-08): 'Nie dziala' (does not work, several users); 'stale chce zebym sie zalogowal' (keeps asking to log in); no suggestions for books; the not-logged-in prompt on all sites; 'acts as if disabled' when nothing cheaper is found. The developer replied on 2026-10-09 asking users to email cenowskaz@allegro.com. An Allegro community thread reports it 'not working in any shop'. Price Tracker: no reviews; no update since 2025-12-10; history limited to 30 days and to your own visits.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the extensions themselves. Context: UOKiK fined Allegro in 2022 for self-preferencing on its marketplace; Cenowskaz extends that marketplace's reach into other shops' pages but no decision concerns it.

**buyer protection path**

Following a Cenowskaz link switches you from a large retailer (e.g. OBI, Leroy Merlin, Media Expert, which are merchant of record with their own returns) to an Allegro marketplace seller. Allegro Ochrona Kupujacych then applies (up to 20,000 PLN, 2 years), and statutory rights run against that seller, who may be smaller, foreign or a white-label importer. Price Tracker: N/A (no purchase).

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Weak. Trampoline case: Cenowskaz helps only if you are browsing a trampoline on one of the listed shops that sell them (obi.pl, castorama.pl, leroymerlin.pl, bricoman.pl, smyk.com, kaufland.pl, carrefour.pl, zakupy.auchan.pl, empik.com) and Allegro has the same product cheaper. Matching is shaky for private-label models without a shared EAN, and Decathlon.pl and brand shops are not covered. It never confirms that the DIY store is the better deal. Price Tracker: useful only if you start opening the shortlisted Allegro offers regularly 2-4 weeks before buying; for a seasonal product (spring peak) that could expose pre-season price inflation, but with no backfill and 30-day retention it gives little on day one. AlleRadar's pooled history and alerts are the better fit for the same job.

**workflow role**

Price and history step. Cenowskaz: a quick 'is it on Allegro cheaper?' check while browsing one of 36 Polish shops. Price Tracker: a personal price log for Allegro offers you revisit. Combine with a neutral comparison engine (Ceneo, idealo) and with AlleRadar or your own snapshots for history.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Free. Installation about 2 minutes each; Cenowskaz also needs an Allegro login. No marginal cost per purchase and no API, token or proxy costs. The hidden cost is privacy: an Allegro-logged-in script on every page you visit (Cenowskaz).

**evidence trail**

Weak. Neither tool exports data. Cenowskaz notifications are not stored for the user. Price Tracker's chart lives only in local browser storage; capture a screenshot of the chart and note dates and prices manually for a vault record (offer URL, date, price series).

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Cenowskaz is free, official and actively updated (v1.0.7, 2026-10-09; 7,000 users, 4.0 stars from 40 ratings), with a published shop list of 36 Polish shops.
  - Cenowskaz needs no manual search: one click from a supported shop page to a matching Allegro offer.
  - Price Tracker has minimal permissions (storage plus allegro.pl only) and keeps data local, so its privacy footprint is low.
  - Price Tracker gives a price-history chart that Allegro itself does not offer.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Cenowskaz is an Allegro affiliate funnel: it fires only when Allegro looks cheaper, rewards Allegro Share points and never endorses the other shop.
  - Cenowskaz's 'collects no data' claim conflicts with its terms (traffic analytics), an Allegro login requirement and an '<all_urls>' content script.
  - Cenowskaz has documented 'does not work' and login-loop reviews (Sept-Oct 2026) and ambiguous product matching.
  - Price Tracker is unmaintained since Dec 2025, has 149 users and no ratings, and builds history only from your own visits (30-day cap, no backfill).
  - Neither tool is drivable from Claude Code or exports evidence.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on review of either extension was found. Coverage of Cenowskaz is a news item (Antyweb 2026-10-08) repeating Allegro's claims, plus a Pepper deal post. Chrome Web Store user reviews for Cenowskaz are mixed (4.0 from 40 ratings; recent 1-star 'does not work' reviews). Price Tracker has no reviews at all. The outline's note of 'only 5 ratings' could not be reproduced: the store showed 0 ratings on 2026-10-15.

**verdict for me**

SKIP both: Cenowskaz is a biased Allegro affiliate funnel injected on every page with an Allegro login, and Price Tracker is an unmaintained 149-user tool with no backfill. Best use instead: if you want Allegro price history, pilot AlleRadar (pooled history plus daily alerts, affiliate use disclosed), or have a Claude browser agent snapshot your shortlisted Allegro offers weekly into the vault.

**conflicting evidence**

- Price Tracker ratings: 'only 5 ratings' (Step-2 outline note) vs no ratings on the Chrome Web Store and 0 reviews on extscope.org (both 2026-10-15). Ratings may have been removed, or the note referred to another extension.
- Ownership framing: the item groups both as 'Allegro' extensions, but the Chrome Web Store lists Price Tracker & History as made by an individual non-trader developer, not Allegro.
- Cenowskaz data collection: landing page and store text say it 'does not collect any data about you' and does not save browsed-page data, vs terms section 7 listing processing of personal identifiers for analytics, including 'traffic passing through the extension', plus the store disclosure 'Authentication information, Website content'.
- Cenowskaz scope: 'works only on selected sites' (landing page) vs a manifest content script matching '<all_urls>' and a user report of the login prompt on every site.
- Cenowskaz launch: 'started at the end of August' 2026 (Antyweb 2026-10-08) vs a store metadata timestamp of 2026-05-11 (possibly an unlisted first upload).
- Shop count: '30+' / 'ponad 30' (Allegro marketing, Antyweb) vs 36 domains listed in the terms' Annex 1 (2026-10-01).

**sources checked**

- **primary**:
  - https://allegro.pl/cenowskaz - landing page, shop list by category, FAQ, privacy claims (opened 2026-10-15)
  - https://allegro.pl/regulaminy/regulamin-rozszerzenia-cenowskaz-allegro-eKqK9nPGKSd - extension terms effective 2026-10-01: provider, affiliate contact, scope, liability, data processing, Annex 1 shop list (opened 2026-10-15)
  - https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cenowskaz-allegro/emfplbdhkmjolghellmiibpnidndmhka - store page: v1.0.7, updated 2026-10-09, 7,000 users, 4.0 from 40 ratings, privacy disclosure, trader data, embedded manifest (fetched 2026-10-15)
  - https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cenowskaz-allegro/emfplbdhkmjolghellmiibpnidndmhka/reviews - user reviews Sept-Oct 2026 and developer replies (fetched 2026-10-15)
  - https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/ledbpomjcjckjackdepdbndlehbimpim - Price Tracker & History store page: v1.0.0, 2025-12-10, 149 users, no ratings, non-trader developer, embedded manifest (fetched 2026-10-15)
  - https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/mppahmgdcnapaalefnpnfoekkpggkkol - AlleRadar store page: features, affiliate disclosure, manifest (fetched 2026-10-15)
- **secondary**:
  - https://www.extscope.org/extension/ledbpomjcjckjackdepdbndlehbimpim - permissions, 146 installs, declining trend (opened 2026-10-15)
  - https://antyweb.pl/allegro-bedzie-wtracac-ci-sie-w-zakupy-zaproponuje-nizsze-ceny-poza-platforma - launch end of Aug 2026, email promotion (opened 2026-10-15; dated 2026-10-08)

### Google Shopping and AI Mode

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY · **Cost:** Free, ad-funded · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Google Shopping (Shopping tab, product listings and product cards built on Google's Shopping Graph) plus the shopping layer of Google AI Mode (the Gemini-powered conversational tab in Google Search). Role type: comparison engine + AI assistant + (US-only) shopping agent with agentic checkout. State on 2026-10-15: AI Mode answers in Polish in Poland, but every agentic shopping feature (price tracking with 'Buy for me', UCP checkout via Google Pay, 'Let Google Call') is US-only or limited to US/CA/AU/JP/IN, and in the EEA free product listings, product carousels and the Shopping tab in the navigation bar were removed in September 2026 for DMA compliance.

**vendor and ownership**

Google LLC (Alphabet Inc.), Mountain View, US; EU-facing entity is Google Ireland Ltd (the defendant in the Polish Ceneo case). Bias-relevant: Google runs both the general search engine and its own comparison shopping service and sells Shopping ads, which is exactly the conduct condemned in the EC 2017 Google Shopping decision and the 23 July 2026 DMA non-compliance decision.

**lifecycle status**

Launched and changing fast; verified 2026-10-15. Milestones: AI Mode launched in the US in May 2025 (I/O 2025); expanded on 7 Oct 2025 to 35+ new languages and 40+ new countries (Google blog), with Polish press reporting the Polish launch from 8 Oct 2025; conversational shopping in AI Mode, agentic checkout and 'Let Google Call' rolled out in the US on 13 Nov 2025 (TechCrunch); Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) checkout launched 11 Jan 2026 (NRF); Google Marketing Live (20 May 2026) promised UCP checkout for Canada and Australia 'in the coming months' and the UK later; the Merchant Center help page updated 6 Oct 2026 says onboarding is rolling out in the US with Australia and Canada 'next year' and a 'UCP Checkout Terms of Service (US only)' (ppc.land, 7 Oct 2026). EEA: on 8 Sep 2026 Google documented EEA-only aggregator ('Comparison sites') and supplier units; between 15 and 18 Sep 2026 free product listings and 'popular products' carousels disappeared across the EEA (Search Engine Roundtable, 18 Sep 2026, Google Ads Liaison confirmed DMA cause); the Shopping tab was dropped from the navigation bar around 17 Sep 2026 (single secondary source: shopappy citing Productrise). DMA compliance deadline was ~21 Sep 2026; no Commission assessment of the new layout found as of verification. Primary sources: Google blog (AI Mode expansion), Google Search Central aggregator-unit docs (last updated 2026-09-18), Google Shopping Help 'About price tracking on Google'.

**cost model**

Free for shoppers; funded by ads (Shopping ads, Search ads, sponsored listings inside AI Mode and AI Overviews, 'Direct Offers' ad pilot in AI Mode). US agentic checkout charges the merchant's price via Google Pay with no stated buyer fee. Programmatic access only through third-party SERP APIs: SerpApi Free 250 searches/month, Starter USD 25/month for 1,000, Developer USD 75/month for 5,000 searches (serpapi.com pricing as summarised in search results, seen 2026-10-15); DataForSEO and Apify actors are pay-per-use alternatives.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **ai mode answers in polish**: PL: yes since Oct 2025 (Polish UI and answers). EU: yes in most member states since Oct 2025; France only from 22 Jul 2026. US: yes since May 2025.
- **rich product results inside ai mode**: US: yes. UK: yes. PL/EU: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed - Productrise (29 Jul 2026) excluded all markets except US and UK because 'many other markets do not yet return rich product results inside AI Mode'.
- **free product listings and popular products carousel**: US/UK/AU: yes. EEA: removed 15-18 Sep 2026 (90-100% drops measured in DE, FR, BE, NL, SE). PL: ⚠ *(unverified)* not directly measured, but PL is in the EEA and the removal is described as EEA-wide.
- **shopping tab in navigation**: EEA: removed from the nav bar around 17 Sep 2026, still reachable via URL parameter (single secondary source). US: yes.
- **paid shopping ads**: PL/EEA: yes, unaffected by the Sep 2026 change (served via Comparison Shopping Services). US: yes.
- **aggregator comparison sites unit and supplier unit**: EEA only (incl. PL) since 8 Sep 2026 for product, hotel, flight, ground transport and local queries. Not in US.
- **price tracking track price**: Only US, Canada, Australia, Japan, India per the official Google Shopping Help page. Not PL, not EU.
- **buy for me agentic checkout ucp google pay**: US only (eligible merchants such as Wayfair, Chewy, Quince, Etsy, select Shopify stores, Walmart/Target via UCP). Canada/Australia planned (2026 promise, help page now says 2027), UK later. No EU or PL timeline found.
- **let google call local stores**: US only (toys, health and beauty, electronics). Not PL.
- **gemini app shopping ideas**: US only at launch (Nov 2025). PL: not available ⚠ *(unverified: no later expansion found)*.
- **ai mode flight price alerts**: ⚠ *(unverified)* 180+ countries; one Polish report (geekweek.interia.pl) says the EEA, including Poland, is excluded, another (imagazine.pl, 28 Aug 2026) implies Poland is likely covered.
- **hotel booking in chat with google pay**: US only (English).
- **chrome shopping insights price history**: US launch Nov 2023 (up to 90 days of history); PL: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed.
- **interface language**: Polish supported for AI Mode answers and Google Search; shopping-agent features only in English/US.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. AI Mode can return comparison tables for comparison queries and the Shopping Graph groups offers under one product using merchant feed identifiers (GTIN/MPN); 'Track price' lets you pin size/colour variants (US). There is no documented handling of retailer-exclusive variants, regional names or white-label OEM rebadges. Evidence of variant mismatch: Productrise (Aug 2026, US/UK) found AI Mode and classic search showed a different first seller for 49.6% of matched products and attributed extreme price gaps to used-vs-new mixing. In PL, AI Mode spec answers are LLM syntheses of web pages without product cards, so specs must be checked against the maker's page.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

Google indexes merchants that send Merchant Center feeds or Product structured data; Shopping Graph is vendor-claimed at 50B+ listings with 2B updated hourly (Google via TechCrunch, Nov 2025). In Poland after mid-Sep 2026 the free multi-shop price comparison on google.pl is largely gone: what remains is paid Shopping ads (CSS-mediated) and the EEA 'Comparison sites' aggregator unit that hands the user to a third-party comparison service. ⚠ *(unverified)* Which Polish channels appear (Allegro, Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon.pl) was not tested; no independent PL coverage count exists. AI Mode in Polish names shops and prices from web text, not from a verified multi-shop table.

**price history and omnibus**

None usable in Poland. Google's price insights and Chrome 'Shopping insights' show a typical price range and up to 90 days of history, launched for US shoppers in Nov 2023; availability in PL not confirmed. No feature shows or derives the Omnibus lowest price of the 30 days before a promotion, and nothing flags fake discounts for Polish shops.

**total landed cost**

Partial at best. Merchant feeds can carry shipping cost and return policy, and Google cards can display them, but nothing computes price + shipping + payment fees + assembly + return shipping + cross-border warranty. AI Mode prices are unreliable as a cost basis: Productrise (9-31 Aug 2026, US/UK, 2M+ listings) found prices differed between AI Mode and the product carousel for 38.1% of matched products, AI Mode was higher in 68.4% of those, and averaged 21.6% higher across all matched products (Google has not verified the study). For a bulky trampoline the freight and return cost must be checked in the shop's cart.

**review and seller verification**

Partial (shop and product ratings only). Google shows aggregated product ratings and store ratings drawn from merchants and third-party review sources; there is no review-authenticity analysis and no seller identity check against CEIDG, KRS, the VAT white list or VIES. It cannot prove a Polish shop is a registered business or that its reviews are genuine.

**safety and compliance checks**

None for the shopper. Google does not surface Safety Gate or UOKiK register hits, GPSR listing fields (manufacturer, EU responsible person, Polish warnings), the claimed EN 71-14 edition or certificate verifiability. AI Mode can be asked to search Safety Gate or Certipedia but nothing runs automatically and answers are not guaranteed to be grounded.

**independent test coverage**

Not a test lab and does not surface lab results in a structured way. AI Mode may cite test pages if asked (e.g. Stiftung Warentest's test of 11 garden trampolines on test.de, paywalled), but there is no guarantee and no indication of test date vs current model year.

**alerts and monitoring**

Track price sends Google-app push and email when the price drops below a target; available only in US, CA, AU, JP, IN (official help page). Activity-based price-drop alerts also exist there. Not available in Poland; no webhook; cannot watch an arbitrary Polish shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

US only. 'Buy for me with GPay': once a tracked item hits the target price, Google adds it to the cart on the merchant's site and pays with Google Pay; the official help page says you get a notification and email and must approve the purchase, payment method and shipping address before any purchase. Built on UCP with AP2 payment mandates; the merchant stays merchant of record; only eligible merchants. No documented spending cap beyond the user-set target price, and no published error/refund procedure. Not usable from Poland; no BLIK or passkey mandate support found.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered. Google Shopping can list used/refurbished offers with a condition label and AI Mode can answer spare-parts questions from web text, but there is no structured view of spare nets/pads/springs, Polish service networks, warranty handling or resale value on OLX/Allegro Lokalnie.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Shopping Graph from Merchant Center feeds, crawled Product/merchant-listing structured data and Google's web index; vendor claims 2B listings updated every hour. AI Mode answers are Gemini syntheses with reference links to source pages (SerpApi exposes these as text_blocks with reference_indexes). Reported lags/mismatches: Productrise price gap study above; only 0.8-1.28% of products in classic results also appeared in AI Mode for the same query on the same day (US/UK). No price snapshots are stored for the user.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial (third-party only). (1) Official API: none for consumers - Google's Merchant API/Content API are merchant-side only, and there is no public AI Mode API. (2) SerpApi: engines google_shopping, google_immersive_product and google_ai_mode (returns text_blocks, references, conditional shopping_results; supports gl/hl/location so gl=pl&hl=pl works); API key auth; Free 250 searches/month, Starter USD 25/1,000, Developer USD 75/5,000. A hosted SerpApi MCP endpoint (mcp.serpapi.com) is named in the research outline - ⚠ *(unverified)* not re-verified here. (3) DataForSEO: Google Shopping API and Google AI Mode SERP API with an ai_overview_shopping element. (4) Apify: several Google Shopping scraper actors usable through Apify's hosted MCP server (mcp.apify.com). (5) Browser agent: Claude in Chrome or browser-use can drive AI Mode in the user's own session, but Google's anti-bot checks and ToS make this fragile. (6) No official Claude skill or Google MCP for shopping. (7) UCP is an open merchant/agent protocol but checkout is US-only, so a Polish buyer cannot use it from Claude Code. Setup effort: about 30 minutes for a SerpApi key plus an MCP or curl wrapper; legal note: Google's DMCA suit against SerpApi was dismissed on 20 Jul 2026 (N.D. Cal.).

**⚠ protocol support**

UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol, co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart; launched 11 Jan 2026) and AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) for user-authorised payment mandates, with Google Pay (PayPal announced as coming). Future-proof on paper, but checkout is US-only and EU timelines are absent. ⚠ *(unverified)* UCP transport bindings (REST/MCP/A2A) not re-verified.

**⚠ open source and licence**

Google Shopping and AI Mode: closed. UCP specification: open source at github.com/universal-commerce-protocol/ucp, described as Apache-2.0 by secondary sources (licence file not opened), with Python/JS SDKs and a conformance suite. ⚠ *(unverified)* AP2 is also published as open source by Google.

**account linking and data access**

Needs a Google account for history, tracking and personalised alerts; personalisation uses Web and App Activity. US checkout needs a Google Pay payment method and shipping address stored with Google. In the EEA Google Ireland is the data controller and GDPR applies; AI Mode queries are logged to the account unless activity saving is off. For this buyer nothing requires handing over payment credentials in Poland because the checkout feature is unavailable there.

**automation legal risk**

Google's ToS forbid automated querying, and Google sued SerpApi in Dec 2025 under the DMCA for circumventing its SearchGuard anti-bot system; the court dismissed the core claims on 20 Jul 2026 (leave to amend on a narrow image claim; follow-up not confirmed). Practical risk for personal, low-volume use through a SERP API is low for the end user (the API provider carries the scraping); direct headless scraping from your own IP risks CAPTCHAs and temporary blocks rather than account bans. EU/PL: SERP data is largely factual, but database-right and ToS arguments remain.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Advertising: Shopping ads, Search ads, sponsored listings inside AI Mode (labelled 'Sponsored'), a Direct Offers pilot (ads offering discounts inside AI Mode). Structural bias: Google ranks its own vertical services and sells the ads it ranks; the EC found self-preferencing in 2017 and again under the DMA on 23 Jul 2026. Productrise data suggests AI Mode surfaces different (and on average pricier) sellers than classic results. In the EEA after Sep 2026, the 'Comparison sites' unit is ranked algorithmically by Google with no published criteria, and one secondary report says Google lists itself among the comparison sites.

**ranking transparency**

Low. AI Mode shows reference links but does not explain why a product was chosen, and you cannot rerun with a source excluded other than by rewording the prompt. Sponsored items are labelled. The EEA aggregator-unit documentation says only that the top-ranked provider is expanded by default, without ranking criteria.

**run to run consistency**

No AI Mode-specific repeat test found and no own test run. Indirect evidence: Product.ai (vendor, 220 shopping prompts x 5 runs on free and paid tiers of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) reported factual conflicts on 86% of prompts and Gemini as the weakest engine (56% of Gemini responses had at least one mistake costly to a buyer); Productrise showed near-zero overlap between AI Mode and classic results for the same query on the same day. Treat AI Mode shortlists as non-reproducible.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

⚠ *(unverified)* No independent study of AI Mode shopping against fake shops, page prompt injection or spoofed reviews was found. Safeguards that exist: Merchant Center misrepresentation and product policies suspend detected scam merchants; US agentic checkout requires explicit user confirmation of item, payment method and address. AI Mode answers in PL are drawn from open web pages, so persuasive seller content and SEO spam can enter the synthesis.

**known failures**

AI Mode shows about 95% fewer product listings than classic search (Productrise, 100k+ queries, Jul 2026, US/UK); price mismatches between AI Mode and the carousel (38.1% of matched products, Aug 2026); eMarketer called the agentic shopping experience short of its promise (Jan 2026 NRF coverage); narrow merchant list for checkout; Google itself called the Sep 2026 EEA redesign the largest quality reduction in Search's history, and EEA users lost free product carousels and merchant names on cards; Gemini topped a Sep 2026 pricing-error benchmark (Product.ai via Android Headlines). Poland-specific gap: no tracking, no checkout, no Let Google Call, and probably no rich product cards in AI Mode.

**regulatory enforcement history**

EC Google Shopping decision 2017 (EUR 2.42B, upheld by the CJEU on 10 Sep 2024, C-48/22 P). DMA non-compliance decisions of 23 Jul 2026: EUR 890M total = EUR 460M for self-preferencing in Search (shopping, hotels, transport, sports; Art. 6(5)) + EUR 430M for Google Play anti-steering; 60 days to comply under threat of periodic penalties; Google evaluating appeal. National damages: Berlin Regional Court, Nov 2025, about EUR 465M to idealo and EUR 107M to Producto (appealable); Stockholm Patent and Market Court, 1 Jul 2026, SEK 14.3B plus interest to Klarna's PriceRunner (Google appealing). Poland: Warsaw District Court interim injunction for Ceneo against Google Ireland (14 Mar 2024) and a Ceneo damages suit of about PLN 2.331B (filed Dec 2024, pending).

**⚠ buyer protection path**

Google is not the seller: the purchase happens on the merchant's site, so the Polish buyer's protection is the merchant's - 14-day withdrawal for distance contracts, 2-year statutory conformity liability (rekojmia/niezgodnosc towaru z umowa), and card chargeback or PayPal protection depending on how you pay. Cross-border EU merchants: ECC Poland (Europejskie Centrum Konsumenckie). In the US flow the merchant also remains merchant of record; Google Pay adds no documented purchase guarantee ⚠ *(unverified)*.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low-to-moderate for a garden trampoline bought in Poland. Useful: a Polish AI Mode query such as 'trampolina ogrodowa 305 cm z siatka - na co zwrocic uwage, porownanie modeli' returns a cited overview (spring count, net type, max load, EN 71-14) and names candidate brands and pages, including test reports if they exist. Not useful: no price tracking, no history, no landed-cost view, no safety-register check, no checkout in PL, and since Sep 2026 the free product carousel that used to compare Polish shop prices is gone from google.pl. Prices from AI Mode must be re-checked on Ceneo, Allegro or the shop page.

**workflow role**

Discovery and first-pass spec orientation (in Polish), plus finding test and review pages. Combine with Ceneo/Allegro for PL prices and history, Safety Gate and the GPSR listing check for safety, idealo/Geizhals for DE price cross-checks, and Stiftung Warentest/Which? for lab tests.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual: free, about 10-20 minutes of prompting and clicking through citations. Programmatic from Claude Code via SerpApi: one trampoline comparison = about 3 google_ai_mode queries + 5 google_shopping queries (gl=pl, hl=pl) = 8 searches; on the Developer plan (USD 75 / 5,000 searches = USD 0.015 per search) that is about USD 0.12, or free within the 250-search free tier; plus roughly 50-100k Claude tokens to read and summarise the JSON. Setup about 30 minutes.

**evidence trail**

Weak in the UI (AI Mode history lives in the Google account; no price snapshots), good via API: SerpApi responses carry search_metadata (id, timestamp, raw HTML link), the query parameters and reference URLs, so a vault note can store: query, gl/hl, timestamp, AI Mode text with cited URLs, shopping_results rows (title, price, seller, link) and the raw-HTML archive link.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Polish-language AI Mode answers with cited sources since Oct 2025 - fast discovery and spec orientation.
  - Largest product graph (vendor-claimed 50B+ listings, 2B updated hourly) and still-live paid Shopping ads in PL.
  - Programmatic access through mature SERP APIs (SerpApi google_shopping/google_ai_mode with gl=pl) that return timestamped JSON for a vault audit trail.
  - Agentic checkout design is relatively careful: explicit confirmation of item, payment method and address before purchase (US).
- **weaknesses**:
  - Every shopping-agent feature (price tracking, Buy for me, Let Google Call, Gemini shopping ideas) is US-only or limited to US/CA/AU/JP/IN.
  - EEA free product listings, carousels and the Shopping tab were removed in Sep 2026 under the DMA, so google.pl no longer compares shop prices for free.
  - AI Mode prices disagree with Google's own carousel for 38.1% of matched products and skew higher (Productrise, US/UK).
  - No price history, Omnibus check, landed-cost calculation, seller registry or safety-register checks for Polish purchases.
  - Structural self-preferencing and ad incentives, confirmed by EC 2017 and DMA 2026 decisions.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test of AI Mode shopping in Poland was found. Independent or semi-independent evidence agrees that AI Mode is a weaker price source than classic Shopping: Productrise studies (vendor analytics firm, published method, US/UK, Jul and Aug 2026, reported by Search Engine Journal and MediaPost) on listing volume and price gaps; eMarketer analysis that agentic checkout under-delivers; Search Engine Roundtable and Search Engine Journal on the degraded EEA layout. Product.ai's multi-engine benchmark is vendor research. Most 'best AI shopping assistant 2026' comparison pages found are GEO/ecommerce-agency marketing without a test method.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY (WATCH for any EU rollout of UCP checkout) - deciding fact: in Poland only the Polish-language AI Mode answer layer works; price tracking, Buy for me and Let Google Call are US-only and free product listings were removed from EEA search in Sep 2026. Best use: one AI Mode query in Polish to build the candidate list and locate test/safety sources, or a logged SerpApi google_ai_mode + google_shopping run with gl=pl saved to the vault, then do prices and history on Ceneo/Allegro.

**conflicting evidence**

- AI Mode flight price alerts: geekweek.interia.pl says the price-alert service covers 180+ countries but excludes the EEA including Poland; imagazine.pl (28 Aug 2026) says flight alerts by email work in 180+ countries and Poland is likely covered.
- DMA fine size: EUR 890M (total of two decisions, 23 Jul 2026) vs EUR 460M (the Search self-preferencing portion that concerns Shopping) - both correct, different scopes; dollar conversions vary (USD 1.0-1.04B).
- UCP checkout timeline: Google Marketing Live (20 May 2026) said Canada and Australia 'in the coming months', UK later; the Merchant Center help page updated 6 Oct 2026 says Australia and Canada 'next year' and lists US-only checkout terms (may refer to merchant onboarding rather than consumer checkout).
- Shopping tab removal in the EEA: reported by shopappy citing Productrise; Search Engine Roundtable's 18 Sep 2026 article covers free listings and carousels but does not mention the tab.
- AI Mode expansion size: Google says 35+ new languages and 40+ new countries (7 Oct 2025); Choose.tv says 36 languages and 50 countries.
- Productrise price-gap figure: most outlets report AI Mode higher in 68.4% of differing prices; one outlet reports 60% with a ~20% median gap.
- CROSS-ITEM CONFLICT (added by orchestrator after batch 4, 2026-10-15): this file says free multi-shop price comparison on google.pl is 'largely gone' after mid-Sep 2026 and price history is 'not confirmed' for Poland. The later SerpApi_MCP_Google_Shopping.json reports a hands-on browser test the same day: google.pl/search?udm=28 (Shopping vertical) still returned a grid of 20+ Polish sellers with a 'Najtaniej (30 dni)' badge, and the Polish product panel showed a 12-month 'Historia cen' table. The report must reconcile these: treat the EEA free-listings removal as partial and re-test before relying on either claim.

### idealo

**Verdict:** PILOT (DE/AT price check only) · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 6 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

idealo is a German price comparison engine (idealo.de, idealo.at, idealo.co.uk, idealo.fr, idealo.it, idealo.es) with product pages, offer lists sorted by price incl. shipping, price history and price alerts (Preiswecker). The 'idealo app in ChatGPT' (live since about March 2026) lets ChatGPT query idealo's catalogue in conversation. Role type: comparison engine + price tracker + AI-assistant integration. There is no idealo.pl; for a Polish buyer it is a cross-border DE/AT price-check tool only.

**vendor and ownership**

idealo internet GmbH, Berlin, Germany. Majority owner: Axel Springer SE (74.9% stake since 2006). In the 2025 Axel Springer split, KKR and CPP Investments took the classifieds businesses (StepStone, AVIV) while idealo stayed in the media/commerce company controlled by Mathias Doepfner and Friede Springer; Axel Springer's May 2026 results still list idealo in its Commerce segment with Awin and Bonial. A 2025 report said the Commerce unit (incl. idealo) was 'under review' for a possible sale - no sale found. Co-CEO Jovan Protic; co-founder Albrecht von Sonntag. Not owned by a marketplace or retailer.

**lifecycle status**

Price comparison: launched 2000, active. idealo checkout/Direktkauf: launched 2015, discontinued on 31 Dec 2022 according to MonsterDealz (Aug 2026) - a Lengow integration page still describes Direktkauf as configurable (conflict). Earlier ChatGPT plugin (beta, 2023, ChatGPT Plus plugin store) - superseded when OpenAI retired plugins. idealo app in ChatGPT: live; reported by report.at on 20 Mar 2026 and by DriversCloud on 26 Mar 2026; the research outline gives a directory listing date of 2026-04-21 (not re-verified). Latest change found: Berlin court damages ruling against Google (Nov 2025, appealable). Verified 2026-10-15 from secondary reports; idealo.de and chatgpt.com could not be fetched (blocked).

**cost model**

Free for shoppers (web, mobile app, ChatGPT app; the ChatGPT app works on ChatGPT plans that allow apps - free tier included at the Apps SDK launch). Merchants pay per click (CPC). Programmatic access only via unofficial scrapers: Apify 'saswave/idealo-scraper' USD 25/month after a 3-day trial; ZenRows from USD 69/month; ScrapingBee and Oxylabs credit-based (seen 2026-10-15 in search-result summaries).

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **markets**: Six: DE, AT, UK, FR, IT, ES. No Polish site or Polish interface.
- **price comparison web and app**: DE/AT/UK/FR/IT/ES: yes. PL: usable from Poland in German/English/etc., but offers are priced for delivery to the market's country (e.g. Germany on idealo.de).
- **shipping cost to poland**: ⚠ *(unverified)* No setting to price delivery to Poland was found; whether a listed shop ships to PL must be checked per shop.
- **price history preisentwicklung**: All idealo markets: yes (length disputed: up to 1 year per Finanztip, 90 days per Giga).
- **price alert preiswecker**: All idealo markets: yes, by email and app push. Watches idealo-listed offers only.
- **checkout direktkauf**: Discontinued 31 Dec 2022 (per MonsterDealz) - not available anywhere ⚠ *(unverified: one vendor page suggests otherwise)*.
- **idealo app in chatgpt**: Available to ChatGPT users in at least Germany (launch market; French coverage reports it too). PL: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed - OpenAI's help center says app availability in the EEA/UK/Switzerland depends on whether the partner provides its service there, and idealo has no Polish market.
- **interface language**: German, English (UK), French, Italian, Spanish. No Polish. The ChatGPT app can be prompted in Polish, but the data is from idealo markets ⚠ *(unverified: Polish prompting not tested)*.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. idealo groups offers under product pages with spec sheets and category filters, and its ChatGPT app is described as analysing technical data sheets and pros/cons. Weakness documented by MonsterDealz (Aug 2026): different storage variants or bundles can land in the same listing, so the cheapest hit is often not the exact variant; own-brand products and bundles without an EAN are often missing. No documented detection of OEM rebadges or retailer-exclusive variants. Spec filtering depth is weaker than Geizhals for technical goods.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Compares prices across shops in each idealo market; merchant count is vendor-claimed and inconsistent (about 24,000 merchant partners per the ChatGPT-app coverage, about 39,000 per MonsterDealz, 50,000 shops per a French listing; offer counts 201M / 350M+ / 500M+ / 600M+ depending on source and date). Polish channels: none indexed (no Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon.pl). EU channels: Amazon.de and thousands of German/Austrian shops on idealo.de/.at. Tested coverage: MonsterDealz (Aug 2026) matched 137 of 150 Amazon promo products (91.3%).

**price history and omnibus**

Shows a price-history chart per product (length disputed: up to 1 year vs 90 days) that helps judge whether a current price is a real low. It does not display or derive the Omnibus 30-day lowest price for a specific shop's promotion and does not flag Omnibus breaches; you can only infer it manually for idealo-listed DE/AT shops. Nothing covers Polish shops.

**total landed cost**

Partial and Germany-centric. Offer lists can be sorted by total price incl. shipping; the ChatGPT app listing says it shows delivery costs, return shipping fees, shipping times, payment options and vouchers (vendor-claimed). Limits: shipping costs come from merchant feeds and are often wrong or missing (MonsterDealz), freight/surcharges for bulky items sometimes only appear in the cart, payment-method surcharges are not compared, and all costs assume delivery to the market country - not Poland. Cross-border warranty enforceability, assembly and return freight for a ~30 kg trampoline box are not computed.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. idealo shows shop ratings (the ChatGPT app says 'verified shop ratings') and product reviews; no published review-authenticity method found. No seller identity checks against Polish registries (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list) or VIES; it relies on its merchant onboarding. Cannot prove a shop ships reliably to Poland.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No Safety Gate/UOKiK hits, no GPSR field checks (manufacturer, EU responsible person, Polish warnings), no EN 71-14 edition check, no certificate verification.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

The ChatGPT app listing says you can ask for test results and expert opinions (vendor claim); German product pages aggregate test reports ⚠ *(unverified: not verified on a live page)*. For trampolines the German market has a Stiftung Warentest test of 11 trampolines on test.de (paywalled; Lidl Crivit 305 cm rated 'gut (1.6)' per a deal-site summary, test.de mid-price as of 14 Feb 2025), but tested models are German-retail models and may not be sold in Poland.

**alerts and monitoring**

Preiswecker: set a target price with or without shipping, get email or app push when any idealo-listed merchant reaches it. Check frequency not published (feed-driven). Cannot watch a Polish shop page. No webhook.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. idealo hands the user to the merchant's site; its own checkout (Direktkauf) ended on 31 Dec 2022 per MonsterDealz. The ChatGPT app compares and links but does not buy. No agent payment, no mandates.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered beyond what product pages and reviews say. No spare-parts, Polish service-network or resale-value features.

#### data and integration

**⚠ data sources and freshness**

Merchant data feeds (CSV/API via feed tools such as Channable, Lengow, Shopware/Shopify plugins) sent at set intervals; MonsterDealz (Aug 2026) notes prices are a snapshot, flash/daily deals often appear late or not at all, and 'in stock' may reflect the last feed. The ChatGPT app answers are 'supplemented with verified product information and current prices from the idealo database' (idealo statement via report.at) and link to offers ⚠ *(unverified: link format not inspected)*.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial (none official for Claude). (1) Official API: no public consumer API; idealo Business/partner interfaces are merchant-side (feeds, click reports). (2) Official agent route: the idealo app in ChatGPT - ChatGPT Apps are built on the Apps SDK (an MCP-based extension), but idealo has not published a public MCP endpoint that Claude Code can call ⚠ *(unverified)*; no idealo server was found in the official MCP registry. (3) Unofficial scrapers: Apify 'saswave/idealo-scraper' (search or product URLs to price, title, store, offers; USD 25/month; callable through Apify's hosted MCP server), Apify 'ecomscrape' idealo actor, ScrapingBee idealo API, Oxylabs (idealo_search source, structured JSON), ZenRows (from USD 69/month). (4) Browser agent: possible but idealo.de blocks automated fetches (our WebFetch was refused) so expect anti-bot friction. (5) Claude skill: none. Setup effort: about 30-60 minutes for an Apify actor via MCP; ToS risk on the user.

**protocol support**

None of the agent-commerce payment protocols (no ACP, UCP, AP2 checkout). Exposed to ChatGPT through OpenAI's Apps SDK (MCP-based). Interoperability for Claude is therefore indirect.

**open source and licence**

Closed.

**account linking and data access**

Web use needs no account; an idealo account is optional for wish lists and Preiswecker (email). The ChatGPT app requires a ChatGPT account and enabling the app; chat content relevant to the query is sent to idealo under the partner's own privacy policy. GDPR applies (German controller). No payment credentials needed - idealo never takes payment.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

idealo forbids automated access in its terms ⚠ *(unverified: ToS not opened)* and actively blocks non-browser fetches. Scraping public prices in the EU is legally grey (database rights under the EU Database Directive, ToS contract claims); personal low-volume use via a commercial scraping provider shifts most risk to the provider. No account-ban risk if used logged-out.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Merchants pay per click to be listed; MonsterDealz notes payments can influence placement and that EU Omnibus rules since 2022 require paid rankings to be labelled. Owner Axel Springer also owns affiliate network Awin and Bonial (commerce/marketing), so commercial links are the business. Positive: not owned by a marketplace; default sort is price. The ChatGPT app adds a second layer - ChatGPT chooses which offers to show.

**ranking transparency**

Moderate on the website (sort by price, total price incl. shipping, filters; paid placements must be labelled). Low in the ChatGPT app - no explanation of why offers were picked and no way to exclude a source other than re-prompting.

**run to run consistency**

Website: N/A (deterministic sort by price at a given feed time). ChatGPT app: no repeat test found and none run; ChatGPT-based shopping answers vary between runs in multi-engine studies (Product.ai, vendor research), so expect shortlist drift.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Website: merchants are contracted partners, which filters most fake shops, but data is merchant-supplied. ChatGPT app: no study of prompt injection or persuasive-content resistance found ⚠ *(unverified)*; the app returns idealo database data rather than scraping arbitrary pages, which narrows the injection surface.

**known failures**

Outdated feed prices and late flash deals; mismatched variants and bundles in one listing; missing items without EAN; wrong or missing shipping costs; payment-method surcharges not compared; 'in stock' lag (all MonsterDealz, Aug 2026). In MonsterDealz's 150-product sample Amazon's promo price beat idealo's best price in 69.3% of matches (mean deviation 9.5%). Poland gap: no Polish shops, no shipping-to-PL pricing. Offer-count claims are inconsistent across idealo's own materials.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A as a defendant - none found. As a claimant: idealo v. Google, Berlin Regional Court (Landgericht Berlin II), Nov 2025: Google ordered to pay EUR 374.1M damages + EUR 91.1M interest (about EUR 465M) for Google Shopping self-preferencing; idealo had claimed EUR 3.3B; both sides can appeal and Google said it will.

**buyer protection path**

Purchase is a distance contract with the German/Austrian merchant: EU 14-day withdrawal right and 2-year legal guarantee apply cross-border, but return freight for a bulky trampoline may be at the buyer's cost if the shop says so. Payment-method protection (PayPal buyer protection, card chargeback) depends on how you pay at the shop. Cross-border disputes: ECC Poland / ECC Germany and the EU ODR route. idealo itself is not merchant of record.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Moderate as a cross-check, low as the main tool. For a ~3 m garden trampoline idealo.de shows dozens of German offers (deal posts in 2025-2026 put 305 cm net trampolines at roughly EUR 120-220 and premium Exit PeakPro 305 at EUR 325-396), price history and a Preiswecker, and links to Stiftung Warentest-tested models. It cannot tell you which shop delivers a 30+ kg box to Poland or at what freight, so the 'best price' is often not reachable; use it to anchor a fair DE price and spot fake discounts on the same model sold in Poland.

**workflow role**

Price and history cross-check for the DE/AT market after the shortlist is fixed; secondary discovery via the ChatGPT app. Combine with Ceneo/Allegro for Polish prices, the shop's own cart for shipping to PL, and Safety Gate/GPSR checks.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual: free, about 10-15 minutes per model (search, open history, check 2-3 shops' delivery-to-Poland terms). ChatGPT app: free within a ChatGPT plan, 5 minutes, but no evidence export. Programmatic: Apify idealo actor USD 25/month flat - one comparison of 5 models = 5 product-URL runs, effectively free within the subscription; plus about 30-60k Claude tokens to summarise.

**evidence trail**

Website: product URL, price-history chart (screenshot) and offer list can be saved manually; no export. ChatGPT app: the chat can be shared/copied but contains no timestamped snapshot. Scraper JSON (Apify) gives a timestamped record. Saved vault record: model name/EAN, idealo URL, date, lowest offer incl. shipping to DE, shop name and rating, history low over the visible window, and whether the shop ships to PL (checked manually).

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Large DE/AT merchant base and price-history chart that exposes fake discounts on models also sold in Poland.
  - Sorting by total price incl. shipping and a Preiswecker (email/app) with or without shipping.
  - ChatGPT app (since ~Mar 2026) brings delivery costs, return fees, payment options and shop ratings into a conversational flow (vendor-claimed).
  - Not owned by a marketplace; merchants pay per click and paid placements must be labelled.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No Polish market, no Polish shops, no shipping-to-Poland pricing - the cheapest DE offer may not deliver to PL.
  - Feed lag, variant/bundle mismatches and unreliable shipping data (MonsterDealz test, Aug 2026).
  - No official API or MCP for Claude Code; idealo.de blocks automated fetches; scrapers are unofficial.
  - ChatGPT app availability for Polish ChatGPT accounts is unconfirmed (partner-dependent in the EEA).
  - No safety, seller-registry or Omnibus checks; no checkout since 2023.

**independent review consensus**

MonsterDealz 'idealo im Test 2026' (18 Aug 2026; deal blog with partner links, so affiliate-flagged; method published: 150 Amazon promo products) - idealo is a good starting point but prices are snapshots, shipping data is unreliable and Amazon promos often beat it. Finanztip (consumer finance portal) recommends idealo and Geizhals and reports best prices within a few percent of each other. No independent test of the ChatGPT app was found; coverage of it (report.at, DriversCloud) is announcement-based.

**verdict for me**

PILOT (as a DE price/history cross-check only) - deciding fact: idealo has no Polish market and prices delivery to Germany/Austria, so it anchors a fair price and exposes fake discounts but rarely gives a buyable offer for a bulky item to Poland. Best use: after shortlisting a trampoline model, open its idealo.de page, note the history low and total price, then confirm in 1-2 shops' carts whether they ship to Poland and at what freight; try the ChatGPT app only if it appears for a Polish account.

**conflicting evidence**

- ChatGPT app launch date: report.at (20 Mar 2026) and DriversCloud (26 Mar 2026) vs the research outline's directory listing date of 2026-04-21.
- Catalogue/merchant size: 201M offers (ChatGPT-app coverage) vs 350M+ offers from 50,000 shops (French listing) vs 500M+ (careers page) vs 600M+ (conference profile); merchants 24,000 (app coverage) vs about 39,000 (MonsterDealz).
- Price-history length: up to one year (Finanztip) vs the last 90 days for most products (Giga).
- Checkout: discontinued on 31 Dec 2022 (MonsterDealz, Aug 2026) vs Lengow integration page (citing 2026 sources) still describing Direktkauf as configurable.
- Polish market: an older IdoSell page says idealo could be used for the Polish, UK and German markets; current sources list only DE, AT, UK, FR, IT, ES and no idealo.pl.
- ChatGPT apps in the EU: at the Oct 2025 Apps SDK launch apps were not offered in the EEA/UK/Switzerland; the OpenAI help center (Dec 2025 version) says availability there is partner-dependent; idealo's German launch implies EU availability for at least Germany.

**sources checked**

- https://www.report.at/trends/recht/idealo-einbindung-in-chatgpt - idealo ChatGPT app announcement with Co-CEO quote, 20 Mar 2026 - accessed 2026-10-15 (secondary)
- https://www.driverscloud.com/en/news/2841/shopping-30-when-the-idealo-comparator-invites-itself-into-your-chatgpt-discussions - app features, 201M offers, six markets, 26 Mar 2026 - accessed 2026-10-15 (secondary, machine-translated)
- https://www.monsterdealz.de/magazin/idealo-test - 'idealo im Test 2026', 18 Aug 2026, 150-product sample - accessed 2026-10-15 (independent but affiliate-funded)
- Search-result summaries (pages not opened): ChatGPT app listing text (delivery costs, return fees, payment options, shop ratings); OpenAI help center 'Apps in ChatGPT' (help.openai.com/en/articles/11487775 returned HTTP 403); Berlin court ruling coverage (heise.de, Engadget, MarketScreener, Nov 2025); Axel Springer split coverage (2024-2026); Finanztip and Giga on price-history length; Apify/ZenRows/Oxylabs scraper listings.
- Not retrievable: www.idealo.de (fetch refused - 'unable to fetch'), chatgpt.com/apps (HTTP 403), getdrio.com app tracker (HTTP 503), LinkedIn launch post (HTTP 999).

#### fields the agent listed as uncertain

- api mcp skill access
- automation legal risk
- data sources and freshness
- feature geo matrix
- independent test coverage
- manipulation and injection resistance

### PriceRunner, PriceSpy and Geizhals

**Verdict:** Geizhals PILOT, others SKIP · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Three non-Polish European price comparison engines (role type: comparison engine + price tracker). PriceRunner: Klarna-owned comparison site (UK, SE, DK sites, plus inside Klarna in 10 more markets). PriceSpy/Prisjakt: Swedish comparison engine in seven countries (SE, NO, FI, UK/IE, NZ, FR as leDenicheur, IT as Pagomeno). Geizhals: Austrian comparison engine strong in electronics and hardware (geizhals.at, geizhals.de, geizhals.eu). None has a Polish site any more: Geizhals' Polish edition cenowarka.pl closed on 31 Oct 2025. Only Geizhals is realistically useful to a Polish buyer, as a DE/AT price, history and spec cross-check.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

PriceRunner: PriceRunner International AB, owned by Klarna Bank AB (Stockholm, Sweden; acquired April 2022) - a BNPL/payments company, which matters for bias. PriceSpy: Prisjakt Sverige AB (founded 2002 in Angelholm, Sweden), sold by Schibsted to private-equity firm eEquity for about SEK 490-500M, closing 13 Jun 2025; an IPO on Nasdaq First North was reported as planned for Q4 2026 at a reduced valuation of SEK 675M ⚠ *(unverified: snippet only)*. Geizhals: Preisvergleich Internet Services AG, Vienna, Austria; part of the Heise group (Heise Medien acquired 75% in 2013-2014, indirect 100% since June 2021 per Wikipedia); also powers the heise Preisvergleich. None is owned by a marketplace or retailer.

**lifecycle status**

All three active as of 2026-10-15. Geizhals: cenowarka.pl (Poland) and skinflint.co.uk (UK) were shut on 31 Oct 2025 (PurePC, 22 Oct 2025); both domains return HTTP 410 Gone on 2026-10-15, and the geizhals.eu country menu now offers only Austria, Germany and EU. PriceRunner: won SEK 14.3B plus interest against Google at the Stockholm Patent and Market Court on 1 Jul 2026 (Klarna values it at about USD 1.97B with interest); Google is appealing and PriceRunner cross-appealed. PriceSpy: ownership change June 2025; about page updated 9 Oct 2025 (older than six months).

**cost model**

Free for shoppers on all three; merchants pay per click (PriceSpy states this explicitly; Geizhals says it does not rank offers by bidding). No paid consumer tiers. Programmatic: Geizhals via Apify actor 'solidcode/geizhals-de-scraper' at USD 1.00 per 1,000 products, USD 4.00 per 1,000 offer-enriched products (tiered from 25 Oct 2026), plus a small per-run fee (seen 2026-10-15). No official API for any of the three.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **pricerunner**: Sites: UK, SE, DK. Inside Klarna (web and Klarna app): NO, US, DE, AT, FI, FR, IE, IT, NL, ES. Poland: not available. Language: no Polish.
- **pricespy prisjakt**: SE, NO, FI, UK, IE, NZ, FR (leDenicheur), IT (Pagomeno). Poland: not available. Language: no Polish.
- **geizhals**: geizhals.at (AT), geizhals.de (DE), geizhals.eu (international, German UI; Mergado 2022 says it lists offers regardless of delivery country and can show German, English or Polish - ⚠ *(unverified)* whether the Polish UI survived the Oct 2025 closure of cenowarka.pl). Poland: no Polish edition since 31 Oct 2025; Polish shops not confirmed on geizhals.eu.
- **price history**: PriceRunner: yes. PriceSpy: yes, per product. Geizhals: yes, up to 12 months (MonsterDealz, Aug 2026). All only for their own markets.
- **price alerts**: Geizhals: price alarm and wish lists with an account. PriceSpy/PriceRunner: ⚠ *(unverified)* price alerts exist in their apps but not verified on primary pages. None watches a Polish shop.
- **agentic checkout**: None of the three. PriceRunner data reaches agents only through Klarna's own products (covered under the Klarna item), not in Poland.

#### capabilities

**⚠ spec and variant comparison**

Geizhals: the strongest of the group and of most comparison engines for technical goods - editorially normalised spec sheets and deep filters (150+ for notebooks; attributes like efficiency class, socket, form factor, refresh rate, PCIe generation), which is useful for choosing the right variant of electronics, tools and appliances. Weak outside tech (MonsterDealz). No documented OEM-rebadge mapping. PriceSpy: spec filters for electronics. PriceRunner: standard product pages. For trampolines none of them offers useful spec filters ⚠ *(unverified: category depth not inspected)*.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Cross-shop comparison in their own markets only. Polish channels indexed: none (no Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon.pl). PurePC noted that even cenowarka.pl lacked Allegro, Media Expert and morele.net offers before it closed. Geizhals merchant rule: EU seat and delivery to AT and DE (Mergado 2022). Scale (vendor/Wikipedia claims): Geizhals about 2.4M products; PriceSpy 'a huge set' of shops (no number); PriceRunner not stated. Not tested.

**price history and omnibus**

Geizhals shows price history (up to 12 months) and calculates displayed price changes over the last 30 days (geizhals.eu homepage), which approximates an Omnibus-style 30-day view for its listed shops but is not a per-shop Omnibus check and does not flag breaches. PriceSpy and PriceRunner show product price history in their markets. None covers Polish shops.

**⚠ total landed cost**

Partial. Geizhals can include shipping in the total price and (per Mergado 2022) sort by price including shipping to a chosen country - ⚠ *(unverified)* whether Poland is selectable after Oct 2025. Shows shipping times and stock. No payment fees, assembly, return-freight or cross-border warranty calculation. PriceSpy/PriceRunner: shipping shown for domestic delivery only.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. Geizhals and PriceSpy show merchant ratings and product reviews; PriceRunner has a 'safe shopping' information page. No review-authenticity method published and no checks against Polish registries (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list) or VIES.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No Safety Gate/UOKiK, GPSR, EN 71-14 or certificate checks.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

Geizhals product pages link to test reports and ratings (Wikipedia feature list) for tech products. Not a test lab. Germany/Austria-relevant labs (Stiftung Warentest, VKI) are not systematically surfaced for garden goods ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

Geizhals price alarm (account required, email); PriceSpy and PriceRunner app alerts ⚠ *(unverified)*. Frequency follows merchant feeds. Cannot watch Polish shop pages. No webhooks.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. All three hand the user to the merchant's site; none buys on the user's behalf.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Merchant feeds sent by contracted shops (Geizhals requires a contract; MonsterDealz notes only contracted merchants are listed), with editorial product normalisation at Geizhals. Refresh frequency not published. Answers are link-backed (each offer links to the shop).

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial for Geizhals, none for PriceRunner/PriceSpy from Poland. (1) Official APIs: none public for consumers. (2) MCP: no official server; Geizhals is reachable through Apify's hosted MCP (mcp.apify.com, OAuth or API token) using the 'solidcode/geizhals-de-scraper' actor, which returns product ID, MPN, best price, offer count and, with full offers, merchant, price, shipping, total and spec sheet for geizhals.de/.at/.eu (5 total users, 100% run success, no reviews - young actor). (3) Community: a Home Assistant 'geizhals' sensor and SearXNG engine have scraped Geizhals. (4) Browser agent: Geizhals pages are plain HTML and fetchable (geizhals.eu fetched fine on 2026-10-15). (5) Claude skill: none. Setup effort: about 30 minutes for Apify MCP. PriceRunner/PriceSpy: only scraping, and their data is irrelevant to Polish delivery.

**protocol support**

None of ACP/UCP/AP2/Klarna APP on the comparison sites themselves. PriceRunner's catalogue feeds Klarna's agentic products (Klarna Agentic Product Protocol, Klarna's Shopping Search app in ChatGPT) - covered under the Klarna item, and PriceRunner data does not cover Poland.

**open source and licence**

Closed (all three).

**account linking and data access**

No account needed for browsing; accounts for alerts/wish lists (Geizhals) and app features. PriceRunner inside the Klarna app ties browsing to a Klarna payments account (BNPL profile) - a data-sharing consideration. GDPR applies to all three (AT, SE controllers).

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Scraping public price pages for personal use is low practical risk; EU database-right and ToS arguments exist. Geizhals content is editorially curated (stronger database-right claim) ⚠ *(unverified: ToS not opened)*. No account-ban risk when logged out.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

CPC from merchants on all three. PriceSpy says payment cannot buy a higher position because offers are sorted by price (vendor claim); Geizhals says it does not rank offers by bidding. PriceRunner's owner Klarna earns from BNPL and merchant fees, so Klarna-enabled merchants and Klarna app placement are a bias vector ⚠ *(unverified: no evidence of biased ranking found)*.

**ranking transparency**

High relative to AI tools: default sort by price (Geizhals ties broken by shipping time, stock, then customer rating per Mergado 2022); filters are explicit. Sponsored placements, where present, must be labelled under EU rules.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - deterministic sorted lists, not AI-generated.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

N/A for AI injection (no LLM layer). Contracted-merchant model filters most fake shops; data is merchant-supplied and can be stale or wrong.

**known failures**

Geizhals: weak assortment outside technology, demanding interface for beginners, only contracted merchants (MonsterDealz, Aug 2026); its Polish edition failed (low recognition vs Ceneo, no Allegro/Media Expert/morele offers, incomplete Polish translation - PurePC) and closed in Oct 2025. PriceRunner/PriceSpy: no Poland coverage. Wikipedia's Geizhals page still lists cenowarka.pl and skinflint.co.uk and gives an implausible '280,000 traders' figure - outdated.

**regulatory enforcement history**

As claimants against Google: PriceRunner (Klarna) v. Google - Stockholm Patent and Market Court, 1 Jul 2026, SEK 14.3B damages plus about SEK 0.4B interest for Google Shopping self-preferencing in the UK, Sweden and Denmark (2008-2023); claim was about SEK 80B; Google appealing, PriceRunner cross-appealing. No enforcement against the three operators found. Geizhals and PriceSpy: N/A - none found.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

None from the comparison sites (not merchants of record). Buying from a DE/AT shop found on Geizhals: EU 14-day withdrawal and 2-year legal guarantee, payment-method protection (PayPal, card chargeback), ECC Poland for cross-border disputes. PriceRunner via Klarna adds Klarna's buyer protection only where Klarna is the payment method ⚠ *(unverified)*.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low for the trampoline: none lists Polish shops, and Geizhals' strength is electronics/hardware, not garden equipment; DE/AT trampoline offers would still need shipping-to-Poland checks. Moderate for other durables in the buyer's pattern (tools, appliances, electronics): Geizhals' normalised specs and filters plus 12-month history make it a good place to pick the right variant (e.g. a cordless drill kit or a dishwasher model number) and to anchor a fair EU price before buying in Poland.

**workflow role**

Geizhals: specs and variants plus DE/AT price-history cross-check for technical durables. PriceRunner and PriceSpy: none for a Polish buyer (context only: market structure, Google litigation). Combine Geizhals with Ceneo/Allegro for Polish prices and the shop cart for shipping to PL.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual Geizhals check: free, about 10 minutes per model. Programmatic: Apify geizhals actor - 5 candidate models with full offers = 5 offer-enriched products = USD 0.02 plus the per-run start fee, effectively cents; plus about 30-50k Claude tokens. PriceRunner/PriceSpy: not worth any spend from Poland.

**evidence trail**

Geizhals product URLs are stable and include the product ID; the price-history chart and offer table can be screenshotted, and the Apify actor JSON carries a scrape timestamp, MPN and per-merchant total price. Vault record: model/MPN, Geizhals URL and ID, date, lowest total price to DE/AT, 12-month low, top 3 merchants with ratings.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Geizhals: best-in-class normalised specs and filters for technical goods - directly supports choosing the right variant.
  - Geizhals: price history up to 12 months and a 30-day price-change view; deterministic price-sorted lists with no bidding.
  - Geizhals is fetchable and has a cheap Apify actor callable through Apify's hosted MCP from Claude Code.
  - PriceRunner/PriceSpy: mature price history in their markets and transparent CPC models.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No Polish coverage anywhere: cenowarka.pl closed 31 Oct 2025; PriceRunner and PriceSpy never covered Poland.
  - Geizhals is weak outside technology, so it does little for garden goods like trampolines.
  - Shipping-to-Poland pricing is unconfirmed after Geizhals' Polish edition closed.
  - No safety, seller-registry or Omnibus-breach checks; no official APIs.
  - PriceRunner is owned by Klarna (BNPL), a potential bias vector inside the Klarna app.

**independent review consensus**

MonsterDealz 'Geizhals & billiger.de 2026' (18 Aug 2026; deal blog with partner links, affiliate-flagged): Geizhals excels at technical filtering and 12-month history, is weak outside tech. Finanztip (cited there) found best prices across major portals within a few percent and rated Geizhals strongest on tech filters. PurePC (22 Oct 2025) on why cenowarka.pl failed in Poland. No independent hands-on test of PriceRunner or PriceSpy relevant to Polish buyers found.

**verdict for me**

PILOT Geizhals for technical durables / SKIP PriceRunner and PriceSpy - deciding fact: none covers Polish shops (cenowarka.pl closed 31 Oct 2025; PriceRunner and PriceSpy never served Poland), but Geizhals' normalised spec filters and 12-month DE/AT history are the best variant-picking tool for electronics, tools and appliances. Best use: pull the Geizhals product page (or Apify JSON via MCP) for 3-5 candidate models to fix the exact variant and a fair EU price, then buy through Polish channels; skip all three for the trampoline.

**conflicting evidence**

- Geizhals countries: MonsterDealz (Aug 2026) says Geizhals is active in Austria, Germany, Poland and the UK; PurePC (22 Oct 2025) reports the Polish and UK editions closed on 31 Oct 2025, confirmed by HTTP 410 on cenowarka.pl and skinflint.co.uk and by the geizhals.eu country menu (AT, DE, EU only) on 2026-10-15.
- Geizhals Polish UI: Mergado (Mar 2022) says geizhals.eu displays items in German, English or Polish; the geizhals.eu homepage fetched on 2026-10-15 showed only German and no language selector.
- PriceRunner award size: SEK 14.3B plus interest reported as about EUR 1.7B (Euronews), about USD 1.5B (SEK 14.3B + SEK 0.4B interest, citizen.digital/MLex-based) and about USD 1.97B with interest (Klarna's own valuation); differences come from interest and exchange-rate assumptions.
- PriceRunner ruling day: reported as Tuesday by one outlet and Wednesday 1 Jul 2026 by others; the court had earlier rescheduled the judgment from 15 Apr to 10 Jun 2026.
- Geizhals founding year: 1996 (Wikipedia infobox) vs 1997 (Wikipedia body, MonsterDealz).
