### Pepper.pl and Okazje.info.pl

**Verdict:** Pepper USE NOW (secondary), Okazje SKIP · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **pepper pl**: Crowd-curated deal community (role: deal community / social price signal). Members and editors post deals, other members vote them 'hot' or 'cold'; the sum is the deal's temperature and deals above 200 degrees reach the hot list. Also runs coupons, keyword alerts, mobile apps and a coupon/deal browser extension (Pepper Shopping Assistant). It is not a comparison engine and has no product database.
- **okazje info pl**: Polish price comparison engine (role: comparison engine) at www.okazje.info.pl, running since 2005. It lists offers from partner shops fed by product feeds, sends clicks to the shop, and runs a shop-rating programme ('Wiarygodne Opinie', certificate 'Polecany Przez Klientow') and a shop ranking site (ranking.okazje.info.pl). It does not sell anything itself.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

- **pepper pl**: Operator per the pepper.pl terms: Atolls Germany GmbH, Radlkoferstrasse 2, 81373 Munich, Germany (HRB 209997, Munich local court). Pepper.com was founded in Berlin in June 2014 by Fabian Spielberger and Paul Nikkel, merged with Global Savings Group (contract announced 2022-12-07), and the combined group was renamed Atolls in September 2024. Atolls is an affiliate, coupon and cashback group (iGraal, Shoop, Coupons.com, CupoNation, mydealz, hotukdeals, Dealabs, Pepper.pl and others) with EUR 165M revenue in 2022 and about 1,000 staff (Wikipedia, secondary). Bias note: the owner earns from affiliate commissions on purchases, which is the same revenue as Pepper.pl itself. ⚠ *(unverified)* Current shareholders are not disclosed in the sources found; the 2022 deal names lending banks (UniCredit, Commerzbank, Citibank, KfW) but no equity investors.
- **okazje info pl**: Grupa Okazje Sp. z o.o., ul. Lakowa 3/5 N, 90-562 Lodz, Poland; KRS 0000513788, NIP 7252071227, REGON 101681944 (from the site's regulamin). Partner services named in the terms: youshop.pl, youstyle.pl, youhome.pl, rabatuj.pl, markety.okazje.info.pl. The same group sells a Google Shopping CSS service (ShopSynergy, shopsynergy.eu) and Google product-campaign management to shops. ⚠ *(unverified)* Shareholders not checked in KRS; a 2012 article named Piotr Broniarczyk as CEO, which may be outdated.

**lifecycle status**

- **pepper pl**: Launched 2014-06-01 (pepper.pl timeline). Active: the public RSS 'hot' feed returned current deals on 2026-10-15 and the site ran an 'Jesienne okazje 2026' campaign. Notable changes: Verified Partners (brands) allowed to post deals, reported 2021-05-14 (Antyweb); operator changed to Atolls after the 2022 merger and 2024 rename. Verified 2026-10-15 against pepper.pl/about, /faq, /strona/regulamin, /strona/code-of-conduct.
- **okazje info pl**: Running since 2005 (footer '(c) 2005 - 2026'). Active on 2026-10-15: search returned live offers (e.g. 299 offers for 'trampolina 305'). No dated changelog found; the regulamin has no version date. Verified 2026-10-15 against okazje.info.pl/s/regulamin.html, /s/onas.html and live search pages.

**cost model**

Free for buyers, both services (seen 2026-10-15). Pepper.pl is funded by affiliate commissions, paid 'promowane'/'sponsorowane' deal slots and a creator-programme ad slot (terms Part B 1.5 and 7). Okazje.info is funded by shops paying per click (it links a 'Minimalne stawki CPC' price list for shops), Google Ad Manager display ads, and CSS / Google-campaign services sold to shops. No paid tier for buyers on either.

**feature geo matrix**

- **pepper pl**: Poland only, Polish interface and Polish community. Deals may point to foreign shops (Amazon.de, Amazon.es etc.); the rules require the price in the foreign currency and in PLN. Keyword alerts, RSS, voting and apps (Android, iOS) all work in Poland. Sister sites cover DE (mydealz), UK (hotukdeals), FR (Dealabs), AT, NL and others, so a cross-border check means visiting those separately. No US-only features apply.
- **okazje info pl**: Poland only, Polish interface, Polish shops plus some marketplace feeds (Allegro and Amazon.pl offers appeared for 'Hudora trampolina'; Empik.com marketplace offers dominated 'trampolina 305'). No EU cross-border coverage. No alerts or AI features.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

- **pepper pl**: None structured. Each deal is free text from the poster, sometimes with a spec list. Comments do catch variant and white-label issues: for example a poster noted that Zipro is Morele's own brand, so the Allegro shop 'ZIPRO' is the same seller. No EAN/GTIN mapping, no lineup comparison. Grade: none.
- **okazje info pl**: Weak. Offers are listed per feed item, not grouped into products: the same EXIT model appears several times in different colours, and raw feed fields such as Gtin, Ean, Producer, Old_price and Sale_price are printed under the offer, which lets a careful reader match EANs by hand. No spec table or variant mapping. Grade: partial at best (EAN visible on some offers).

**price comparison and pl coverage**

- **pepper pl**: Not a price comparison. Coverage is whatever members post: Allegro, Morele, Empik, x-kom-type shops, Amazon.de and local stores (Auchan, Brico Marche). A search for 'trampolina' on 2026-10-15 returned about 30 deals, almost all budget or private-label brands (Zipro, Neo-Sport, RevoGym, 4Fizjo, Rebel, Motion, Corciano, Total Sport); none from Berg, EXIT, Salta, Hudora, Kettler or Springfree appeared on that page. Deal posts often cite the next cheapest offer found elsewhere ('Podobne w necie od okolo 430 zl').
- **okazje info pl**: Compares offers from feeding shops. Own tests on 2026-10-15: 'trampolina 305' gave 299 offers, the first page mostly Empik.com marketplace items plus bonideco.pl, fitshop.pl and tyletegotu.pl; 'Kettler Jump 305' gave 1 offer (fitshop.pl, 1,159 zl); 'Zipro Jump Pro 312' gave 1 offer (Empik.com); 'Berg Champion 330' gave 0; 'Hudora trampolina' gave 19 (15 Allegro, 4 Amazon.pl). No Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon offers seen in these tests. Shop count not published (vendor gives no figure). Coverage is far thinner than Ceneo for durables.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

- **pepper pl**: No native price history. The deal record carries a poster-entered 'nextBestPrice' (seen in the deal page JSON), and the FAQ tells posters to check a price comparison site because shops raise prices before promotions, and to quote the next-best market price rather than the shop's inflated 'before' price. The code of conduct does not require the Omnibus 30-day lowest price. Members add it voluntarily: one trampoline post quotes 'Najnizsza cena z ostatnich 30 dni to 399 zl', another warns the in-store tag lacked the 30-day price. Real-vs-fake discount judgement therefore comes from the crowd (temperature plus comments), not from data.
- **okazje info pl**: No price history or Omnibus field seen in the current search UI (2026-10-15). Feed fields 'Old_price' are shown raw and are not checked: several offers showed Old_price below Sale_price (77.69 vs 87.85 zl; 573.47 vs 593.58 zl), so the 'old price' is not a reliable discount reference. ⚠ *(unverified)* robots.txt still lists an 'Ajax,drawProductPriceChart' endpoint, which suggests a price chart exists or existed on some product view; none was found in the pages tested.

**⚠ total landed cost**

- **pepper pl**: Informal only. Posters often state delivery ('Dostawa 14,99 zl, darmowa ze Smart!em', 'Darmowa dostawa') and coupon steps; nothing computes returns, assembly or warranty. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether Pepper.pl deal prices must include shipping was not confirmed (mydealz debated and kept shipping-inclusive prices).
- **okazje info pl**: No. Offers show item price and a delivery-time hint ('1 dzien'); no shipping, return or assembly costs.

**review and seller verification**

- **pepper pl**: None formal. The support team moderates deals (new users first), and comments often warn about bad shops, but nothing checks CEIDG/KRS/VAT lists or shop ratings. Grade: none (community warnings only). It cannot prove a seller is legitimate.
- **okazje info pl**: Partial for shops only. 'Wiarygodne Opinie' sends a survey link by email after a purchase; shops above a rating and volume threshold get the 'Polecany Przez Klientow' badge. The page does not explain how purchases are verified or whether unverified opinions are shown, and gives no Omnibus statement on review verification. No product-review authenticity checks, no registry checks. Grade: partial.

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A for both - neither checks Safety Gate, UOKiK registers, GPSR listing fields, EN 71-14 versions or certificates. Nothing can run automatically here.

**independent test coverage**

N/A for both - neither surfaces Stiftung Warentest, VKI, CHOICE or other lab results. Pepper comment threads occasionally link outside tests, but not systematically.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

- **pepper pl**: Keyword alerts on deal titles with a minimum-temperature threshold (account needed), delivered in the app and by email/push; comment subscriptions per deal; public RSS feed of hot deals (https://www.pepper.pl/rss/gor%C4%85ce, live 2026-10-15). It cannot watch a specific Polish shop page. ⚠ *(unverified)* Exact delivery channels per alert type were not tested with an account.
- **okazje info pl**: None found. Only a local 'Ulubione' favourites list.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No for both. They only link out to the merchant; payment, checkout and confirmation all happen at the shop.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered. Pepper occasionally carries spare-part deals (trampoline nets, mats, spring covers) and outlet/returned units (e.g. a Zipro outlet trampoline), which helps with parts pricing; Okazje.info lists spare nets and covers as ordinary offers. Neither covers service networks, warranty handling or resale value.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

- **pepper pl**: User and editor posts, moderated; each deal has publish and update timestamps and an expiry flag. Deals expire automatically after 30 days or when users mark them ended, so a deal can show a price that no longer exists (the page JSON had 'stale': true and 'isExpired': true on a 2026 trampoline deal). Each answer is backed by a link to the shop, not a price snapshot.
- **okazje info pl**: Shop product feeds (raw feed fields visible in results, e.g. Custom_label_1, Old_price, Sale_price). Refresh frequency not published. Offers link out through redirects; no snapshot.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: partial (Pepper RSS) / none (Okazje.info)
- **pepper pl**: No official API, no MCP server, no Claude skill. Usable routes: (1) public RSS of hot deals (https://www.pepper.pl/rss/gor%C4%85ce, plain XML with merchant, price and temperature in the title; the old /rss/hot redirects there) that a Claude Code skill can fetch with curl at near-zero setup; (2) manual use of keyword alerts; (3) browser agent on deal pages. robots.txt disallows /search, /rest-api/, /graphql and filter parameters for all agents, and blocks ClaudeBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, CCBot and Google-Extended from the whole site (checked 2026-10-15), so automated search scraping is against the site's stated wishes. Third-party scrapers exist for the sister site hotukdeals on Apify (not checked). Setup effort: 15 minutes for an RSS reader; anything beyond that is scraping.
- **okazje info pl**: No API, MCP or skill. Pages are server-rendered HTML and can be fetched with curl (done in this research), and there is an OpenSearch template (https://www.okazje.info.pl/search/?q={searchTerms}), but robots.txt disallows /search/, /json/ and /redirect/. Fallback: manual use. Grade: none.

**protocol support**

None for both (no ACP, UCP, AP2, MCP, Klarna APP or Web Bot Auth support found).

**open source and licence**

Closed (both).

**account linking and data access**

- **pepper pl**: Browsing is anonymous; an account is needed to vote, post, comment and set alerts. Pepper says it uses basic, anonymous profile data through Google Ad Manager to personalise promoted slots (opt-out offered). The Pepper Shopping Assistant extension (Atolls Germany GmbH) reads partner-site URLs to show deals and auto-test coupons, and its links are monetised. No payment credentials. EU operator, GDPR applies.
- **okazje info pl**: No account needed. Google Tag Manager and Google Ad Manager (doubleclick) load on search pages; cookie consent is by browser settings only ('Mozesz nie wyrazic zgody przez ustawienia przegladarki'). No payment data.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

- **pepper pl**: Moderate. robots.txt blocks AI crawlers and AI user agents entirely and blocks search for everyone; the terms bar unauthorised reproduction or copying of the platform and offers (Part A 4.1) and voting manipulation; no explicit anti-bot clause was found. Accounts using VPNs or foreign IPs may be blocked under the community rules. Reading the RSS feed is the low-risk route.
- **okazje info pl**: Low to moderate. robots.txt disallows search and JSON paths; ⚠ *(unverified)* the regulamin was not checked for an explicit scraping clause. Low-volume personal checks are unlikely to trigger action.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

- **pepper pl**: Affiliate commissions on outbound links (FAQ: 'obecnie stosujemy linki, dzieki ktorym mozemy otrzymac prowizje'); paid 'promowane'/'sponsorowane' slots that partners buy for short-term exposure, which can still appear in the hot list; Verified Partner accounts (brands) posting their own deals since 2021; a creator programme placing banner ads near user content. The owner Atolls is an affiliate and cashback company. In the UK, the ASA upheld a complaint against sister company Pepper Deals Ltd (hotukdeals) on 2020-03-18 because affiliate links were not obviously identifiable as ads. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether individual Pepper.pl deal links are labelled as affiliate links was not checked deal by deal. Bias vector: deals from affiliate-paying shops are more likely to be posted and promoted; temperature favours cheap, exciting prices over quality.
- **okazje info pl**: Shops pay per click and the ranking disclosure on every result page says order takes into account match, price, promotions, discount coupons, 'oplaty ponoszone przez sprzedawcow' (fees paid by sellers) and popularity. Paid placement therefore affects order and is not marked per offer. Owner also sells Google CSS and campaign services to the same shops.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

- **pepper pl**: Partial. Temperature = sum of hot and cold votes; above 200 degrees a deal is hot; new deals show 'Nowe' for a few minutes to stop early votes from skewing them; promoted deals are labelled. ⚠ *(unverified)* An older review states vote weight differs by user; Pepper does not publish weights. You cannot rerun with a source excluded.
- **okazje info pl**: Low. One generic sentence lists the ranking factors including seller fees; no per-offer sponsored label, no weights, and default sort is 'wg trafnosci' (relevance). Price sort ascending/descending is available.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - non-AI tools. Note that Pepper temperatures and Okazje.info order change over time, so record the date of any check.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

- **pepper pl**: Rules forbid multiple accounts, selling or lending accounts, self-promotion, user affiliate links and vote manipulation (including tactical cold votes); penalty points lead to bans. Evidence of attempts: job ads on Useme asked for posting a shop's deals from an account with history to avoid removal (403 on re-open, seen in search results only); users accuse some accounts of bot-posting Amazon deals for creator-programme revenue (unverified); after several accepted posts, new posts go live without moderator review. No published data on scale. Not an AI agent, so prompt injection does not apply.
- **okazje info pl**: Feed content is shown as the shop sends it (raw feed labels such as 'Custom_label_1: bestoffers' and inconsistent old prices reached the page), so a shop can present misleading 'old prices'. Review rules forbid fake or repeated reviews; no detection method published.

**known failures**

- **pepper pl**: Stale deals that still look live after the price changes; coverage skewed to budget and private-label goods; temperature measures price excitement, not product quality or safety; local in-store deals that cannot be reproduced; paid seeding and partner posts mixed with community posts; no structured specs.
- **okazje info pl**: Very thin coverage for named durable models (0-1 offers for Berg, Kettler and Zipro models tested); results flooded by one marketplace feed (Empik.com); unchecked 'old price' fields, sometimes lower than the sale price; ranking influenced by seller fees; no history or alerts.

**regulatory enforcement history**

No UOKiK, DSA or court decision against Pepper.pl, Atolls or Grupa Okazje found (searched 2026-10-15). Related: UK ASA ruling A19-1034186 against Pepper Deals Ltd (hotukdeals) upheld 2020-03-18 over unlabelled affiliate links.

**buyer protection path**

Neither is the merchant of record and both disclaim liability for purchases (Pepper terms Part A 8.2). Protection is whatever the destination shop gives: Allegro Protect when the deal is on Allegro, PL statutory warranty (rekojmia) and the 14-day withdrawal right for distance purchases from a business, card chargeback or PayPal buyer protection depending on payment, and the ECC route for EU cross-border deals such as Amazon.de. Marketplace deals (Empik.com marketplace, Allegro) may be sold by third-party or foreign sellers, which changes who you claim against.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

- **pepper pl**: Moderate as a cheap secondary check. For the trampoline: set a keyword alert 'trampolina' with a minimum temperature, and when a shortlisted model appears, read the comments for price context, private-label notes and delivery issues. It cannot compare premium brands (none appeared on 2026-10-15), cannot judge safety, and trampoline deals cluster in spring, so it is a timing and sanity tool, not a selection tool.
- **okazje info pl**: Low. For the trampoline, the named models tested returned 0-1 offers and the generic search was dominated by one marketplace feed with unchecked old prices; Ceneo covers the same job better.

**workflow role**

Price and deal-timing step only (after the shortlist and safety checks): Pepper.pl as a social 'is this promo real' signal and keyword alert; Okazje.info as an occasional extra feed check. Combine with Ceneo price history, the shop's Omnibus 30-day lowest price, and seller identity checks.

**effort and cost per purchase**

EUR 0. Pepper: about 5 minutes per product (search plus reading comments), or a one-time 15-minute RSS fetch in a skill (no API cost). Okazje.info: about 2 minutes per search. Arithmetic for one trampoline comparison: 2 searches x 0 credits = 0; the only cost is the user's time.

**evidence trail**

Pepper deal URL with publish date, temperature, price, merchant and comment thread; the RSS item gives title with temperature and price as text that can be pasted into a vault note. Okazje.info: search URL, offer price, shop name and the GTIN/EAN when shown. Neither keeps price snapshots, so save a dated screenshot or the RSS text. Suggested record: 'Pepper 2026-xx-xx, 312 degrees, Zipro Jump Pro 12ft 589 zl @ Morele, comments: same price on Allegro ZIPRO shop, code DEAL26' plus URL.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Pepper: crowd judgement on whether a 'promo' is real, with posters told to quote the next-best market price instead of the shop's inflated old price (FAQ).
  - Pepper: comments surface private-label links (Zipro = Morele) and Omnibus lapses that no tool flags.
  - Pepper: free keyword alerts with a minimum-temperature threshold and a public RSS feed usable from a skill.
  - Okazje.info: shows EAN/GTIN for some offers and discloses its ranking factors, including seller fees.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Pepper: no price history, no specs, no safety signal; coverage skewed to budget brands for trampolines.
  - Pepper: affiliate and promoted-slot revenue for an affiliate-group owner; sister site hotukdeals lost an ASA case on unlabelled affiliate links.
  - Pepper: robots.txt blocks AI agents and search for all crawlers, so automation beyond RSS is unwelcome.
  - Okazje.info: 0-1 offers for named durable models, raw unchecked old prices (some below the sale price), seller fees in ranking.
  - Okazje.info: no price history, Omnibus field or alerts.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on evaluation of either service's accuracy was found. Secondary coverage: Antyweb (2021-05-14) was sceptical of Pepper.pl opening posting to verified brand partners; a Tabletowo piece covered the same expansion (not opened); the UK ASA ruling (2020) on hotukdeals is the only regulator finding for the group. Okazje.info appears only in lists of Polish comparison sites (Spider's Web tag pages) without testing. The findings above come from this research's own checks on 2026-10-15.

**verdict for me**

Pepper.pl: USE NOW, as a free secondary check - set a 'trampolina' keyword alert with a temperature threshold and read the deal thread before buying a shortlisted model, but never use it to choose the model. Okazje.info.pl: SKIP - named trampoline models returned 0-1 offers and its 'old prices' are unchecked feed values; use Ceneo instead.

**conflicting evidence**

- Pepper ownership: pepper.pl/about says Pepper belongs to an 'independent group' with an office in Berlin, while the pepper.pl terms name Atolls Germany GmbH in Munich as operator (Atolls = former Global Savings Group, merged with Pepper in 2022, renamed 2024).
- Pepper moderation: the FAQ says the support team checks every deal, while the same FAQ says that after several successful posts new deals go to the front page automatically.
- Okazje.info price history: no chart seen in any tested page (2026-10-15), but robots.txt still lists an 'Ajax,drawProductPriceChart' endpoint.

### Keepa and CamelCamelCamel

**Verdict:** Keepa USE NOW (not Amazon.pl), CamelCamelCamel SKIP · **Cost:** Free extension; Keepa Pro EUR 29 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 4 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **keepa**: Amazon price tracker and data service (role: price tracker + data API + official MCP server). Browser extension (Chrome v5.72, updated 2026-10-13; Firefox v5.66, updated 2026-09-21) adds price-history charts and alerts to Amazon product pages; Keepa Pro adds seller/sales-rank tools; the Keepa API returns price, offer, deal and seller data as JSON with price history back to 2011, and the same API plan powers a hosted MCP server at https://keepa.com/mcp.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Free Amazon price tracker (role: price tracker). Price-history charts for the Amazon, third-party new and third-party used price lines, email price-drop alerts, wishlist import, and The Camelizer browser extension. No API.

**vendor and ownership**

- **keepa**: Keepa GmbH, Berndorfer Str. 10, 95478 Kemnath, Germany; Amtsgericht Weiden i.d.OPf. HRB 5942; managing directors Julian Johann and Sascha Arthur; VAT ID DE313904564 (keepa.com disclaimer, 2026-10-15). Independent of Amazon; self-declared EU 'trader' on the Chrome Web Store. Funding not disclosed; revenue from subscriptions and API plans.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Cosmic Shovel, Inc. (US), founded 2008 by Daniel Green (Wikipedia; RevenueGeeks 2026-08-05 lists a four-person team). Independent of Amazon; revenue from Amazon affiliate commissions per RevenueGeeks, and Wikipedia cites a donation page.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

- **keepa**: Active and changing. Price history since 2011. API changelog entries on 2026-02-23 (price types switched from lowest listing price to lowest landed price), 2026-04-20 (fields removed, search page size 20), 2026-08-25 (new 'savingBasis' fields for Amazon strikethrough reference prices), 2026-10-08 (latest). Terms and Conditions version of 2026-10-07. Hosted MCP server live on 2026-10-15 ⚠ *(unverified)* (launch date not stated on Keepa's pages). Verified 2026-10-15 on keepa.com (#!api, #!data, #!terms, #!disclaimer), keepa.com/api-docs and the Chrome/Firefox listings.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Active since 2008; Walmart sister site camelmart.com reported in 2026 (RevenueGeeks, not verified). The Camelizer extension last updated June 2024 per RevenueGeeks (older than six months). Site sits behind a Cloudflare bot check, which blocked this research's browser on 2026-10-15, so live status was confirmed only indirectly. Past incidents: database outage of several days in January 2019; stopped tracking some regions at Amazon's request during COVID-19 (Wikipedia).

**cost model**

- **keepa**: Freemium. Free: price-history charts in the extension and price-drop/stock alerts (free account for alerts). Keepa Pro: EUR 29/month (keepa.com/#!data, seen 2026-10-15; EUR 290/year per RevenueGeeks 2026-08-20) with a quota that refills 5% per hour. API (includes the MCP connector): from EUR 49/month for 20 tokens/min, EUR 459 for 250, EUR 2,499 for 2,000, EUR 11,099 for 10,000 tokens/min (keepa.com/#!api, 2026-10-15); slider steps such as 60 tokens/min for EUR 129 are reported by RevenueGeeks. Prepaid monthly by card via Stripe, cancel any time, no discounts, no pro-rata refunds. Token costs: 1 per product, +6 per offer page, 10 per search page, 5 per 150 deals, 50 per best-seller list.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Free; no paid tier, no API plan (RevenueGeeks 2026-08-05).

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **keepa**: Marketplaces: 11 - US, UK, DE, FR, JP, CA, IT, ES, IN, MX, BR (keepa.com/#!api, 2026-10-15). Amazon.pl is NOT supported: absent from the API's Domain enum, the extension's supported-domain list and the Firefox permission list; users have asked for it and a seller-tool vendor lists Poland among marketplaces without Keepa graphs. Usable from Poland for Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es purchases. Interface: English extension listing; no Polish UI found. No US-only restrictions on features.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Marketplaces: US, UK, CA, DE, FR, IT, ES, AU (Wikipedia; RevenueGeeks 2026); an older official features page also lists Japan ⚠ *(unverified)*. No Amazon.pl, no NL/SE/BE. English, German, French, Italian and Spanish interfaces.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A for specs - both track one ASIN at a time. Keepa's Pro 'Variation Data' compares all variations of a listing by price and review share, and the API returns parent/variation relationships; it does not map EAN/GTIN across shops or across other Amazon marketplaces' different ASINs. CamelCamelCamel has no variant view. Grade: partial (Keepa, within Amazon only) / none (CCC).

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Amazon only; no Polish shops, no Allegro, no Ceneo shops. Keepa offers 'international price comparison' across its 11 Amazon locales (DE/FR/IT/ES/UK are the useful ones from Poland). Neither covers Amazon.pl, which is the main gap for a Polish buyer. Vendor claim: Keepa tracks 7.9 billion products (keepa.com counter, 2026-10-15) - vendor-claimed.

**price history and omnibus**

Both show long price history (Keepa back to 2011; CCC since tracking began per product) for the Amazon price and third-party new/used offers. Neither shows a labelled Omnibus value, but Keepa's API stats (minInInterval, avg30/avg90/avg180) let you derive the 30-day lowest price, and since 2026-08-25 the API exposes Amazon's strikethrough reference price ('savingBasis'), so an agent can test whether an Amazon.de 'was' price respects the 30-day rule. This is the strongest fake-discount check available, but only for Amazon marketplaces Keepa covers.

**total landed cost**

Partial. Since 2026-02-23 Keepa's NEW/USED price types use the lowest landed price (item plus shipping) rather than the listing price, and stats include import-fee flags for the Buy Box. Neither tool covers delivery to Poland specifically, return shipping, assembly or warranty enforceability. CCC shows item prices only.

**review and seller verification**

Keepa: partial for Amazon sellers - seller lookup with rating history and storefronts (Pro/API), offer-level seller and fulfilment data; it can show whether Amazon itself sells the item. No review-authenticity analysis (an old 'isScam' field was removed on 2026-02-23). CCC: none. Neither checks CEIDG/KRS/VIES.

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A - neither checks Safety Gate, GPSR fields, EN 71-14 versions or certificates.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - neither surfaces lab tests.

**alerts and monitoring**

- **keepa**: Price-drop, back-in-stock and Lightning Deal alerts. Channels: email, browser push, Telegram and RSS (third-party guides; one user reports Telegram alerts within 20-30 seconds) and webhooks via the API /tracking endpoint (keepa.com/#!api). Tracked products refresh about hourly, popular ones more often (developer statement in an older Firefox review; API tracking interval default 1 hour). Cannot watch Polish shop pages or Amazon.pl.
- **camelcamelcamel**: Email alerts at a target price or percentage drop, set without an account via email confirmation; RSS per product and price type. Refresh schedule not published.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. Neither buys anything; links go to Amazon, where the buyer checks out.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: the used-price line (Keepa and CCC) shows the Amazon used/Warehouse market for a product, a weak proxy for resale value; no spare parts, service network or OLX/Allegro Lokalnie data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Keepa: its own crawl of Amazon product and offer pages, with time-stamped history; tracked items roughly hourly; Keepa states shown data are historical records collected at the indicated time and may differ from the live price. CCC: own crawl of Amazon, refresh not published (a product page showed a scan five hours old per RevenueGeeks). Answers are chart links, not snapshots of the Amazon page; Keepa's Graph Image API can render a PNG.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full (Keepa, paid) / none (CamelCamelCamel)
- **keepa official api**: REST over HTTPS, key as 'key' parameter, token-bucket rate limit (tokens refill per minute, expire after 60 minutes, max burst = rate x 60). Docs: https://keepa.com/api-docs/ . Official Java and PHP clients; community Python client 'keepa' (pip). Endpoints include /product (history and stats), /query (Product Finder), /deal, /bestsellers, /seller, /tracking (webhook alerts), /graphimage. Offered for commercial and professional use only (T&C section 18: directed at entrepreneurs; a sole trader buying for business use qualifies).
- **keepa official mcp**: Hosted Streamable-HTTP MCP server https://keepa.com/mcp, included in every API plan. Claude Code: 'claude mcp add --transport http keepa https://keepa.com/mcp', then /mcp to authenticate with OAuth, or add '--header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"'. Capabilities: product lookup with prices, stats and Buy Box; decoded price histories; chart rendering; Amazon search; Product Finder queries; price drops and Lightning Deals; best sellers; seller/storefront inspection; tracking with notifications. Tool calls cost the same tokens as API calls. Remote, no local install. Community MCP servers (keepa-mcp etc.) are a separate item.
- **camelcamelcamel**: No API, no MCP, no skill. RSS feeds per product are the only machine-readable output. The site uses a Cloudflare bot challenge that stopped this research's browser agent on 2026-10-15, so browser automation is unreliable.
- **setup effort**: Keepa MCP: about 5 minutes plus a EUR 49 monthly subscription. Keepa free extension: 1 minute, manual. CCC: manual only.

**protocol support**

Keepa implements MCP (official hosted server). No ACP, UCP, AP2 or Web Bot Auth. CCC: none.

**open source and licence**

Both closed. Keepa's official Java client is open source (github.com/keepacom/api_backend, Apache-2.0, 85 stars); the API itself is proprietary.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Keepa extension: host permissions on keepa.com and Amazon domains (incl. amazon.nl and amazon.com.au), cookies and declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess 'to reveal hidden MAPs and third-party merchant stock counts', storage; sends the ASIN of the open Amazon page to keepa.com (Keepa says it is not logged); the Chrome listing declares it handles personally identifiable information (account email). ⚠ *(unverified)* How the stock-count feature interacts with the user's own Amazon session was not tested. No Amazon login or payment data. API requires a card on Stripe. CCC: email address for alerts; optional account. GDPR: Keepa is a German company; CCC is US-based.

**automation legal risk**

Keepa T&C (version 2026-10-07) forbid obtaining data with scraping tools, spiders, robots and crawlers, assert database-maker rights (section 87a UrhG), and forbid resale or redistribution of Pro data; API results may be shown to the user's own end users but not resold as datasets or used to train a model that reproduces the data. Personal research notes in a vault are within 'own purposes'. Using the official API/MCP is the compliant route; scraping keepa.com is not. CCC: Cloudflare challenge; scraping is unwelcome; RSS is the sanctioned route.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Keepa: paid subscriptions and API plans; eBay affiliate links in the Keepa box (Chrome listing and disclaimer); no sponsored placements in charts. Low bias - data is observational. CCC: Amazon affiliate commissions on click-through (RevenueGeeks) plus donations; no paid placements. Neither ranks products, so there is little room for bias beyond the choice of affiliate link.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - neither ranks or recommends; they show raw price series with timestamps.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - non-AI data tools. Repeated API calls return the same history; current price changes with Amazon.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Not an agent, so prompt injection does not apply to the tools themselves; MCP responses are data and should still be treated as data by the agent. Price history is the antidote to seller manipulation of 'was' prices on Amazon. Keepa removed its 'isScam' field (2026-02-23), so it no longer flags suspicious listings.

**known failures**

No Amazon.pl coverage (both) - the main gap for a Polish buyer. Keepa: Chrome rating 3.4/5 from 5.1K ratings and Firefox 4.2/5 from 674 reviews (complaint themes not analysed); alert delays reported anecdotally; API is business-only. CCC: no API, sparse support (four-person team), reported stale third-party/used lines (Reddit 2021, older), Camelizer not updated since June 2024, Japan coverage dropped around 2020 per a Reddit thread.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - no UOKiK, DSA, DMA or court decision against Keepa GmbH or Cosmic Shovel found (searched 2026-10-15).

**buyer protection path**

Purchases happen on Amazon, so protection is Amazon's: Amazon is merchant of record for items 'sold by Amazon', A-to-z Guarantee for marketplace sellers, statutory warranty (2 years in DE/PL for consumers), 14-day EU withdrawal right (Amazon offers longer return windows), card chargeback, and the ECC route for cross-border disputes with Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es. Keepa and CCC carry no liability.

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

Narrow but strong where it applies. For the trampoline: if a shortlisted model (e.g. a Hudora or Berg 305) is sold on Amazon.de and can be delivered to Poland, Keepa shows whether today's price is near the 30-, 90- or 365-day low and whether the strikethrough 'was' price is honest. ⚠ *(unverified)* Bulky items such as 3 m trampolines are often not shippable from Amazon.de to Poland, which limits use. For the same model on Amazon.pl, Allegro or Polish shops, neither tool helps.

**workflow role**

Price and history step, Amazon only: confirm a deal on Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es is real before buying. Combine with Ceneo (PL shops), an Amazon EU comparison extension that covers Amazon.pl (PriceRoo/Histozon), and seller and safety checks.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Free route: Keepa extension, about 2 minutes per ASIN, EUR 0. Agent route: Keepa API/MCP at EUR 49/month minimum (one month, cancellable). Arithmetic for one trampoline comparison of 10 candidate ASINs on Amazon.de with stats and one offer page each: 10 x (1 + 6) = 70 tokens; the 20 tokens/min plan generates about 864,000 tokens a month, so the marginal cost is about 0.008% of the plan (about EUR 0.004), but the fixed fee is EUR 49 for the month. CCC: EUR 0, manual.

**evidence trail**

Good. Keepa: chart PNG via Graph Image API or screenshot, API JSON with timestamps, current/avg/min stats, and the 'savingBasis' reference price - a vault note can store 'ASIN, marketplace, date, current, 30-day min, 90-day avg, strikethrough price, verdict'. CCC: product URL and chart image; RSS item per price change.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Keepa: price history back to 2011 with 30/90/180-day stats; best tool to expose fake Amazon discounts.
  - Keepa: official hosted MCP server (https://keepa.com/mcp) works with Claude Code via OAuth or API key.
  - Keepa: API exposes Amazon strikethrough reference prices since 2026-08-25 and landed prices since 2026-02-23.
  - CCC: free email alerts without an account.
  - Both: no paid placement in data; low bias.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Neither covers Amazon.pl (Keepa has 11 locales, CCC 8).
  - Amazon only - no Allegro, Ceneo shops or brand stores.
  - Keepa API is business-only and starts at EUR 49/month; scraping keepa.com is forbidden by its T&C.
  - CCC has no API and sits behind a Cloudflare bot check.
  - No safety, spec or seller-identity checks.

**independent review consensus**

No independent lab-style test of accuracy found. Secondary reviews (RevenueGeeks 2026-07/08, affiliate-funded with an advertiser disclosure) agree Keepa is the deeper tool and CCC the simpler free one; they disagree on Keepa Pro's price (EUR 19 in an older page vs EUR 29). Most other comparison pages found were low-quality SEO content and were not used.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW (Keepa free extension) for any Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es purchase, and PILOT the official Keepa MCP for one month (EUR 49) only if Amazon EU is a regular channel - deciding fact: neither Keepa nor CamelCamelCamel covers Amazon.pl. CamelCamelCamel: SKIP (adds nothing Keepa's free tier lacks for EU buyers, and no API).

**conflicting evidence**

- Keepa Pro price: EUR 29/month on keepa.com (2026-10-15) and RevenueGeeks (2026-08-20) vs EUR 19/month in an older RevenueGeeks page and USD 19/month in the Histozon extension listing (2026-09-30).
- Keepa API free tier: socket.dev's keepa-mcp page mentions a free 100 tokens/min tier, while keepa.com says plans start at EUR 49 and RevenueGeeks says there is no free tier.
- Keepa API tiers: keepa.com lists 20/250/2,000/10,000 tokens per minute; RevenueGeeks also lists 60 (EUR 129) and 500 (EUR 879) as slider steps.
- Keepa marketplaces: extension description lists 10-11 locales while its Firefox permissions also include amazon.nl and amazon.com.au; keepa.com says 11 marketplaces.
- CamelCamelCamel locales: an older official features page lists Japan and omits Australia; Wikipedia and RevenueGeeks (2026) list Australia and say Japan is not covered.
- Amazon's own price history: PC-WELT (2026-08-19) reports Amazon now shows 30-day/3-month/1-year price history on some products from its own data, which may reduce the need for Keepa; the article does not name which marketplaces, and this research did not confirm it on Amazon.de or Amazon.pl.
