### Amazon EU price-compare extensions

**Verdict:** PriceRoo PILOT, Histozon WATCH, Hagglezon SKIP · **Cost:** Free, affiliate-funded · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 6 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **histozon**: Chrome extension 'Histozon - Amazon Price Tracker' v1.3.2 (role: price tracker + cross-marketplace comparison). On an Amazon product page it shows the price in the other EU Amazon stores, a 90-day price-history chart, drop alerts and a watchlist; paired web app at histozon.com/app.
- **hagglezon**: Website hagglezon.com plus Android and iOS apps (role: comparison engine for Amazon EU). You search or paste an Amazon link and it lists the same item's price on each European Amazon store, cheapest first. No browser extension found.
- **priceroo**: Browser extension 'PriceRoo - Amazon Europe Price Comparison' v2.3.3 for Chrome/Edge and Firefox, plus priceroo.com (role: comparison + shared price history). Compares the same ASIN and variant across 10 EU Amazon stores by confirmed delivered total for a chosen delivery country.

**vendor and ownership**

- **histozon**: Chrome Web Store lists the publisher as 'SBS', 16 Pl. des Quinconces, 33000 Bordeaux, France, contact@x-cleaner.app; declared NON-trader, so the store warns that EU consumer rights do not apply to contracts with this developer. No company registration or funding found.
- **hagglezon**: HAGGLEZON SL, Ronda del General Mitre 126, 08021 Barcelona, Spain, NIF B67601237 (legal notice, 2026-10-15). Founders and funding not found. Spanish law, Spanish DPA.
- **priceroo**: Individual developer: Andrej Gluchow, Brahmsstrasse 6, 57577 Hamm (Sieg), Germany (priceroo.com imprint updated 2026-08-14; Chrome listing declares him an EU trader). No company, no funding disclosed. Hosting on Vercel and Supabase; prices fetched through a third-party 'product-retrieval infrastructure'.
- **none owned by amazon**: All three state they are independent of Amazon and earn Amazon Associates commissions.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

- **histozon**: Live; Chrome v1.3.2 updated 2026-09-30; 83 users, no ratings (2026-10-15). Launch date not stated; ⚠ *(unverified)* the outline's earlier figure of 29 users suggests it is weeks or months old.
- **hagglezon**: Live for years: iOS app ID dates from about 2017 ⚠ *(unverified)*; Android app updated 2026-03-09 (4.5 from 507 reviews); iOS v1.4.1 (4.5 from 6 ratings, NL store). Website live 2026-10-15 with a 10-marketplace list.
- **priceroo**: Live; Chrome v2.3.3 updated 2026-08-16 (242 users, 4.2 from 5 ratings); Firefox v2.3.3 updated 2026-08-15 (29 users, 2.0 from 2 reviews); methodology reviewed 2026-08-13; privacy policy effective 2026-08-10. Young project.
- **verified**: 2026-10-15 via Chrome Web Store listings (fetched with a consent cookie), addons.mozilla.org, hagglezon.com and priceroo.com.

**cost model**

All free for the buyer (seen 2026-10-15), funded by Amazon Associates affiliate commissions on click-through. Histozon states 3-10% commission by category and 'no premium tier'. PriceRoo says 'currently free' and that any future paid feature will be described before use. Hagglezon: 'Amazon pays us a commission, so you don't'.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **amazon pl coverage**: All three list Amazon.pl (vendor-claimed): Histozon 8 stores (FR, DE, IT, ES, NL, BE, PL, SE; its summary line says '13 EU/US stores'); Hagglezon 10 (DE, ES, FR, IT, NL, PL, SE, BE, IE, UK); PriceRoo 10 (DE, FR, IT, ES, UK, NL, SE, PL, BE, IE) and PL is in its required host permissions. Not tested end-to-end on an Amazon.pl product in this research.
- **language**: Histozon UI English/French (listing languages include Polish); PriceRoo UI includes Polish; Hagglezon site in several languages, Polish not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **delivery country**: Only PriceRoo evaluates offers for a selected delivery country (e.g. Poland) and ranks only offers confirmed deliverable there. Hagglezon shows item price with VAT and leaves shipping to Amazon checkout. Histozon claims 'shipping factored in' without method.
- **us only**: No US-only features involved.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Same-ASIN only. PriceRoo stores variant relationships (colour, size, model) and says a different variant must not win because it is cheaper - the only one of the three that handles variants explicitly. Histozon and Hagglezon match by ASIN/search and do not compare specs or different makers. None maps EAN/GTIN or white-label rebadges. Grade: partial (PriceRoo) / none (others).

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Compare one product across EU Amazon stores only - no Allegro, Ceneo shops or brand stores. Amazon.pl is the Polish channel they add, which Keepa and CamelCamelCamel do not cover. All coverage figures are vendor-claimed; none was independently tested.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

Histozon: 90-day history chart per product (vendor-claimed) and a 'Euro Saver' banner when another store is at least 10% cheaper; it positions itself against 'fake -40% inflated baselines' but shows no Omnibus value. PriceRoo: shared price history built from on-demand observations, two series (native item price and delivered total), deal assessment using historical lows and rolling references; history density depends on how often users check a product. Hagglezon: no price history seen ⚠ *(unverified)*; a competitor review (EuroSaver, 2025-08-22) says it has no price indicator. None reads or verifies the Omnibus 30-day lowest price shown by Amazon.

**total landed cost**

PriceRoo: yes, partly - delivered total = item price + confirmed delivery for the selected country, with ECB-dated currency conversion; coupons and promotions labelled conditional; no return costs. Histozon: claims shipping factored in, no method published. Hagglezon: no - item price with VAT only, shipping shown at Amazon checkout; it notes intra-EU purchases carry no customs. None covers return shipping for bulky goods or cross-border warranty handling.

**review and seller verification**

None. PriceRoo records seller and condition per observation and ranks only confirmed offers, but does not verify sellers. No review-authenticity checks. Grade: none.

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A - none checks Safety Gate, GPSR fields or certificates.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - none surfaces lab tests.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

- **histozon**: Drop alerts at a target price, watchlist up to 50 products synced across browsers, price-drop badge (vendor-claimed). Check frequency not stated.
- **hagglezon**: Alerts and favourites for registered users (privacy policy lists 'products from which the user wants to receive alerts'); channel not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **priceroo**: Email alerts via a free account on priceroo.com, up to 5 active alerts, each refreshed at most once every 12 hours ('explicitly not real-time'); the extension itself has no background checks, watchlist or notifications.
- **polish shop pages**: None can watch non-Amazon Polish shop pages.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. All three only redirect to the chosen Amazon store with an affiliate tag; checkout and payment stay on Amazon.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: PriceRoo can show used offers' condition per observation; nothing on spare parts, service or resale.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

- **histozon**: Fetches prices by ASIN from its own servers 'hosted in Europe (France)' (vendor-claimed); refresh and lag not stated.
- **hagglezon**: Claims all ten marketplaces 'checked in real time' and prices 'obtained legally'; method not disclosed. A competitor says results can be outdated (unverified, competitor source).
- **priceroo**: Checks localized Amazon product and offer pages on demand through a third-party retrieval service; a confirmed result is reused for up to 12 hours; every result shows its observation time; ECB rates via Frankfurter. Best documented of the three.
- **snapshot**: Only PriceRoo timestamps each observation and links to a product history page.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: none (all three); partial fallback via PriceRoo's public pages
- **histozon**: No API, MCP or skill. Extension only; histozon.com/app not tested. Manual use.
- **hagglezon**: No API, MCP or skill. Search on hagglezon.com is gated by a Cloudflare Turnstile 'Verify you are human' check (hit on 2026-10-15), so a browser agent cannot use it without solving a CAPTCHA, which is off-limits. Manual use only.
- **priceroo**: No API, MCP or skill. Public product price-history pages on priceroo.com are server-rendered and fetchable, so a Claude Code skill or browser agent could read an existing history page for an ASIN; triggering fresh comparisons runs through the extension or site. The privacy policy mentions a PriceRoo API used by the extension, but it is not documented for third parties.
- **setup effort**: Install an extension (1 minute) and use manually. No agent route worth building; for an agent, Keepa's MCP covers Amazon DE/FR/IT/ES/UK but not Amazon.pl.

**protocol support**

None.

**open source and licence**

Histozon: closed. Hagglezon: closed. PriceRoo: declares MIT licence on addons.mozilla.org but links no repository, and no public repo was found - effectively unverifiable.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

- **histozon**: No account. Claims it only sees ASINs from Amazon product pages, no browsing history outside them, no tracking cookies. Chrome privacy section: 'will not collect or use your data' - which conflicts with a cloud watchlist synced across browsers. ⚠ *(unverified)* Requested permissions were not visible in the listing text.
- **hagglezon**: Optional account with name and email or Facebook social login; stores favourites, alert products, recent searches and usage tracking; legal basis consent; no third-party sharing claimed. Cookie banner offers only 'I accept' and mentions targeted ads.
- **priceroo**: Extension host permissions on amazon .de/.fr/.it/.es/.co.uk/.nl/.se/.pl/.com.be/.ie, optional priceroo.com. Sends ASIN, marketplace, delivery country and optional postal code to its API; salted IP hash for rate limiting; Google Analytics after consent; Vercel/Supabase hosting. Chrome listing declares it handles location, web history and website content. No Amazon credentials or payment data.
- **general risk**: Small extensions with host access to Amazon pages from individuals or unregistered publishers are a supply-chain risk (ownership can change and updates install silently). Use a separate browser profile not signed in to Amazon for research if concerned.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Low for the buyer using them manually. The tools themselves retrieve Amazon data (PriceRoo via a third-party retrieval service) - their compliance with Amazon's terms is their risk, not the user's. Automating Hagglezon would mean bypassing a Turnstile challenge (not acceptable). Chrome Web Store affiliate policy (from 2025-06-10) requires affiliate tags only on user action; all three claim click-through only ⚠ *(unverified)* - not tested.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Amazon Associates affiliate tags on outbound links for all three (Histozon 'Buy on cheapest market' button; Hagglezon 'As an Amazon Associate, Hagglezon earns from qualifying purchases'; PriceRoo 'Amazon links are affiliate links'). All three claim commissions do not change the ranking (vendor-claimed, untested). Bias vector: the tools earn only when you buy on Amazon, so they never suggest a non-Amazon shop that may be cheaper; affiliate rates differ by marketplace, which could tempt reordering. Hagglezon's site says 'No ads' while its cookie banner mentions targeted ads.

**ranking transparency**

PriceRoo: high - published methodology (only confirmed, deliverable offers rank; delivered total; 12-hour cache; timestamps). Hagglezon: sorted by price, method undisclosed. Histozon: 'deal detected' rule (>=10% cheaper) stated, nothing else. No sponsored items in any.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - non-AI tools; results change with live prices and cache age (PriceRoo up to 12 hours).

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Not AI agents, so prompt injection does not apply. Risk lies in third-party sellers on the cheaper marketplace: none checks the seller, so a cheaper Amazon.de or Amazon.it offer may come from a marketplace seller with weaker after-sales.

**known failures**

PriceRoo: a Firefox reviewer reported it flagged another country as cheaper when the current store was cheaper; the developer said a stale 'cheapest country' result could persist after switching stores (fix status unknown). Hagglezon: competitor review says results can be outdated and shipping is missing (competitor source). Histozon: inconsistent store count (8 vs 13) and factual errors in its own listing ('Keepa \$19/month' while keepa.com shows EUR 29; 'Honey discontinued 2024', not confirmed by any source found). All three: tiny user bases (Histozon 83, PriceRoo 242 + 29) and almost no independent reviews; nothing tested on Amazon.pl here.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - none found for SBS/Histozon, Hagglezon SL or PriceRoo (searched 2026-10-15).

**buyer protection path**

Purchase is on the chosen Amazon store, so Amazon's protections apply (merchant of record when 'sold by Amazon', A-to-z Guarantee for marketplace sellers, 14-day EU withdrawal, statutory warranty, card chargeback). Buying cross-border (e.g. Amazon.de delivered to Poland) means returns go back to that store and disputes use the ECC route. The extensions carry no liability; Histozon's Chrome listing explicitly states EU consumer rights do not apply to contracts with that developer (non-trader).

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low to moderate for the trampoline. They answer one question: is the same ASIN cheaper on another EU Amazon store than on Amazon.pl? PriceRoo is the useful one because a 3 m trampoline is bulky and often cannot be delivered cross-border; it ranks only offers confirmed deliverable to Poland and shows delivered totals. Histozon is the only one with a stated 90-day history that includes Amazon.pl. None helps choose between makers or checks safety, and Amazon is a minor channel for trampolines in Poland compared with Allegro and Polish shops.

**workflow role**

Price step for an Amazon purchase only: after choosing a model and confirming it is on Amazon, check PriceRoo (delivered total to Poland) and, for history on Amazon.pl, Histozon; use Keepa for long history on Amazon.de. Combine with Ceneo for Polish shops and with seller and safety checks.

**effort and cost per purchase**

EUR 0. Install one extension (1 minute), then about 1 minute per product page. Arithmetic for one trampoline comparison: 1 ASIN x 10 marketplaces checked by the tool = 0 credits, 0 tokens; PriceRoo result may be up to 12 hours old.

**evidence trail**

PriceRoo: best - each result has an observation timestamp, native price, shipping, delivered total and ECB date, and a shareable product history page URL; store URL + screenshot in the vault note. Histozon: chart screenshot only. Hagglezon: search result page URL (behind Turnstile) - screenshot needed. Suggested record: 'ASIN, delivery country PL, date/time, Amazon.pl delivered total, cheapest deliverable store and total, tool and version'.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - All three include Amazon.pl, which Keepa and CamelCamelCamel do not cover.
  - PriceRoo ranks only offers confirmed deliverable to the chosen country and shows delivered totals with timestamps (published methodology).
  - PriceRoo handles product variants explicitly.
  - Histozon claims a 90-day history chart and target-price alerts covering Amazon.pl.
  - Free; no account needed for basic use.
- **weaknesses**:
  - All claims are vendor-claimed; no independent tests; tiny user bases (83, 242+29).
  - Amazon-only and affiliate-funded, so they never point to cheaper non-Amazon shops.
  - No API or MCP; Hagglezon search is behind a Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA.
  - Histozon publisher ('SBS', Bordeaux) self-declares as a non-trader, uses a contact address on another product's domain (x-cleaner.app) and has factual errors in its listing.
  - Hagglezon ignores shipping, which matters most for bulky goods.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found. The only comparative text is a competitor's blog (EuroSaver vs Hagglezon, 2025-08-22) and two user reviews on addons.mozilla.org for PriceRoo (one 3-star noting a wrong-cheapest bug, one 1-star). Many similar extensions exist with similar claims: 'Amazon Price Compare' (dealfinder.altervista.org, about 4,000 users, 3.8 from 34 ratings, updated 2026-10-09, shipping and return info, affiliate tags), EuroSaver, Comparezon, Molo, Weflax and Komparzon - none reviewed independently either.

**verdict for me**

PILOT PriceRoo only - deciding fact: it is the one tool here that ranks Amazon offers by confirmed delivered total to Poland with timestamps; use it on the Amazon.pl product page as the last price check for any Amazon purchase, in a browser profile without your Amazon login. Histozon: WATCH (self-declared non-trader, errors in its listing, 83 users). Hagglezon: SKIP (no shipping, CAPTCHA-gated, no history).

**conflicting evidence**

- Histozon store count: summary line says '13 EU/US Amazon stores', the body lists 8 EU stores.
- Histozon privacy: Chrome privacy section says the developer will not collect or use data, while the description offers a watchlist synced across browsers and a cloud watchlist at histozon.com/app.
- Hagglezon coverage: older Android listing named only DE, FR, IT, ES, UK; hagglezon.com (2026-10-15) lists ten marketplaces including PL.
- Hagglezon ads: homepage says 'We don't run ads', while its cookie banner says cookies are used to 'show personalised content and targeted ads'.
- PriceRoo alerts: the extension listing says no watchlist, notifications or alerts; priceroo.com offers email alerts through a free account (up to 5, refreshed every 12 hours) - both true for different surfaces.
- PriceRoo openness: addons.mozilla.org shows an MIT licence, but no repository is linked or found; Firefox listing declares 'location' collection while the text says precise location is not collected.
- Histozon vs keepa.com: Histozon says Keepa costs USD 19/month; keepa.com shows Keepa Pro at EUR 29/month (2026-10-15).

**sources checked**

- https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/cejhjdgmbeokoedpfdeciemodcccdhfi (Histozon listing, fetched 2026-10-15)
- https://www.hagglezon.com/en (2026-10-15, browser)
- https://www.hagglezon.com/en/legal-notice (2026-10-15)
- https://www.hagglezon.com/en/privacy-policy (2026-10-15)
- https://www.hagglezon.com/en/s/Hudora%20trampoline%20300 (blocked by Cloudflare Turnstile, 2026-10-15)
- https://apps.apple.com/nl/app/hagglezon-compare-prices/id1273547948 (2026-10-15)
- https://apps.appfollow.io/android/hagglezon-compare-prices/com.hagglezon.app?country=gb (Google Play mirror, 2026-10-15)
- https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/nikbmhomnbmdahjdjhajldhiddjidnpk (PriceRoo listing, fetched 2026-10-15)
- https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/priceroo/ (2026-10-15)
- https://priceroo.com/uk, /uk/about, /uk/imprint, /uk/methodology, /uk/privacy, /uk/amazon-price-tracker (2026-10-15)
- https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/lpioecjgaljbjbpnjjnbnhonfalgcnle ('Amazon Price Compare' alternative, 2026-10-15)
- https://eurosaver.net/blog/eurosaver-vs-hagglezon (competitor blog, 2025-08-22, older than six months)

#### fields the agent listed as uncertain

- account linking and data access
- alerts and monitoring
- automation legal risk
- feature geo matrix
- lifecycle status
- price history and omnibus

### Self-hosted price trackers

**Verdict:** PILOT (changedetection.io) · **Cost:** Free self-hosted; hosted USD 8.99 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 6 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **changedetection io**: Self-hosted web page change monitor (role: price tracker / change monitor / scraper). Version 0.60.9 (2026-10-12). Watches any URL; the 'Re-stock & Price detection for single product pages' processor reads schema.org JSON-LD, microdata and OpenGraph price/availability, keeps a price graph, and alerts on upper/lower limits, percentage change, and in/out of stock. Optional LLM layer (price/stock fallback, plain-language alert rules, change summaries).
- **pricebuddy**: Self-hosted multi-store price tracker (role: price tracker). Version v1.0.55 (2026-10-05). Laravel/Filament web app: paste a product URL, add several shop URLs per product, schedule checks (every 5 min to 24 h), price history with min/max/avg, unit-price comparison, availability states, target-price and drop alerts. Optional AI (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, local Ollama) fills missing prices and repairs broken scrape rules. Companion CLI (pricebuddy-cli v1.0.0) doubles as an MCP server.
- **discount bandit**: Self-hosted multi-user price tracker (role: price tracker). Latest release V4.0.4 (2026-05-23); active work on a v4.0.5 branch. Laravel/Filament app with built-in store classes (Amazon in 22 locales incl. amazon.pl, eBay, AliExpress, MediaMarkt ES/BE/DE, Argos, Currys and others), 'Smart Fetch' custom stores, per-link alert rules (desired price, % drop, lowest in X days, official seller only, stock, any change) and per-rule extra costs (fixed amount, percentage, shipping-included flag).

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

- **changedetection io**: Maintainer dgtlmoon (GitHub). Hosted service run by 'Web Technologies s.r.o.' per the changedetection.io site footer, described as the official provider and 'made in Europe'; the s.r.o. form suggests a Czech or Slovak company ⚠ *(unverified)*. No external funding found; revenue from the USD 8.99/month hosted plan and proxy referral links (Bright Data, Oxylabs) in the README.
- **pricebuddy**: Jeremy Graham (jez500, jez.me), individual open-source maintainer; README says it was inspired by Discount Bandit. No company or funding; optional 'support the project' affiliate tags are enabled by default.
- **discount bandit**: Cybrarist (individual GitHub maintainer); docs at discount-bandit.cybrarist.com, Discord community. No company or funding found.
- **bias note**: None of the three is owned by a marketplace or retailer.

**lifecycle status**

- **changedetection io**: Active. Repo created 2021-01-27; releases 0.60.7 (2026-09-17), 0.60.8 (2026-09-28), 0.60.9 (2026-10-12); last push 2026-10-15; 35,025 stars, 403 open issues. LLM features added in the 0.55-0.60 line (per-watch LLM settings PR #4354, 2026-09-01). Verified 2026-10-15 via GitHub API.
- **pricebuddy**: Active. Repo created 2025-02-09; releases roughly monthly (v1.0.53 2026-07-06, v1.0.54 2026-08-09, v1.0.55 2026-10-05); last push 2026-10-11; 1,410 stars, 78 open issues. CLI repo jez500/pricebuddy-cli created 2026-06-20, single release v1.0.0, 0 stars, last push 2026-06-30. Verified 2026-10-15 via GitHub API.
- **discount bandit**: Active but slower. Repo created 2023-07-06; V4 released 2025-11-07, V4.0.2 2026-01-31, V4.0.4 2026-05-23; master last commit 2026-06-01; v4.0.5 branch has commits on 2026-10-14/15 (link history chart, bulk add, links ordered by price with currency conversion); 'plugin' branch for a browser extension started 2026-10-12 (docs say 'coming soon'). 751 stars, 13 open issues. Verified 2026-10-15 via GitHub API.

**cost model**

- **changedetection io**: Free self-hosted (Apache-2.0). Hosted plan USD 8.99/month (currency shown only as '\$'), up to 5,000 URLs, checks from about every 5 minutes, one Chrome browser, EU/US/Tor proxies, cancel anytime (changedetection.io, seen 2026-10-15). LLM features bill your own provider; README claims GPT-4o-mini or Gemini Flash cost 'fractions of a cent per check' (vendor-claimed). Residential proxies for blocked shops are a separate paid cost.
- **pricebuddy**: Free, self-hosted only (no hosted plan). Costs: your Docker host, optional AI provider tokens, optional SearXNG instance.
- **discount bandit**: Free, self-hosted only. Optional free/paid ExchangeRate-API key for currency conversion.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

Self-hosted, so features are not geo-gated: every feature works in Poland, the EU and the US as long as the target shop answers requests from your server. The limit is the shop's anti-bot layer, not the tool. Own probe 2026-10-15 (single plain HTTP request from a Polish connection, the method each tool uses by default): mediamarkt.pl product page 200 with JSON-LD price; x-kom.pl, castorama.pl, obi.pl, ceneo.pl, empik.com, smyk.com, lidl.pl home pages 200; decathlon.pl, mediaexpert.pl and kaufland.pl 403 (Cloudflare challenge); allegro.pl and leroymerlin.pl 403 (DataDome captcha); amazon.pl 202 with an empty body. Browser fetchers were not tested. UI languages: changedetection.io ships a Polish translation (among 19 locales); PriceBuddy and Discount Bandit are English-only ⚠ *(unverified)* (no translation folders found). Hosted changedetection.io offers EU proxies.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

None for specifications. Variants: PriceBuddy and Discount Bandit group several URLs (shops or listings) under one product, so you can put the EU 'Salta Premium Black Edition 305 round' and a retailer-exclusive variant side by side, but the mapping is manual - none of the three reads EAN/GTIN to match products across shops or detect rebadged OEM models. PriceBuddy computes unit price (per tablet/bag), irrelevant for trampolines. changedetection.io treats each URL independently. Grade: none (specs) / partial-manual (variants).

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

- **summary**: Compare only the URLs you add; they do not discover shops. Polish coverage depends on which shops answer a plain or headless request.
- **changedetection io**: Any URL; one watch per URL; tags group watches; no side-by-side price view across shops (issue #4496 asks for custom price badges for sites without schema.org data). Decimal-comma prices such as '39,99' were stored 100x too high until 0.60.9 (issue #4493, fixed by PR #4494, 2026-10-01); a locale fix for LLM-extracted prices ('1.299,95') was merged 2026-10-13 and is only on the :dev image as of 2026-10-15.
- **pricebuddy**: Multi-URL products with a cross-store comparison; default seeded store definitions cover only Australia and the USA (database/seeders/Stores: australia.php, usa.php); Polish shops need a store definition (JSON-LD first, then CSS/regex/JSONPath) or AI auto-creation. Open issue #173 (2026-08-11): de_DE thousands separator misread for prices above EUR 1,000 - relevant to PLN prices such as '1 649,00 zl' ⚠ *(unverified: whether fixed by the October currency-parsing changes)*.
- **discount bandit**: Built-in stores include amazon.pl (PLN), amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es/.nl/.se/.com.be, ebay.de, mediamarkt.es/.be/.de, fnac.com, eprice.it; no Allegro, Ceneo, x-kom, Media Expert or Decathlon classes (code search 2026-10-15). Other shops via 'Smart Fetch' custom stores or community store files. v4.0.5 orders a product's links by price with currency conversion.
- **shop counts**: No vendor counts of indexed shops - not applicable to self-hosted scrapers.

**price history and omnibus**

All three record their own price history from the day you start watching (changedetection.io graph of price and stock; PriceBuddy min/max/avg charts and 'lowest' CLI command; Discount Bandit price and link-history charts). None knows the Omnibus 30-day prior price unless you were already watching for 30 days before the promotion. Discount Bandit's 'lowest price within X days' rule and PriceBuddy's 'lowest'/'insights' commands let you test a promotion against your own record, which is the only way to judge a fake discount with these tools. None parses the shop's displayed 'lowest price in 30 days' label automatically; changedetection.io could watch that text with a CSS/XPath filter.

**total landed cost**

Discount Bandit: partial - each notification rule has extra_costs_amount, extra_costs_percentage and is_shipping_included fields (app/Models/NotificationSetting.php), so a trampoline's 99 PLN delivery or a cross-border surcharge can be added to the alert threshold; values are typed by you, not scraped. PriceBuddy: none - feature request #80 'Ability to add additional costs to grabbed price' still open (2026-10-15). changedetection.io: none (only Jinja2 arithmetic in notification text). None covers return shipping, assembly or warranty.

**review and seller verification**

None. They do not read reviews or check seller identity (CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list/VIES). Discount Bandit has an 'official sellers only' alert rule for marketplace stores such as Amazon, and PriceBuddy issue #176 notes its Amazon scraper sometimes reads 'Other sellers' prices - both show seller identity is at most a filter. Grade: none.

**safety and compliance checks**

None automatically. changedetection.io can watch a page for text changes, so it could monitor a Safety Gate search URL or a UOKiK recall page for a brand name, but that is a generic page watch, not a compliance check.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - they do not surface lab tests. changedetection.io could watch a test.de or konsument.at page for updates.

**alerts and monitoring**

- **changedetection io**: Price above/below limits, % change, back in stock / out of stock, any text change, AI intent rules ('notify me only when the price drops below X'). Check interval per watch, minimum about 3 seconds self-hosted (MINIMUM_SECONDS_RECHECK_TIME), hosted from about 5 minutes. Channels via Apprise: 85+ types incl. email, Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy, generic JSON webhooks. Can watch any Polish shop page that does not block it.
- **pricebuddy**: Target price, percentage drop, opt-in back-in-stock. Frequency per product, 5 minutes to 24 hours. Channels: in-app, email, Pushover, Gotify, Apprise, Telegram, Discord webhook, ntfy.
- **discount bandit**: Desired price, % drop, lowest in X days, official seller, in stock, any price change; several rules per link. Global CRON default every 5 minutes. Channels: ntfy, Telegram, Gotify, Apprise (code: app/NotificationsChannels, User model).

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. None of the three can buy; alerts carry a link and you check out on the shop yourself. changedetection.io Browser Steps can log in or add to cart to read a price, but that is for monitoring, and putting shop credentials into it is not recommended.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: any of them can watch spare-part pages (a Decathlon 360 mat, Berg nets) or an OLX/Allegro Lokalnie search page for used units (changedetection.io page watch); none models resale value or service networks.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Own scraping of the URLs you add, nothing else. changedetection.io: plain HTTP or a Playwright/WebDriver browser (sockpuppetbrowser container), price from JSON-LD/microdata/OpenGraph via a pure-Python extractor then extruct, LLM fallback reading up to LLM_RESTOCK_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS (default 15,000 characters). PriceBuddy: HTTP (curl) by default or SeleniumBase headless Chrome container; strategies JSON-LD, CSS, regex, JSONPath; AI fills a missing price or proposes new selectors. Discount Bandit: per-store PHP classes, some with chromium_crawler enabled (Chromium is installed in the image), JSON-LD schema read first. Freshness = your check interval. Each record is a timestamped scrape of your own; changedetection.io keeps HTML/text snapshots and screenshots (with a browser fetcher), the others keep price points only.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full (changedetection.io, PriceBuddy) / partial (Discount Bandit)
- **changedetection io**: Official REST API for watches, tags, notifications and history, key in the x-api-key header (Settings > API); interactive docs https://changedetection.io/docs/api_v1/index.html and OpenAPI spec docs/api-spec.yaml. MCP: community only - rusty4444/changedetection-mcp (PyPI changedetection-mcp v0.1.0, single maintainer, stdio, run with 'uvx changedetection-mcp', env CHANGEDETECTION_BASE_URL and CHANGEDETECTION_API_KEY; tools: watch CRUD, recheck, snapshot history and diffs, tags, search, health). Treat as early-stage; review code before giving it a key. No official skill. Claude Code can also call the REST API with curl.
- **pricebuddy**: REST API with Laravel Sanctum tokens (docs https://pricebuddy.jez.me/api.html). Official companion CLI jez500/pricebuddy-cli (Go, Apache-2.0, v1.0.0 2026-06-20): '--agent' JSON output, '--dry-run' for writes, confirmation for destructive actions, commands deals/lowest/history/drops/insights/meta-extract/products create/product-sources search-all, local SQLite mirror. Same repo builds 'pricebuddy-mcp' (stdio MCP server) and a Claude Desktop .mcpb bundle; for Claude Code: 'go install github.com/jez500/pricebuddy-cli/cmd/pricebuddy-mcp@latest' then 'claude mcp add pricebuddy -e PRICEBUDDY_BASE_URL=... -e PRICEBUDDY_API_TOKEN=... -- pricebuddy-mcp' ⚠ *(unverified: Claude Code wiring not tested; docs show Claude Desktop only)*. CLI has 0 stars and one release - young.
- **discount bandit**: Sanctum-token API in routes/api.php: POST /links/add, apiResource stores and products, GET /link/search-url, /link/{id}/related, /link/{id}/history; token from POST /sanctum/token with email/password. Undocumented on the docs site; built for the coming browser extension. No MCP, no CLI, no skill.
- **browser agent**: All three have web UIs a browser agent could drive, but the APIs are the better route.
- **setup effort**: changedetection.io: about 5 minutes for 'docker run -p 127.0.0.1:5000:5000 -v datastore-volume:/datastore dgtlmoon/changedetection.io', plus about 10 minutes to add the sockpuppetbrowser container (PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_URL=ws://browser-sockpuppet-chrome:3000, shm 2 GB). PriceBuddy: about 15-20 minutes - download docker-compose.yml, create an empty .env, 'docker compose up -d' brings up app (port 8080), MySQL 8.2 and the SeleniumBase scraper (port 3030); change the default admin@example.com/admin login and set AFFILIATE_ENABLED=false; plus Go install for the CLI/MCP. Discount Bandit: about 15 minutes - compose file with one container (port 8080) and SQLite, but APP_KEY must be generated first and stores enabled one by one.

**protocol support**

No agent-commerce protocols (ACP, UCP, AP2, Web Bot Auth). MCP only via PriceBuddy's official CLI (pricebuddy-mcp) and a community server for changedetection.io.

**⚠ open source and licence**

- **changedetection io**: Open source, Apache-2.0, github.com/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io, 35,025 stars, 2,147 forks, last push 2026-10-15.
- **pricebuddy**: Source-available under a custom LICENSE.md titled 'copyleft-LICENSE / GPL-3.0 WITH MODIFICATIONS' that adds a non-commercial clause (no selling hosted access, no use in a product or service that makes money); GitHub detects it as NOASSERTION. Personal use for your own purchases is fine; using it inside a paid client deliverable is not. github.com/jez500/pricebuddy, 1,410 stars, last push 2026-10-11. CLI: Apache-2.0.
- **discount bandit**: No LICENSE file (GitHub licence: none), so default copyright applies - source is visible but reuse rights are not granted ⚠ *(unverified: docs may state a licence elsewhere; none found)*. github.com/Cybrarist/Discount-Bandit, 751 stars.

**account linking and data access**

Nothing is shared with a third party by default except: changedetection.io 'check version' telemetry (DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=true turns it off) and, if you enable AI, page diffs and extracted text sent to your chosen LLM provider (README warns about this); PriceBuddy sends page content to the AI provider if enabled and rewrites Amazon/eBay URLs with the developer's affiliate tags by default (AFFILIATE_ENABLED=true; tags 'pricebuddy07-20' for Amazon incl. amazon.pl/.de, eBay campaign IDs incl. ebay.pl); Discount Bandit calls ExchangeRate-API if a key is set. No shop accounts or payment data needed. GDPR: data stays on your server; the shops see your server's IP.

**automation legal risk**

You are the scraper. Polish shops behind Cloudflare or DataDome (Allegro, Leroy Merlin, Decathlon, Media Expert, Kaufland in the 2026-10-15 probe) return 403 to plain requests; getting through needs a headless browser and often residential proxies, which tends to breach shop terms that forbid automated access. Low-frequency checks of a few public product pages for personal use carry low practical risk, but accounts are not involved, so the realistic consequence is an IP block, not an account ban. EU database-right (sui generis) and ToS claims make republishing scraped data riskier than private monitoring. Do not use logged-in Browser Steps on Allegro.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

No ranking, so little room for bias. changedetection.io: hosted subscription plus proxy referral links in the README (Bright Data matches a first deposit via its link). PriceBuddy: affiliate tags injected into Amazon and eBay links by default (switch off with AFFILIATE_ENABLED=false) - does not change prices or which product is shown. Discount Bandit: none found.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - they do not recommend; they show your own price series and your own rules. PriceBuddy's dashboard sections ('What's good to buy now', 'Recently dropped') and CLI 'insights' are rule-based on your data.

**run to run consistency**

N/A for the core trackers (deterministic scrapes). The optional LLM price fallback and AI alert rules are not deterministic, and changedetection.io's README warns that AI output 'must never be relied upon as complete or accurate'; keep structured-data extraction as the source of truth.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Prices come from the shop's own markup, so a shop can show a scraper a different price than a browser (cloaking) and the trackers will not notice. With AI enabled, page text goes into an LLM prompt (changedetection.io AI rules and price fallback, PriceBuddy self-healing), so a malicious page could inject instructions; impact is limited to a wrong price or a suppressed alert because the LLM has no tools. Keep AI off for unknown shops.

**known failures**

changedetection.io: decimal-comma prices stored 100x too high before 0.60.9 (#4493, fixed 2026-10-01); thousands separator read as decimal (#4500, closed 2026-10-01); LLM fallback missed Amazon.de prices beyond the 8,000-character limit (#4213, made configurable); Playwright memory growth from about 200 MB to several GB needs periodic restarts (wiki); 'Re-stock detection setting not respected' (#4476, open). PriceBuddy: de_DE thousands separator misparse (#173, open), price reported as 0 (#174, open), Amazon reads 'Other sellers' price (#176, open), no extra-cost field (#80). Discount Bandit: few store classes for Poland, browser extension not released, docs thin (FAQ answers three questions), no licence file. Common to all: anti-bot blocks on key Polish shops; selectors break when shops redesign.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - none found for any of the three (searched 2026-10-15).

**buyer protection path**

N/A as a route - the purchase happens on the shop, so protection is the shop's: Polish statutory warranty (rekojmia, 2 years for consumers), 14-day withdrawal for online purchases, card chargeback, Allegro Protect where relevant, ECC-Net for cross-border EU purchases. The trackers carry no liability.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Good for the 'wait for the right price' phase once the shortlist is fixed. Example: after choosing a round ~305 cm trampoline (say Salta Premium Black Edition 305 or Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300), add the mediamarkt.pl page (plain HTTP works, JSON-LD price present), the brand store and an Amazon.de/.pl listing; set a target in PLN and, in Discount Bandit, add 99 PLN delivery as an extra cost; get a Telegram or ntfy alert when the landed price falls below target or stock returns before the season. Cannot do: find shops, verify the product, compare specs, or see prices on Allegro, Decathlon.pl, Media Expert or Leroy Merlin without a browser fetcher and probably proxies. Trampolines are seasonal (spring), so watching from autumn gives months of own history to judge spring 'discounts'.

**workflow role**

Price and history step (after discovery, spec and safety checks), plus restock alerts. Combine with Ceneo/idealo for shop discovery and current price ranges, Keepa for Amazon history, and test/safety sources for product choice.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup once: 5-20 minutes per tool on an existing Docker host (see api_mcp_skill_access); EUR 0 software. Running cost on an existing home server: about EUR 0; a browser container adds about 0.5-2 GB RAM. Hosted changedetection.io instead: USD 8.99/month. One trampoline comparison: 3 candidate models x 4 shops = 12 watches, checked every 6 hours = 48 checks/day, about 1,440/month; plain HTTP costs nothing; if the LLM fallback ran on every check at the README's 'fraction of a cent' (assume USD 0.001-0.005) it would cost about USD 1.4-7/month, so keep AI off except for shops without structured data. Residential proxies for DataDome/Cloudflare shops would add a paid proxy plan ⚠ *(unverified: cost)*.

**evidence trail**

Good for price, weak for context. Each tool stores timestamped price points; changedetection.io also keeps page snapshots, diffs and screenshots per check, and its API/MCP can export them. PriceBuddy CLI 'history --agent' and Discount Bandit's /link/{id}/history return JSON. A vault record could read: 'product, shop URL, first seen date, min/avg/max over N days, price at purchase, alert that triggered, screenshot link'.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Watch any Polish shop that answers requests - the gap Keepa (Amazon only) leaves; own probe got a JSON-LD price from mediamarkt.pl with plain HTTP.
  - changedetection.io: mature (35k stars, release every 2-3 weeks), Polish UI, REST API with OpenAPI spec, Apprise notifications, page snapshots for audit.
  - PriceBuddy: multi-shop products, official agent-oriented CLI with an MCP server, optional AI with local Ollama.
  - Discount Bandit: only one of the three that adds shipping and other costs to alert thresholds; amazon.pl built in; 'lowest in X days' rule.
  - Data stays on your server; no account linking, no payment data.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Key Polish shops block plain requests (Allegro and Leroy Merlin via DataDome; Decathlon.pl, Media Expert, Kaufland via Cloudflare in the 2026-10-15 probe).
  - History starts when you start watching, so no Omnibus 30-day baseline for a promotion already running.
  - Locale price parsing bugs with decimal commas and thousands separators (fixed in changedetection.io 0.60.9; open in PriceBuddy #173).
  - No product discovery, spec matching or GTIN mapping; every URL is added by hand.
  - Licensing: PriceBuddy is non-commercial; Discount Bandit has no licence file; PriceBuddy injects affiliate tags by default.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test of these trackers' price accuracy found. Secondary pages (hosting marketplaces, 'best change monitoring tools' roundups, some from competing vendors such as PageCrawl) agree changedetection.io is the most capable free self-hosted option and that self-hosting needs maintenance; a Lemmy r/selfhosted thread notes some sites block it outright and need proxies or captcha solvers. No independent coverage of PriceBuddy or Discount Bandit beyond GitHub activity. Evidence here rests on primary sources (repos, docs, issue tracker) and the own probe.

**verdict for me**

PILOT changedetection.io (deciding fact: it already has a REST API, Polish UI and fixed decimal-comma parsing in 0.60.9) for the shortlisted trampoline pages that answer plain requests, add Discount Bandit only if landed-cost alerts with shipping matter, and WATCH PriceBuddy's CLI/MCP. Best use: after choosing the model, put 5-12 product URLs under watch in autumn and buy when the landed price beats your own 30-90-day record.

**conflicting evidence**

- PriceBuddy licence: the research brief calls it GPL-3.0, but LICENSE.md is a custom 'GPL-3.0 WITH MODIFICATIONS' text with a non-commercial clause, and GitHub reports NOASSERTION.
- changedetection.io AI availability: the README says AI features are 'available in our subscription/hosted service from June 2026', while the self-hosted docker-compose has LLM_FEATURES_DISABLED and LLM_RESTOCK_MAX_CONTENT_CHARS settings and issue #4213 shows a self-hosted Ollama user - AI works self-hosted too.
- Discount Bandit browser extension: docs say 'coming soon', but the API already has an AddLinkFromBrowserPluginAction endpoint and a 'plugin' branch started 2026-10-12.
- Discount Bandit store list: the features page lists 28 stores; the master StoreSeeder also includes amazon.pl and other Amazon locales not named on the page.
- PriceBuddy docs say auto store creation uses only HTTP and no AI, while the features page says AI can create a new store from a product URL - both exist (plain auto-create vs AI 'self-healing' bootstrap).

## B. Product verification, independent tests and safety

### Trampoline lab tests

**Verdict:** USE NOW · **Cost:** EUR 4.90 to unlock the test.de result · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 4 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Three recent lab tests of garden trampolines (role: test lab / study). Two are one joint European test published twice; the third is an Australian test to a different standard.
- **stiftung warentest**: 'Trampoline im Test - Vor Freude springen', test.de, published 22.04.2025 (magazine test 05/2025). 11 round spring trampolines of about 3 m with safety nets, EUR 219-695. Result: 1 'sehr gut', 8 'gut', 1 'befriedigend', 1 'mangelhaft'.
- **vki konsument**: VKI (Austria) joint test with Stiftung Warentest, press release 22.04.2025, KONSUMENT 05/2025 (online from 24.04.2025). The same set minus the Lidl Crivit: 10 trampolines, EUR 269-695. Result: 1 'sehr gut', 7 'gut', 1 'durchschnittlich', 1 'nicht zufriedenstellend'.
- **choice**: CHOICE (Australia) 'Best trampolines' review and article 'Too many trampolines still failing CHOICE safety tests', last updated 14 Oct 2025. Tested to the voluntary AS 4989:2015. Summary line: 'Of the 8 models tested, all but two had serious failures'; the two that passed are Springfree models.

**vendor and ownership**

- **stiftung warentest**: Stiftung Warentest, Berlin, Germany - foundation set up by the federal government; financed by sales of test and Finanztest plus a federal subsidy; carries no advertising (Wikipedia, 2026-10-15). ICRT member.
- **vki**: Verein fuer Konsumenteninformation (VKI), Vienna, Austria; publishes KONSUMENT. Joint testing partner of Stiftung Warentest in ICRT.
- **choice**: CHOICE (Australian Consumers' Association), Sydney, Australia; member-funded consumer group; buys test units at retail; testing sent to an external lab for trampolines because its NATA lab lacks ceiling height.
- **note**: None is linked to a retailer or trampoline brand. Test seals are reused by manufacturers (Hudora press release 23.05.2025) and retailers in marketing.

**lifecycle status**

- **stiftung warentest**: Published 22.04.2025; no later update shown on test.de (checked 2026-10-15) - about 18 months old, older than six months. Eight models bought October 2024; three 'good' models reuse April 2019 pre-test results because the providers said they are sold unchanged (checked only for plausibility); prices surveyed February 2025.
- **vki**: Press release 22.04.2025, magazine 24.04.2025; no update found. Same age caveat.
- **choice**: Page last updated 14 Oct 2025 (about 12 months old at verification); the product list spans more than one test round and includes discontinued models (e.g. Vuly Thunder Medium).
- **model year drift found 2026 10 15**:
  - Kettler Jump 305 (the 'mangelhaft' model): kettlershop.com now sells a 'NEW: redesigned ... updated version' with a spare kit, three-point net fastening and GS mark at EUR 349 + EUR 9.99 postage; the page does not mention the test or say what changed. The test verdict may not apply to the revised version.
  - Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300 (the only 'sehr gut'): listed at EUR 695 and 'Ausverkauft' (sold out) on hudora.de on 2026-10-15.
  - Three models carry 2019 lab data; the free part of test.de does not name which.

**⚠ cost model**

- **stiftung warentest**: Free summary (model names, criteria, weights, headline findings); per-model grades and the full report EUR 4.90 per test unlock or a test.de flatrate (test.de, 2026-10-15).
- **vki**: Free press release names the two worst models; full table on konsument.at for logged-in users, online flatrate from EUR 4.00/month or a 24-hour ticket (konsument.at, 2026-10-15).
- **choice**: Methodology and failure summary free; ratings and per-model scores need CHOICE membership (price not captured) ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **cheapest route**: EUR 4.90 once on test.de covers the European set; KONSUMENT adds nothing beyond the Austrian grading scale.

**feature geo matrix**

Access: all three sell online access to buyers in Poland (card payment; no geo-block seen). Language: test.de and konsument.at in German, CHOICE in English; no Polish publication found - a search for a Federacja Konsumentow release of this test returned nothing (2026-10-15). Relevance to Poland: high for Stiftung Warentest/VKI (EU brands, EN 71-14), low for CHOICE (mostly Australian brands; only Springfree reaches Poland, through a Czech marketplace seller on decathlon.pl).

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial and useful. test.de lists technical data per model (e.g. Lidl Crivit 305: provider max user weight 100 kg, 56 springs, frame height about 75 cm) and the free page gives exact model names. Variant traps found while checking Polish availability: 'Salta Premium Black Edition' on mediamarkt.pl is a rectangular 214x305 cm version, not the tested round 305; Hudora sells 'Fantastic Complete Max 300' (sehr gut, 1.4), 'Fantastic 300V' (gut, 1.9) and a cheaper 'Fabulous 300V' (kaufland.pl) - three similar names; 'Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition' also exists as a 244 cm / 75 kg model (decathlon.de). A test grade only transfers to the exact model, size and enclosure version.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A for price comparison - the tests report average prices at test time (Feb 2025), not shops. Polish availability of the tested models, checked 2026-10-15 via shop pages and search snippets: Decathlon Domyos 360 - decathlon.pl (1,199 PLN promo to 29 Jul 2026, regular 1,499 PLN); Berg Favorit - decathlon.pl marketplace, sold by BERG PL (InGround 330 from 2,489 PLN; the tested Regular 330 grey not confirmed); Exit Silhouette 305 - kaufland.pl 1,649 PLN, e-katalog.pl 1,869-2,589 PLN; Zero Gravity Ultima 4 - kaufland.pl marketplace 1,452.55 PLN (size not shown); Salta Premium Black Edition - mediamarkt.pl only in the rectangular 214x305 variant (JSON-LD price 1,995 PLN in own probe; a search snippet showed 2,279 PLN earlier); Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300, Exit Elegant Premium, Salta Comfort Edition 305, Kettler Jump 305 and Lidl Crivit 305 - no Polish listing found ⚠ *(unverified)*. Springfree (CHOICE pass) - decathlon.pl marketplace via MarketLink Int. s.r.o. (CZ).

**price history and omnibus**

N/A - lab tests, no price tracking.

**total landed cost**

N/A for price. Indirect inputs: Stiftung Warentest weights 'Handhabung' (assembly and winter storage) at 25%; the Kettler sets could not be assembled because frame bars did not fit; VKI's project lead estimates 5-10 years life for quality models vs first wear after 2-3 years for cheap ones - useful for cost per year of use.

**review and seller verification**

N/A - tests assess products, not sellers or reviews. Units were bought anonymously at retail (Stiftung Warentest, CHOICE), so results reflect retail stock.

**⚠ safety and compliance checks**

- **stiftung warentest vki**: Safety per DIN EN 71-14:2019-03 (toys - trampolines for domestic use) plus the German GS test principle EK2/AK 2.2 14-01:2019; drop of a 120 kg sandbag against nets and posts; mat loaded to five times the maximum user weight; 48 h salt spray (EN ISO 9227:2017) on metal parts and springs; 400 h UV ageing of net, mat and edge; pollutants: PAH, phthalates and chlorinated paraffins in edge cover and mat, azo dyes in net and mat; five testers of 48-80 kg. Criteria weights: entry and jumping 35%, safety 25%, handling 25%, workmanship (incl. corrosion) 10%, pollutants 5%.
- **choice**: AS 4989:2015 based: structural loads on frame, mat and enclosure; impact absorption of padding and enclosure; head and finger entrapment, clothing snags, sharp edges, protruding bolts (an accessible head-entrapment gap is a serious failure); marking and safety information; ease of use. CHOICE does NOT run the standard's UV and salt-spray tests (time and cost). Score: 70% performance, 30% ease of use; models with serious failures are not recommended.
- **failure mode checklist**:
  - Frame parts that do not fit or a leg that deforms when a heavy body hits the net (Kettler Jump 305; Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition in the 120 kg sandbag test).
  - Rust on posts and springs after salt spray (Kettler Jump 305) - not tested by CHOICE.
  - PAH in the jumping mat (Kettler Jump 305; VKI: limits met but elevated; test.de: 'large amounts').
  - Weak net anchoring / enclosure stability (Zero Gravity, per secondary summary of test.de).
  - Padding that does not cover springs or does not absorb impact, or wears quickly (CHOICE).
  - Pinch, limb and head entrapment gaps (CHOICE).
  - Instructions that are missing or hard to follow, leading to unsafe assembly (CHOICE).
  - Padding colour that does not contrast with the mat (CHOICE, minor).
- **standard version note**: The European test used EN 71-14 in its 2019 German edition; whether a 2025 revision of EN 71-14 changes requirements was not checked here ⚠ *(unverified)*. Neither test checked GPSR listing fields or Safety Gate entries.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

- **results known**:
  - **sehr gut**: Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300 - 1.4 (test winner; one of the pricier models).
  - **gut**: Lidl Crivit 305 cm - 1.6; Berg Favorit Regular 330 Grey + Safety Net Comfort - 1.8; Salta Premium Black Edition 305 - 1.8; Decathlon Domyos Trampolin 360 - 1.9 (fastest assembly); Hudora Fantastic Trampolin 300V - 1.9; Exit Silhouette 305, Exit Elegant Premium (Deluxe net), Salta Comfort Edition 305 - 'gut', exact marks not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*.
  - **befriedigend**: Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition (cheapest in the VKI set; a leg deformed in the load test; VKI scale: 'durchschnittlich').
  - **mangelhaft**: Kettler Jump 305 - frame bars did not fit in any tested set (Kettler: one-off batch defect, replacement parts via customer service), posts heavily rusted after 48 h salt spray, elevated PAH in the mat (VKI: 'nicht zufriedenstellend').
  - **source of per model marks**: Per-model marks are paywalled on test.de; marks above come from secondary reports (t-online, kaufda, produkte-im-test.de with Amazon affiliate links, Hudora press release) that agree on the top five; the 'mangelhaft' and 'befriedigend' identities are confirmed by VKI's free press release.
- **choice results**: Serious failures: Kahuna Classic 10ft (2), Kmart 12ft Springless (1), Lifespan HyperJump3 (1), Lifespan Hyperjump4 10ft (1), Little Nation 10ft (1), OzTrampolines 10ft Round Summit (3), Plum 10ft Space Zone II Springsafe (2), Plum Space Zone V3 30212 (1), Premier 10ft Jump (2). No serious failures: Springfree Medium Square S72 and R79 Medium Round (AUD 2,099 each, 100% performance score), Vuly Thunder Medium (discontinued).
- **related tests**: Which? (UK) tested 8 trampolines in May 2024 and July 2022 incl. Zero Gravity Ultima 4 and Plum Space Zone II and says all passed its checks (Best Buys paywalled) - see the separate Which? item. Stiftung Warentest ran an earlier trampoline test in April 2019; test.de also reported a Lidl recall of an older Crivit trampoline whose net could tear.
- **date vs model year**: Units bought October 2024 (2025 season); three models from 2019 data. Buying for the 2027 season means checking that the model, size and enclosure version are still the tested ones (see lifecycle_status drift).
- **surfaced by tools**: Polish comparison sites and marketplaces do not surface these results systematically; German retailers (Lidl.de, Galaxus) and Hudora display the seal.

**alerts and monitoring**

N/A - publications; no alerts. A page watch (changedetection.io) on the test.de article URL would flag an update.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A - information source; no purchase function.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: tests do not rate spare parts or service. Useful facts: Kettler sends replacement frame parts via customer service and now ships a spare kit; Decathlon sells individual 360 spares (mat, frame segment, T-connector, L/V feet) on its EU sites; VKI's 5-10 year vs 2-3 year lifespan estimate.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Own lab measurements on retail-bought units (October 2024 purchase; 2019 data for three models), provider-stated technical data, and prices requested from providers in February 2025. CHOICE: units bought at retail, external lab, page updated October 2025. Answers are backed by the publisher's page; no snapshots or open data.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: none
- **detail**: No API, no MCP server, no skill for any of the three. Free summary pages are readable by WebFetch (test.de, konsument.at and choice.com.au summary pages all returned text on 2026-10-15). Paywalled tables need the user's own logged-in browser; a browser agent could read them only in a session the user has already signed into (the agent must not enter the password). Fallback: buy once, read manually, store a short private summary.
- **setup effort**: About 5 minutes to buy the test.de unlock; reading 15-20 minutes.

**protocol support**

N/A - publications.

**open source and licence**

Closed, copyrighted publications. Test methods are described publicly; the result tables are paid content.

**account linking and data access**

A test.de or konsument.at account and card payment for paid content; no shop accounts. Data kept: account email and purchase. GDPR: German and Austrian publishers, EU data protection applies; CHOICE is outside the EU.

**automation legal risk**

Scraping paywalled tables or republishing per-model grades verbatim infringes the publishers' copyright and terms; Stiftung Warentest also controls advertising use of its results through a logo licence. This vault is published publicly at brain.lipowczan.pl, so a public note should carry the free facts (names, criteria, weights, the free headline findings) and a link, and keep the paid per-model table out of the published content.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Low at source: Stiftung Warentest carries no ads (sales plus federal subsidy); VKI and CHOICE are consumer organisations funded by members and sales; units bought anonymously. Bias enters downstream: secondary 'Testsieger' pages (produkte-im-test.de with Amazon affiliate links, retailer blogs) and manufacturer PR repeat grades with their own prices and sometimes the wrong variant; produkte-im-test.de even gives two different prices for the test winner (EUR 499 vs 695).

**ranking transparency**

High for method: Stiftung Warentest publishes criteria and weights (35/25/25/10/5) and test standards; CHOICE publishes its 70/30 scoring and test list. Individual grades are behind the paywall. No sponsored items.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - lab tests, not AI tools. Note that Stiftung Warentest reused 2019 results for three models instead of retesting.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Lab results are hard to game because units are bought anonymously at retail. Downstream risks: seals shown on a different size or a revised model (Kettler's 2026 'updated version'), look-alike names (Hudora Max 300 / 300V / Fabulous 300V), and an AI agent repeating a secondary site's grade for the wrong variant. Per the Wharton agentic-shopping report, one authoritative source can dominate an agent's pick, so a single 'Testsieger' page should not decide alone.

**known failures**

Age: 18 months old at verification with visible model drift. Coverage: 11 round ~3 m spring models only - no rectangular, in-ground or springless designs in the European test. Three results date from 2019. Count confusion: VKI 10 vs Stiftung Warentest 11 (Lidl Crivit was only in the German set). Different grade scales (befriedigend vs durchschnittlich). CHOICE's '8 tested, all but two failed' line does not match its product list of 12 models. Secondary sites disagree on prices and on marks below the top five.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the test labs. Context: CHOICE campaigns for mandatory product-safety rules because AS 4989 is voluntary in Australia; in the EU, trampolines for domestic use fall under the Toy Safety Directive with EN 71-14 as the harmonised standard.

**buyer protection path**

N/A as a route. Practical use: a defect the test documents (parts that do not fit, early rust) is a non-conformity claim under Polish statutory warranty (rekojmia, 2 years for consumers) against the seller.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

High - the most relevant evidence for the reference purchase. Concrete use: shortlist from the 'gut' group that is actually sold in Poland (Decathlon Domyos 360 at 1,199-1,499 PLN on decathlon.pl; Exit Silhouette 305 around 1,649 PLN; Berg Favorit via BERG PL), avoid Kettler Jump 305 unless it is the revised version and evidence exists, and treat Zero Gravity Ultima 4 with caution. Use the failure-mode checklist (rust, net anchor stability, padding coverage, entrapment gaps, PAH smell) when judging any untested model. Limits: the tested winner is hard to buy in Poland and sold out on hudora.de.

**workflow role**

Independent tests and safety step, right after discovery. Combine with a Safety Gate / UOKiK register check, exact-variant matching (EAN, size, enclosure), Polish availability and price (Ceneo, shop pages) and a price tracker.

**effort and cost per purchase**

EUR 4.90 for the test.de unlock (covers the European set) plus about 20 minutes of reading; KONSUMENT (from EUR 4.00/month) is redundant; CHOICE optional and of low relevance. Total about EUR 5 and 30 minutes for one trampoline decision.

**evidence trail**

Good if done manually: record publisher, title, URL, publication date (22.04.2025), purchase date of units (10/2024), exact model names and sizes, overall mark, and the failure reasons, plus the date checked. Keep the paid per-model table in a private, non-published file; the public note links to test.de and quotes only the free facts.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Lab tests on retail-bought units with published standards and weights (EN 71-14, salt spray, UV, pollutants).
  - Covers EU brands sold in Poland (Decathlon, Berg, Exit, Hudora, Salta, Zero Gravity).
  - Clear failure modes (non-fitting parts, rust, PAH, net anchor) usable as a checklist for untested models.
  - Cheap: EUR 4.90 for the full European table.
  - CHOICE adds entrapment and padding failure modes and a strong result for springless designs.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Published April 2025; models have changed since (Kettler revised, Hudora winner sold out).
  - Three results reuse 2019 data.
  - Per-model grades paywalled; secondary sources disagree on prices and lower marks.
  - Several tested models are not listed in Polish shops; exact variant matters.
  - CHOICE skips UV and salt-spray tests and covers mostly Australian brands.

**independent review consensus**

The two European publications are one joint test and agree: most ~3 m spring trampolines are good, the Kettler Jump 305 fails, the Zero Gravity Ultima 4 is weak, the Hudora Max 300 wins. CHOICE finds more failures, but on different (mostly Australian) brands and a different method; Which? (UK) reports that all its tested models passed its checks, including a Zero Gravity Ultima 4 (different size/market not confirmed). Secondary German coverage (t-online, kaufda, galaxus, produkte-im-test.de - the last with Amazon affiliate links) repeats the same top results.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW - the 22.04.2025 test.de result (EUR 4.90) is the only lab evidence covering trampoline brands sold in Poland; buy it once, match exact model and size to Polish listings, and apply the combined failure-mode checklist to anything untested.

**conflicting evidence**

- Count: VKI says 10 trampolines, Stiftung Warentest 11 - the Lidl Crivit 305 is in the German set only (derived by comparing the two model lists).
- Grade wording for Zero Gravity Ultima 4: 'befriedigend' (Stiftung Warentest per secondary sources) vs 'durchschnittlich' (VKI) - different scales.
- Kettler failure cause: test.de says the mat contained 'large amounts' of pollutants; VKI says PAH was elevated in places but relevant limits were met.
- Kettler defect: VKI says no set could be assembled; Kettler calls it a one-off batch error, and a redesigned Jump 305 is now sold without saying what changed.
- CHOICE: summary says 8 models tested and all but two had serious failures; the product list shows 9 with serious failures and 3 without (rounds combined).
- Test-winner price: produkte-im-test.de shows EUR 499 in its table and EUR 695 in its conclusion; hudora.de shows EUR 695 and sold out; other listings show EUR 439-499.
- Which? says all trampolines it tested passed its checks, while Stiftung Warentest/VKI and CHOICE report failures - different models and methods.
