### Wirecutter, RTINGS and Which?

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY (RTINGS USE NOW for electronics) · **Cost:** Paid memberships · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 8 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **wirecutter**: New York Times product-recommendation site (role: test lab / review publisher). Guides name one or two picks per category after hands-on testing; US market, US retailers. Paywalled since August 2021.
- **rtings**: RTINGS.com, lab-measurement review site (role: test lab) covering 28 categories - TVs, soundbars, projectors, monitors, mice, keyboards, keyboard switches, printers, routers, VPNs, laptops, headphones, speakers, vacuums, robot vacuums, dehumidifiers, air conditioners, humidifiers, air purifiers, mattresses, toasters, toaster ovens, air fryers, blenders, microwaves, refrigerators, running shoes, cameras (rtings.com, 2026-10-15). Claims 5,000 products bought and tested. Full results members-only.
- **which**: Which?, the UK Consumers' Association (role: test lab / consumer organisation). Lab tests with Best Buy and Don't Buy labels across appliances, tech, garden machinery and children's products, including trampolines; ICRT member. Scores members-only.
- **wharton finding**: Wharton Generative AI Labs, 'Agentic Shopping is Complicated and Contingent' (Prompting Science Report 6, 27 Aug 2026; SSRN 7355899): about 26,000 runs in the ACES simulator choosing among eight fitness watches. One screenshot of a Wirecutter review moved Gemini 3.5 Flash to Wirecutter's pick in essentially every run (+99 percentage points); bundling sources in one tool call moved GPT-5.5 +53 pp toward Wirecutter's pick; when sources conflicted, agents did not average them - Wirecutter won for both Claude models (Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.8); a Reddit + Strategist pair moved no model.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

- **wirecutter**: Wirecutter, Inc., owned by The New York Times Company (USA) since October 2016 (bought for about USD 30 million). Plaintiff with NYT against Perplexity (filed 5 Dec 2025, SDNY; amended complaint 20 Mar 2026).
- **rtings**: RTINGS.com, independent company; HQ in Canada (Montreal area) ⚠ *(unverified: not confirmed on a primary page)*. No outside owner found. Ads served by Antengo (USA) and PubLift (worldwide); badge and quote licensing via Wright's Media.
- **which**: Consumers' Association (trading as Which?), UK not-for-profit; member of ICRT, the testing consortium that also includes Stiftung Warentest and VKI.
- **bias note**: None is owned by a retailer or marketplace; all three earn affiliate commissions.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

- **wirecutter**: Active. Paywall since August 2021; 'How We Make Money' page reportedly updated 3 March 2026 (secondary commentary, page not opened - nytimes.com is blocked for this research tool).
- **rtings**: Active. Display ads introduced from May 2025 ('You Might Start Seeing Ads', published 2025-05-15); 'How We Make Money' updated 2026-07-07; secondary forum source says on 31 Mar 2026 RTINGS renamed 'Insider' to 'RTINGS.com Membership' and moved full test results behind it, citing weaker Google/affiliate traffic and AI reuse of its data ⚠ *(unverified: primary announcement not found)*. Join page live with PLN prices on 2026-10-15.
- **which**: Active. Trampoline guide dated 13 Jul 2026, models tested May 2024 and July 2022, page 'last checked' June 2026 (verified 2026-10-15).
- **wharton**: Report 27 Aug 2026; Wharton AI & Analytics summary 28 Sep 2026.

**⚠ cost model**

- **wirecutter**: Subscription: standalone USD 5 per 4 weeks or USD 40/year at the 2021 launch, included in NYT All Access and Home Delivery; a limited number of free articles (10/month at launch). Current price not verified ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **rtings**: Membership seen from Poland 2026-10-15 (rtings.com/join, geo PL): PLN 17.86/month or PLN 80/year; a 30% promo cut the first month to PLN 12.50 and the first year to PLN 56. Much of the site stays free; full results and tools need membership.
- **which**: Which? Digital: GBP 5/month for the first 3 months (offer on the trampoline page, 2026-10-15); annual plans auto-renew at GBP 89 (Digital), GBP 79 (Magazine), GBP 109 (Full Access) per Which? signup pages (search snippets, 2026).

**feature geo matrix**

Wirecutter: US products, US prices and US retailers; English only; nothing for Poland. RTINGS: English; mostly US-market units; RTINGS community posts show regional variants differ (e.g. US Samsung QN90A vs EU QN90A with lower peak brightness and no wide-angle layer), so EU buyers must match the model code; membership is priced in local currency (PLN shown from Poland). Which?: English; UK models and UK retailers (Argos, Currys, John Lewis, Smyths); many products overlap with EU ranges through ICRT joint tests, but the trampoline set is mostly UK brands. No Polish interface for any. Price alerts and buy features: none.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

RTINGS: strongest - numeric measurements, side-by-side compare tool, 'test bench' versions, notes on size and regional variants (members for full data). Which?: specs plus scores per model; no EAN mapping. Wirecutter: narrative picks with 'also great'/budget alternatives; no structured specs. None maps EAN/GTIN or retailer-exclusive variants; all three test a specific regional model.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

None. Each shows a handful of affiliate retailer links (Wirecutter: US retailers; Which?: UK retailers and says cheaper prices may exist elsewhere; RTINGS: retailer links plus member-exclusive deals). No Polish shops.

**price history and omnibus**

None. RTINGS has deals pages and member-only negotiated discounts; Wirecutter has a deals team; neither tracks history or Omnibus prices.

**⚠ total landed cost**

None. Which? sometimes reports running costs (energy) for appliances ⚠ *(unverified)*; nothing on shipping, returns or cross-border warranty.

**review and seller verification**

None for sellers or reviews (grade: none). Which? campaigns and investigates fake reviews and unsafe marketplace listings in the UK and runs Which? Trusted Traders for UK tradespeople, but that is not a per-purchase seller check for Polish shops.

**safety and compliance checks**

Which?: partial - trampoline checks include enclosure strength (60 kg hung from the top), finger entrapment in the net, mat load (150 kg for 10 minutes), tipping stability, frame height of at least 50 cm and enclosure height (150 cm for 8 ft, 180 cm for 10 ft+); the page does not cite EN 71-14 and says all trampolines tested so far passed. Which? Don't Buy labels flag poor performers in other categories. RTINGS and Wirecutter: no safety-standard checks beyond noting recalls. None checks Safety Gate, GPSR listing fields or certificates.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

- **trampolines**: Wirecutter: no trampoline guide found (a secondhand blog claims a Jumpflex Hero 15ft top pick; a Walmart listing claims 'NY Times chose Sportspower as best budget trampoline' - both unverified) ⚠ *(unverified: , nytimes.com could not be fetched)*. RTINGS: no trampoline or outdoor category. Which?: 8 trampolines tested May 2024 and July 2022 - Jump Power Elite, Kanga Premium, Plum Space Zone II, Sportspower Outdoor Kids, Techsport, Thorpe Sports, TP Toys Up, Zero Gravity Ultima 4; two Best Buys (names paywalled). Zero Gravity Ultima 4 and Plum Space Zone II overlap with Stiftung Warentest/VKI (which rated the Ultima 4 Black Edition only 'befriedigend') and CHOICE (Plum models had serious failures) - different sizes, markets and methods.
- **other durables**: RTINGS: electronics and some home/kitchen appliances (vacuums, air purifiers, refrigerators, air conditioners) - strong for these if the EU model matches. Which?: broad durables incl. garden machinery (lawn mowers, robot mowers, trimmers, leaf blowers, pressure washers; pressure washer Best Buy needs 75%+, Don't Buy below 45%). Wirecutter: very broad incl. tools and outdoor gear, but US models.
- **access**: All three paywall the detailed scores; Which? and RTINGS publish methods for free.
- **model year**: Which? trampoline data is 2.3-4 years old relative to a 2026/2027 purchase.

**alerts and monitoring**

None for prices or stock. Newsletters only (RTINGS 'The Essential' and deals newsletters; Wirecutter deals newsletter).

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. Links go to retailers; the buyer checks out there.

**⚠ after sales and resale**

Brief: Which? publishes brand reliability survey data for many appliance categories ⚠ *(unverified: for garden goods)*; RTINGS runs long-term tests in some categories ⚠ *(unverified)*; none covers Polish service networks, spare parts or resale.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Own testing of retail-bought units (RTINGS and Which? state they buy everything; Wirecutter combines hands-on testing and expert interviews). Freshness varies per guide: Which? trampolines tested 2022/2024; RTINGS updates reviews when its test bench changes and retests; Wirecutter guides carry an 'updated' date. Each answer is a dated web page, no snapshot API.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: none
- **wirecutter**: No public API, MCP or skill. nytimes.com refused this research tool's fetcher (2026-10-15); NYT is suing Perplexity partly over Wirecutter summaries, so automated extraction is legally sensitive. Manual reading with a subscription is the only route.
- **rtings**: No public API; data licensing is for badges and quotes via Wright's Media. Free pages embed article JSON in the HTML (readable with curl on 2026-10-15) and use Cloudflare Turnstile; members' data needs a logged-in browser session the user opens. A browser agent could read pages in the user's own session; the agent must not enter credentials.
- **which**: No public API, MCP or skill. Free method pages are readable with WebFetch; scores require login.
- **setup effort**: Subscription signup 5 minutes each; reading per category 15-30 minutes. No agent integration worth building.

**protocol support**

None (publishers, not commerce endpoints).

**open source and licence**

Closed, copyrighted publications.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Subscription account and payment card; affiliate cookies on outbound links (Which? states it tracks clicks with cookies to earn commission). No shop or payment linking. Wirecutter (US) and RTINGS (Canada) process data outside the EU; Which? is UK (adequacy decision applies) ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

High for Wirecutter: NYT v. Perplexity (filed 5 Dec 2025, SDNY, amended 20 Mar 2026) alleges copyright and trademark harm from AI summaries of Wirecutter reviews and ignoring robots.txt blocks; unresolved as of the latest report found. RTINGS reportedly paywalled results partly because of AI reuse ⚠ *(unverified)*. Which?: paywalled scores; copying them into a public vault note would breach copyright. Low-volume personal reading in your own session is fine; scraping or republishing is not.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Wirecutter: affiliate commissions on purchases through its links are the main revenue, plus subscriptions and (per Nieman Lab 2026) advertising; it states picks are made before commerce decisions. RTINGS: membership, affiliate commissions, display ads (since 2025; none for paying members) and badge licensing; states brands cannot pay for reviews and products are bought at retail; community votes choose what is tested. Which?: subscriptions, affiliate commissions (Amazon, Argos, John Lewis and specialists, mostly automated outside editorial control), and logo licensing to companies, with a statement that licensees are not judged more favourably. Bias risk: low inside the tests; affiliate links shape which retailers are shown, and 'best' lists favour widely sold products.

**ranking transparency**

RTINGS: high - per-test measurements and published methodology (scores members-only). Which?: methods and thresholds public (e.g. 75% for Best Buy), scores paywalled. Wirecutter: explains why it picked and tested, but no numeric scores. No sponsored placements in any. You cannot rerun them with a source excluded.

**run to run consistency**

N/A for the publications themselves. Relevant agent evidence: the Wharton report shows an agent's pick depends on whether a Wirecutter review is in context (up to +99 pp), on source order (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite) and on bundled vs separate tool calls (GPT-5.5 +53 pp) - so an agent that reads one of these sites is less consistent than one that reads none.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

The labs buy retail units anonymously, so the tests themselves are hard to game. Downstream risks: SEO spam pages imitate the Wirecutter brand ('Best Wirecutter hammock 2025' style pages found in search), sellers claim picks that cannot be verified (Walmart Sportspower listing), and Perplexity allegedly attributed praise to Wirecutter for a product it never reviewed (NYT complaint). Per Wharton, a single authoritative-looking source can override an agent's judgement, so a fake 'Wirecutter pick' is an effective injection vector.

**known failures**

Wirecutter: US-only products and retailers; no Polish relevance; paywall; no trampoline guide found. RTINGS: no garden/outdoor/sports categories; US units may differ from EU variants; full results moved behind membership. Which?: UK-only ranges (trampoline set mostly UK brands); trampoline checks did not fail any model, so they discriminate less than Stiftung Warentest/CHOICE; test data 2022/2024.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - no UOKiK, DSA or court decisions against these publishers found. NYT/Wirecutter is a plaintiff (v. Perplexity), not a defendant.

**buyer protection path**

N/A - information sources; protection depends on the shop where you buy (Polish statutory warranty, 14-day withdrawal, chargeback, ECC-Net cross-border).

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Trampoline: low. Which? is the only one with trampoline data, on UK models (two overlap by name with the European test), and its free page gives only method and model names; Stiftung Warentest/VKI is the better source for Poland. Other durables: RTINGS is high value for a TV, monitor, vacuum or air purifier if the EU model code matches; Which? is useful for appliances and garden machinery sold in the EU under the same model code; Wirecutter only when the US pick is sold identically in the EU.

**workflow role**

Independent tests step for electronics and appliances (RTINGS first, Which? second); context only for trampolines. Also a design input for the agent workflow: present each test source separately with its date and market, require agreement across at least two sources, and never let one 'pick' decide (Wharton).

**effort and cost per purchase**

RTINGS: one month PLN 17.86 (about EUR 4) or PLN 80/year when buying electronics; Which?: GBP 5 for one month during the intro offer; Wirecutter: not worth paying from Poland. Trampoline decision: GBP 5 (Which?) only if a UK-tested model is on the Polish shortlist, otherwise EUR 0. Time 15-30 minutes per category.

**evidence trail**

Moderate: stable URLs with update dates, test-bench version (RTINGS) and test dates (Which?). Save 'publisher, URL, model code and region, test date, score/label, date read' in a private note; do not copy paywalled score tables into the public vault.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - RTINGS: numeric lab measurements, public methodology, retail-bought units, 28 categories, cheap membership in PLN.
  - Which?: broad durables incl. garden machinery and trampolines, clear Best Buy / Don't Buy thresholds, ICRT links to European tests.
  - Wirecutter: very broad category coverage and clear single picks for US products.
  - All three buy products anonymously and state that advertisers cannot buy reviews.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No Polish market coverage; Wirecutter and Which? are US- and UK-centric.
  - Trampolines: only Which?, on UK models with 2022/2024 data and no failing model.
  - Paywalls on scores; no APIs; Wirecutter is legally sensitive to automate (NYT v. Perplexity).
  - Wharton: one Wirecutter screenshot can swing an AI agent's pick by up to 99 pp, so feeding these sources to an agent needs guardrails.

**independent review consensus**

No independent audit of these labs' accuracy found. Coverage agrees on roles: Wirecutter is affiliate-funded but editorially separated (Nieman Lab, Fortune 2016 - older); RTINGS is the reference for measured electronics data and moved toward paid membership and ads (RTINGS' own pages; secondary forum source for the 2026 paywall step). The Wharton report (primary, 2026) is the only rigorous evidence on how these sources affect AI agents.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY for the trampoline (deciding fact: none tests EU trampoline brands except Which?'s UK set, which overlaps by only two model names); USE NOW RTINGS for electronics/appliance purchases with a one-month membership, and build the Wharton lesson into the agent - present each lab separately and require two agreeing sources.

**conflicting evidence**

- Wirecutter trampoline coverage: a third-party blog says Wirecutter's top pick is the Jumpflex Hero 15ft and a Walmart listing says the NYT chose Sportspower as best budget trampoline; no Wirecutter page could be found or fetched to confirm either.
- RTINGS access: its 2025 ads page and current homepage say much of the site is free and membership unlocks full results; a forum summary calls RTINGS '100% behind a paywall' after 31 Mar 2026 - the same source calls that framing an overstatement.
- RTINGS membership price: forum figures of USD 10/month and USD 45/year vs PLN 17.86/month and PLN 80/year on the join page seen from Poland (2026-10-15).
- Wirecutter advertising: Fortune (2016) said few ads; Nieman Lab (2026) says Wirecutter also earns from advertising.
- Trampoline safety: Which? says every trampoline it tested passed its checks, while Stiftung Warentest/VKI rated a Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition only 'befriedigend' - different sizes, markets and methods.

### Polish test and owner-experience sources

**Verdict:** USE NOW (Pro-Test, German tests) · **Cost:** Pro-Test PLN 139 a year · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 16 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Not a single tool: a map of where independent tests and owner experience for durable goods actually exist for a Polish buyer, verified 2026-10-15. Findings: (1) Federacja Konsumentow (FK) publishes no current comparative tests; it does legal advice, reports and campaigns. (2) The Polish source of lab tests is Fundacja PRO-TEST (pro-test.pl), the Polish ICRT member, publishing ICRT joint tests in Polish behind a paywall (2025-2026 tests: TVs, air fryers, robot vacuums, soundbars, kettles, children's bike helmets) - no trampoline test. (3) For trampolines the relevant lab tests are Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 and VKI KONSUMENT 05/2025, both German-language. (4) Owner experience in Polish lives in purchase-linked reviews (Allegro, Ceneo Zaufane Opinie), Opineo for shops, and forums (forum.murator.pl, forum.budujemydom.pl, forumogrodnicze.info, forum.gazeta.pl, Elektroda for electronics and tools, Wykop, r/Polska), but search engines surface retailer guides and affiliate 'rankings' instead. (5) Reddit Answers (Reddit's AI search) supports English plus French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese since 2025-10-16; Polish is not supported. Role types: test lab, consumer organisation, review platform, forum, AI search.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

Fundacja PRO-TEST: foundation, ul. Filtrowa 67/106, 02-055 Warszawa, KRS 0000318692, NIP 7010161613; says it has tested since 2001; ICRT member (Wikipedia ICRT list, confirmed by Pro-Test's own post); its 2026 ICRT membership fee of EUR 5,159.66 is co-funded by the state Narodowy Instytut Wolnosci under PROO priority 5 (agreement dated 2026-05-15). Federacja Konsumentow: NGO founded 1981, public-benefit organisation, KRS 0000075284, about 48 local clubs (Wikipedia, last edited 2018). Stiftung Warentest: German foundation; VKI: Austrian consumer association; both ICRT members. Reddit Answers: Reddit, Inc. (US), runs on a Google AI model (TechCrunch). Allegro and Ceneo: Allegro.eu group. Forums: various publishers ⚠ *(unverified: owners of Murator forum, Elektroda and Wykop not verified in this session)*.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

Pro-Test: active; newest test 'Wielki test malych telewizorow' (54 models) dated 2026-09-26, newest free article 2026-10-15; site footer 2026. FK: active as an advice and advocacy body (latest news 2026-10-12) but no comparative tests on the site; its only test-related page is an archived EU project 'Capacity building in consumer testing and magazines in new member states' (about 2009). test-konsumencki.pl (FK with Consumentenbond): defunct; the domain returns an empty page and Wayback shows the last HTTP 200 capture in 2017. swiatkonsumenta.pl: now a payday-loan affiliate site, unrelated to consumer testing despite the name. Stiftung Warentest trampoline test: published 2025-04-22, about 18 months old. VKI test: published 2025-04-22. Reddit Answers: beta 2024-12 (US English), five more languages 2025-10-16, 15 million weekly actives in Q4 2025 and being merged into core Reddit search (TechCrunch 2026-02-05); no Polish announcement found. Forums: forumogrodnicze.info shows posts dated 2026-10-15; forum.gazeta.pl live; forum.budujemydom.pl live; forum.murator.pl returned HTTP 403 to scripts; elektroda.pl timed out from this session ⚠ *(unverified)*. Opineo live (user terms updated 2025-05-05). Verified 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

Pro-Test: PLN 139 per year (one payment, no auto-renewal) or PLN 16.99 per test article; some articles free (seen 2026-10-15). Stiftung Warentest: EUR 4.90 to unlock the trampoline test (or a flat-rate subscription). VKI: paywalled online results ⚠ *(unverified: price not checked)*. FK advice, forums, Opineo, Allegro and Ceneo reviews and Reddit Answers: free.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Pro-Test: Polish, tests of products sold in Poland (ICRT joint tests with Polish prices) ⚠ *(unverified: Polish price sourcing not verified)*. FK: Polish advice only. Forums and Allegro/Ceneo reviews: Polish. Reddit Answers: Polish language not supported; whether a Polish account with English as default language gets Answers is not confirmed for Poland.
- **EU**: Stiftung Warentest (Germany) and VKI (Austria) publish German-language tests, often of models also sold in Poland; dTest (Czech Republic) is the Czech ICRT member but no dTest trampoline test was found. Reddit Answers: French, German, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese for users whose default language is one of these (Brazil, France, Germany, Spain, Mexico, Italy named).
- **US**: Reddit Answers launched in the US (English, beta December 2024); Consumer Reports is the ICRT member there.
- **language**: Polish sources in Polish; lab tests for trampolines in German; Reddit Answers in EN, FR, DE, ES, IT, PT only.
- **US only or agentic features**: None of these sources has agentic or purchase features.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Lab tests are the best variant anchors because they name exact model codes. Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 lists e.g. Hudora Fantastic Trampolin 300V 65731/01, Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300 65760, Decathlon Domyos Trampolin 360 8799832, Lidl Crivit Gartentrampolin 305 cm 373605, Exit Elegant Premium 08.20.10.80, plus Berg Favorit Regular 330, Exit Silhouette 305, Kettler Jump 305, Salta Comfort Edition 305, Salta Premium Black Edition 305 and Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition. Matching these codes to Polish listings (Ceneo, Allegro) is manual. Forums and Reddit give no structured specs; owner posts often omit the model code.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A - none of these is a price tool. Test.de shows supplier prices in EUR (mid-2026); Pro-Test shows prices at test time ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A.

**total landed cost**

N/A, with one useful input: VKI gives component lifetimes for trampolines (frame 5-10 years, mat 3-7, springs 3-6, net and padding 2-5; premium models 5-10 years overall, cheap ones show wear after 2-3 years), which feeds a cost-per-year comparison.

**⚠ review and seller verification**

Partial for review provenance, none for seller identity. Ceneo Zaufane Opinie are purchase-verified (see Ceneo item). Allegro product reviews can reportedly be written only by buyers with a completed purchase in the last 12 months, within 12 months of purchase ⚠ *(unverified: secondary source, tabletowo; Allegro rules not re-opened)*; an Allegro forum user reported the same accounts reviewing one product (anecdotal). Opineo rates shops and runs a 'Wiarygodne Opinie' verification scheme ⚠ *(unverified: not examined)*. Forums and Reddit: no verification; astroturfing possible. UOKiK fined review sellers (Opinie.pro PLN 40,000 in 2022; Best-Review and SeoSem24 PLN 85,618 in 2024), which shows that paid reviews target Polish platforms.

**safety and compliance checks**

Lab tests include safety: Stiftung Warentest assessed trampolines against DIN EN 71-14:2019-03 plus a German test principle (entrapment, mat load at five times maximum user mass, stability, net attachment under dynamic load, 400 h UV, 48 h salt spray) with safety weighted 25% and pollutants 5%; VKI flagged a leg deforming under a 120 kg sandbag test and PAH in one model. Pro-Test publishes a 'Czarna lista produktow 2026' (blacklist) of failed products such as car seats and blood-pressure monitors (2026-08-05). UOKiK and Inspekcja Handlowa publish control reports (2025 controls of 263 recreation businesses including trampoline parks; a 2016 lab test of a 16 ft trampoline led to a UOKiK decision; search summaries only) - see the Safety Gate / UOKiK item. Forums: anecdotes about rust, broken springs and torn nets.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

Trampolines: Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 (published 2025-04-22; 11 models about 3 m, EUR 219-695, bought October 2024; 8 good, 1 very good, 1 'mangelhaft' from a known brand; full grades EUR 4.90) and VKI KONSUMENT 05/2025 (10 models EUR 269-695; 1 very good, 7 good, 1 average - Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition; Kettler Jump 305 failed on fit, rust and PAH). Brands in those tests sold in Poland include Berg, Hudora, Salta, Exit and Decathlon. Pro-Test: no trampoline test (site search 2026-10-15); its 'Dom i ogrod' category covers robot mowers, air purifiers, tools and children's toys, and recent tests include 112 large TVs (2026-07-09), 54 small TVs (2026-09-26), 33 air fryers (2026-05-14), 62 robot vacuums (2025-11-29), 74 soundbars, 36 coffee machines, 15 kettles (2026-01-14) and 17 children's bike helmets (2026-04-13). These are ICRT joint tests, so the same models often appear in Stiftung Warentest, VKI or Which? results. FK: no tests. Polish tech media (Chip, PurePC, Benchmark) review electronics but are not lab tests of durables in the ICRT sense ⚠ *(unverified: not examined)*. None of these sources is surfaced automatically by a shopping tool.

**alerts and monitoring**

None that suits monitoring. Forums allow thread subscriptions by e-mail; Pro-Test promises new tests monthly to subscribers; Reddit Answers has no alerts.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No purchasing. Not applicable.

**⚠ after sales and resale**

Forums are the main Polish source on spare parts (nets, pads, springs), assembly problems and long-term rust; Allegro reviews add durability remarks months after purchase (reviews allowed up to 12 months after purchase ⚠ *(unverified)*). Resale (OLX, Allegro Lokalnie) is not covered by any of these sources.

#### data and integration

**⚠ data sources and freshness**

Pro-Test: ICRT joint laboratory tests; laboratory names deliberately undisclosed (stated policy); dated articles. Stiftung Warentest and VKI: own lab programmes with published criteria and weights, products bought months before publication. Reddit Answers: Reddit posts and comments summarised by a Google model, with links to the threads ⚠ *(unverified: citation format not seen)*. Forums and marketplace reviews: user posts with timestamps. Each source has stable URLs for citation.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. (1) Pro-Test: WordPress site; robots.txt allows articles and disallows only search (?s=) and cart paths; a sitemap index exists; free summaries are fetchable by WebFetch or curl; full results need the user's paid account (do not hand credentials to an agent; read them yourself or export the PDF). No API or MCP. (2) Stiftung Warentest: free part fetchable by WebFetch (worked 2026-10-15); paid tables need the user's account. (3) VKI: press-release PDFs fetchable. (4) FK: static site, fetchable, but nothing to extract. (5) Reddit: unreachable for Claude's built-in search and fetch tools (reddit.com is refused for Anthropic's user agent), unauthenticated JSON returns 403; access needs a Reddit OAuth app under the Data API terms or a browser agent at human pace. No Reddit Answers API found ⚠ *(unverified)*. (6) Forums: forum.murator.pl returned 403 and elektroda.pl timed out for scripts; forumogrodnicze.info, forum.budujemydom.pl and forum.gazeta.pl were fetchable; use each forum's own search via a browser agent, because web search did not index trampoline threads. (7) Allegro and Ceneo reviews: browser agent or manual copy (Ceneo terms ban automation; Allegro uses bot protection). No MCP server or Claude skill for Polish forums or Pro-Test found. Setup effort: about 1 hour for a browser-agent recipe per forum.

**protocol support**

None.

**open source and licence**

closed (all sources are proprietary websites or publications).

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Pro-Test and test.de: a paid account for full results (the user pays and reads; no payment data to an agent). Reddit Answers: a Reddit account with a supported default language ⚠ *(unverified: whether logged-out use works)*. Forums: optional accounts to post. GDPR exposure is low; do not post personal data when asking forums.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Medium. Paid test results are copyrighted: keep them in content/_raw, publish only conclusions. Reddit restricts automated access to its Data API terms and has taken legal action against unauthorised scraping, including a 2025 suit against Anthropic ⚠ *(unverified: not re-opened)*. Forum terms generally prohibit bulk copying ⚠ *(unverified)*. Ceneo terms ban automated access (see Ceneo item). Low risk for manual reading and occasional browser-agent use at human pace.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Pro-Test: paid access, state grants (NIW PROO 2026) and a paid service letting producers use test results in advertising ('Reklama z wykorzystaniem testow'); it says it carries no ads. The licensing creates an incentive around good grades but happens after publication. Stiftung Warentest and VKI: sales and subscriptions, no ads. The main bias risk in Polish search: affiliate 'ranking' sites (videotesty.pl, prorankingi.pl which discloses commissions, zestawienie.pl) and retailer buying guides (Decathlon, Castorama, OBI, Media Expert) dominate results for 'trampolina ogrodowa jaka wybrac' and can be mistaken for tests. Reddit Answers: search not yet monetised as of February 2026 (TechCrunch); ads appear in the Reddit feed.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

Lab tests: high for Stiftung Warentest (weights published: jumping 35%, safety 25%, handling 25%, workmanship 10%, pollutants 5%); Pro-Test publishes results but keeps lab names secret. Affiliate rankings: low. Reddit Answers: shows source threads ⚠ *(unverified)*. Forums: none.

**run to run consistency**

N/A for tests and forums. Reddit Answers: no evidence found on repeatability.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Forums and Reddit: open to astroturfing and seeded posts; Reddit Answers summarises user content, so a planted thread can steer an answer ⚠ *(unverified: no study found)*. Name-alike domains are a trap: swiatkonsumenta.pl, once associated with consumer journalism, now hosts payday-loan rankings. Paid-review firms fined by UOKiK posted on Polish review sites. Lab tests resist manipulation best (anonymous purchase, published criteria).

**known failures**

(1) FK is often cited as a test source, but it publishes no current tests; its joint site test-konsumencki.pl is dead. (2) No Polish lab test of trampolines; Pro-Test covers mostly appliances, electronics, food and cosmetics. (3) German tests may cover models or variant codes not sold in Poland, and are 18 months old. (4) Search engines do not surface Polish forum threads for durables; six Polish queries on 2026-10-15 returned only shops and affiliate pages. (5) Reddit Answers does not support Polish and Polish-language Reddit content is thin. (6) Some forums block scripts (Murator 403) or did not respond (Elektroda). (7) Owner reviews skew to the first weeks after purchase; durability problems (rust, net UV damage) appear after one or two seasons.

**regulatory enforcement history**

None found against Pro-Test, FK or the forums. Related: UOKiK soft intervention against Ceneo and Opineo (2021) over hidden negative reviews; UOKiK fines for review sellers 2022 and 2024; charges against Nocowanie.pl in June 2026 over unverified reviews (search summaries).

**⚠ buyer protection path**

N/A - information sources only. FK provides free consumer legal advice (complaints, statutory warranty, withdrawal) through its advice offices and helpline, which is useful after a failed purchase ⚠ *(unverified: helpline number not re-checked)*.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Mixed. For the trampoline: buy the Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 table (EUR 4.90) or read VKI, then check which tested model codes are sold in Poland on Ceneo or Allegro (e.g. the round Salta Premium Black Edition 305 and the Hudora Fantastic models; Polish availability of the exact tested codes was not verified); use Allegro and Ceneo verified reviews plus forumogrodnicze.info or forum.murator.pl searches for one-to-two-season durability (rust, net, springs); skip Pro-Test and FK for this category. For appliances and electronics (TVs, robot vacuums, air fryers, coffee machines, kettles): Pro-Test is the best Polish-language independent source, PLN 16.99 per test. Reddit Answers can be used in English for r/BuyItForLife-style durability questions about international brands (Berg, Vuly, Springfree) but not for Polish shops or Polish-only brands.

**workflow role**

Independent tests and owner experience (durability, after-sales). Combine with: price tools (Ceneo, Skapiec, idealo), the EN 71-14 / Certipedia check, the Safety Gate / UOKiK register and a review-analysis skill for Allegro and Ceneo reviews.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Trampoline: EUR 4.90 (test.de) + about 30 minutes reading and matching model codes + 15-30 minutes of forum and review searches = about EUR 5 and under 1 hour. Appliance or TV: PLN 16.99 per Pro-Test article or PLN 139 per year if more than 8 tests a year are needed (139 / 16.99 = 8.2). Reddit Answers: free, minutes, English only.

**evidence trail**

Save: test name, publisher, publication date and URL (e.g. test.de 'Trampoline im Test', 2025-04-22), tested model codes, grade and price at test time (paid data in content/_raw only); Pro-Test article URL and date; forum thread URLs with post dates and short paraphrases; Reddit Answers question, date and linked thread URLs. Publish only conclusions in the public vault.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Pro-Test gives Polish-language ICRT lab tests with dated, current 2025-2026 coverage of appliances and electronics at PLN 16.99 per test
  - Stiftung Warentest and VKI tested 11 and 10 garden trampolines in 2025 with published criteria and named model codes, several sold in Poland
  - Purchase-linked Polish reviews (Ceneo Zaufane Opinie, Allegro buyer-only reviews) and active garden and building forums cover long-term durability
  - Reddit Answers adds a free English AI summary of global owner experience
- **weaknesses**:
  - FK publishes no current tests and its former test site is dead
  - No Polish lab test of trampolines; German tests are 18 months old
  - Polish forum threads are hard to find via search and some forums block scripts
  - Reddit Answers does not support Polish and Reddit blocks Claude's built-in fetch tools
  - Affiliate ranking sites dominate Polish search results and imitate tests

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of Pro-Test's methods was found; its credibility rests on ICRT membership (listed by ICRT's Wikipedia page and stated by Pro-Test in August 2026) and the shared ICRT protocols. Stiftung Warentest and VKI results agree on the trampoline field: most 3 m models are good, one Kettler model failed, and safety outcomes depend on net placement and build quality. Coverage of Reddit Answers is press reporting (TechCrunch, Clubic, retail-news.de), not tests of answer quality. Affiliate ranking sites (prorankingi.pl discloses commissions) are not independent.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW for Pro-Test (appliances and electronics) and for Stiftung Warentest / VKI (trampoline); CONTEXT ONLY for forums and Allegro/Ceneo reviews as durability evidence; WATCH Reddit Answers; SKIP Federacja Konsumentow as a test source. Deciding fact: Pro-Test, not FK, is the Polish ICRT member with current tests, and the only trampoline lab tests are German. Best use: in the buying skill, look up the latest ICRT-family test for the category first (Pro-Test, then test.de or VKI), map tested model codes to Polish listings, then add a durability pass over verified Polish reviews and one forum search.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- FK and tests: the outline note and older sources (Wikipedia PL last edited 2018, e-prawnik.pl on test-konsumencki.pl) describe FK as doing product testing; on 2026-10-15 FK's site shows no tests and its joint test site is dead.
- Polish ICRT member: some 2009 sources describe FK and Pro-Test as partners in EU-funded testing; current evidence (ICRT list, Pro-Test post 2026-08-07) shows Pro-Test alone as the ICRT member.
- Reddit Answers scale: 'more than 6 million users' (Huffman, August 2025, cited by TechCrunch 2025-10-16) vs '15 million weekly actives in Q4 2025' (TechCrunch 2026-02-05) - different periods and metrics.
- Reddit Answers model: TechCrunch (2025-04-09 headline) says it uses Google Gemini; the 2025-10-16 article body only says 'a Google AI model'.
- Trampoline test counts: Stiftung Warentest tested 11 models (EUR 219-695) and VKI reported 10 (EUR 269-695) from the same joint programme; the price floors differ, so the German set apparently included one model not in the Austrian set ⚠ *(unverified: which model was not checked)*. VKI calls the Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition the cheapest model in its set.
- Allegro review eligibility: tabletowo reports buyer-only reviews limited to active buyers; an Allegro forum user reports repeated reviews by the same accounts on one product (anecdotal).

### Fake-review checkers

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY (PILOT a review step in a skill) · **Cost:** Free, Amazon-only · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

A family of review-authenticity checkers for Amazon listings. Status on 2026-10-15: Fakespot (Mozilla) and the Firefox Review Checker built on it are discontinued; ReviewMeta (statistical adjusted rating) is not serving its app; three small AI-based successors are live and free: RateBud (ratebud.ai, trust score 0-100 and grade A-F), Null Fake (nullfake.com, grade A-F, fake percentage, adjusted rating) and FakeFind (fakefind.ai, trust score 1-10, adjusted rating). All three take an Amazon product URL only. None covers Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl. The realistic replacement for Polish platforms is an LLM-plus-statistics review analysis inside a Claude skill fed with reviews collected by the user or a browser agent. Role type: AI assistant / web tool (and, for the replacement, skill).

**vendor and ownership**

Fakespot: Fakespot Inc. (US), acquired by Mozilla in 2023. ReviewMeta: US one-person project founded 2015; founder sought a successor in a post dated 2021-01-11 and no visible successor took over (Nova Analytics directory page, a vendor source). RateBud: operator not named anywhere on the site; contact support@ratebud.ai; terms governed by US law with AAA arbitration. Null Fake: Shift8 Web (web agency, Toronto, Canada); a public MIT-licensed repo exists (alanwynn/nullfake). FakeFind: built by an individual, Andrew Kane, per its about page; no company or country named; site links to an 'immatrix-labs' hosting domain. None is owned by a marketplace; FakeFind and Null Fake earn Amazon affiliate commission.

**lifecycle status**

Fakespot: discontinued 2025-07-01 (website, apps, extensions); Firefox Review Checker discontinued 2025-06-10; announced in Mozilla's blog 2025-05-22, which fakespot.com now redirects to (verified 2026-10-15). ReviewMeta: not working. On 2026-10-15 reviewmeta.com, /blog/ and product URLs returned HTTP 403 with a raw Kubernetes API error body ('system:anonymous cannot get path /') behind Cloudflare, i.e. the domain no longer serves the application; Nova Analytics reported a server error on 2026-09-03; FakeFind says it went offline in early 2026; Protegez-Vous (July 2025) found it working intermittently. RateBud: live; llms-full.md 'Last Updated September 2026', terms updated 2026-10-02; Firefox add-on created 2025-07-22, last updated 2025-11-29. Null Fake: live and active; product sitemap entries last modified 2026-10-15; Chrome extension v2.9.84 updated 2026-10-09; public GitHub repo last pushed 2025-06-12 (stale relative to the live service). FakeFind: live; Chrome extension v1.0.3 last updated 2026-02-27. All three successors launched in mid-2025 after the Fakespot announcement. Verified 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

All three live tools are free with no sign-up (vendor-stated, seen 2026-10-15). RateBud: 'completely free', no tiers. Null Fake: free, no daily limits, no premium tiers per homepage, but its Chrome Web Store listing says 'Offers in-app purchases' and the extension asks for an API key from nullfake.com ⚠ *(unverified)*. FakeFind: free, funded by Amazon affiliate links. The replacement skill costs LLM tokens only: roughly 10-30k input tokens for 100-300 short reviews plus metadata per product ⚠ *(unverified: estimate, not measured)*.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Amazon.pl only. RateBud lists amazon.pl among 20 supported Amazon domains (llms.txt). Null Fake has 5 public amazon.pl analyses (sitemap, 2026-10-15), e.g. Bose SoundLink Flex 2 analysed 2026-09-24 with Polish reviews. FakeFind does not list domains. No tool supports Allegro, Ceneo, Allegro Lokalnie, OLX, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl.
- **EU**: Amazon EU stores only: RateBud lists amazon.de, .fr, .it, .es, .nl, .se and .pl; Null Fake has 774 amazon.de, 125 .fr, 57 .es, 56 .it, 34 .nl, 6 .se analyses. No support for idealo, Otto, bol.com, Zalando or eMAG found.
- **US**: Primary market for all three (Null Fake: 6,034 of 8,962 public analyses are amazon.com). Fakespot also covered US retailers such as Walmart and Best Buy before closing ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **language**: Interfaces in English. The underlying LLMs read non-English reviews: the Null Fake amazon.pl page analysed Polish and Spanish reviews and rendered parts of the page in Polish.
- **US only or agentic features**: No agentic or purchase features. Browser extensions for Chrome and Firefox show scores on Amazon pages.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

None. Analyses are per ASIN; they do not merge variants or detect review hijacking across variants explicitly, although FakeFind lists 'review hijacking' as a detected pattern (vendor-claimed). A Polish skill replacement should group reviews by EAN or model code because Allegro and Ceneo cards can merge or split variants.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A - no price comparison. FakeFind and Null Fake link to Amazon with affiliate tags.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A - none of these tools tracks prices.

**total landed cost**

N/A.

**review and seller verification**

Review authenticity: partial, Amazon only. Methods (vendor-described): RateBud combines reviewer behaviour, review velocity spikes, language patterns, verified-purchase ratio and rating distribution (missing middle ratings, excess 5-star) into a 0-100 score; Null Fake uses GPT-4 as the primary model with DeepSeek cross-checks and statistical checks, flags reviews scoring at least 70 as likely fake and grades by fake share (A 0-10%, B 11-25%, C 26-40%, D 41-60%, F 61%+), analysing a sample for large products; FakeFind uses timing patterns, linguistic fingerprints and behavioural anomalies. None publishes an accuracy benchmark; RateBud says so explicitly. Seller verification: none (no seller identity, VAT or KRS checks). What they cannot prove: that a review is fake (only probabilistic flags), anything about Allegro or Ceneo, incentivised reviews from real buyers, or that the sample reflects all reviews. Research caveat: in arXiv 2506.13313 (June 2025) humans scored 50.8% when separating real from AI-written product reviews and seven LLMs did about as poorly, so text-only LLM judgement is weak; structural signals matter more.

**safety and compliance checks**

None.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - these tools do not surface lab tests. Independent evaluation of the tools themselves: Protegez-Vous (Canada, July 2025) tried post-Fakespot alternatives and reported ReviewMeta intermittent and The Review Index broken (article returned 403 to this session; search summary only). No benchmarked comparison of RateBud, Null Fake and FakeFind found.

**alerts and monitoring**

None. Null Fake re-analyses cached products older than 30 days on demand (open-source README); RateBud caches 24 h (Redis TTL per llms-full.md) and shows the analysis date with a re-run button. No alerts.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No purchasing. Not applicable.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Amazon public review pages. Null Fake's open-source version fetched reviews through the third-party Unwrangle API and stored them with the OpenAI result; the live methodology page says it collects publicly visible review data (text, rating, date, helpful votes, display name, verified status). RateBud: 'extracts product data and reviews' (method not named), Redis cache with 24 h TTL. FakeFind: not described. Each result has a permanent public URL with the analysis date (e.g. nullfake.com/amazon/pl/<ASIN>/<slug>, ratebud.ai/product/<ASIN>/<slug>), usable as a citation. Amazon page-layout changes break extraction (Shift8 blog).

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. (1) RateBud: llms.txt advertises POST https://www.ratebud.ai/api/analyze with body {url}, but robots.txt disallows /api/* and terms section 3.2 forbid automated scraping or bulk analysis without permission, so use only with permission or one request at human pace. Public product pages are crawlable and allowed for AI crawlers including ClaudeBot. (2) Null Fake: no documented public API; the extension uses an API key from nullfake.com; robots.txt allows all crawlers; existing analyses are readable at stable URLs and listed in sitemap-products.xml (8,962 entries), so an agent can check whether an ASIN was already analysed without submitting anything. Self-hosting: the MIT repo alanwynn/nullfake (PHP/Laravel 12, needs OpenAI and Unwrangle keys; 1 star, 8 forks, last push 2025-06-12). (3) FakeFind: no API; web form plus Chrome extension (773 users, rating 1.3 from 3). (4) MCP: crawde/reviewradar-mcp (MCP server for a 'ReviewRadar' service; 0 stars, last push 2026-04-16, no licence) is the only fake-review MCP found; not evaluated. (5) Claude skill: nexscope-ai/eCommerce-Skills 'amazon-review-checker' SKILL.md (MIT, repo 1,156 stars, last push 2026-08-26) analyses pasted reviews offline with weighted heuristics (time clustering 25%, content similarity 20%, rating distribution chi-square 20%, verified-purchase ratio 15%, length 5%, keywords 5%) and needs no API key; it is platform-agnostic if fed Allegro or Ceneo reviews as JSON. (6) Replacement design for Poland: browser agent or manual export collects reviews from Allegro or Ceneo (text, stars, date, verified flag or 'Zaufana Opinia' badge, variant), then the skill computes structural signals and asks the LLM only to cluster complaints (rust, net tears, missing parts) and flag templated text. Setup effort: about 0.5-1 day to adapt the nexscope skill plus a collector.

**protocol support**

None (no ACP, UCP, AP2 or MCP from the vendors).

**open source and licence**

Fakespot: closed (discontinued). ReviewMeta: closed. RateBud: closed. Null Fake: live service closed; an older version is public under MIT at github.com/alanwynn/nullfake (README credits Shift8 Web; last push 2025-06-12; 1 star). FakeFind: closed. Replacement skill: nexscope-ai/eCommerce-Skills, MIT.

**account linking and data access**

None: no account or payment data. Browser extensions read Amazon pages you visit; RateBud claims no data collection and no tracking, but its own architecture notes list Vercel Analytics. Analyses become public pages on all three sites, so a product you check is published. GDPR: low exposure; avoid submitting URLs that contain personal tracking parameters. A self-built skill keeps all data local.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Medium. Amazon's conditions of use prohibit scraping, so collection by these tools or a self-hosted Null Fake relies on third-party scrapers (Unwrangle) ⚠ *(unverified: Amazon terms not re-opened)*. RateBud's terms prohibit bulk or automated analysis without permission. For Polish platforms: Allegro uses DataDome bot protection and its terms restrict automated collection; Ceneo's terms (section 14.7) ban automated access and carry a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per copying violation (see Ceneo item). Manual or low-rate browser-agent collection for personal research is the low-risk route; do not republish review texts in the public vault.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

FakeFind: Amazon affiliate links shown with results (about page). Null Fake: Amazon Associates tag (e.g. nullfakeus-20) and an affiliate disclosure on the amazon.com trampoline analysis; the amazon.pl page showed a plain link. RateBud: no affiliate disclosure in terms; revenue model not stated. Bias vector: affiliate income rewards sending users to Amazon after a 'B' grade; grades skew mild (both sampled Null Fake pages were B with -0.28 rating adjustment). Marketing pages position each tool as 'the Fakespot alternative' and publish comparison pages against rivals.

**ranking transparency**

Partial. RateBud and Null Fake publish grade bands and signal lists; Null Fake pages give a plain-language explanation and quote suspicious reviews; no weights or accuracy figures. No option to exclude a signal or re-run with different settings except RateBud's re-run button.

**run to run consistency**

No evidence. Null Fake caches a result for up to 30 days and RateBud for 24 h, so repeated queries return the cached grade; an LLM re-run may differ. Two Null Fake samples on 2026-10-15 both showed grade B with an adjusted rating 0.28 below Amazon's.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Weak by design for LLM-based tools: review text is untrusted input fed to GPT-4 or other models, so a seeded review containing instructions could bias the explanation ⚠ *(unverified: no test found)*. The arXiv 2506.13313 result (humans 50.8%, LLMs similar) shows AI-written fakes evade text judgement. Safeguards claimed: statistical checks alongside the LLM (Null Fake, RateBud). For a self-built skill, treat review text as data, never instructions, and weight structural signals (verified-purchase share, burst timing, distribution) above text verdicts.

**known failures**

(1) Lifecycle churn: Fakespot and Review Checker closed in 2025; ReviewMeta dead by 2026; The Review Index reported broken in 2025. (2) Amazon-only coverage; no Polish marketplace. (3) No published accuracy for any surviving tool. (4) Small and young user bases: Null Fake Chrome 1,000 users (3.9 from 25 ratings), Firefox 151 users; RateBud Firefox 693 users (4.0 from 3); FakeFind Chrome 773 users (1.3 from 3). (5) Inconsistent coverage claims (Null Fake '14+ countries' vs 21 listed; open repo says 'Amazon (US)'). (6) Sampling on large listings and Amazon layout changes break extraction. (7) Operators of RateBud and FakeFind are not identified as legal entities.

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

None against these tools found. Context that shapes their usefulness: EU Omnibus Directive (2019/2161) requires traders who show reviews to state whether and how they verify them, in force in Poland since 2023-01-01; UOKiK fined review sellers Opinie.pro (PLN 40,000) and SN Marketing (PLN 30,000) in November 2022 and Best-Review (PLN 35,000) and SeoSem24 (PLN 50,618) in July 2024, and charged Nocowanie.pl in June 2026 over unverified reviews (search summaries). In the US the FTC rule on consumer reviews and testimonials took effect 2024-10-21 ⚠ *(unverified: not re-opened)*.

**buyer protection path**

N/A - information tools; protection depends on where the purchase is made (Amazon A-to-z, Allegro Protect, statutory warranty).

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

Low for the Polish trampoline purchase. Useful only if the candidate is sold on Amazon.de or Amazon.pl: e.g. check whether nullfake.com already has an analysis of the ASIN (774 amazon.de analyses exist; trampoline analyses exist for amazon.com), or run RateBud once. For Allegro and Ceneo listings, which dominate the Polish trampoline market, they do nothing. A trampoline buyer's real questions (rust after a season, net tearing, missing parts, spare springs) are better answered by clustering verified owner reviews than by a fake-share score; the replacement skill should do that. Note that Allegro product reviews come only from buyers (reportedly buyers active in the last 12 months ⚠ *(unverified)*) and Ceneo marks purchase-verified 'Zaufane Opinie', so the Polish problem is less fake text than incentivised, selective or merged-variant reviews.

**workflow role**

Review sanity check within the verification step, Amazon EU candidates only. Combine with: lab tests (Stiftung Warentest, VKI, Pro-Test), Allegro and Ceneo verified-review clustering in a skill, and seller checks.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Hosted tools: free, about 1-2 minutes per Amazon ASIN; checking the Null Fake sitemap for an existing analysis costs one HTTP request. Replacement skill: collecting 100-300 reviews per product by browser agent or manual copy takes 5-15 minutes; analysis about 10-30k tokens per product ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*. Arithmetic for comparing 3 trampolines across Allegro and Ceneo: 3 x (2 platforms x ~100 reviews) = ~600 reviews, roughly 40-90k tokens in total ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*.

**evidence trail**

Hosted tools give a public, dated URL per ASIN (grade, fake %, adjusted rating, explanation), which can be cited in a vault note with the access date; save a screenshot because cached results are overwritten on re-run. A skill run can save the raw review sample (in content/_raw only), the computed signals table, the clustered complaints with counts, and the final verdict with links to the source listing.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Free, no account, results in seconds, with permanent public result URLs that work as citations
  - RateBud and Null Fake cover amazon.de and amazon.pl, the EU Amazon stores a Polish buyer uses
  - Null Fake explains its grade and quotes suspicious reviews; RateBud publishes grade bands and admits it has no benchmark
  - An MIT-licensed skill (nexscope amazon-review-checker) and an MIT Null Fake codebase give a starting point for a self-hosted, platform-agnostic replacement
- **weaknesses**:
  - Amazon-only; nothing for Allegro, Ceneo or other Polish shops
  - No published accuracy for any tool; LLM text judgement is near chance on AI-written fakes (arXiv 2506.13313)
  - High lifecycle risk: Fakespot and ReviewMeta died within about a year; successors are tiny (hundreds to about a thousand extension users) and partly anonymous
  - Affiliate monetisation (FakeFind, Null Fake) and mild grade distribution
  - Automation is restricted by RateBud terms and Amazon terms

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test of RateBud, Null Fake or FakeFind with a published method was found. Coverage is dominated by the tools' own 'Fakespot alternative' pages, vendor directories (Nova Analytics, Shulex, AlternativeTo listings) and affiliate roundups. Consumer journalism (Protegez-Vous, July 2025) and Mozilla's own post agree on the Fakespot shutdown dates and that the replacements are rough signals. Academic work (Meng et al., arXiv 2506.13313, June 2025) indicates that neither humans nor current LLMs reliably spot AI-written reviews.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY for the hosted checkers; PILOT the replacement skill. Deciding fact: all surviving checkers are Amazon-only and unbenchmarked, while the Polish market runs on Allegro and Ceneo. Best use: build a small review-analysis step in the buying skill (adapt nexscope amazon-review-checker, feed it Allegro and Ceneo reviews, weight structural signals, use the LLM to cluster durability complaints) and use RateBud or an existing Null Fake page only for Amazon.de or Amazon.pl candidates.

**conflicting evidence**

- ReviewMeta shutdown date: FakeFind says it went offline in early 2026; Nova Analytics says a server error on 2026-09-03 and that the exact month cannot be verified; Protegez-Vous found it intermittent in July 2025; on 2026-10-15 the domain returned a Kubernetes API 403 body.
- Fakespot date: Mozilla's blog (2025-05-22) gives shutdown 2025-07-01 and Review Checker 2025-06-10; Nova Analytics says Fakespot 'shut down in May 2025', conflating announcement and shutdown.
- Null Fake pricing: homepage says free with no premium tiers; Chrome Web Store listing says 'Offers in-app purchases' and the extension asks for an API key.
- Null Fake coverage: homepage claims '14+ countries' and elsewhere '10+ other countries' while listing 21 Amazon stores; the public repo says 'Amazon (US)'; the live sitemap shows analyses in 17 country stores.
- RateBud API: llms.txt advertises POST /api/analyze for AI use; robots.txt disallows /api/* and terms 3.2 forbid automated or bulk analysis without permission.
- RateBud privacy: claims no data collection and no tracking, while its architecture section lists Vercel Analytics.
- RateBud rating: homepage cites a 4.9 extension rating; Firefox AMO shows 4.0 from 3 ratings (2026-10-15).
