### EN 71-14, GS mark and Certipedia

**Verdict:** USE NOW · **Cost:** Free checks; standard text paid · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 8 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Not a product but a verification checklist for safety claims on domestic trampolines and similar toys. Components: (1) EN 71-14 'Safety of toys - Part 14: Trampolines for domestic use', current CEN edition EN 71-14:2025 (Polish adoption PN-EN 71-14:2026-03, English text only), harmonised edition still EN 71-14:2018; (2) the German voluntary GS mark ('Gepruefte Sicherheit') under the Produktsicherheitsgesetz (ProdSG 2021, sections 20-22), issued by authorised GS bodies such as TUV Rheinland, TUV SUD or Intertek; (3) TUV Rheinland Certipedia (certipedia.com), the public certificate database where a test-mark ID or QR code resolves to the certificate holder, model numbers, standards and issue date. Role type: regulation / standard plus registry. An agent can apply most checks automatically; the standard text itself is paywalled.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

EN 71-14: CEN technical committee CEN/TC 52 (Safety of toys) ⚠ *(unverified: TC number not re-opened)*, national adoption in Poland by PKN technical committee KT 237 (Artykulow dla Niemowlat i Malych Dzieci oraz Bezpieczenstwa Zabawek) per the PKN product page. Legal basis: Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC (harmonised-standard citations in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/740 and amendments 2025/1785, 2025/2519 and 2026/2032), to be replaced by Toy Safety Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 from 2030-08-01. GS mark: German federal law (ProdSG 2021); GS bodies are authorised by the ZLS (Zentralstelle der Laender fuer Sicherheitstechnik, Munich) and listed by BAuA (Bundesanstalt fuer Arbeitsschutz und Arbeitsmedizin), which also publishes GS-mark misuse cases. Certipedia: TUV Rheinland AG (Cologne, Germany), a commercial testing and certification company; entries exist because manufacturers pay TUV Rheinland for certification, so Certipedia only covers TUV Rheinland certificates.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

EN 71-14:2025: approved by CEN 2025-09-22 ⚠ *(unverified: from SGS summary)* and published 2025-10-29; supersedes EN 71-14:2018 (STC notice, 2025-11-06). CEN dates: announcement 2026-01-31, national publication 2026-04-30, withdrawal of conflicting national standards 2026-10-31. Poland: PN-EN 71-14:2026-03 published 2026-03-31 (English version, 47 pages); PN-EN 71-14:2019-03 withdrawn 2026-03-31 but flagged by PKN as 'aktualna w ocenie zgodnosci' (current for conformity assessment) until 2026-10-31. Germany: DIN EN 71-14:2025-12. Harmonisation: NOT cited in the Official Journal as of the EC summary list generated 2026-09-14; the latest amendment, Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2032 (OJ 2026-09-14), added EN 71-4:2020+A1:2025, EN 71-15:2025 and EN 71-16:2025 only. The cited trampoline standard remains EN 71-14:2018 (OJ L 195, Decision 2019/1254, presumption from 2019-07-23, no end date). Toy Safety Regulation (EU) 2025/2509: published OJ 2025-12-12, applies from 2030-08-01, introduces a digital product passport per toy model. GS mark regime: ProdSG 2021 in force. Certipedia: live and current on 2026-10-15 (newest trampoline-related certificate seen issued 2026-07-06). Verified 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

Checking is free: Certipedia lookups, the EC summary list (XLSX), ProdSG text, BAuA misuse database and the TUV Rheinland Warning List cost nothing. The standard text is paid: PKN PN-EN 71-14:2026-03 costs PLN 249.60 net / PLN 307.01 gross (file or paper, English), or PLN 32.10 for a 30-minute reading-room session (PKN shop, seen 2026-10-15). For a manufacturer, GS certification and annual surveillance are paid services priced per project ⚠ *(unverified: no public price list)*. For the buyer, the indirect cost is a premium for GS-certified models; no figure found.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Toy rules (Directive 2009/48/EC, CE marking) and GPSR (EU) 2023/988 apply. PN-EN 71-14:2026-03 is available from PKN in English only. GS is a German voluntary mark but appears on trampolines sold in Poland (e.g. Salta, Hudora). Certipedia has a Polish interface option. Product-safety enforcement is UOKiK and Inspekcja Handlowa (see the separate Safety Gate / UOKiK item).
- **EU**: Same EU law. EN 71-14:2018 is the harmonised reference across the EU as of 2026-09-14; national adoptions of the 2025 edition exist (DIN EN 71-14:2025-12, STN EN 71-14 March 2026, EVS-EN 71-14:2025 valid from 2025-11-17 per search summary). GS is recognised mainly in Germany and Austria as a consumer signal.
- **US**: EN 71-14 and GS are not the US references; US trampoline standards are ASTM F381 (components) and ASTM F2225 (enclosures) ⚠ *(unverified: not re-opened)*. Certipedia is global.
- **language**: Standards: English (PKN), German (DIN). Certipedia UI: Chinese, English, German, Polish, Spanish. Certificate texts are in English.
- **US only or agentic features**: None. No agentic features; these are reference checks.

#### capabilities

**⚠ spec and variant comparison**

Useful for variant control, which is central to 'choosing the best version'. A GS certificate on Certipedia lists the exact model designations it covers. Worked example (2026-10-15): Salta B.V. holds one TUV Rheinland product attestation, GS-Mark Approval S 50702520 (test-mark ID 1111309398, issued 2026-07-06) for 'Sports Toy (Toy Trampoline)' models 5201 to 5209. The Salta Premium Black 214x305 cm rectangular trampoline listed on Ceneo as model 5362 is not among those model numbers, so a 'TUV/GS' claim for model 5362 cannot be verified on Certipedia and must be asked of the seller or Salta. The round Salta Premium Black Edition 305 tested by Stiftung Warentest in 05/2025 is a different product whose model code was not checked against the certificate ⚠ *(unverified)*. The same logic catches retailer-exclusive variants and rebadges: the certificate covers listed model codes only, and TUV Rheinland states that the award expires automatically if the tested product changes. Certipedia also shows that many EU brands source GS-certified trampolines from Chinese OEMs (e.g. Jiangsu Baoxiang, Anhui Qidi, Suzhou HighTen as certificate holders), which helps spot white-label families.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A - a standards and certificate check, not a price tool.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A - no price data.

**total landed cost**

N/A - no cost computation. Indirect relevance: a model outside a valid certificate may face recall or withdrawal costs later (see UOKiK decision practice in the Safety Gate item).

**review and seller verification**

None for reviews. Partial for the manufacturer: a Certipedia certificate names the certificate holder and its postal address (e.g. Salta B.V., Galvanistraat 36, 7651 DH Tubbergen, Netherlands), which can be compared with the manufacturer or EU responsible person shown on the listing under GPSR Article 19. It cannot verify the Polish seller.

**⚠ safety and compliance checks**

This item IS the check. Agent checklist (each step marked auto = an agent can do it from public data, manual = needs the seller or a paid text): (1) Scope, auto: is the product a toy trampoline for domestic use (EN 71-14) and not a fitness or gymnastic trampoline (EN 13219), inflatable (EN ISO 25649), public-playground equipment (EN 1176) or inclined mat? The 2026 PKN scope text also excludes trampolines with added functions such as tents or basketball hoops. (2) CE marking present, auto from photos and listing. CE on toys is normally the manufacturer's own declaration when harmonised standards are applied ⚠ *(unverified: legal reading, Directive 2009/48/EC Article 19 not re-opened)*. (3) Claimed standard edition, auto: EN 71-14:2018 = currently harmonised, acceptable; EN 71-14:2025 = current CEN state of the art, acceptable but not OJ-cited as of 2026-09-14; EN 71-14:2014 (presumption ended 2019-02-28) or EN 71-14:2014+A1:2017 (ended 2020-01-22) = red flag for an outdated test report; plain 'EN 71' without part 14 = incomplete claim; also expect EN 71-1, EN 71-2 and EN 71-3 on toy certificates. (4) GS or TUV mark, auto: read the 10-digit ID under the mark (TUV Rheinland IDs seen: 1111xxxxxx and 1419xxxxxx), open certipedia.com/quality_marks/<ID>, confirm holder, product type, exact model number, standards and issue date; the award is valid for at most 5 years from issue (ProdSG section 20(5)) and ends on any product change; surveillance is 'regular' by law (section 22(4)) and 'usually annual' per TUV Rheinland. For other GS bodies use their own published certificate lists (ProdSG section 22(1) obliges every GS body to publish one; TUV SUD runs a Product Service certificate explorer). (5) Misuse lists, auto: BAuA GS-mark misuse database (176 entries in a cached listing, newest cached entries from 2022 ⚠ *(unverified)*) and the TUV Rheinland Warning List (about 210 undated entries, no trampolines, several toys; counted 2026-10-15). (6) GPSR Article 19 listing fields, auto: manufacturer name, postal and electronic address; EU responsible person if the manufacturer is outside the EU; picture, type and model identifier; warnings and safety information in Polish, visible before purchase. (7) Warnings, manual from photos or manual: one user at a time, maximum user mass, minimum age, assembly and anchoring, supervision, and for activity toys the domestic-use warning of the Toy Safety Directive ⚠ *(unverified: Annex V Part B wording not re-opened)*; the 2025 edition updated warnings, markings and instructions (details paywalled). (8) Safety Gate and UOKiK register search for the brand and model, auto (separate item). (9) Independent lab cross-check, semi-auto: Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 tested 11 trampolines against DIN EN 71-14:2019-03 plus a German GS test principle (entrapment, mat load at 5 times maximum user mass, stability, net attachment under dynamic load, 400 h UV, 48 h salt spray). What it cannot prove: that the unit shipped matches the certified type, that a certificate was not withdrawn after the Certipedia snapshot, or anything about a mark from a body without a public database.

**independent test coverage**

Stiftung Warentest 'Trampoline im Test' published 2025-04-22 (test 05/2025): 11 round steel-spring garden trampolines about 3 m in diameter, EUR 219-695, bought October 2024; 9 recommended (8 good, 1 very good), 1 rated 'mangelhaft'. Named models: Berg Favorit Regular 330, Decathlon Domyos 360 (8799832), Exit Elegant Premium, Exit Silhouette 305, Hudora Fantastic 300V (65731/01), Hudora Fantastic Complete Max 300 (65760), Kettler Jump 305, Lidl Crivit 305 cm (373605), Salta Comfort Edition 305, Salta Premium Black Edition 305, Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition. Full grades cost EUR 4.90. VKI (Austria) published the joint test of 10 models on 2025-04-22 (KONSUMENT 05/2025): Kettler Jump 305 failed (frame tubes did not fit, heavy rust after salt spray, raised PAH in places), Zero Gravity Ultima 4 Black Edition only average because a leg deformed under a 120 kg sandbag test. Both tests are about 18 months old relative to 2026-10-15 but the models are still sold. Several of these brands are sold in Poland (Berg, Hudora, Salta, Exit, Decathlon). No Polish lab test of trampolines found (see the pl-community-sources item). Certipedia and the standard do not surface these tests.

**alerts and monitoring**

None built in. Certipedia has no watch or alert function found. An agent can re-check a Certipedia ID page and the EC harmonised-standards summary XLSX on a schedule (e.g. monthly) to detect certificate removal or OJ citation of EN 71-14:2025.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A - no purchasing. This is a pre-purchase gate: the purchase workflow should block or flag a candidate that fails steps 3, 4 or 6 of the checklist until a human confirms.

**after sales and resale**

Indirect: the certificate holder address and GPSR responsible person give the warranty and spare-parts contact. VKI gives component lifetimes useful for spares planning: frame 5-10 years, mat 3-7, springs 3-6, net and padding 2-5. No resale data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

EC summary list of harmonised standards: XLSX regenerated per amendment ('Generated 14 September 2026'), the most practical machine-readable source; EUR-Lex is authoritative but blocked scripted access in this session. PKN shop: live catalogue with publication and withdrawal dates. Certipedia: TUV Rheinland's own database; the certificate page states the standards 'reflect the status at the time of the release of this certificate', so later standard changes are not reflected. BAuA misuse database: fed by GS bodies under ProdSG section 22(2); freshness unknown. Every answer is backed by a stable URL (certipedia.com/certificates/<number>, certipedia.com/quality_marks/<ID>).

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial (scriptable via plain HTTP, no official API or MCP). (1) Certipedia: no public API found. Direct pages /quality_marks/<ID>?locale=en, /certificates/<number>?locale=en and /companies/<id>/product_certificates are allowed by robots.txt and fetched fine with curl on 2026-10-15; the search endpoints (/search/matching_product_certificates and /search?) are disallowed in robots.txt and a Crawl-delay of 10 s is set, so an agent should look up by ID from the product label rather than crawl search results. (2) EC harmonised-standards XLSX: downloadable without authentication from single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu; parsed with Python zipfile in seconds. (3) EUR-Lex: returned an empty response to curl and WebFetch (WAF), so use the EC XLSX or a browser agent. (4) PKN shop: product pages fetchable; prices and status in HTML. (5) ProdSG: gesetze-im-internet.de fetchable. (6) BAuA: HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and curl in this session, needs a browser agent or manual check. (7) TUV SUD certificate explorer: not tested. MCP servers or Claude skills for certificate checking: none found. Setup effort: about 1-2 hours to write a small skill that takes model number and mark ID, fetches the Certipedia page, the EC XLSX and the listing, and emits a checklist table.

**protocol support**

None. Future relevance: the Toy Safety Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 digital product passport (QR or other data carrier on the toy, retained 10 years) will give agents a machine-readable compliance record from 2030; not usable yet.

**open source and licence**

closed (standards are copyrighted and sold by CEN members; Certipedia is a proprietary TUV Rheinland service; ProdSG and EU acts are public law texts).

**account linking and data access**

None needed for checks. Certipedia, the EC list and ProdSG need no account. Buying the standard from PKN needs a shop account and payment, which the user should do himself. Certipedia sets analytics cookies only with consent.

**automation legal risk**

Low if the agent respects robots.txt: Certipedia allows ID pages and disallows search pages with a 10 s crawl delay. The standard text is copyrighted; do not copy clauses into the public vault. EUR-Lex and BAuA actively block scripted clients, so use a browser agent at human pace or the EC XLSX.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

GS bodies and TUV Rheinland are paid by the manufacturers they certify, a structural conflict mitigated by state authorisation (ZLS) and the misuse and withdrawal rules in ProdSG section 22. Certipedia also markets 'your Certipedia entry' as a promotional tool for certificate holders, and optional modules (images, downloads) are promotional. Retail guides (e.g. Decathlon Poland) treat 'TUV and CE' as proof of rigorous testing, overstating CE on toys, which is usually self-declared ⚠ *(unverified: legal reading)*.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - no ranking. Transparency of the certificate itself is good: standards, issue date, model list and holder are shown; test reports and expiry dates are not.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - deterministic lookups, not an AI tool.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Known manipulation: fake or misused GS and TUV marks, manipulated certificates and advertising with invalid certificates are common enough that TUV Rheinland keeps a Warning List of about 210 cases and BAuA a misuse database; a 2017 Baden-Wuerttemberg market-surveillance release reported about 7 percent of checked GS products showed signs of improper use (old, regional figure). Safeguard: resolve the ID on the issuer's own domain, never through a link or QR code supplied by the seller (a QR code can point to a look-alike site). Certipedia pages are not an LLM surface, so prompt injection is not a concern there; seller listings that 'quote' certificates are.

**known failures**

(1) EN 71-14:2025 has not been cited in the OJ about 11 months after publication, so listings may cite either edition; neither is a red flag on its own. (2) Certipedia shows issue date but not an explicit expiry date; the 5-year maximum must be computed. (3) A certificate covers listed model codes only, while listings often use marketing names (e.g. 'Premium Black Edition') without the code. (4) Certipedia covers TUV Rheinland only; TUV SUD, Intertek, SGS or DEKRA marks need other lookups. (5) BAuA and EUR-Lex block scripted access. (6) The standard text is paywalled and English-only in Poland, so warning wording cannot be checked against the text without buying it. (7) Third-party summaries disagree on harmonisation timing (see conflicting_evidence).

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the standard itself. Related: UOKiK decision practice on toy trampolines that failed toy-safety requirements (e.g. 2016 decision on trampoline TX-T-16 16FT after a laboratory test, search summary only); covered in the Safety Gate / UOKiK item.

**buyer protection path**

Indirect. A product placed on the market without a valid basis for safety claims gives the buyer grounds under statutory warranty (rekojmia, non-conformity with the contract) and lets UOKiK act; a misused GS mark is an offence under ProdSG in Germany. Certificate evidence saved before purchase strengthens a complaint.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

High for the trampoline and other toys and GS-relevant goods (power tools, ladders, appliances where GS is common in Germany). For a round 3 m trampoline the agent can, in a few minutes: confirm the EN 71-14 edition claimed, resolve the GS ID on Certipedia, check the exact model code against the certificate (Salta 5201-5209 listed, Salta 5362 rectangular not listed), check GPSR fields and Polish warnings on the Allegro or Ceneo listing, search the misuse lists, and cross-check the Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 table. It cannot judge bounce quality, rust resistance or long-term net durability; lab tests and owner reviews cover those.

**workflow role**

Safety and compliance gate, after shortlisting and before seller and price checks. Combine with: Safety Gate and UOKiK registers, Stiftung Warentest or VKI tests, seller identity checks (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list) and GPSR listing review.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual: about 10-15 minutes per model, free. Scripted skill: a few HTTP requests (Certipedia ID page, EC XLSX, listing page) per model, seconds of runtime and negligible token cost; one-off build about 1-2 hours. Optional paid inputs: Stiftung Warentest unlock EUR 4.90; PKN standard PLN 307.01 gross only if the user wants to read the warnings clause.

**evidence trail**

Good. Save into the vault: date accessed; listing URL and screenshot of GPSR fields and mark; Certipedia quality-mark URL and certificate URL (e.g. certipedia.com/certificates/50702520?locale=en), certificate number, holder, model list, standards, issue date and computed latest expiry (issue + 5 years); EC summary list generation date and the EN 71-14 row; result of misuse-list searches; Stiftung Warentest test reference (test 05/2025, test.de URL). Keep paid test grades in content/_raw only.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Mostly automatable from free public sources: Certipedia ID pages, the EC harmonised-standards XLSX and ProdSG are fetchable without login
  - Certificates list exact model codes, holder address, standards and issue date, which catches wrong-variant and rebadge claims (Salta 5201-5209 certified, Salta 5362 not listed)
  - Clear legal anchors: GS award max 5 years and void on product change (ProdSG s.20(5)); GS bodies must publish certificate lists and report misuse (s.22)
  - Edition logic is simple and checkable: 2018 harmonised, 2025 current CEN, 2014 editions outdated
- **weaknesses**:
  - EN 71-14:2025 not yet OJ-cited (as of 2026-09-14), so edition claims are ambiguous during the transition
  - Certipedia covers only TUV Rheinland and shows no expiry date; other GS bodies need separate lookups
  - Standard text paywalled and English-only in Poland (PLN 307.01), so warning wording cannot be verified cheaply
  - BAuA and EUR-Lex block scripted access; misuse data freshness unknown
  - A valid certificate proves type conformity, not that the shipped unit matches

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of Certipedia's completeness was found. Testing-house notes (SGS SafeGuard 150/25, October 2025; STC notice 2025-11-06) agree that EN 71-14:2025 brings no major technical change versus 2018: structural removal of EN 71-1 exemptions, slightly revised pinching and crushing requirements focused on bystander access to springs, and updated warnings, markings and instructions. These are commercial testing firms (they sell testing), but they report the CEN content consistently. Stiftung Warentest and VKI used the 2018 edition (DIN EN 71-14:2019-03) as their safety baseline in 2025.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW - deciding fact: the GS/Certipedia model-code check and the EN 71-14 edition check run in minutes from free sources and catch the commonest false safety claims. Best use: make it a mandatory gate in the buying skill (inputs: listing URL, model code, mark ID; outputs: pass/flag table with saved URLs), run before price comparison.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- Harmonisation timing: SGS (October 2025) said EN 71-14:2025 is not harmonised and timing unknown; STC (2025-11-06) said OJ citation was 'expected shortly'; the EC summary list generated 2026-09-14 still cites only EN 71-14:2018.
- Validity of the 2018 edition: PKN marks PN-EN 71-14:2019-03 as current for conformity assessment only until 2026-10-31 (the CEN withdrawal date), while the OJ citation of EN 71-14:2018 has no end date, so presumption of conformity under EU law appears to continue until the Commission amends the list ⚠ *(unverified: legal interpretation)*.
- GS surveillance frequency: TUV Rheinland's certificate text says inspections 'usually take place on an annual basis'; ProdSG section 22(4) only requires regular checks without a fixed interval.
- Meaning of CE plus TUV: Polish retail guides (Decathlon) present TUV and CE as proof of rigorous testing; CE on toys is normally a manufacturer self-declaration and TUV marks vary in meaning (GS-Mark Approval vs TUV-Mark Approval vs Certificate of Conformity all appear in Certipedia trampoline results).
- UK divergence: a BSI page reportedly shows BS EN 71-14:2018 withdrawn on 2025-10-31 (search summary), a year earlier than the CEN withdrawal date of 2026-10-31; UK designated standards follow a separate regime.

### EU Safety Gate and UOKiK registers

**Verdict:** USE NOW (negative screen) · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 3 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

EU Safety Gate (formerly RAPEX) is the European Commission's rapid alert system and public portal for dangerous non-food consumer and professional products. National market surveillance authorities notify measures, and the Commission publishes alerts in a weekly report every Friday (GPSR (EU) 2023/988, Art. 25-26 and 34). The public portal (ec.europa.eu/safety-gate-alerts) offers free-text search, filters (product category, risk type, notifying country, country of origin, year, alert type, publication dates), weekly reports, email subscriptions and PDF/Excel/XML exports in 28 languages including Polish. The Polish counterpart is UOKiK, but the national 'rejestr produktow niebezpiecznych' was abolished on 3 Jan 2026 (Art. 98 of the Act of 7 Nov 2025, Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1826). What remains public in Poland: (a) the UOKiK 'Rejestr wyrobow niezgodnych z wymaganiami lub stwarzajacych zagrozenie' (Hermes system; harmonised products under the 2016 conformity-assessment and market-surveillance act; about 370 entries; searchable by product-name prefix, EAN prefix and entry date); (b) BIP 'Powiadomienia o produktach niebezpiecznych' (business recall notifications under GPSR Chapter III; about 580 entries); (c) BIP 'Ogloszenia o produktach niebezpiecznych' (about 70 entries, latest dated 10 Dec 2025); (d) UOKiK decisions published under Art. 21 of the 2025 Act. Role type: registry (regulator database).

**vendor and ownership**

Safety Gate: European Commission, Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers (DG JUST), Brussels; funded from the EU budget. Each national authority that notifies an alert is responsible for its content. Polish side: the President of UOKiK (Urzad Ochrony Konkurencji i Konsumentow, Warsaw) is the single national contact point for Safety Gate (Art. 13 of the 2025 Act). Voivodeship Trade Inspection offices (WIIH) carry out inspections. Public bodies with no commercial ownership and no marketplace ties.

**lifecycle status**

Safety Gate: live and actively maintained. RAPEX started in 2003; the 2025 report calls 2003 the launch year of the system. Latest change found: weekly report 2026-40 published on 9 Oct 2026 (94 alerts). The 2025 annual report was released in early March 2026 (5 March per the EC Cyprus representation, 9 March on the main Commission news page). 2025 figures: 4,671 alerts, the highest on record and 13% more than in 2024; cosmetics 36%, toys 16%, electrical appliances 11%; chemical risks 53%, injuries 14%, choking 9%; 5,794 follow-up actions (+35%); more than 1,200 online marketplaces registered by the end of 2025; Poland notified 170 alerts (170 in 2024) and 419 follow-up actions. UOKiK: the national dangerous-products register and the national information system on dangerous products were abolished on 3 Jan 2026 (Arts. 98-99; data kept for 5 years, then archived). The Hermes 'ProduktNiebezpieczny' register type returns 'Brak danych' (no data). The non-compliant products register is live (latest entry 19/2026, dated 2026-10-01). BIP notifications are live (latest 13 Oct 2026, BenQ GV31 mini projector). The Hermes SOAP web service documented in the manual (v1.1) returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-15. All verified on 2026-10-15.

**cost model**

Free. No account is needed to search, view or export. Email subscriptions are free. Businesses notify through the Safety Business Gateway at no charge. Third-party Apify wrappers charge for the same public data (e.g. darknezz/safety-gate-scraper USD 0.02 per result plus USD 0.01 per run; studio-amba/safety-gate-scraper free; seen 2026-10-15). They are not needed, because the official endpoints are free.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Full portal and search in Polish. language=pl returns translated alert fields (e.g. 'Zabawki', 'Zadlawienie'). A Polish search for 'trampolina' returned 21 alerts against 26 for 'trampoline' in English (2026-10-15). UOKiK Hermes and BIP lists are Polish-only.
- **EU**: All EU member states plus the EEA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and the UK in respect of Northern Ireland (code XI) notify alerts. The portal is available in 28 languages (24 EU languages plus NO, IS, UK, AR).
- **US**: Not covered. US recalls sit with the CPSC; the OECD GlobalRecalls portal (globalrecalls.oecd.org, reachable on 2026-10-15) aggregates several jurisdictions.
- **language**: UI and alert texts in Polish via translations (⚠ *(unverified)* probably machine translation; the Polish text of the week-40 toy alert reads like machine output).
- **US only or agentic features**: None. Reporting a dangerous product as a consumer goes through the Consumer Safety Gateway and needs an EU Login account.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A as a comparison tool. Alerts identify a product by category, product type, brand, name, type/model, batch, barcode, description, package description and photos, but many fields are empty. In weekly report 40/2026, 41 of 94 alerts had a brand, 65 had a model or type, 33 had a barcode and 14 had a batch number. Matching an alert to the exact variant you plan to buy needs a manual comparison of photos, model numbers and descriptions. White-label rebadges often appear without a brand, so a name search will miss them.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A. No prices or shops. Coverage relevant to Poland: Poland notified 170 alerts in 2025, but alerts from any member state matter because products circulate EU-wide. The alert detail field 'reactingCountries' lists the other countries that found the same product.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A. No prices.

**total landed cost**

N/A. No prices or delivery data.

**review and seller verification**

None for reviews. Partial for sellers: Safety Gate alerts carry an 'onlineTrader' field (marketplace name, e.g. 'Cdiscount'; present in 61 of 94 alerts in week 40/2026) and measures such as 'Removal of this product listing by the online marketplace'. They do not identify the seller entity and do not link to CEIDG, KRS or VIES. UOKiK register entries name the economic operator (e.g. 'Wytworca w UE FLORENTYNA Sp. z o.o., Pleszew' for the Botti kettle), and BIP notifications name the notifying company (e.g. BenQ Europe BV).

**safety and compliance checks**

This is the safety check itself. What runs automatically today: (1) Safety Gate free-text search through the portal's own undocumented JSON API, POST https://ec.europa.eu/safety-gate-alerts/public/api/search (no auth; tested 2026-10-15). It matches product name, specific name and brand. It does not match barcodes or model/type numbers: an EAN from a week-40 alert returned 0 hits, and model '26046' returned a different alert. Matching is by substring, so 'Berg' returned 63 hits including Weinsberg, Varberg and Ibergarden; filter results on the brand field. (2) Alert detail: GET /public/api/notification/{id}?language=pl. (3) The official weekly XML (CC0), a list of every report since 2005 plus per-week XML; build a local index from it to match EANs and model numbers. (4) UOKiK Hermes register via GET parameters NazwaProduktu (name prefix) and KodWyrobu (EAN prefix): EAN 5907758602041 returned entry 19/2026 (Botti kettle, withdrawal ordered). Trampoline test on 2026-10-15: Safety Gate returned 26 alerts for 'trampoline' (2007-2026), including Salta Luxe 153x214 cm (2017, injuries), Exit Twist (2018), Berg Twinhoop basketball set for trampolines (2024), a Domyos trampoline net (2011), an INNOVA GOODS 140 cm kids trampoline (2025, padding moves) and bungee carabiners and pulleys (2026). UOKiK Hermes returned 0 hits for 'trampolina'. Out of scope: GPSR listing fields, the EN 71-14 edition and certificate validity. A missing alert is not evidence that a product is safe.

**independent test coverage**

N/A. Not a test lab. Alerts and UOKiK entries sometimes say a lab test was done (e.g. 'Przeprowadzono badania laboratoryjne' and a measured nickel release of 49 ug/cm2/week), but they do not compare product quality.

**alerts and monitoring**

Safety Gate: free email subscriptions by criteria and language (screen/webReport/subscription) and a weekly digest on Fridays. There is no official webhook or RSS feed, but the weekly XML list can be polled each Friday for new reports. UOKiK: no subscription for the registers was found. The Hermes 'Kanal RSS' link points to the old uokik.gov.pl/rss.php, and uokik.gov.pl robots.txt disallows /feed/. Neither system can watch a shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A. It cannot buy anything; it is read-only reference data.

**after sales and resale**

Useful after a purchase: recall notices tell owners what to do (e.g. BenQ GV31: stop use, repair or replacement campaign; the GPSR recall remedy must offer at least two options per the UOKiK page). Check before reselling on OLX or Allegro Lokalnie, because recalled products should not be resold. It does not cover spare parts or resale value.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Data comes from notifications by national market surveillance authorities. Businesses notify authorities through the Safety Business Gateway. The Commission validates alerts and publishes them weekly, about 100 per week in 2025 (94 in week 40/2026). Each alert has a stable URL (screen/webReport/alertDetail/{id}), a case reference (e.g. SR/02826/26) and photos. Lag: a week-40/2026 toy alert had measures dated 16-17 Jul 2026 and was published on 9 Oct 2026, about 12 weeks later. Updates and corrigenda are flagged in 'report_addendum'. UOKiK: entry 19/2026 had a decision dated 2026-08-31 and a register entry dated 2026-10-01, about one month later.

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. There is no documented official API, but public machine-readable endpoints work without auth. (1) Official machine-readable data: the weekly-report XML list (https://ec.europa.eu/safety-gate-alerts/api/download/weeklyReport/list/xml/en; 391 KB; CC0 1.0 per data.europa.eu) and a detail XML per report (week 40/2026: 220 KB, 94 alerts with brand, name, model, batch, barcode, risk, measures, notifying country, origin, online trader and picture URLs). The UI also exports PDF and Excel (the bundle sets a 5,000-row Excel export limit). (2) The portal's own JSON API, found in its JS bundle and tested 2026-10-15: POST /safety-gate-alerts/public/api/search with body {fullTextSearch, criteria{year[], productCategoryType, riskType, notifyingCountry, countryOrigin, alertType, publicationDateFrom/To}, language, pagination{numberElements, page, sortField:'PUBLICATION_DATE', sortOrder}}; GET /public/api/notification/{id}?language=xx; images at /public/api/notification/image/{id}. About 0.3 s per call. Being undocumented, it can change without notice. (3) MCP and skills: no official or community Safety Gate MCP server or Claude skill was found (gh search on 2026-10-15). Community code that calls the API: fuji97/Recalls (Android, MIT, 0 stars, pushed 2026-10-01), GaetanRAYNAUD/Alerte-Rappel---API (MIT), sveitser/product-safety, pkar70/Wycofania (a Polish recalls app, GPL-3.0, pushed 2025-11-09). Apify actors exist (studio-amba, darknezz, steadydata, nexgenwatch, parseforge), each with 2-3 users. (4) WebFetch or a browser agent: the portal is a single-page app (1.7 KB HTML shell), so call the API directly. ec.europa.eu robots.txt has no rule for /safety-gate-alerts and does not block AI agents. (5) UOKiK Hermes: GET Rejestr.ashx with query parameters returns HTML to parse; the Hermes host has no robots.txt (404). The documented SOAP web service (Hermes.svc, no auth) is dead (404). uokik.gov.pl itself blocks ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai and GPTBot for the whole site, so read BIP pages manually. Setup effort: 1-2 hours to write a small skill (search POST, detail GET, Hermes GET, optional local weekly-XML index for EAN matching).

**protocol support**

N/A. It is a data source and implements no agent-commerce protocol. GPSR Art. 34 provides an interoperable interface for online marketplaces, which is not open to consumers.

**⚠ open source and licence**

The portal code is closed. The data is open: the data.europa.eu dataset 'rapex-rapid-alert-system-non-food' lists the weekly XML under CC0 1.0 and the XLS statistics under CC BY 4.0, with other pages under the Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU). The 2025 report allows reuse if the source, extraction date and language version are acknowledged. UOKiK: BIP public information; the Hermes footer reads '(c) UOKiK 2014. Wszelkie prawa zastrzezone'. ⚠ *(unverified)* Formal reuse terms for UOKiK register data were not checked.

**account linking and data access**

Search, detail and export need nothing. A subscription needs an email address. The Consumer Safety Gateway (for reporting accidents or dangerous products) needs an EU Login account. No payment data is involved. GDPR exposure is minimal; the only personal data you would hand over is the subscription email.

**automation legal risk**

Low. These are public-sector data with an explicit open licence (CC0/CC BY with attribution). ec.europa.eu robots.txt places no restriction on /safety-gate-alerts. The JSON API is undocumented, so cache results and poll weekly rather than hammering it. UOKiK: uokik.gov.pl robots.txt blocks AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, anthropic-ai, GPTBot and others), so automated fetching of BIP pages goes against the site's stated preference; use manual reading or the Hermes host, which has no robots.txt. No terms of service with an anti-scraping clause were found. No risk of account bans, because no account is used.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

None commercial: a public authority with no ads, affiliates or paid placement. Structural biases: notifications depend on each member state's enforcement priorities; cosmetics dominate because of the BMHCA (Lilial) ban (1,278 alerts in 2025); sports and garden products such as trampolines are rarely notified. Results therefore over-represent heavily checked categories, and a missing alert proves nothing.

**ranking transparency**

Results are sorted by publication date by default, or by another explicit sort. There is no paid ranking. Each alert shows its risk level ('Serious risk' or other) and the notifying country. Sponsorship: N/A.

**run to run consistency**

N/A. It is a deterministic database; the same query returns the same results until a new weekly report is added.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Low exposure. Content is written by authorities, not traders, so seller persuasion or fake reviews do not apply. An agent should still treat the free-text fields (description, danger) as data. The main errors are false negatives (rebrands, missing brand or barcode) and false positives (substring matches).

**known failures**

(1) Many alerts lack brand or barcode (week 40/2026: brand 41/94, barcode 33/94). (2) Full-text search does not index barcodes or model numbers (tested), so EAN lookup needs a local XML index. (3) Substring matching gives false positives ('Berg' matched Weinsberg, Varberg and Ibergarden). (4) Polish texts are translations. (5) Publication lag of weeks to months after the national measure. (6) By default the UI searches only the last 10 years unless the archive is included; older alerts (e.g. 2007-2013 trampoline alerts) appear only with archived results. (7) Poland: the national dangerous-products register is abolished, the Hermes SOAP service is dead, the RSS link points to the old site, the Hermes name search matches by prefix only, and uokik.gov.pl blocks AI agents. Many Polish guides (rp.pl, poradnikprzedsiebiorcy.pl, podatki.biz) still describe the abolished register.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A. This is the regulators' own tool. Context: from 3 Jan 2026 UOKiK gained new powers under the 2025 Act, including fines of up to PLN 1,000,000 for placing dangerous products on the market or for marketplaces failing to execute orders, and orders to remove offers from online marketplaces.

**buyer protection path**

Indirect. If a product you own appears in a recall, use the recall remedy (GPSR recall rules; UOKiK states the consumer must be offered at least two options such as repair or replacement) plus statutory non-conformity rights against the seller (rekojmia / niezgodnosc towaru z umowa) and the 14-day withdrawal right for distance purchases. Report a dangerous product to UOKiK (ePUAP or post), to the competent WIIH, or through the Consumer Safety Gateway. Cross-border: ECC Poland.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Good as a negative screen, useless as a positive verdict. Trampoline example (2026-10-15): 'trampoline' returned 26 alerts. Brand checks: Salta 1 (a 2017 alert on the Salta Luxe 153x214 rectangular model, not the round 305 cm models); Berg 2 relevant (a 2024 trampoline basketball set and a balance bike) among 63 substring hits; Exit 2 (Exit Twist 2018, Bounzy mini 2017); Hudora 1 (a 2013 scooter); Zipro 0; Domyos 1 (a 2011 net). A buyer comparing a Salta, Zipro or Berg 305 cm trampoline therefore gets 'no alert for this model', with a note of brand history and of accessory risks (bungee pulleys, basketball hoops, sprinklers). It cannot confirm the EN 71-14 edition, test certificates or GPSR listing data, and it says nothing about build quality. The same pattern applies to appliances and electronics, where alerts are more common (electrical appliances were 11% of 2025 alerts).

**workflow role**

Safety step: a pre-purchase screen and a post-purchase recall watch. Combine with a GPSR listing-data check, a certificate check (Certipedia or the lab's register), independent lab tests, the UOKiK BIP notifications and Hermes register, and OECD GlobalRecalls or CPSC for brands also sold in the US.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Free. Manual: 5-10 minutes (brand, model and product-type searches in Polish and English, open hits). Automated: 3-6 API calls (brand, model, product type x en/pl) at about 0.3 s each, USD 0, plus one Hermes GET by EAN. Optional local index for EAN matching: one-time download of all weekly XML reports since 2005. Week 40/2026 was 220 KB, so roughly 100-200 MB in total (⚠ *(unverified)* extrapolated, not measured). LLM tokens to summarise a handful of alert JSONs: negligible.

**evidence trail**

Strong. Stable alert URLs (ec.europa.eu/safety-gate-alerts/screen/webReport/alertDetail/{id}), case references (SR/xxxxx/yy), a per-alert PDF export (api/download/notification/detail/pdf/{id}/{lang}) and weekly report numbers. Vault record: date and time; every query run (term, language, filters) with its total hit count; matched alerts (reference, URL, product, brand, risk, measures, date); an explicit 'no match for queries X, Y, Z on date D'; the Hermes query URL and result; attribution 'Source: European Commission - Safety Gate', as the licence allows storing the data.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Official, free, EU-wide register with record coverage (4,671 alerts in 2025) and a Polish interface
  - Scriptable today: a no-auth JSON search and detail API plus official CC0 weekly XML, so it fits a Claude Code skill
  - Stable references, photos and PDF exports give a clean, citable evidence trail
  - Marketplaces must take it into account under GPSR Art. 22(6)-(7), so alerts lead to listing removals
  - The UOKiK Hermes register adds EAN-searchable Polish decisions for harmonised products
- **weaknesses**:
  - No search by EAN or model number; many alerts lack brand or barcode (41/94 and 33/94 in week 40/2026)
  - Substring matching gives false positives; Polish texts are translations; lag of weeks to months
  - A missing alert proves nothing; garden trampolines are rarely notified
  - The Polish national dangerous-products register was abolished on 3 Jan 2026; Polish sources are fragmented and the Hermes SOAP service is dead
  - uokik.gov.pl blocks AI agents in robots.txt; the Safety Gate JSON API is undocumented and may change

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of the portal's search quality or completeness was found. Secondary coverage (Spielwarenmesse, Mason Hayes & Curran, Cosmeticobs) repeats the Commission's 2025 figures. A community developer review (fuji97/Recalls docs/LEGAL.md, reviewed 2026-09-27; 0-star repository, not authoritative) independently confirms that the /public/api/search and /public/api/notification endpoints work without a key and that the data is reusable with attribution. The research outline's claim that UOKiK keeps a national register is outdated (see conflicting_evidence).

**verdict for me**

USE NOW. Deciding fact: it is official, free and scriptable today (no-auth JSON search plus CC0 weekly XML) under a clear licence, the cheapest safety screen to automate. Best use: in a Claude Code purchase skill, query brand, model and product type in English and Polish via /public/api/search, filter hits on the brand field, fetch details, add a UOKiK Hermes EAN query, and save the hit list (or an explicit 'no hits for queries X') with alert URLs in the vault. Treat a clean result as 'no known alert', not 'safe'.

**conflicting evidence**

- UOKiK register: the research outline and older Polish guides (rp.pl, poradnikprzedsiebiorcy.pl, podatki.biz) say UOKiK keeps a national dangerous-products register, but Art. 98 of the Act of 7 Nov 2025 (Dz.U. 2025 poz. 1826, in force 3 Jan 2026) abolished it, and the Hermes 'ProduktNiebezpieczny' type showed no data on 2026-10-15. Only the non-compliant products register and the BIP notification lists remain.
- Report date: 5 March 2026 (EC Cyprus representation and one trade site) vs 9 March 2026 (main Commission news page).
- Licence: data.europa.eu lists the weekly XML as CC0 1.0 and the statistics XLS as CC BY 4.0; the community LEGAL.md says CC BY 4.0 overall; the 2025 report says reuse is allowed if source, extraction date and language version are acknowledged.
- API path: an Apify listing claims a public JSON endpoint '/api/alerts'; the portal code actually uses /public/api/search and /public/api/notification/{id}. '/api/alerts' was not verified.
- UOKiK web service: the Hermes manual (v1.1) says a SOAP service at publikacje.uokik.gov.pl/hermes3_ws/Hermes.svc is available without authentication, but it returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-15 (WSDL and service URL, http and https).
- Hit counts differ by language: 21 for 'trampolina' (pl) vs 26 for 'trampoline' (en) on the same day, because search runs over translated texts.

### GPSR listing checks and EPREL

**Verdict:** USE NOW (EPREL for appliances only) · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Two checks an agent can run on a listing before purchase. (1) GPSR, Regulation (EU) 2023/988 on general product safety, applicable since 13 Dec 2024. Art. 19 requires every online or other distance-sales offer to 'clearly and visibly indicate' at least: (a) the manufacturer's name, registered trade name or trade mark, plus a postal and an electronic address; (b) where the manufacturer is not established in the EU, the name, postal and electronic address of the EU responsible person (GPSR Art. 16(1) / Regulation 2019/1020 Art. 4(1)); (c) information identifying the product, including a picture, its type and any other product identifier; (d) any warning or safety information, in a language consumers can easily understand as set by the member state. In Poland that language is Polish (Art. 4 of the Act of 7 Nov 2025). A batch or serial number is a marking duty on the product itself (Art. 9(5)), not an explicit listing field. Art. 22(9) makes online marketplaces provide the fields and display them on the listing. Role type: regulation, turned into an agent checklist. (2) EPREL, the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (eprel.ec.europa.eu), where suppliers must register energy-labelled models (Regulation (EU) 2017/1369). The QR code on the label opens the public EPREL entry with the energy class, the label and the product information sheet. Role type: registry. It verifies a claimed energy class for appliances, lighting, TVs, tyres and similar products; it does not apply to trampolines.

**vendor and ownership**

GPSR: EU legislation (European Parliament and Council). In Poland it is enforced by the President of UOKiK and the Voivodeship Trade Inspection (WIIH) under the Act of 7 Nov 2025 on supervision of general product safety. EPREL: European Commission, DG ENER. Suppliers enter the data, and the Commission does not verify it; the API's own message says correctness 'is the responsibility of national market surveillance authorities'. No commercial ownership or bias.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

GPSR: entered into force in June 2023 and applies from 13 Dec 2024 (Art. 52). Products placed on the market before 13 Dec 2024 that comply with Directive 2001/95/EC may still be sold (Art. 51), which explains some legacy listings without GPSR data. The Polish implementing Act has been in force since 3 Jan 2026; its Art. 76 sets a fine of up to PLN 500,000 for not meeting Art. 19 duties. EU enforcement: the first GPSR product safety sweep (1 Apr-15 May 2025) checked 1,741 childcare listings on 47 marketplaces and produced 252 takedown orders (CCPC release, 18 Jul 2025). A second sweep, presented 7 Sep 2026, checked about 1,700 childcare and gym listings on 35 marketplaces: only 58% of listings showed manufacturer, responsible person and product identification together, 91% of marketplaces were registered in Safety Gate (53% a year earlier), and authorities sent 560 orders (Brussels Times, reporting the Commission statement). EPREL: live. Registration has been mandatory for models placed on the market since 1 Jan 2019 (⚠ *(unverified)* date from general knowledge, not re-opened). The public API key process (a qualified e-seal or signature) was seen on the live site on 2026-10-15. Verified 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

Free for a buyer. Reading a listing, the EPREL website, QR links and fiche PDFs costs nothing. EPREL Public API: the key itself is free, but the request needs an 'EPREL Declaration' signed with a qualified electronic seal (organisation) or a qualified electronic signature (individual) (EPREL site text, 2026-10-15). In Poland a qualified signature is a paid certificate (⚠ *(unverified)* roughly PLN 200-400 per year from commercial trust providers; not checked). The single-model endpoint by registration number answered without a key on 2026-10-15. Seller-side GPSR tools cost money (e.g. CompliScan Shopify app Pro at USD 29 per month, seen in search results) but are not needed by a buyer.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Art. 19 applies to every offer aimed at Polish consumers; warnings must be in Polish (Act of 7 Nov 2025, Art. 4). Allegro has collected GPSR data from sellers since Dec 2024 (responsible person, safety information, plus a flag for products marketed before 13 Dec 2024). ⚠ *(unverified)* How Allegro displays them to buyers was not verified, because Allegro blocked automated access (HTTP 403 with captcha). UOKiK's FAQ lists the four Art. 19 elements in Polish.
- **EU**: The same regulation applies in all member states, with the language set by each state. Amazon.de product pages carry a 'Produktsicherheit' block with 'Herstellerinformationen', 'Verantwortliche Person' and 'Produktdokumente' (e.g. Sicherheitsinformationen PDF), seen on trampoline accessory listings on 2026-10-15. That block loads dynamically, so the static HTML only shows 'Problem beim Laden der Informationen'.
- **US**: N/A. GPSR does not apply; US listings follow CPSC rules. EPREL is EU/EEA only.
- **language**: Checks are run against Polish text. EPREL pages and product information sheets are available in Polish (the fiche redirect returned Fiche_2000000_PL.pdf).
- **US only or agentic features**: None.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

GPSR: indirect. The Art. 19(c) type or model identifier ties a listing to a specific model, which is what a Safety Gate or certificate lookup needs; a listing without a model number cannot be checked. EPREL: strong for energy-labelled products. Every model identifier has its own registration with the full product information sheet; the fridge record tested had 76 fields, including annual energy use, volumes, energy class range and guarantee duration. That allows an exact comparison of variants in a line, e.g. a retailer-exclusive suffix vs the base model, when both are registered. The difficult step is mapping a shop's product name to the EPREL model identifier, since retailers often add suffixes.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A. No prices or shop coverage.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A. No prices.

**total landed cost**

N/A for price and shipping. EPREL adds one cost-of-ownership input: declared annual energy consumption (e.g. kWh per year) for appliances, to turn into running cost at the buyer's tariff. Not relevant to a trampoline.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. The Art. 19 data lets an agent check the manufacturer and the EU responsible person: that they are present, that the email domain matches the brand, that the address is real, and that the company exists in KRS, CEIDG or VIES. A non-EU manufacturer with no EU responsible person is a hard red flag, because under Art. 16(1) such a product may not be placed on the market. It cannot prove that the named responsible person actually accepted the role, or that the warnings are complete. EPREL exposes supplier and trademark verification status (e.g. orgVerificationStatus and trademarkVerificationStatus 'VERIFIED' for a Hafele light source) and returns 'UNVERIFIED_SUPPLIER' for models from suppliers that have not completed identity verification. No review checks.

**safety and compliance checks**

This item is the check itself. Agent checklist per listing: (1) manufacturer name plus postal address plus electronic address; (2) if the manufacturer is outside the EU, the EU responsible person's name, postal address and electronic address; (3) picture, type or model, and any other identifier (EAN, SKU); (4) warnings and safety information in Polish (for a garden trampoline: age range, maximum user weight, one user at a time, adult supervision, outdoor domestic use, assembly and anchoring warnings); (5) pass the identifiers to Safety Gate and UOKiK lookups; (6) for appliances: an EPREL registration number or QR code is present, and the energy class in the listing equals EPREL's 'energyClass'. What runs automatically: (1)-(3) as presence checks on a rendered page (brand stores, Ceneo shops and Amazon.de with a browser agent; Allegro only in the user's own browser session); (4) language detection, though whether the content is adequate needs a human; (6) EPREL lookup by registration number. Not covered: the EN 71-14 edition, test certificates and Certipedia. Missing data is reportable: a notice to the marketplace (DSA Art. 16; under GPSR Art. 22(8) marketplaces must process product-safety notices within 3 working days), UOKiK or the competent WIIH (ePUAP or post), or the Consumer Safety Gateway when the product itself is dangerous. Exception: legacy stock placed on the market before 13 Dec 2024 may lawfully lack some GPSR data (Art. 51).

**independent test coverage**

N/A. A legal and registry check, not a test. EPREL values are declared by suppliers, and only market surveillance authorities test them.

**alerts and monitoring**

N/A. Neither GPSR nor EPREL sends consumer alerts. An agent can re-run the checklist on a saved listing URL before checkout.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A. Neither can buy. The check fits as a pre-checkout gate in a purchase workflow: block or warn when an Art. 19 field is missing.

**after sales and resale**

The Art. 19 manufacturer and EU responsible person contacts are the route for safety issues, recalls and spare parts when a seller disappears. EPREL records a declared guarantee duration for some product groups (field 'guaranteeDuration'). Resale: N/A.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

GPSR data is text supplied by the seller on each listing. There is no central register, and marketplaces check that fields are filled, not that they are true. It is as fresh as the listing. EPREL: supplier-entered and updated in real time, with versioning ('versionId', 'lastVersion'); the Commission does not verify correctness. Every EPREL answer has a stable URL (screen/product/{group}/{regNo}) and a PDF label and fiche.

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. GPSR check: no API or MCP exists for buyers; it is a checklist an agent applies to a rendered page. Route: a Claude Code skill that opens the product URL in a browser agent (Claude in Chrome or Playwright, because Amazon.de loads its safety block dynamically and Allegro blocks bots with a captcha), extracts the four Art. 19 fields into JSON, flags gaps, and checks the EU responsible person in VIES or KRS. Existing tools are seller-side only: CompliScan and Lexply (Shopify catalogue scanners), the Apify actor formnexa/gpsr-catalog-compliance-auditor (presence check), the free VIMM checklist, WooCommerce plugins (e.g. the-jey/jeytech-gpsr-guard, 0 stars), Amazon SP-API Listings Items GPSR attributes, and Allegro seller endpoints (GET /sale/responsible-persons; PUT /sale/offer-modification-commands/{commandId} with responsiblePerson or safetyInformation). No buyer-side GPSR checker, MCP server or Claude skill was found (gh search, 2026-10-15). EPREL: the official Public API requires a key for 'searching and retrieving models' (EPREL site text), requested through a form plus an EPREL Declaration sealed or signed with a qualified e-seal or e-signature. Observed on 2026-10-15: GET https://eprel.ec.europa.eu/api/product/{registrationNumber} returned the full model JSON without a key (undocumented behaviour that may change); list endpoints such as /api/products/washingmachines2019 returned 403 'Forbidden' without a key; /qr/{regNo} redirects to the public product screen; /api/products/{group}/{regNo}/fiches?language=PL redirects to the Polish PDF fiche. Community clients: topten-dev/eprel-client (JS, MIT, pushed 2026-04-20), maschmann/eprel-public-api-client (PHP), dvdzapata/EPREL; all 0-1 stars. No EPREL MCP server was found. Setup effort: GPSR skill 2-4 hours (prompt, extraction schema, browser step); EPREL lookup by registration number 30 minutes; full EPREL search needs the key process (days, plus a qualified signature).

**⚠ protocol support**

N/A. Neither implements agent-commerce protocols. The GPSR fields are what an agent-commerce catalogue would need to expose; ⚠ *(unverified)* none of ACP, UCP or AP2 was checked for GPSR fields.

**⚠ open source and licence**

GPSR: public law text (EUR-Lex). EPREL: closed system; public data are reusable, and the API requires accepting EPREL Terms and Conditions with a key (⚠ *(unverified)* terms not opened). Community EPREL clients are MIT (topten-dev/eprel-client).

**account linking and data access**

GPSR check: none; it reads public listing pages. Allegro must be read in the user's own logged-in or normal browser session, because automated access is blocked. EPREL: the website and per-model lookups need nothing. A Public API key needs organisation or person data, a contact email and a qualified e-seal or signature, so it reveals the requester's identity to the Commission. No payment data is involved.

**automation legal risk**

GPSR check: low legal risk for reading a single page the user is looking at. Bulk crawling of marketplaces runs into their terms and anti-bot systems (Allegro returned a captcha and HTTP 403 to a plain request on 2026-10-15). Use the user's own browser for Allegro. EPREL: public-sector data. Calling the keyless single-model endpoint at low volume is low risk. Bulk searching without a key is not possible, and the key comes with terms of use.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

None. A regulation and a public registry, with no ads or affiliates. The bias risk is upstream: marketplaces show the fields but do not verify them, and sellers can enter generic or rented responsible-person addresses.

**ranking transparency**

N/A. No ranking.

**run to run consistency**

N/A for the rules and the registry. LLM extraction of fields from a page can vary between runs, so use a fixed JSON schema and keep a screenshot of the safety section as ground truth.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Listing text is seller-controlled, so an LLM extracting fields could be steered by instructions planted in the description. Treat page text as data, extract into a fixed schema, and verify the responsible person against KRS or VIES rather than trusting the page. Known evasions: responsible-person data only inside images, placeholder addresses, a marketplace's own address given as the manufacturer, 'see packaging' instead of warnings. EPREL: suppliers self-declare, and the Commission states it does not verify correctness; unverified suppliers are flagged.

**known failures**

(1) Amazon.de loads the safety block dynamically, so a static fetch shows a loading error; a rendered browser is required. (2) Allegro blocks non-browser clients (captcha, HTTP 403). (3) Sellers put GPSR data in images or PDFs that need OCR. (4) Legacy stock placed on the market before 13 Dec 2024 is exempt, which creates false positives unless the 'marketed before' flag is read. (5) The 2026 EU sweep found that 42% of checked listings lacked key details, so failures are common and the check discriminates. (6) EPREL: retailer names rarely match the model identifier; keyless search is not possible; some models come from unverified suppliers; the keyless single-model endpoint is undocumented.

**regulatory enforcement history**

2025 EU GPSR sweep: 1,741 childcare listings on 47 marketplaces (including Amazon, Shein, Etsy, eBay, Temu and Zalando), 252 takedown orders; the CCPC alone issued 72, all removed (CCPC, 18 Jul 2025). 2026 sweep: about 1,700 childcare and gym listings on 35 marketplaces, 58% complete on manufacturer, responsible person and identification together, 560 orders (7 Sep 2026; Brussels Times). Poland: no published UOKiK result of a GPSR listing sweep was found as of 2026-10-15. The new Act allows fines of up to PLN 500,000 for Art. 19 breaches (Art. 76) and up to PLN 1,000,000 for marketplaces that do not execute orders (Art. 81).

**buyer protection path**

Missing GPSR data does not by itself give a refund right. It mainly predicts how hard after-sales will be. An offer from a non-EU seller without an EU responsible person leaves no EU entity to pursue for safety or recall issues. Statutory non-conformity rights (rekojmia / niezgodnosc towaru z umowa) and the 14-day withdrawal right still apply against the seller. A misstated energy class is a non-conformity with the contract description, so the buyer can claim repair, price reduction or withdrawal. Report missing data to the marketplace (3-working-day handling under Art. 22(8)) and to UOKiK or WIIH. Cross-border: ECC Poland.

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

GPSR check: high fit for a trampoline. Garden trampolines are toys under EN 71-14 and come from many EU and Chinese makers through marketplaces. Example: two 305 cm trampolines at similar prices. One lists a Polish or EU manufacturer with an address and email and a Polish warnings PDF. The other is a marketplace offer from a non-EU seller with no EU responsible person and no warnings, which is a red flag and is reportable. The check takes minutes and screens out the riskiest offers before price comparison. It cannot judge build quality or confirm EN 71-14 test results. EPREL: not applicable to trampolines (no energy label). Useful for the other durables in scope (fridges, washing machines, dishwashers, TVs, light sources, tyres; ⚠ *(unverified)* smartphones and tablets since mid-2025) to confirm the energy class and get the official product information sheet in Polish.

**workflow role**

Safety and seller check step, between discovery and price comparison: drop listings that fail Art. 19, then run Safety Gate and UOKiK on the identifiers of the survivors. EPREL sits in the specs and variants step for appliances. Combine with Safety Gate, certificate checks, KRS, CEIDG or VIES for the responsible person, and a price tool.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Cash cost zero. Manual: 2-3 minutes per listing (scroll to the product-safety section, check four items). Agent: one rendered page load plus extraction, about 5-15k LLM tokens per listing (⚠ *(unverified)* estimate), plus a free VIES check of the responsible person's VAT number. For 5 shortlisted listings, roughly 25-75k tokens, cents at API prices. EPREL: one GET by registration number, free; a full search needs the API key (one-off qualified-signature cost).

**evidence trail**

Good if captured deliberately. Save per listing: URL, date and time, a screenshot of the product-safety section, the extracted JSON {manufacturer, manufacturer_address, manufacturer_email, eu_responsible_person, rp_address, rp_email, model_identifier, other_ids, warnings_language, warnings_present} with a pass/fail per field, and the VIES or KRS lookup result. For EPREL: registration number, public URL, energy class, the fiche PDF in Polish, and the supplier verification status. All of this fits a vault note's appendix.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - A legal, objective checklist (GPSR Art. 19) that applies to every EU listing and is easy for an agent to run
  - Failures are common (42% of listings in the 2026 EU sweep), so it separates offers in practice
  - Missing data is reportable, with fines of up to PLN 500,000 in Poland (Art. 76 of the 2025 Act)
  - EPREL gives an official per-model record (energy class, fiche in Polish, supplier verification) reachable by registration number without a key
  - Free, and leaves a clear evidence trail (screenshots, extracted fields, registry URLs)
- **weaknesses**:
  - It checks presence, not truth: marketplaces do not verify the data, and responsible-person addresses can be generic or rented
  - No buyer-side tool exists; a custom skill is needed, and Allegro blocks automation while Amazon.de needs a rendered page
  - Legacy stock placed before 13 Dec 2024 is exempt, which causes false alarms
  - EPREL search needs an API key tied to a qualified e-seal or signature; mapping shop names to model identifiers is error-prone
  - Says nothing about build quality or EN 71-14 test results; EPREL does not apply to trampolines

**independent review consensus**

The independent evidence is the regulators' own sweeps. The 2025 and 2026 coordinated EU sweeps agree that GPSR information gaps on marketplace listings are widespread (252 orders in 2025; 42% incomplete listings and 560 orders in 2026) and that marketplace registration improved (53% to 91%). No independent evaluation of buyer-side GPSR checking tools was found, since none exist. For EPREL, no independent test of data accuracy was found; the Commission itself disclaims verification. Secondary practitioner guides (vimm.be, Fieldfisher, caspers-mock.de) describe Art. 19 consistently with the regulation text.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW (GPSR check as a skill); EPREL USE NOW for appliances only, CONTEXT ONLY for the trampoline. Deciding fact: Art. 19 gives four objective, machine-checkable fields that 42% of audited listings fail, and a missing EU responsible person is a hard red flag. Best use: a Claude Code step that opens each shortlisted listing in the browser, extracts the four fields into JSON with a screenshot, checks the responsible person in VIES or KRS, drops failing offers, and (for appliances) confirms the energy class via the EPREL registration number from the label QR code.

**conflicting evidence**

- Listing fields: the research outline says a listing must show 'model/batch'. GPSR Art. 19(c) requires a picture, the type and any other identifier; a batch or serial number is a product-marking duty (Art. 9(5)), so a listing without a batch number is not by itself a breach.
- EPREL access: the EPREL site states an API key is required to search and retrieve models, yet GET /api/product/{registrationNumber} returned full data without a key on 2026-10-15, while list endpoints returned 403.
- 2025 sweep compliance rate: one secondary summary says only 52% of products met GPSR requirements (65% on very large platforms); the CCPC release gives no rate. The 2026 sweep press coverage gives 58% complete listings. The Commission's full sweep reports were not opened.
- Allegro enforcement: a community moderator said running offers without GPSR data would not be ended but could not be renewed or newly listed, while Allegro also offers a 'placed on the market before 13 Dec 2024' flag that legitimately skips the fields; buyer-side display was not verified.
