## C. Seller, shop and legal checks

### Trusted Shops, Opineo and TrustMate

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY (manual seller signal) · **Cost:** Free to read; Buyer Protection free up to 10,000 PLN · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 10 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

External review and trust-mark systems used by Polish online shops. They are a seller-check signal, not product data. (1) Trusted Shops (trustedshops.pl; consumer sites moving to trstd.com since March 2025): a trustmark after a certification check of the shop, Buyer Protection up to PLN 10,000 per order, shop and product reviews collected after real orders, and a free Chrome/Firefox extension that marks certified shops in Google results. (2) Opineo.pl: an open review portal for shops, companies and products since 2007. 'Wiarygodne Opinie' come from post-transaction surveys sent for paying shops ('Sluchajacy'); 'zwykle opinie' can be posted by anyone and are not confirmed. It runs category rankings, certificates and the OpiConnect dispute channel. (3) TrustMate.io: review-collection software for shops (email and SMS invitations after an order, widgets, Google seller-rating syndication, product reviews, public profiles at trustmate.io/opinie/<shop>). It acquired Zaufane.pl, an eKomi-based review-collection service from Rzeszow, in April 2026 and claims over 50% of Polish shops that use an external review system. Name clash: 'Zaufane Opinie' is also Ceneo's purchase-verified review programme, covered in the Ceneo item; Zaufane.pl is a different company. Role type: review platforms and trust marks.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

- **Trusted Shops**: Trusted Shops SE, Subbelrather Strasse 15c, 50823 Cologne, Germany (Amtsgericht Koln HRB 120336). Management board: Jean-Marc Noel (chair), Michael Burdack. Registered in Germany as an insurance intermediary (D-B6MZ-QKA67-38). Polish office: Trusted Shops Poland sp. z o.o., Warsaw (KRS 0000744076, share capital PLN 5,000). ⚠ *(unverified)* Shareholders and investors not verified; a claimed HGGC stake could not be confirmed.
- **Opineo**: Operated by Ringier Axel Springer Polska sp. z o.o., Warsaw (KRS 0000420780, NIP 527-267-70-09); correspondence address Wroclaw. RASP is a media group (Onet). ⚠ *(unverified)* Opineo ratings also appear on Skapiec, which suggests a group link, not confirmed on a primary page.
- **TrustMate**: TrustMate S.A., ul. Bartoszowicka 3, 50-062 Wroclaw (KRS 0000737597, NIP 8971854393, share capital PLN 3,163,170). CEO (prezes zarzadu) Jerzy Krawczyk. The 2026 share issue was taken 90% by Mansun Capital with business angels, plus existing investors INventures and Next Road Ventures (ITwiz, 23 Apr 2026).
- **Zaufane pl**: Zaufane.pl sp. z o.o., ul. Trembeckiego 11A, 35-234 Rzeszow (KRS 0001057326, NIP 5170439594). Its service runs on the eKomi platform (smartforms.ekomi.com; login at zaufane.ekomiapps.de). Being acquired by TrustMate (announced April 2026).
- **bias note**: All four are paid by the shops they rate. Opineo also lets non-paying shops be reviewed openly.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

All live on 2026-10-15. Trusted Shops: consumer websites moving to trstd.com/xx since March 2025 (Trusted Shops newsroom); trstd.com/pl-pl redirects to trustedshops.pl; footer '(c) 2026 Trusted Shops SE'. Opineo: status confirmed active. User terms updated 05.05.2025 (weighting and verification wording changed), footer '(c) 2007-2026', and the Media Expert profile shows 59 reviews dated Aug-Oct 2026. TrustMate: active. The acquisition of Zaufane.pl was announced on 23 Apr 2026 (ITwiz); branches in Romania and Italy opened at the end of 2025; another CEE acquisition is planned (vendor statement). Zaufane.pl: the site is still live and selling (footer '(c) 2019-2025', sister sites in CZ, SK, HU and RO). Clients are moving to TrustMate per ITwiz; ⚠ *(unverified)* when or whether the Zaufane.pl brand will be retired.

**⚠ cost model**

Free for consumers: reading reviews, the Trusted Shops browser extension, and Trusted Shops Buyer Protection (free basic cover up to PLN 10,000 per order, available right after ordering even without an account, per trustedshops.pl on 2026-10-15). Shops pay: Trusted Shops membership (price list at business.trustedshops.pl/ceny, not opened); the Opineo 'Sluchajacy' programme and certificates (price list not opened); TrustMate subscription with a free trial ('Wyprobuj za darmo'; /pricing not opened); Zaufane.pl priced by quote. ⚠ *(unverified)* Merchant prices not verified.

**feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: All four operate in Polish. Trusted Shops: Polish site, Buyer Protection in PLN, Warsaw office. Opineo: Poland only. TrustMate: Polish home market. Zaufane.pl: Polish, with CZ, SK, HU and RO sister sites.
- **EU**: Trusted Shops: 12 country sites (DE, AT, CH, NL, BE, FR, IT, ES, PT, PL, UK, EU). TrustMate: RO and IT branches; profile sitemaps in about 30 languages; review translation through DeepL or the Google API. Opineo: none outside Poland.
- **US**: N/A. None of them targets the US.
- **language**: Polish UI and Polish reviews. TrustMate shows machine-translated reviews with a link to the original.
- **US only or agentic features**: None. No agentic checkout or AI shopping features were found.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A. These are shop-review systems. Product reviews exist per shop (TrustMate /p/<shop>/product/..., Opineo products, Trusted Shops product reviews) but are not mapped across shops or variants.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A for prices. Coverage of Polish shops: TrustMate claims over 50% of Polish online shops that use an external review system (vendor-claimed; the ITwiz article gives no method). Trusted Shops claims about 25,000 certified shops and 160 million reviews, Europe-wide and vendor-claimed; ⚠ *(unverified)* the number of Polish shops is unknown because the directory renders in JavaScript and showed no count. Opineo is open, so any shop can be reviewed even if it is not a client (Media Expert has 14,741 reviews). Zaufane.pl has no public shop directory; its reviews appear on shop sites, Google and eKomi certificates.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A for prices. The Omnibus point here is review-verification disclosure. Under the Polish Unfair Commercial Practices Act (consolidated text Dz.U. 2023 poz. 845), art. 6(4)(7) makes it material information whether and how a trader ensures published reviews come from consumers who used or bought the product. Art. 7(25) and (26) blacklist claiming reviews are genuine without reasonable and proportionate checks, and posting or distorting fake reviews. What each platform discloses (2026-10-15): Trusted Shops PL says reviews need a unique transaction reference number and are 'in most cases' invitation-only, with a verification team and 'zero tolerance'; its German profile page lists three types: verified, unverified (written proactively by users) and imported (excluded from the score). Opineo separates 'Wiarygodne' (post-transaction survey) from 'zwykle' (open, purchase not confirmed) and computes a weighted average with weight 2 vs 1. Its terms say Opineo does not control or monitor review authenticity. TrustMate publishes a detailed method on /review-collection: 'zweryfikowano' (email or SMS invitation tied to an order, weight 2), 'niepotwierdzona zakupem' (open widget or profile, weight 1), 'opinia zewnetrzna' (imported from Google, Trustpilot, Trusted Shops or eKomi, weight 1), translated, and QR/NFC (anyone can post). Zaufane.pl says it invites only customers with an Order_ID, moderates before publication, and has no open forms. Remember that the shop itself must also disclose this beside its review widget, so check the shop page as well as the platform.

**total landed cost**

N/A. One indirect input: Trusted Shops Buyer Protection covers a refund that is not paid after withdrawal, which matters when returning a bulky item.

**⚠ review and seller verification**

Partial; this is the core of the item. What the systems can show: an invitation-based review is tied to an order number in the shop's system. TrustMate's public profile embeds per-review JSON with 'verified', 'notVerified', 'imported', 'importSource', 'orderNumber', 'weight' and 'mediationExists'; on aurora-garden.pl, 25 of 26 reviews in the page payload were verified with weight 2 (2026-10-15). Opineo offers a 'Tylko Wiarygodne' filter and shows counts for 30 days, 12 months and all time, plus withdrawn or removed reviews (Media Expert: 172). Trusted Shops adds a certification check of the shop and buyer protection. What they cannot prove: that the shop invites every buyer and not only happy ones; that the orders themselves were real; the legal identity of the shop (TrustMate shows a NIP, while the Opineo Media Expert card shows 'brak adresu'); or that ratings agree across platforms (Media Expert: Opineo 1.9/5 with 12% recommending, 161 reviews in 12 months, vs Ceneo 4.7/5 from 3,430 reviews, same day). None of them runs CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list or VIES checks for consumers; ⚠ *(unverified)* the depth of Trusted Shops' certification of company identity was not verified. Grade: partial.

**safety and compliance checks**

None for product safety (no Safety Gate, GPSR or certificate checks). The only compliance angle is Omnibus review disclosure, described above.

**independent test coverage**

N/A. These are not test labs. Related independent work: Stiftung Warentest tested four shop seals including Trusted Shops in 2019 and found they protect consumers 'to differing degrees' (secondary summary; older than six months). The Bundeskartellamt's 2020 inquiry into user reviews found portals rarely checked in advance that reviewers had bought the product (secondary).

**alerts and monitoring**

N/A for prices or stock. Trusted Shops accounts track protected orders. TrustMate and Opineo notify reviewers about mediation or OpiConnect messages. There is no shop-watch feature for buyers.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

None. They cannot buy. Trusted Shops Buyer Protection is a human opt-in after checkout in a certified shop; no agent payment is involved.

**after sales and resale**

Trusted Shops Buyer Protection (up to PLN 10,000) covers non-delivery, a refund not paid after withdrawal and return, shop insolvency, and other listed cases. Opineo OpiConnect and TrustMate mediation (up to 21 days) give a channel to push a shop to resolve a complaint. No spare-parts, service-network or resale features.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Reviews come from consumers, either invited from the shop's order system (email or SMS after the order) or through open forms (Opineo 'zwykle', TrustMate widget or QR/NFC). Publication is near real-time after moderation. TrustMate filters automatically before publication (behavioural and semantic filters, a 30-day limit per device). Zaufane.pl moderates every review before publication. Trusted Shops has a verification team for flagged reviews. Imported reviews (TrustMate, Trusted Shops) come from third-party platforms whose verification the importer cannot see. Every review links to a stable profile URL, and TrustMate also gives a per-review public identifier.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial for reading public pages; none for an official consumer API. Trusted Shops: the eTrusted API and SDKs are for shops; no consumer API was found (⚠ *(unverified)* an older public reviews API by shop ID was not tested). The public shop directory renders in JavaScript. robots.txt blocks a list of AI crawlers but not ClaudeBot. Opineo: no public API. Terms §6.1 ban access by bots, scripts or tools that automatically download or aggregate content. robots.txt blocks GPTBot and disallows /opinia/, /produkt/ and search URLs. Shop profiles at /opinie/<shop> answered a plain HTTP request (200). TrustMate: the client API sits under /integration/api and /public/api (both disallowed in robots.txt). Public profiles at /opinie/<shop-domain> server-render review JSON with verification flags, so they are machine-readable without a key, but the user terms ban 'automatyczne rozwiazania informatyczne'. Zaufane.pl: no public profiles; reviews show on shop sites, Google and eKomi certificates. MCP and skills: none found (gh search for trustmate, opineo, trusted shops and ekomi on 2026-10-15 found only shop-side plugins and a 2019 Opineo scraper, krzynio/Opineo.pl-scraper, 0 stars). Browser agent: works for human-initiated single lookups. Setup effort: a small skill that, given a shop domain, opens the TrustMate, Opineo and Trusted Shops pages in the user's browser and extracts rating, counts and the verified share, about 1-2 hours. Bulk scraping would break the terms.

**protocol support**

None found (no ACP, UCP, AP2, MCP, Klarna APP, Visa TAP or Web Bot Auth). TrustMate markets 'GEO' (visibility of reviews in AI assistants), which is marketing, not a protocol.

**open source and licence**

Closed: all four are proprietary services. Only shop-side SDKs and plugins exist on GitHub (e.g. trustedshops/trustedshops-ios-sdk, 6 stars, last push 2023; lcbrq/openmage-trustmate).

**account linking and data access**

Reading needs no account. Writing a review needs an email address, and for verified reviews the shop passes the buyer's email or phone and order number to the platform. TrustMate says the shop needs a legal basis and checkout notice for the invitation email. Trusted Shops Buyer Protection uses the order email and, optionally, an account. No payment credentials are needed. Cookie banners: decline non-essential cookies.

**automation legal risk**

Moderate for automated collection, low for manual reading. Opineo and TrustMate terms explicitly forbid automated access and aggregation, and Opineo blocks GPTBot. Reviews are third-party content and personal data (first names), so republishing them in a public vault note raises copyright and GDPR issues: store counts and short summaries, not review text. Trusted Shops robots.txt does not block ClaudeBot, but its terms of use were not opened. A low-volume, user-initiated lookup of one shop profile carries little practical risk; scheduled crawling does not.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Every platform is paid by the shops it rates, which is the main bias. Opineo: paying 'Sluchajacy' shops get the survey system whose 'Wiarygodne' reviews count double in rankings, and the Wiarygodne badge requires an average of at least 4.5 over 30 days; certificates and rankings are sold and promoted. TrustMate: sells widgets, Google stars, review translation and 'GEO' to shops; shops control invitation timing and can start mediation or withdraw product reviews under defined conditions. Trusted Shops: membership fees fund the trustmark and buyer protection. Zaufane.pl: paid by shops; reviews also feed Google seller ratings. Open-review channels (Opineo 'zwykle', TrustMate unverified) are the counterweight to shop-controlled invitations.

**ranking transparency**

Opineo publishes its ranking formula in the terms (weighted average of all reviews, Wiarygodne weight 2, zwykle weight 1) and a definition of positive (3.25 or higher) and negative (2.25 or lower) reviews. TrustMate publishes a weights table (verified 2; unverified, external and QR 1; withdrawn or in mediation 0). Trusted Shops says imported reviews do not count toward the overall score; its treatment of 'unverified' reviews was not stated on the page checked. None allows excluding sources on the consumer side except Opineo's 'Tylko Wiarygodne' filter.

**run to run consistency**

N/A. Not an AI tool; profile ratings are deterministic at a point in time.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Documented risks: selective invitations, where the shop decides which orders trigger invites and when; negative reviews withdrawn after compensation through OpiConnect, with Opineo showing the count; TrustMate mediation, which masks a review behind a notice and sets its weight to 0 for up to 21 days, so the average can be temporarily inflated, though the text can still be revealed; review-selling firms (UOKiK fined Opinie.pro and SN Marketing in Nov 2022, over PLN 70,000 combined, and SeoSem24 and Best-Review in Jul 2024); domain takeovers that keep old reviews (Ceneo item). Safeguards: order-number binding, per-device limits and automated filters (TrustMate), a verification team (Trusted Shops), pre-moderation (Zaufane.pl), DSA notice channels. For an LLM agent, review text is untrusted input and could carry prompt injection; extract counts and flags, not instructions.

**known failures**

(1) Ratings diverge sharply across platforms (Media Expert: Opineo 1.9/5 vs Ceneo 4.7/5 on the same day). (2) Opineo's terms disclaim any control of authenticity, yet the 'Wiarygodne' badge is conditional on a rating of at least 4.5. (3) TrustMate mediation temporarily removes negative reviews from the average. (4) Coverage is opt-in: a small trampoline shop may have no profile anywhere except open Opineo or Google reviews. (5) Zaufane.pl has no public profile pages, so its reviews are only visible on the shop's own widget and Google. (6) The Trusted Shops directory is JS-rendered and Polish coverage is unclear. (7) Merchant-side complaints: the Trusted Shops Shopify app is rated 2.1/5 from 20 reviews in its Polish listing (search result; merchants, not consumers). (8) A name clash between Ceneo 'Zaufane Opinie' and Zaufane.pl confuses research and buyers.

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

Opineo: UOKiK soft intervention in April 2021, together with Ceneo, over hiding negative reviews while a seller contacted the reviewer; Opineo agreed to show the number of removed negative reviews, which its profiles now do. No UOKiK decision against Trusted Shops, TrustMate or Zaufane.pl was found. Context: the EU review sweep of January 2022 (223 websites) found at least 55% potentially breaching the UCPD, and 104 did not inform consumers how reviews are collected. UOKiK fined review-selling firms in 2022 and 2024. A Spider's Web article (2 Apr 2026) claims stricter UOKiK review oversight from March 2026 with fines of up to 10% of turnover, but quotes only TrustMate's CEO and names no law (⚠ *(unverified)*; UOKiK's 10%-of-turnover fine for collective consumer interests predates 2026).

**⚠ buyer protection path**

Trusted Shops: Buyer Protection up to PLN 10,000 per order in certified shops, regardless of payment method, covering non-delivery, a refund not paid after withdrawal, shop insolvency and other listed cases; full terms are in the Buyer Auto Protection Terms PDF (⚠ *(unverified)* insurer, claim deadlines and registration window not opened). Opineo, TrustMate and Zaufane.pl give no financial protection, only dispute or mediation channels. Statutory rights against the seller always apply: non-conformity (rekojmia / niezgodnosc towaru z umowa), the 14-day withdrawal right for distance purchases, card chargeback or BLIK/PayU disputes depending on payment, UOKiK or a municipal consumer ombudsman, and ECC Poland for cross-border cases.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Useful for the seller step when the cheapest trampoline offer comes from an unfamiliar shop. Example (2026-10-15): the garden-decor shop aurora-garden.pl shows 4.9 from 1,346 TrustMate reviews with 25 of 26 visible reviews invitation-verified and a NIP on the profile, which can then be checked in the VAT white list. A shop with only open or unverified reviews, a recent run of delivery-damage complaints, or reviews hidden under mediation notices deserves caution for a 30-50 kg parcel whose return costs a lot. For a PLN 1,000-3,000 purchase, a Trusted Shops-certified shop adds PLN 10,000 Buyer Protection, which matters if a refund after returning a bulky trampoline is not paid. Limits: they say nothing about the trampoline itself (safety, EN 71-14, build quality), and many niche garden shops have no profile on any of these systems.

**workflow role**

Seller and shop check, after the price sweep and before purchase. Combine with KRS, CEIDG and the VAT white list (seller identity), Ceneo and Google shop ratings (cross-platform comparison), the GPSR listing check, and the payment method's chargeback rights. Trusted Shops Buyer Protection also belongs at the purchase step.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Free. Manual: about 5 minutes per shop (open the TrustMate or Opineo profile, filter to verified or last 12 months, read the negative reviews, check the trustmark validity). Agent-assisted in the user's browser: 2-3 page loads per shop and about 5-10k LLM tokens to extract rating, counts, verified share and recent negatives (⚠ *(unverified)* token estimate); for 3 candidate shops, roughly 15-30k tokens. No API cost; bulk automation is not allowed under the terms.

**evidence trail**

Moderate. Stable profile URLs (trustmate.io/opinie/<domain>, opineo.pl/opinie/<shop>, Trusted Shops certificate page) and per-review identifiers (TrustMate 'publicIdentifier'). Vault record: date; profile URL per platform; overall rating; total reviews; reviews in the last 12 months; verified vs unverified share; withdrawn or mediation count; 2-3 one-line summaries of recent negative themes (not verbatim text); trustmark status and Buyer Protection limit; the shop's own Omnibus disclosure text location. Keep screenshots in the non-published _raw area, because review texts are third-party content.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Invitation-based reviews are tied to real order numbers (TrustMate exposes per-review 'verified' and 'orderNumber' flags; Trusted Shops requires a transaction reference)
  - Trusted Shops Buyer Protection up to PLN 10,000 per order, free for buyers, independent of payment method
  - Disclosed verification and weighting rules (Opineo weights 2:1; TrustMate weights table and status labels) meet the Omnibus disclosure duty
  - Opineo is open, so non-client shops can still be reviewed, and it shows withdrawn-review counts after the 2021 UOKiK intervention
  - Free to read, with stable profile URLs for the evidence trail
- **weaknesses**:
  - Paid by the shops they rate; shops control invitations, mediation and some withdrawals
  - Ratings diverge sharply across platforms (Media Expert 1.9 on Opineo vs 4.7 on Ceneo)
  - No official consumer API; Opineo and TrustMate terms forbid automated access, so it is hard to drive from Claude Code at scale
  - Opt-in coverage: many niche shops have no profile; Zaufane.pl has no public profiles; Trusted Shops' Polish footprint is unclear
  - Nothing about the product itself, its safety or the seller's legal identity

**independent review consensus**

No independent Polish test of these platforms was found. Independent context: the EU review sweep of January 2022 (55% of 223 sites potentially non-compliant), the Bundeskartellamt's 2020 inquiry (portals rarely verify purchase beforehand), Stiftung Warentest 2019 on shop seals (secondary, old), and UOKiK's 2021 intervention against Opineo and Ceneo. Much recent Polish coverage is vendor-sourced: the TrustMate market-share claim (ITwiz, based on a company statement) and Spider's Web (Apr 2026, quoting only the TrustMate CEO). Platform pages are self-descriptions. Treat these as vendor-claimed.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY as data sources for automation; USE NOW manually as one seller signal, and use Trusted Shops Buyer Protection whenever the shop is certified. Deciding fact: they are paid by the shops, cover only opted-in shops (except Opineo's open reviews) and ban automated access, but invitation-verified review shares and PLN 10,000 buyer protection are real risk reducers for an unfamiliar shop. Best use: for each shortlisted unfamiliar shop, open its TrustMate, Opineo and Trusted Shops profiles in the browser, record rating, 12-month count, verified share and negative themes in the vault, cross-check against Ceneo and Google, and prefer a Trusted Shops-certified seller for the final purchase.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- Market share: TrustMate claims over 50% of Polish shops using external review systems (ITwiz, 23 Apr 2026, company statement, no method); no independent market data was found.
- Trusted Shops verification: the Polish page says only verified reviews with a unique transaction reference are shown ('zero tolerance'), while the German profile page lists 'unverified' reviews written proactively by users as one of three review types.
- Opineo authenticity: the Opineo terms (05.05.2025) say Opineo does not control or monitor review authenticity, while its marketing calls Wiarygodne Opinie 'the best way to verify shop quality', and the Wiarygodne badge is conditional on an average of at least 4.5.
- Ratings: Media Expert 1.9/5 on Opineo (161 reviews in 12 months; 14,741 total) vs 4.7/5 on Ceneo (3,430 reviews), both on 2026-10-15.
- Legal citation: TrustMate's /review-collection page cites 'art. 7aa' of the Polish Unfair Commercial Practices Act; the consolidated text (Dz.U. 2023 poz. 845) puts the duties in art. 6(4)(7) and art. 7(25)-(26). ⚠ *(unverified)* whether a later amendment added an art. 7aa.
- 2026 rule change: Spider's Web (2 Apr 2026) reports stricter review rules from March 2026 with fines of up to 10% of turnover and a 42% unverified-reviews figure, citing only TrustMate; no primary legal source or UOKiK statement was found to confirm a March 2026 change.
- Zaufane.pl: ITwiz says its clients are moving to TrustMate, but zaufane.pl was still live and taking sales enquiries on 2026-10-15.
- Name: 'Zaufane Opinie' in the research outline points to TrustMate and Zaufane.pl, but 'Zaufane Opinie' is the name of Ceneo's own purchase-verified review programme.

### Shop reputation and blocklists

**Verdict:** USE NOW (negative filter only) · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 6 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

A bundle of five unrelated reputation sources that are commonly used to vet a web shop before paying. (1) Lista Ostrzezen przed niebezpiecznymi stronami (lista.cert.pl, data at hole.cert.pl/domains/v2/): CERT Polska's statutory blocklist of fraudulent domains. (2) UOKiK consumer warnings ('ostrzezenia konsumenckie', uokik.gov.pl/bip/ostrzezenia-konsumenckie) plus UOKiK press releases and decision register. (3) ScamAdviser: an algorithmic 1-100 website trust score. (4) Trustpilot: an open review platform with TrustScores. (5) WHOIS/RDAP: domain registration data (NASK for .pl, other registries for gTLDs such as .shop). Role types: registry/blocklist, regulator register, algorithmic scorer, review platform, registration-data protocol. Central finding: no source in this bundle can prove that a shop is trustworthy. A hit is strong evidence of fraud; a miss proves nothing.

**vendor and ownership**

- **lista cert pl**: Run by CSIRT NASK (CERT Polska) inside NASK-PIB, the state research institute under the Polish digital-affairs ministry. Legal basis: art. 20 of the act of 28 July 2023 on combating abuse in electronic communication (consolidated text Dz.U. 2024 poz. 1803). The list exists under an agreement between the UKE President, the digital-affairs minister, NASK and telecom operators (original signatories Orange Polska, Polkomtel/Plus, P4/Play, T-Mobile Polska). Publicly funded.
- **uokik**: Urzad Ochrony Konkurencji i Konsumentow, the Polish government consumer and competition authority, Warsaw. Warnings are issued by decision of the UOKiK President.
- **scamadviser**: Maintained by Ecommerce Operations B.V. (Netherlands) according to its own FAQ; described as part of the Ecommerce Foundation since 2018 (Global Cyber Alliance profile). Founded 2012. General manager Jorij Abraham. Earns money from data feeds, API access, brand alerts and white-label products; commercial partners include Trend Micro (Foundation Partner since 2021), Group-IB, EBRAND and EverC.
- **trustpilot**: Trustpilot Group plc, Copenhagen, listed on the London Stock Exchange (TRST). Revenue from business subscriptions (review invitations, widgets, analytics). Trustpilot states that over 97% of businesses on the platform do not pay.
- **whois rdap**: For .pl: NASK-PIB as registry (whois.dns.pl, rdap.dns.pl). For gTLDs: each registry and registrar, reachable through the IANA bootstrap (e.g. rdap.org redirect). Public infrastructure, no commercial bias.

**lifecycle status**

All five are live, verified 2026-10-15. lista.cert.pl: launched March 2020 (gov.pl), statutory since the 2023 act; current data format is v2, where entries expire after 6 months unless re-added; the old v1 URLs (hole.cert.pl/domains/domains.txt) now return HTTP 301; the newest entry was inserted 2026-10-15T14:18Z. The 2025 actions log holds 244,344 'block' and 643 'unblock' actions. UOKiK consumer warnings: 20 entries in total from 30 Dec 2015 to 22 Apr 2025 (iGenius LLC); none since then. ScamAdviser: active since 2012; vendor-claimed database of 30,778,253 sites and 2,631,881 scam sites (API page, seen 2026-10-15). Trustpilot: active; vendor-claimed 400m+ active reviews (Dec 2025) and 7.8 million fake reviews removed in 2025; short-seller Grizzly Research attacked the company on 4 Dec 2025 (shares fell 32% that day; Trustpilot rejects the claims). NASK RDAP: available since 20 March 2025 (NASK news, secondary summary); WHOIS on port 43 answered on 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

Free for a consumer in every case (seen 2026-10-15). lista.cert.pl: free, including commercial use, no warranty. UOKiK: free public pages. WHOIS/RDAP: free. ScamAdviser: website free; Domain Trust Score API and Data Feed priced on quote by call volume, no public price list. ⚠ *(unverified)* A RapidAPI listing 'scamadviser-lite' (provider 'scamadviser1') was reported by search results as USD 0 for 20 requests/month, USD 39/month for 10,000 and USD 199/month for 100,000; the listing page did not render and its link to ScamAdviser was not confirmed. Trustpilot: reading is free; the official API requires a Trustpilot Business account with the API module (paid plans, price not published). Google Safe Browsing (an adjacent blocklist) is free for non-commercial use only; Google Web Risk is the paid commercial version.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: lista.cert.pl is fed by Polish reports (incydent.cert.pl, SMS forward to 8080, mObywatel) and blocks domains at participating Polish telcos' DNS; it contains many impersonations of Allegro (9,343 active entries), OLX (2,576), Vinted (1,817) and InPost (182), and fake outlets of brands sold in Poland. UOKiK: Polish regulator, warnings mostly about investment and pyramid schemes. WHOIS/RDAP for .pl from NASK. Trustpilot has a Polish interface (pl.trustpilot.com), but coverage of Polish shops is thin: Media Expert has 2,578 reviews, Zipro (a trampoline maker) has no profile. ScamAdviser covers any domain worldwide.
- **EU outside Poland**: lista.cert.pl lists domains on any TLD (most active entries are .com 36,454 and .shop 15,320) and is also used by Quad9 and NextDNS, but it is reported mainly by Polish users. Comparable national sources: Watchlist Internet and the Fake-Shop Detector (Austria, DACH focus, vendor-claimed 10,000+ fake shops) and the Verbraucherzentrale fake-shop finder (Germany); not tested here. ScamAdviser, Trustpilot and RDAP work EU-wide.
- **US**: ScamAdviser, Trustpilot and RDAP work globally. lista.cert.pl and UOKiK are Polish-only in scope.
- **language**: lista.cert.pl data is language-neutral (domain lists); CERT and UOKiK pages are in Polish with partial English. Trustpilot: Polish UI and reviews. ScamAdviser: multilingual site ⚠ *(unverified)* Polish UI not confirmed.
- **US only or agentic features**: None. No source here buys, pays or offers agentic checkout.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A - these sources assess the shop or domain, not products or variants.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A for price comparison. Shop coverage relevant to Poland, measured 2026-10-15: lista.cert.pl holds 125,845 active domains (rolling 6-month window since 2026-04-15) and added on average about 597 domains per day over the last 30 days. Active entries include brand-clone shops such as 4foutlet.shop, homla-outlet.shop, decathlon-outlet.top, jysk-limitedtimeoffer.shop, pepcoplsale.shop and two trampoline clones (trampoliny-sklep.shop, trampolinyoutlet-pl.shop). Trustpilot covers mainly large Polish retailers.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A - none of these sources tracks prices. UOKiK's July 2025 fake-shop release lists 'very large discounts, especially without the lowest price from the previous 30 days' as a warning sign, which links this check to the Omnibus item.

**total landed cost**

N/A - no cost data.

**review and seller verification**

- **grade**: partial - a negative filter only; none of the five sources can confirm a shop's legal identity or that it delivers
- **lista cert pl**: Proves: a listed domain was judged by CSIRT NASK to be fraudulent. The statutory test (art. 20(3)) is a domain whose primary purpose is to mislead users into giving up data or 'unfavourably disposing of their property', so fake shops qualify, not only credential phishing. Cannot prove: anything about an unlisted shop. Listing is reactive (anyone may report; CERT also acts on its own initiative), fraudsters register new domains daily, entries drop out after 6 months unless re-added, and a registered company that simply fails to deliver, a hidden dropshipper or a misleading but real trader is outside the criterion. Matching is per exact domain plus its subdomains, not the parent domain. The domain owner can object to the UKE President, who decides within 14 days (art. 21-22).
- **uokik warnings**: Proves: UOKiK formally suspected a specific trader of a practice that may cause significant losses. Cannot prove anything about shops: all 20 warnings issued since 2015 concern investment, pyramid, financial or telecom schemes; no online shop has ever been listed. UOKiK decisions and charges (decyzje.uokik.gov.pl, press releases) do name large retailers, e.g. Zalando, Temu, H&M, but for unfair practices, not fraud. UOKiK's 3 Jul 2025 release on fake shops gives red flags (social-media ads, odd TLDs such as .xyz/.lol/.top, 'first name + city' shop names, typo brand names, countdown timers, missing company data, Asian return addresses) and no list of shops.
- **scamadviser**: Proves: only a probability-like score from more than 40 criteria (technical set-up, domain age, hosting, contact details, reviews, blacklists). Its own FAQ says it relies partly on information 'whose accuracy cannot be directly verified', that owners can hide identities, and that it 'can't catch and report every single site'. The weights are not published, and no independent study linking scores to actual delivery was found. A co-founder admitted that similar fake sites can get different scores (Trend Micro interview, 2022). Cannot prove legal identity or delivery.
- **trustpilot**: Proves: what reviewers wrote, with labels showing whether a review was verified ('Zweryfikowane') or invitation-based, and notices such as 'company has not invited recently'. Cannot prove authenticity: anyone can review without proof of purchase, and Which? (27 Jul 2022) bought 19 fake 5-star reviews within 3 weeks, reaching a TrustScore of 4.6. Ratings diverge sharply between platforms: on 2026-10-15 Media Expert scored 3.4/5 on Trustpilot (2,578 reviews, 49% 1-star, 42% 5-star), 4.7/5 on Ceneo and 2.1/5 on Opineo (Ceneo item, same day).
- **whois rdap**: Proves: domain creation date, last change, expiry, registrar and, for .pl, only the registrant type ('individual' or 'organization'). NASK publishes no registrant identity, even for organisations (allegro.pl shows only 'organization'). The registrant type is not a reliable proxy for the operator: ceneo.pl, run by Ceneo.pl sp. z o.o., shows 'individual'. Example: the fake shop trampoliny-sklep.shop was registered 2026-05-19T07:15Z at Dynadot and entered the CERT list at 08:22Z the same day. A young domain is a red flag; an old domain is not a trust signal, because expired or taken-over domains keep their age (the Skyteel.pl case, 2020, Ceneo item).

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A for product safety (no Safety Gate, GPSR or certificate checks). These are fraud-safety checks. Automatable: lista.cert.pl lookup (local file), RDAP domain age, Trustpilot page read. Not automatable without breaking the vendor's gate: the ScamAdviser public score.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

N/A as a product-test source. Independent evidence about the tools themselves: Which? (27 Jul 2022) showed Trustpilot can be gamed. No independent accuracy study was found for ScamAdviser (a factually.co review notes the absence) or for lista.cert.pl. For lista.cert.pl the 2025 log shows 643 'unblock' actions against 244,344 'block' actions (0.26%). ⚠ *(unverified)* It is not documented whether 'unblock' means a corrected false positive, an upheld objection or a routine removal.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

lista.cert.pl is maintained 24/7, and CERT tells integrators to refresh every 5 minutes. People on a participating Polish mobile or fixed network, or on Quad9 or NextDNS, are redirected to a CERT warning page automatically. Full per-year 'actions_YYYY.log' files (2020 onward) allow a check of whether a domain was ever listed. ScamAdviser sells 'Scam & Brand Alerts' and score-change alerts to API customers. Trustpilot and RDAP have no consumer alerts for a shop (⚠ *(unverified)* for Trustpilot, not checked in its consumer app). An agent can watch a domain by re-checking the CERT file and RDAP before payment.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A - none of these sources can buy. Best use in an agent workflow is as a hard pre-payment gate: stop on any lista.cert.pl hit; require human review when the domain is younger than about 6 months, when the trader's identity is missing, or when Trustpilot or ScamAdviser show red flags.

**after sales and resale**

N/A. Trustpilot reviews sometimes describe return and complaint handling, which is anecdotal. Nothing covers spare parts, service or resale.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

lista.cert.pl: public reports plus CERT's own detection; each entry carries RegisterPositionId, DomainAddress, InsertDate and DeleteDate, but no reason or category. Live (newest entry minutes old on 2026-10-15). ScamAdviser: over 40 sources; data-feed files every 5 minutes; the cache API returns 503 when data is older than 30 days; a fresh scan can take up to 25 seconds. Trustpilot: user and invited reviews, live. UOKiK: HTML pages updated ad hoc (latest warning April 2025). NASK WHOIS: delay of at most 15 minutes behind the registry; RDAP responses carry a 'last update of RDAP database' timestamp. Answers are backed by the source record (CERT entry, RDAP JSON, review page), so each can be cited.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full for lista.cert.pl and WHOIS/RDAP; partial for Trustpilot and ScamAdviser; none for the UOKiK warning list (HTML only, though trivially fetchable)
- **lista cert pl**: No authentication. Downloads under https://hole.cert.pl/domains/v2/: domains.txt (2.5 MB, one domain per line), domains.json (22 MB with insert/delete dates), domains.csv, domains.xml, domains_adblock.txt, domains_hosts.txt, domains_mikrotik.rsc, domains_rpz.db, plus actions_YYYY.log history. API spec 'certpl_lista_ostrzezen_api_v2.pdf' and the repo CERT-Polska/warning-list-tools (BSD-3-Clause, 21 stars, last push 2026-10-09). From Claude Code: curl the txt file once a day and grep the shop domain and its parents. Setup about 5 minutes. No MCP server found.
- **whois rdap**: RDAP JSON at https://rdap.dns.pl/domain/<name>.pl and via https://rdap.org/domain/<name> for gTLDs; NASK WHOIS on whois.dns.pl port 43. All three were queried successfully on 2026-10-15. Community MCP servers: bharathvaj-ganesan/whois-mcp (60 stars, updated 2026-10-11), modelcontextprotocol-servers/whois-mcp (21 stars), simplebytes-com/rdap-mcp (1 star); none audited here. Setup: minutes.
- **scamadviser**: Official API (docs at https://api.scamadviser.cloud/docs/): Single cache API, Single API, Batch API v2, mutations and Data Feed v2; API key issued by the product team; monthly call quota; result fields include trust score 0-100, score reasons, WHOIS, aggregated reviews and technologies. Pricing on quote. The public web checker requires pressing a 'verify you are human' button; WebFetch returned no score for the two tested domains, and that gate should not be automated. Other routes: a Maltego transform (some data without an API key) and a community Apify actor (automation-lab/scamadviser-trust-score-scraper), which scrapes the site against its evident intent. No MCP server found.
- **trustpilot**: Official REST API: GET https://api.trustpilot.com/v1/business-units/find?name=<domain> with an 'apikey' header, then the public business-unit and review endpoints. Keys come from a Trustpilot Business account with the API module (third-party guides; Trustpilot's docs do not say who may obtain a key). robots.txt (checked 2026-10-15) allows Claude-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and GPTBot except /evaluate and /error, blocks 'anthropic-ai', and disallows everything for '*'. A WebFetch of pl.trustpilot.com/review/www.mediaexpert.pl worked. Community Apify scrapers exist. No official MCP found.
- **uokik**: No API. The register page uokik.gov.pl/bip/ostrzezenia-konsumenckie (20 entries, paginated) and the monthly sitemaps uokik.gov.pl/blog-posts-YYYY-MM.xml can be fetched and grepped. The decision register decyzje.uokik.gov.pl has no API.
- **adjacent**: Google Safe Browsing API v4 covers malware, unwanted software and social-engineering sites; Google labels v4 deprecated and non-commercial only, with Web Risk as the paid route. It does not target fake shops explicitly.

**protocol support**

None of ACP, UCP, AP2, Klarna APP, Visa TAP or Web Bot Auth. Relevant standards: RDAP (IETF JSON protocol), DNS RPZ and adblock formats for the CERT list. These checks would sit in front of any agent-commerce protocol as an independent pre-payment gate.

**open source and licence**

lista.cert.pl data: open, usable by anyone for any purpose including commercial, no guarantees of completeness or accuracy (CERT terms); tools repo BSD-3-Clause. UOKiK pages: public information. RDAP/WHOIS: open protocol, data subject to registry terms. ScamAdviser: closed. Trustpilot: closed.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Nothing needed for lista.cert.pl, RDAP/WHOIS, UOKiK or reading Trustpilot. A local copy of the CERT list lets an agent check domains without sending browsing history anywhere. The Trustpilot API needs a business account; the ScamAdviser API needs a contract. ScamAdviser's browser extension necessarily sees visited URLs ⚠ *(unverified)* (its data handling was not reviewed). GDPR: NASK and most gTLD registries redact registrant personal data, so WHOIS cannot identify a sole trader.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Low for lista.cert.pl (explicitly free for any use) and for RDAP/WHOIS at personal volumes ⚠ *(unverified)* (NASK's WHOIS query limits were not checked). Low for fetching UOKiK pages. Medium for Trustpilot: robots.txt permits user-triggered Claude fetches of review pages, but bulk scraping is disallowed for generic agents and the terms were not retrieved. High for ScamAdviser web scraping: the site gates scores behind a human-verification click; use the official API or a manual check instead.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

lista.cert.pl and UOKiK: public bodies, no commercial bias; the risk is false positives, handled by the UKE objection route. ScamAdviser: sells data, API access, brand-protection alerts and white-label tools; site owners can contest scores by contact form with no formal appeal process; no paid ranking was found. Trustpilot: business subscriptions buy invitation tools that tend to raise scores; Grizzly Research (Dec 2025) alleged that Trustpilot pressures businesses into subscriptions and protects subscribers' ratings, which Trustpilot 'categorically rejects'. WHOIS/RDAP: none.

**ranking transparency**

lista.cert.pl: binary listing with the statutory criterion public, but no per-entry reason in the data. ScamAdviser: shows positive and negative highlights per site; weights undisclosed. Trustpilot: per-profile transparency section explaining how reviews are collected and moderated, plus verified and invited labels. UOKiK: each warning is a formal decision. Sponsored placement does not apply.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - not AI tools. Note: ScamAdviser scores change as data refreshes, and its co-founder acknowledged inconsistent scores across similar fake sites. CERT entries are timestamped and deterministic.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Fraudsters rotate disposable domains, e.g. clusters such as allegro.pl-sklep7produkt512812497.shop with OLX, Vinted and Allegro Lokalnie variants, so a blocklist always lags new domains. Trustpilot reviews can be bought (Which? 2022); Trustpilot says it removed 4.5 million fake reviews in 2024 (7.4% of submissions) and 7.8 million in 2025 (vendor figures). ScamAdviser can be gamed with aged domains and seeded reviews. When an agent reads Trustpilot pages, review text is untrusted input that could carry prompt-injection attempts; treat it as data.

**known failures**

- Treating absence as trust: a shop missing from lista.cert.pl or the UOKiK warnings is unproven, not verified.
- The UOKiK warning list is the wrong tool for shops: 20 entries since 2015, all schemes or financial firms, latest April 2025.
- lista.cert.pl entries expire after 6 months; a domain listed in April 2026 can silently drop out in October 2026 unless re-added. Check the actions logs for history.
- ScamAdviser: opaque weights, unverified inputs, no independent validation, public score gated against automation.
- Trustpilot: thin coverage of Polish SMEs (no profile for Zipro), purchasable fake reviews, large rating divergence from Ceneo and Opineo.
- WHOIS for .pl hides the registrant even for companies; the registrant type can mislead (ceneo.pl shows 'individual').
- Google Safe Browsing v4 is deprecated and not built for fake shops.

**regulatory enforcement history**

lista.cert.pl: objection route to the UKE President, then an administrative court; no rulings found. ScamAdviser: none found. Trustpilot: no regulatory decision found; the main controversy is the Grizzly Research short report (4 Dec 2025) and Trustpilot's rebuttal (5 Dec 2025); Trustpilot has itself sued fake-review buyers (Global Migrate case). UOKiK: N/A as a target.

**buyer protection path**

These sources give no protection. If a shop turns out to be fraudulent: report the domain to CERT (incydent.cert.pl or SMS to 8080), report to the police, and contact the bank at once; UOKiK points to a card chargeback as the most likely recovery route. Use the rzecznik konsumentow or Inspekcja Handlowa for disputes with Polish traders, and ECC Poland for traders in other EU states. Card or buyer-protected platforms beat BLIK or bank transfer, which are hard to reverse.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Good as a cheap fraud filter, weak as a trust signal. Trampoline example (2026-10-15): the CERT list contains trampoliny-sklep.shop and trampolinyoutlet-pl.shop, the typical 'trampoline outlet' clone advertised on social media; the first was blocklisted about an hour after registration. For a real Polish garden-equipment shop selling a 305 cm trampoline at PLN 800-2,300, the bundle typically returns: no CERT hit, a domain age, probably no Trustpilot profile (Zipro has none) and an opaque ScamAdviser score. That says little, so seller registers (CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list) and purchase-verified reviews (Ceneo Zaufane Opinie) must carry the decision.

**workflow role**

Seller check, step one: run immediately before payment for any shop that is not a major known retailer or marketplace. Combine with: seller registers (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list with bank-account check, VIES), purchase-verified review sources (Ceneo, Opineo, Allegro seller ratings), the Omnibus 30-day price field as a fake-promotion check, and payment by card.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Per shop: CERT check is one grep of a 2.5 MB file (download once a day), under 1 second, PLN 0. RDAP: one HTTP request, PLN 0. Trustpilot: one page fetch, PLN 0. ScamAdviser: one manual click, about 30 seconds, PLN 0. UOKiK: one page, PLN 0. For three shortlisted shops: about 10 seconds automated plus about 2 minutes of manual ScamAdviser and Trustpilot reading, PLN 0 in total. The ScamAdviser API route has no published price.

**evidence trail**

Good for CERT and RDAP, which return citable machine records. Suggested vault record (keep in content/_raw): check time (UTC); shop domain; CERT result (hit with RegisterPositionId and InsertDate, or 'not listed in v2 file downloaded at <time>'); RDAP JSON excerpt (registration, last changed, expiration, registrar, registrant type); Trustpilot URL, score, review count, share of 1-star reviews, verified or invited labels, screenshot; ScamAdviser score and highlights, screenshot; UOKiK: 'no warning' with the register URL. State explicitly that 'not listed' is not evidence of trust.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - lista.cert.pl is official, free, machine-readable, updated 24/7 and fast: a trampoline clone shop was listed within about 1 hour of registration
  - The statutory criterion covers fake shops (unfavourable disposal of property), not only credential phishing
  - RDAP/WHOIS gives a free, citable domain age, a strong red flag for brand-new 'outlet' shops
  - Trustpilot pages expose verified and invited labels and invitation notices, and Claude-User fetches are allowed by robots.txt
  - Everything is free for a consumer, and the CERT list and RDAP need no account
- **weaknesses**:
  - No source proves trust; absence from every list is compatible with fraud
  - The UOKiK warning list has never covered an online shop (20 entries since 2015)
  - CERT entries expire after 6 months and listing is reactive
  - ScamAdviser is opaque and gated against automation; its API is priced on quote only
  - Trustpilot is manipulable, sparse for Polish SMEs and divergent from Polish review platforms; .pl WHOIS hides the registrant

**independent review consensus**

Limited independent evidence. Which? (27 Jul 2022, hands-on) showed Trustpilot accepted 19 bought 5-star reviews in 3 weeks. A factually.co fact-check found no independent validation of ScamAdviser scores against delivery outcomes. No independent audit of lista.cert.pl accuracy was found. Official consumer advice agrees on method: NASK's guide 'Okazja czy pulapka?' (Nov 2025) tells buyers to check seller data in CEIDG or KRS and read independent reviews, and UOKiK (Jul 2025) lists red flags rather than shops. Trend Micro, which interviewed ScamAdviser's co-founder, is a ScamAdviser partner, so it is not independent.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW, as a negative filter only. Deciding fact: lista.cert.pl and RDAP are free, official or standard, machine-readable and catch blatant clone shops quickly, but nothing in this bundle can certify a shop. Best use: a Claude Code pre-payment script that greps the daily CERT file and pulls RDAP age, then stops or escalates to the seller-register checks; read Trustpilot and ScamAdviser manually only for unknown shops, and never count 'not listed' as a pass.

**conflicting evidence**

- Scope of lista.cert.pl: the task note says it covers only phishing and credential theft. The statute (art. 20(3)) covers domains that mislead users into 'unfavourable disposal of property', and the live data on 2026-10-15 held fake shops such as trampoliny-sklep.shop and 4foutlet.shop. Both sides agree that absence is not a trust signal.
- Daily volume: about 265 domains per day (older CERT figure in search snippets), about 670 per day in 2025 (secondary coverage of the CERT 2025 report: almost 250,000 domains in 2025), and about 597 per day measured over the last 30 days from the live file.
- ScamAdviser location and entity: Amsterdam (Global Cyber Alliance profile) vs London (CB Insights); its FAQ names Ecommerce Operations B.V.
- Trustpilot integrity: Grizzly Research (Dec 2025) alleges subscription pressure and selective moderation; Trustpilot says the report contains factual inaccuracies and that over 97% of businesses do not pay.
- Media Expert shop rating on 2026-10-15: 3.4/5 on Trustpilot (2,578 reviews) vs 4.7/5 on Ceneo (3,430) vs 2.1/5 on Opineo (14,741), the last two from the Ceneo item.
- Retirement of CERT list v1: a search snippet dates it to 1 June 2025; the CERT page opened did not state the date, but the v1 URLs now return HTTP 301.

### Seller identity registers

**Verdict:** USE NOW · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 4 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

The four public registers that establish who a seller legally is before you pay. CEIDG (Centralna Ewidencja i Informacja o Dzialalnosci Gospodarczej): register of Polish sole traders and civil-partnership partners. KRS (Krajowy Rejestr Sadowy): court register of companies (sp. z o.o., S.A., partnerships, foundations). VAT white list (Wykaz podatnikow VAT, 'biala lista'): Ministry of Finance list of VAT status and the bank accounts each taxpayer has reported. VIES: the European Commission's validator of EU VAT numbers across member-state databases. Useful adjuncts: GUS REGON (BIR1 API) and KRZ (Krajowy Rejestr Zadluzonych, insolvency and restructuring). Role type: registry.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

All public, no commercial bias. CEIDG: run for the minister responsible for the economy and published via biznes.gov.pl and the data warehouse dane.biznes.gov.pl ⚠ *(unverified)* (current ministry name not re-checked). KRS: Ministry of Justice and the registry courts; Open API api-krs.ms.gov.pl. VAT white list: Ministry of Finance / National Revenue Administration (KAS), legal basis art. 96b of the VAT act, live since 1 Sep 2019. VIES: European Commission (DG TAXUD), which queries each member state's national VAT database in real time. GUS REGON: Statistics Poland. KRZ: Ministry of Justice.

**lifecycle status**

All live, verified by API calls on 2026-10-15. VAT white list: API documentation v1.6.1 dated 12 Oct 2026 (previous v1.6.0 dated 1 Jan 2025). From 15 Oct 2026 the production base URL is https://wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl/api/; the old https://wl-api.mf.gov.pl stays available until 1 Dec 2026. Both answered on 2026-10-15. History goes back about 5 years: a 2021 date returned data, a 2019 date returned error WL-118 ('date before register range'). KRS Open API: live; the test extract showed 'stan z dnia 09.09.2026'. VIES REST: live, and the check-status endpoint reported all member states available. CEIDG data-warehouse API v3: live (HTTP 401 without a token); integrator docs ship as a .7z archive; CEIDG-1 form schemas are dated 01.01.2026 and 14.10.2026. KRZ: covers proceedings opened since 1 Dec 2021.

**cost model**

Free in every case (seen 2026-10-15). VAT white list, KRS Open API and VIES REST: free with no key. CEIDG API: free after registering for the CEIDG data warehouse with a biznes.gov.pl account and Profil Zaufany; an API key is e-mailed. GUS BIR1: free user key requested by e-mail (regon_bir@stat.gov.pl); a public test key works against an anonymised test database. Commercial aggregators (e.g. Compabase, nipregon) resell combined data; not needed for a consumer.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Full: CEIDG for sole traders, KRS for companies, VAT white list for VAT status and bank accounts, KRZ for insolvency. All return Polish-language field values.
- **EU outside Poland**: VIES validates VAT numbers in all EU member states (plus XI for Northern Ireland). Name and address come back only where the member state discloses them: PL returned the name and address on 2026-10-15; DE returned validity only, with name and address shown as '---' (Zalando SE). Several third-party tools report the same for Spain ⚠ *(unverified)* (not tested). For company details in other states, use national registers (e.g. Handelsregister) or the EU BRIS search, not tested here.
- **US**: N/A - no coverage. For non-EU sellers (e.g. Chinese marketplace sellers) these registers say nothing; rely on the marketplace's trader disclosure and buyer protection.
- **language**: Polish register UIs and Polish JSON field values (e.g. statusVat 'Czynny'); VIES in English and other EU languages.
- **US only or agentic features**: None. Read-only checks; no purchase features.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A - registers identify the seller, not products.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A - no prices. Coverage of sellers: every Polish trader must be in CEIDG or KRS. Only VAT-registered taxpayers (active or exempt) have bank accounts on the white list. Only taxpayers registered for intra-EU trade (VAT-UE) show as valid in VIES.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A - no price data.

**total landed cost**

N/A. Indirectly relevant: the seller's registered seat (KRS, CEIDG, VIES) tells you whether warranty and withdrawal claims run against a Polish or a foreign trader, which affects return-shipping cost and the dispute route for bulky goods.

**review and seller verification**

- **grade**: full for legal identity, VAT status and bank-account ownership; none for reputation or delivery reliability
- **ceidg**: Proves that a sole trader exists, its status (active, suspended, resumed or deleted), start date, business and delivery addresses, NIP, REGON and PKD codes, and any website or e-mail the trader declared. Cannot prove that a given web shop is run by that trader unless the domain matches the declared website; declared contact data is self-reported.
- **krs**: Proves that a company exists, its legal form, seat, share capital, management board, representation rules, PKD codes, and entries on liquidation or bankruptcy (section 6). The JSON extract masks personal data (e.g. names as 'P********', PESEL as '8**********'); the PDF extract is needed for full names. Cannot prove that a given website belongs to the company.
- **vat white list**: Proves VAT status on a chosen date (e.g. 'Czynny' = active), NIP, REGON, KRS number, registered addresses and the bank accounts the taxpayer reported to the tax office. Also supports a reverse lookup: given an account number from a shop's transfer instructions, it returns the owning taxpayer (verified with a Ceneo account number), and a 'check' call returns TAK/NIE for a NIP-account pair. Cannot prove: that the shop really is that taxpayer (fraudsters paste real firms' NIPs), anything about payments through gateways (PayU, Przelewy24, BLIK go to the operator's account, not the shop's), or anything about small traders not registered for VAT. 'hasVirtualAccounts: true' means some accounts are virtual or masked.
- **vies**: Proves an EU VAT number is valid for intra-EU trade on the query date, plus name and address where the member state discloses them. Cannot prove domestic VAT status: a Polish trader that is active for VAT but not registered for VAT-UE shows as invalid, so use the white list for Polish sellers.
- **krz**: Proves whether bankruptcy, restructuring or enforcement proceedings opened since 1 Dec 2021 exist against a trader; older cases may be missing. No public API.
- **identity cloning check**: A fake shop that copies a real company's identity can be caught by cross-checking: the shop's domain and e-mail domain against the CEIDG or KRS website entry; the transfer account against the white list for that same NIP; the phone and address against the register. A mismatch is a red flag even when the NIP is 'active'.
- **legal hook**: Art. 12(1)(2) of the Polish consumer rights act requires a distance seller to state, before the contract, its identifying data, in particular its business name, the authority that registered it and its registration number. Missing data is itself a warning sign.

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A for product safety. Marginal use for GPSR: when a listing names an EU manufacturer or EU responsible person, VIES and KRS can confirm that the entity exists.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - registers, not product tests.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

No consumer alerts from the public APIs. The white list and KRS accept a date parameter or show the extract date, so an agent can re-run the check on the payment date. Commercial monitoring services exist but were not tested. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether the CEIDG data warehouse offers change notifications was not confirmed.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A - checks only, no purchasing. Ideal as a hard gate before any payment step: the NIP exists and is active, the registered name matches the shop's legal notice, and for a bank transfer the account is on the white list for that NIP (check = TAK). Otherwise escalate to a human and do not pay.

**after sales and resale**

The registers give the legal address for complaints, returns and statutory warranty claims. KRS section 6 and KRZ show liquidation or insolvency, which makes long warranty claims (e.g. on trampoline frame parts) risky. Nothing covers spare parts or resale.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

VAT white list: tax-office registration data; API answers for any date in about the last 5 years; a hashed flat file (NIP-account pairs, including virtual accounts) is published daily and updated once per working day; each response has a requestId and requestDateTime. KRS: court register; the extract states 'stan z dnia' and the date of the last entry. CEIDG: live register built from traders' own applications. VIES: real-time query to the member state; may fail with a member-state-unavailable error. KRZ: proceedings since Dec 2021. Every answer comes straight from an official source and can be cited.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full - three of the four registers have keyless official APIs that worked from the command line on 2026-10-15; CEIDG needs a free token
- **vat white list**: No authentication. GET https://wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl/api/search/nip/{nip}?date=YYYY-MM-DD; /search/nips/{up to 30 comma-separated}; /search/bank-account/{nrb}?date=; /check/nip/{nip}/bank-account/{nrb}?date=. Limits (MF page): 'search' 100 queries per day with up to 30 subjects each; 'check' up to 5,000 ⚠ *(unverified)* (MF does not say whether per query or per day); a separate WL2 API allows 50,000 queries per day. Exceeding a limit blocks access until midnight. Test environment: wykazpodatnikowvat-test.mf.gov.pl. Error codes seen: WL-115 (invalid NIP), WL-118 (date out of range). Migrate any code from wl-api.mf.gov.pl before 1 Dec 2026.
- **krs**: No authentication. GET https://api-krs.ms.gov.pl/api/krs/OdpisAktualny/{krs}?rejestr=P&format=json (also OdpisPelny; rejestr=S for associations). Lookup works by KRS number only, so chain NIP to the white list's 'krs' field, then to KRS. Name search exists only through an undocumented endpoint behind wyszukiwarka-krs.ms.gov.pl (used by soba-labs/krs-mcp), which may change without notice.
- **ceidg**: GET https://dane.biznes.gov.pl/api/ceidg/v3/firmy?nip={nip} with an 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT>' header; returns HTTP 401 without one (verified). Access: register for the CEIDG data warehouse at dane.biznes.gov.pl (portal page 034872) with a biznes.gov.pl account and Profil Zaufany; the API key arrives by e-mail. Documentation: the 'Hurtownia Danych API v3' archive on akademia.biznes.gov.pl. ⚠ *(unverified)* One third-party note measured a limit of about 50 requests per 180 seconds and reports that the token payload contains the account holder's PESEL, so keep the token out of repositories; 204 means no entry (e.g. a KRS company).
- **vies**: No authentication. GET https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/rest-api/ms/{CC}/vat/{number}; POST /rest-api/check-vat-number (returns a consultation number when you supply your own VAT number as requester, per third-party docs); GET /rest-api/check-status. The SOAP checkVatService also exists. No published rate limit was found.
- **gus regon**: BIR1.1 SOAP API (WS-Addressing, session token); free key by e-mail. Community MCP SmartMobileHouse/regon-mcp (MIT, 1 star, Aug 2026) wraps it and defaults to the public test key.
- **krz**: No public API; a third-party audit reports HTTP 403 from the site's WAF for automated access. Use manually at krz.ms.gov.pl.
- **mcp servers**: All community-built, low adoption, unaudited here. bartosz-kuc/honest-nip-krs-mcp (Python, MIT, 0 stars, created 2026-07-22, last push 2026-09-27; tools lookup_by_nip, check_bank_account, lookup_by_krs; no keys). soba-labs/krs-mcp (Node 22, MIT, 2 stars, last push 2026-10-15; tools search_companies, get_company, get_company_full, get_board; returns provenance JSON with source URL and retrieval time). VIES: vzeman/vies-mcp-server, ShepDogSk/check-vat-vies-mcp, bartosz-kuc/honest-vies-mcp (0-1 stars). emilpinski/mcp-polish-data (KRS, CEIDG, GUS BDL; 0 stars). Commercial: ContentWriterco/Compabase-MCP.
- **skill and setup**: No Claude skill was found. Writing one is easy: three curl calls (white list, KRS, VIES) need no keys; about 30-60 minutes to build a skill that saves the raw JSON into the vault. CEIDG adds a one-off registration with Profil Zaufany ⚠ *(unverified)* (approval time not documented). Browser-agent fallback: aplikacja.ceidg.gov.pl, wyszukiwarka-krs.ms.gov.pl, podatki.gov.pl white-list search and the VIES web form all work manually.

**protocol support**

N/A - plain REST/JSON (white list, KRS, CEIDG, VIES REST) and SOAP (VIES, GUS BIR). No agent-commerce protocol. These checks are protocol-independent and can sit in front of any ACP/UCP/AP2 checkout as a seller-identity gate.

**open source and licence**

Registers: official public data (KRS, CEIDG and the white list are public by law). MCP wrappers listed above: MIT-licensed, community-maintained, 0-2 stars.

**account linking and data access**

None for the white list, KRS or VIES. CEIDG API: your own biznes.gov.pl account and Profil Zaufany identity, so the token is tied to you personally. VIES can optionally take your VAT number as requester. GDPR: sole traders' register data is personal data, public by law, but republishing it in a public vault note is unnecessary; store raw register responses only in the non-published content/_raw area and cite the NIP and check result in published notes.

**automation legal risk**

Low. These are official machine interfaces intended for automated checks. Respect the white list quota (block until midnight on breach) and the CEIDG terms. Avoid the undocumented KRS search endpoint for anything critical, and do not try to get around the KRZ WAF.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

None - public registers with no ads, affiliates or ranking. Commercial aggregators and paid MCPs layering ratings on top add their own scoring, which is not part of these registers.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - authoritative records, no ranking or recommendation.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - deterministic and date-parameterised; the same query returns the same record for the same date.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

The data is authoritative, but the link between a web shop and a register entry is the weak point: fake shops display real companies' NIP and KRS numbers. Defend by cross-checking the domain, e-mail domain, phone and transfer account against the register (see review_and_seller_verification). Account checks protect only direct bank transfers. Register fields are plain data; prompt injection is not a realistic vector, but treat all returned text as data.

**known failures**

- VIES returns no name or address for some member states (DE verified on 2026-10-15), so it cannot confirm that a German Amazon.de seller is the company it claims to be
- VIES shows Polish sellers as invalid unless they are registered for VAT-UE, even when the white list shows them active for VAT
- White list: 100 search queries per day; the base URL changed on 15 Oct 2026 (old URL ends 1 Dec 2026); small traders not registered for VAT do not appear
- Payments through PayU, Przelewy24 or BLIK go to the operator's account, so the account check applies only to direct transfers
- The KRS API needs the KRS number (no official NIP or name search) and masks personal data in JSON
- The CEIDG API needs a token obtained with Profil Zaufany; the rate limit is undocumented publicly
- KRZ has no API and only covers cases since Dec 2021
- None of the registers says anything about delivery reliability, reviews or product safety

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the registers themselves. Related enforcement showing why identity checks matter: UOKiK charged Zalando, Booking and Travelist on 4 Sep 2023 over failing to disclose whether sellers are businesses and how duties are split between platform and seller, and examined 'who is the seller on the Temu platform'.

**buyer protection path**

The registers do not protect a buyer; they make the protection enforceable. A verified legal name and address are needed for a statutory warranty (rekojmia) claim, a 14-day withdrawal, a complaint to the rzecznik konsumentow or Inspekcja Handlowa, an ECC Poland case against an EU seller (VIES or the national register confirms the state), or a claim against an insolvent seller (KRZ). Paying by card keeps chargeback available. Paying by transfer only to an account the white list confirms for that NIP reduces the risk of misdirected payment.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

High value for little effort. Trampoline example: a small garden-equipment shop offers a 305 cm trampoline at PLN 1,200 and asks for a bank transfer. The agent reads the NIP from the shop's terms; the white list returns name, status 'Czynny' and the account list; the check call confirms the transfer account (TAK/NIE); the KRS number from the same response pulls the company extract (seat, board, no liquidation entry), or for a sole trader the CEIDG API (token) confirms status and declared website. For an Amazon.de marketplace seller with a German VAT number, VIES confirms validity only, without a name. Total time about 10 seconds automated per shop.

**workflow role**

Seller check: step two, after the blocklist and reputation screen and before payment. Combine with lista.cert.pl and RDAP domain age (fraud filter), purchase-verified reviews (Ceneo, Opineo, Allegro), marketplace trader disclosure, and a card or other buyer-protected payment.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Arithmetic for one purchase with three shortlisted Polish shops: 1 white-list call with up to 30 NIPs batched (1 of 100 daily search queries) + 3 KRS or CEIDG calls + up to 3 white-list account checks + optional VIES calls = about 7-10 HTTP requests, under 10 seconds, PLN 0. Manual equivalent: about 5 minutes per shop across four web forms. One-off setup: about 1 hour to write a Claude Code skill; CEIDG registration extra.

**evidence trail**

Excellent: every source returns a citable machine record. The white list returns a requestId plus requestDateTime (an official query identifier). The KRS extract states 'stan z dnia' and the last entry date. VIES returns requestDate, plus a consultation number when a requester VAT number is supplied. CEIDG returns JSON. Suggested vault record (raw JSON in content/_raw): check date and time; shop domain; NIP as printed on the shop; white-list result (name, statusVat, krs, regon, requestId, account check TAK/NIE with the account checked); KRS or CEIDG status and seat; VIES result for EU sellers; any mismatch noted.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Official, free and authoritative; three of four have keyless REST APIs that worked from curl on 2026-10-15
  - The white list's reverse bank-account search and TAK/NIE check directly expose transfer-to-wrong-account scams
  - Date-parameterised history (about 5 years on the white list) and official request IDs make an audit trail
  - Community MCP servers already wrap the white list, KRS, REGON and VIES for Claude Code
  - The legal duty to disclose identity (art. 12 consumer rights act) makes missing data itself a red flag
- **weaknesses**:
  - Nothing on reputation, delivery or product quality
  - Identity cloning: a real NIP on a fake shop passes the register check unless domain, account and contacts are cross-checked
  - VIES gives no name for Germany and marks non-VAT-UE Polish sellers invalid
  - CEIDG API gated by a Profil Zaufany registration; KRS has no official NIP or name search; KRZ has no API
  - Account checks are irrelevant when paying through payment gateways

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of register accuracy was found, and none is really needed: they are the legal source of truth. Official consumer advice agrees on using them: NASK's guide 'Okazja czy pulapka?' (Nov 2025) tells buyers to check seller data in CEIDG or KRS. Accounting-software vendors and tax portals (Comarch, infakt, fakturaxl, poradnikprzedsiebiorcy) consistently explain that VIES covers only VAT-UE registrations and that the white list is the Polish domestic check. Multiple third-party VIES tools corroborate the German no-name behaviour that was reproduced live here.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW. Deciding fact: the white list, KRS and VIES are keyless official APIs that answered from the command line today, and the white list's NIP-account check directly blocks the most common transfer fraud. Best use: a Claude Code skill (or the honest-nip-krs-mcp / krs-mcp servers after a code review) that, before any payment, resolves the shop's NIP, confirms status, matches name, domain and account, and saves the raw JSON with requestId into the vault's _raw area.

**conflicting evidence**

- White-list 'check' limit: the MF page states 'up to 5,000' without saying whether per query or per day; 'search' is clearly 100 queries per day with 30 subjects each.
- White-list base URL: wl-api.mf.gov.pl is used by most existing tools and MCP servers; MF moved production to wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl on 15 Oct 2026 and keeps the old URL only until 1 Dec 2026. Both answered on 2026-10-15.
- VIES name disclosure: third-party tools say Germany returns empty fields; the live call on 2026-10-15 returned the placeholder '---' rather than empty values, so parsers must handle both.
- CEIDG API rate limit: about 50 requests per 180 seconds per a third-party measurement (Sep-Oct 2026); no official figure found.

#### fields the agent listed as uncertain

- alerts and monitoring
