### Omnibus lowest-price field

**Verdict:** USE NOW (red-flag reader) · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 6 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

The mandatory 'najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka' (lowest price in the 30 days before the reduction) that a Polish trader must show next to every announced price reduction of a specific product. Legal basis: art. 4(2)-(5) of the act of 9 May 2014 on informing about prices of goods and services (consolidated Dz.U. 2023 poz. 168), in force since 1 Jan 2023; it implements art. 6a of Directive 98/6/EC as amended by the Omnibus Directive (EU) 2019/2161. Role type: regulation, and an on-page data field. For a buying agent it is a seller-declared reference price that can be read from the page and must be checked against independent price history.

**vendor and ownership**

No vendor; it is a legal duty of each trader. Enforcement: the UOKiK President (practices infringing collective consumer interests, fines up to 10% of turnover) and the voivodeship inspectors of Inspekcja Handlowa (art. 6: up to PLN 20,000 per decision, up to PLN 40,000 after three breaches within 12 months). EU interpretation: Commission guidance on art. 6a (adopted 17 Dec 2021) and the CJEU. The field itself is generated by the trader or its platform: Allegro computes it automatically per offer; Shoper computes it after the merchant enables it; WooCommerce shops often use the iworks 'Omnibus' plugin (10,000+ active installs).

**lifecycle status**

In force and increasingly enforced; verified 2026-10-15. EU rule applies from 28 May 2022; Polish rule from 1 Jan 2023 (consolidated text Dz.U. 2023 poz. 168, ELI status 'in force'). UOKiK guidance published 2023 and still linked from UOKiK's January 2026 release. CJEU C-330/23 Aldi Sud, 26 Sep 2024. Recent milestones: Azagroup (Renee, Born2Be) fined PLN 14.9 million for perpetual promotions on 27 May 2025; Zalando and Temu fined on 12 Jan 2026 (Polish release; English version dated 14 Jan 2026); EU Black Friday sweep results on 26 Mar 2026; Inspekcja Handlowa results on 31 Mar 2026; charges against Black Red White, Zabka Nano and Peek & Cloppenburg on 29 Apr 2026; charges against H&M and Peek & Cloppenburg online on 27 May 2026. Six more proceedings and over 70 informal 'soft' interventions were reported in January 2026.

**cost model**

Free to read on any shop page. Independent verification costs depend on the price-history source: Ceneo 6-month history (free with login), Skapiec 1-year history (free, per the Ceneo item), Keepa for Amazon (see that item), or self-run monitoring (PageCrawl plans USD 0 for 6 pages and 220 checks/month, USD 8/month for 100 pages; vendor pricing seen 2026-10-15). Compliance cost falls on traders.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **Poland**: Mandatory for every announcement of a reduction of a specific good or service: product card, search results, listing, recommendations, cart, app and advertising, 'in the same place and time' as the reduction (UOKiK guidance, section IV). For general announcements such as 'boots up to -20%', the price must appear as soon as the reduction can be tied to a product.
- **EU outside Poland**: Art. 6a applies in every member state, with national options for perishable goods, new products and progressive reductions. Germany (PAngV section 11): Amazon.de labels the reference 'zuletzt niedrigster Preis' ⚠ *(unverified)* (one German guide says Amazon uses an average 'Statt-Preis' instead). Wording differs per language, e.g. 'Niedrigster Preis der letzten 30 Tage'.
- **US**: N/A - no equivalent federal rule; US deal labels such as 'was' or 'list price' have no 30-day legal anchor.
- **language**: Polish shops use varied wording: 'Najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka', 'Najnizsza cena z 30 dni', 'Cena z 30 dni'; non-compliant variants seen in UOKiK cases include 'cena referencyjna', 'cena Omnibus', 'bylo', '30-dniowa najlepsza cena' and 'najnizsza maksymalna z cen obowiazujacych 30 dni przed promocja'.
- **US only or agentic features**: None. No agent-commerce protocol was found to carry this field ⚠ *(unverified)* (product-feed specs of ACP or UCP not checked).

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A for specs. Variant pitfall: the reference must be correct for each variant on promotion; Temu was charged for showing it only for one size or colour while all were discounted. An agent must read the field for the exact variant (size, colour, set) it would buy.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Not a market comparison. The reference is the trader's own lowest price, per sales channel or store: a promotion in a Krakow store is not the reference for the chain's Warsaw store (UOKiK guidance V.2). On marketplaces the platform may show either the lowest price of that seller or the lowest price on the whole platform, and must explain which in a tooltip. Allegro computes it per offer. Ceneo's 'Superceny' pages use a stricter 30-day low across all shops on the service (Ceneo item). A true 30-day low can still be well above other shops' current prices.

**price history and omnibus**

- **what it shows**: One number: the lowest price the trader charged for that product in the 30 calendar days before the first day of the reduction. The UOKiK guidance specifies: the window is fixed at the start of the promotion and does not move while the promotion runs unchanged, even beyond 30 days; any price actually offered counts, whether or not anyone bought; days when the item was out of stock still count; for products on sale fewer than 30 days, the window starts at first offer; for perishable goods, the price before the first reduction applies; percentage and amount savings ('-20%', 'save PLN 50') must be computed from this price, confirmed by CJEU C-330/23; showing several 'lowest prices' is wrong.
- **fake discount tests an agent can run**: (1) Real discount = (ref30 - current) / ref30. If the current price is at or above ref30, there is no reduction: the BRW case had promo PLN 989, strikethrough PLN 1,439 and ref30 PLN 899; the P&C skirt was marked -43% at PLN 199.99 with ref30 also PLN 199.99. (2) The advertised % does not match ref30: the discount was computed from a 'regular', 'initial' or RRP price (Zalando fined; illegal per C-330/23 when presented as a reduction). (3) A strikethrough or '-x%' with no ref30 nearby: a breach (Temu, IH 2025 findings). (4) ref30 changes from day to day while the selling price and promotion stay the same: a manipulation signal (Zalando and Temu fined for exactly this). (5) The label is vague or renamed ('cena referencyjna', '30-dniowa najlepsza cena').
- **what it cannot tell**: Whether ref30 itself is true (it is self-declared); whether the price was raised more than 30 days before the sale; whether a long promotion is effectively the permanent price (the reference stays frozen; UOKiK says permanent promotions can mislead even when ref30 is correct, as in the Azagroup case); and the market price. Verify with independent history: Ceneo 6-month trend, Skapiec 1-year history, Keepa for Amazon, or your own snapshots.

**total landed cost**

N/A - ref30 covers the item price only, not delivery, payment fees or returns. For bulky goods such as trampolines, compare the delivery-inclusive price separately.

**review and seller verification**

N/A as a review check. Weak seller signal: UOKiK's July 2025 fake-shop release lists 'very large discounts, especially without the lowest price from the previous 30 days' as a red flag, so a missing ref30 on a big discount should push the shop into the full seller check (blocklists and registers).

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A for product safety. This is itself a price-compliance check that can run automatically: detect a reduction claim, look for a ref30 label in the same view, parse the numbers and recompute the discount.

**independent test coverage**

- **lab tests**: N/A - no product tests.
- **compliance evidence**: Inspekcja Handlowa 2025, published 31 Mar 2026: 3,026 physical establishments (shops, service points, petrol stations, car parks, hotels) and 461,437 products checked; 1,462 establishments (almost half) gave incorrect price information of some kind; 60,001 products (13%) affected; 899 traders fined PLN 1,204,194 in total. Missing 30-day prices and discounts computed from the regular price were among the findings, but the release gives no separate count for them and no online data. EU sweep of Black Friday and Cyber Monday 2025 (CCPC, 26 Mar 2026): 314 online traders checked by authorities from 23 EU states plus Iceland and Norway, Poland not listed; 30% referenced discounts incorrectly; 34% used price comparisons, and 6 in 10 of those did not explain the reference price; 18% used pressure selling. EU sweep of Black Friday 2022: 16,000 products on 176 websites; 23% of discount announcements clearly inconsistent with EU law; violations on at least 43% of sites. UOKiK consumer survey (ARC Rynek i Opinia, CAWI, n=2,019, fieldwork May 2024, published 16 May 2025): 85% knew the term, and over half of those had difficulty finding the price while shopping.

**alerts and monitoring**

None built in; the field is static text on the page. Monitoring options: Ceneo price alerts (Ceneo-listed offers only); PageCrawl or similar change monitors (screenshots, rule 'advertised reference above recorded 30-day low', alerts to Slack, Telegram or webhook; vendor blog Aug 2026); or a Claude Code scheduled job that snapshots the product page daily for 30 days before an expected sale (e.g. Black Week or end of the garden season).

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A - read-only signal. As a guardrail: an agent must never present a deal as a reduction unless ref30 is visible for the exact variant and the discount recomputed from ref30 is positive; it should flag the cases in fake_discount_tests and hand the decision to the human.

**after sales and resale**

N/A. Related consumer right: art. 5 of the price act lets a consumer demand the most favourable price when prices diverge or are unclear (e.g. ad price vs shelf price, the Zabka Nano case).

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

The trader's own price log. Allegro: computed automatically per offer, anchored to the campaign start, and sellers cannot set it (Allegro help; community moderators). Shoper: computed automatically once the merchant enables the setting, including out-of-stock days; manual correction is possible for main products. WooCommerce 'Omnibus' plugin (iworks): logs prices from activation and backfills missing data with the current price; a July 2026 user review of v3.0.4 reports a new sale price shown immediately as the '30-day lowest price'. So the field is only as reliable as the shop's price log, which can be reset by migrations, ERP imports, manual edits or plugin bugs.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: partial - readable only by parsing rendered pages; no API, no standard structured field, no MCP or skill found
- **structured data**: schema.org and Google merchant listings offer only priceSpecification with priceType 'https://schema.org/StrikethroughPrice', defined by Google as 'the full, original listing price', which may be the regular price, not ref30. Google's docs do not mention the EU 30-day rule. A JSON-LD strikethrough price therefore cannot stand in for ref30.
- **extraction**: Render the page in a headless or real browser and regex the visible text near the price block for '(najni[zż]sza\s+cena\s+z\s+(ostatnich\s+)?30\s+dni|cena\s+z\s+30\s+dni)' (Polish) and 'niedrigster Preis der letzten 30 Tage|zuletzt niedrigster Preis' (German), then parse the PLN or EUR amount and the current price, and record the strikethrough and percentage badge. Tooltips may hide it: on Allegro, community moderators said in 2023 the explanation appeared on hover and not in the app ⚠ *(unverified)* (current app behaviour not re-checked). Check listing, product card and cart, because the field must appear at each stage.
- **access obstacles**: Many Polish shops block plain fetchers: WebFetch got HTTP 403 from decathlon.pl and an allegro.pl article on 2026-10-15; Allegro uses DataDome and Ceneo's terms ban automation (Ceneo item). A browser agent driven by the user (Claude in Chrome, Playwright on a personal profile) at personal volume is the practical route.
- **tools found**: GitHub search on 2026-10-15 for 'omnibus najnizsza cena', 'omnibus 30 days lowest price', 'omnibus price checker' and 'lowest price 30 days scraper' returned no repositories. Vendor option: PageCrawl compliance monitoring (not tested). Setup effort for a home-made Claude Code skill: about 1-2 hours (regex plus browser step plus snapshot to the vault).

**⚠ protocol support**

N/A - a legal field, not a protocol. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether agentic-commerce product feeds (ACP, UCP) carry a prior-price attribute was not verified; an agent-checkout flow that shows a 'discount' would itself be an announcement of a reduction subject to the rule.

**⚠ open source and licence**

The law and UOKiK guidance are public. Shop-side implementations: Allegro and Shoper closed; iworks 'Omnibus' WordPress plugin is public on wordpress.org ⚠ *(unverified)* (licence assumed GPL, not confirmed). No open-source consumer-side checker found.

**account linking and data access**

Usually none needed. Caveat: member, club, app-only or newsletter prices also require ref30 when they are announced for specific products (UOKiK guidance; H&M charged over club prices), so the logged-out view may differ from what a member sees. Loyalty rewards not tied to specific products (e.g. '-20% on your next order') are outside the rule. The agent must read the same view the buyer will pay in.

**automation legal risk**

Reading prices for personal decisions is low risk. Automated scraping of shops that ban bots (Ceneo terms with a contractual penalty; Allegro anti-bot) carries ToS and account risk. Storing your own dated snapshots privately is fine; republishing whole price tables from a shop in a public vault note may conflict with database rights (see Ceneo item).

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Traders have a direct incentive to inflate the apparent discount. Platform mechanics shape the displayed discount: Allegro badge thresholds require at least 3% (Okazja) or 5% (Allegro Days) below the offer's 30-day low, and Allegro's automatic price-cutting programmes ('Allegro Ceny', price rules) change prices hourly. Marketplaces choose whether to show the seller-level or platform-level reference.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - no ranking. Transparency depends on the label: a clear 'Najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka: X zl' next to the price is compliant; hover-only text, footnotes or vague names are not.

**run to run consistency**

N/A as an AI property, but a useful test: during one unchanged promotion, ref30 should stay constant. Capturing the field on two or more days and seeing it move while the selling price stays put matches the pattern UOKiK fined Zalando and Temu for.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Known manipulation patterns: raising the price more than 30 days before a sale (invisible to the field); perpetual or renamed promotions (Azagroup, PLN 14.9 million); computing % from RRP, 'regular' or 'initial' prices (Zalando); exempt formats (conditional and bundle offers such as '3 for 2', 'buy for PLN 100 get 10% off', 'buy 2 get the third free'); 'upcoming price' comparisons for new stores; channel-specific references; long promotions with a frozen reference; ⚠ *(unverified)* relisting a product as a new offer on a marketplace, which may restart the per-offer history (not documented). Prompt injection: not applicable to the number itself, but page text read by an agent is untrusted.

**known failures**

- Missing at some stages (listing, cart, app, external ads): Zalando and Temu
- Reference changed daily while the selling price stayed the same: Zalando and Temu
- Discount computed from regular, initial or RRP price instead of ref30: Zalando; IH 2025 'usually' found discounts calculated from the regular price
- Promo price at or above ref30, so no real saving: BRW (PLN 989 vs 899), P&C (PLN 199.99 vs 199.99)
- Vague or invented labels: '30-dniowa najlepsza cena' (P&C), 'najnizsza maksymalna' (Zabka Nano), 'cena referencyjna'
- Reference shown for one variant only (Temu)
- Hover-only or not shown in the mobile app (Allegro, 2023 community reports, current state unconfirmed)
- Platform and plugin bugs: a WooCommerce plugin reportedly shows a new sale price as the 30-day low (July 2026 review); Shoper allows manual edits
- Legally exempt formats look like discounts to a buyer but carry no ref30: bundles, conditional offers, loyalty rewards not tied to products

**regulatory enforcement history**

Poland, UOKiK: Zalando SE PLN 30,945,000 and Whaleco Technology Limited (Temu) PLN 5,910,900, both on 12 Jan 2026 and not final (missing or incorrect ref30, reference changing daily, % from 'initial' or 'regular' price; Temu stopped the practices during the proceedings, on 22 Oct 2025 per media coverage). Azagroup (Renee, Born2Be) PLN 14,910,599 on 27 May 2025 for perpetual promotions and unreal reference prices (not final), with separate Omnibus charges pending. Charges: Temu (29 May 2025), Black Red White, Zabka Nano and Peek & Cloppenburg (29 Apr 2026), H&M and Peek & Cloppenburg online (27 May 2026). Ongoing proceedings (Jan 2026): Media Markt, Sephora, Glovo, Shell Polska, AzaGroup, Jeronimo Martins Polska, plus over 70 soft interventions. Inspekcja Handlowa 2025: 899 traders fined PLN 1.2 million in total for price-information breaches of all kinds. EU: CJEU C-330/23 Aldi Sud (26 Sep 2024): any announced % or 'price highlight' must be computed from the 30-day prior price.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

A misleading reduction is an unfair commercial practice: report it to UOKiK or the local Inspekcja Handlowa (WIIH). Art. 5 of the price act gives the right to the most favourable price when prices diverge. ⚠ *(unverified)* Individual remedies under the unfair-market-practices act (damages, price reduction or termination, as extended in 2023) were not re-read. The 14-day distance-sale withdrawal right still applies, so a buyer who discovers the discount was fake can return the goods, at the cost of return shipping for bulky items.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Useful and cheap, but only as a red-flag reader. Trampoline example: a shop shows a 305 cm trampoline at PLN 1,199 with a strikethrough PLN 1,999 and '-40%'. The agent looks for 'Najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka'; if it reads PLN 1,249, the real reduction is 4%, not 40%, and the 40% badge is unlawful under C-330/23. If it reads PLN 1,199 or less, there is no reduction at all. Then cross-check the same EAN on Ceneo (6-month trend) and Skapiec (1-year history). Garden products are seasonal, so real reductions cluster at the end of summer and in Black Week; a 'promotion' running all spring with a frozen reference is a known pattern (Azagroup).

**workflow role**

Price-and-history step. Read the field on every shortlisted offer, recompute the real discount, then verify against independent history (Ceneo, Skapiec, Keepa) and a delivery-inclusive comparison. A missing field on a large discount also sends the shop to the seller-check step (blocklists, registers).

**effort and cost per purchase**

Reading: PLN 0, about 1 minute per offer manually, seconds for a browser agent. Verification: one Ceneo history view (free, login) and one Skapiec view per product, about 3 minutes. Pre-sale monitoring arithmetic: 3 shops x 1 check per day x 30 days = 90 page loads, which fits PageCrawl's free tier (6 pages, 220 checks per month) or a local Playwright job at no cost. Skill build: about 1-2 hours once.

**evidence trail**

Good if the agent captures it; the shop gives none. Suggested vault record (raw in content/_raw): capture time; product URL and exact variant; EAN if shown; current price; strikethrough price and its label; the ref30 label text verbatim and its amount; advertised % or amount; recomputed real discount from ref30; promotion dates if shown; a screenshot of the price block; the same fields on a second day to test whether ref30 is stable; the cross-check source (Ceneo or Skapiec history screenshot).

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Mandatory for every announced reduction in Poland since 2023, on every surface including ads and cart, and backed by real fines (Zalando PLN 30.9 million, Temu PLN 5.9 million)
  - Gives the agent a legally defined anchor to recompute the true discount; CJEU C-330/23 makes any % computed from another price unlawful
  - Simple deterministic tests catch common fake promotions (promo price at or above ref30, % mismatch, daily-changing ref30)
  - Free and requires no account in most cases
- **weaknesses**:
  - Self-declared and widely mishandled: 30% of 314 EU online traders got the discount reference wrong in the 2025 sweep, and IH found problems at almost half of 3,026 Polish establishments in 2025 (all price-information breaches)
  - No API or standard structured field; schema.org StrikethroughPrice is not ref30; shops often block fetchers
  - Blind to price bumps more than 30 days earlier, perpetual promotions with a frozen reference, and market-level prices
  - Exempt formats (bundles, conditional offers, general loyalty rewards) look like discounts but carry no ref30
  - Platform logic varies: per offer (Allegro), per store or channel, seller-level vs platform-level; plugin bugs reported

**independent review consensus**

Regulators and consumer bodies agree that compliance is poor and that the field alone does not stop fake promotions: EU sweeps in 2022 (23% of announcements clearly unlawful, 43% of sites) and 2025 (30% of traders), Inspekcja Handlowa 2025, and a stream of UOKiK cases in 2025-2026. A French consumer magazine (Que Choisir) concluded after the 2022 sweep that the Omnibus rule did not have the expected effect. No empirical before-and-after study of 'price bumping' under art. 6a was found; Lipowska (e-mentor 1/2025) is theoretical. Vendor blogs (PageCrawl, Sellforte, Prisync) were used only for implementation details and are marked as vendor sources.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW, as a red-flag reader, never as proof of a good deal. Deciding fact: the field is mandatory and legally defined, so a missing, vague or shifting ref30, or a % not computed from it, is strong evidence of a fake promotion; a correct-looking ref30 is still self-declared. Best use: a Claude Code browser step that captures the ref30 label and price block for each shortlisted offer, recomputes the real discount, repeats the capture on a second day, and cross-checks Ceneo or Skapiec history before the human decides.

**conflicting evidence**

- Inspekcja Handlowa figure: the task note says about half of 3,026 checked businesses mislabelled prices in 2025. UOKiK's release (31 Mar 2026) counts 3,026 establishments (placowki, physical outlets only), of which 1,462 had incorrect price information of any kind, mostly missing prices; it gives no separate count for 30-day-price breaches.
- Zalando/Temu announcement date and amounts: Polish UOKiK release dated 12 Jan 2026 vs English release dated 14 Jan 2026; media rounded Zalando to PLN 31 million (exact PLN 30,945,000) and Temu to PLN 6 million (exact PLN 5,910,900).
- Amazon.de reference: German tech media report Amazon now shows 'zuletzt niedrigster Preis' (30-day low) for time-limited offers; testundtipps.de reports Amazon's 'Statt-Preis' is an average selling price and found no 30-day price on pages it reviewed.
- Loyalty discounts: Sellforte (vendor blog) says art. 6a does not apply to loyalty programmes; UOKiK guidance says loyalty and newsletter discounts announced for specific products do require ref30, and only rewards not tied to specific products are exempt.
- Allegro display: community moderators (2023) said the explanation was hover-only and absent in the app; Allegro English help (2026) says the 30-day low is shown crossed out with campaign badges. Current app behaviour not re-verified.

### ECC Poland and buyer-protection paths

**Verdict:** USE NOW · **Cost:** Free · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 10 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

A cheat-sheet item, not one product. It covers the free or low-cost redress routes a Poland-based consumer has when an online purchase goes wrong. (1) ECC Poland (Europejskie Centrum Konsumenckie, the Polish member of ECC-Net) gives free out-of-court help with cross-border disputes against traders in another EU state, Norway or Iceland. (2) Domestic help: the miejski or powiatowy rzecznik konsumentow (municipal or county consumer ombudsman, about 400 offices), the consumer hotline and e-advice service, and Inspekcja Handlowa ADR (mediation and permanent consumer arbitration courts). (3) Statutory rights under the Consumer Rights Act (ustawa o prawach konsumenta, consolidated text Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1244): the 14-day withdrawal right (chapter 4) and liability for lack of conformity (chapter 5a). Chapter 5a replaced the Civil Code rekojmia for consumer sales from 1 Jan 2023; rekojmia still governs B2B and private sales. (4) Payment-layer protections: card chargeback (Visa and Mastercard scheme rules), PayPal Buyer Protection, and Allegro Ochrona Kupujacych (formerly Allegro Protect). The EU ODR platform was shut down on 20 July 2025, so ECC-Net is now the main free EU-level route for cross-border cases. Role type: regulation + public advisory/ADR service + payment-rail and marketplace protection programmes.

**vendor and ownership**

ECC Poland: part of ECC-Net, which the European Commission co-funds. It is housed at UOKiK headquarters (Pl. Powstancow Warszawy 1, 00-950 Warszawa) and is funded by the Commission and UOKiK (superbiz.se.pl summary of the 2024 report). It has operated since 2005. Rzecznicy konsumentow: officials of local government (powiat or gmina). Inspekcja Handlowa: voivodeship inspectorates (WIIH) under UOKiK supervision. Rzecznik Finansowy: state ombudsman for financial-market clients, including disputes with a bank over a refused chargeback. Card chargeback: the card scheme's private rules (Visa, Mastercard), run by the card-issuing bank. Chargeback has no statute of its own (Bankier.pl, 19 Sep 2025). PayPal Buyer Protection: PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l. et Cie, S.C.A. (Luxembourg). PayPal decides claims 'at its own discretion'. Allegro Ochrona Kupujacych: Allegro sp. z o.o., Poznan (KRS 0000635012). It is a marketplace's own commercial programme: Allegro joins the seller's debt when it pays and then recovers the money from the seller. Ownership matters: the two private programmes are run by parties with an interest in keeping buyers on their platform, while the public routes have no commercial interest.

**lifecycle status**

Verified 2026-10-15. ODR platform: Regulation (EU) 2024/3228 repealed the ODR Regulation. New complaints stopped on 20 Mar 2025 and the platform was discontinued on 20 Jul 2025 (CMS, iubenda, ECC Malta; the Commission's ADR page lists a 'Discontinuation of the ODR platform' document dated 19 Dec 2024). Successor framework: Directive (EU) 2025/2647 amends the ADR Directive 2013/11/EU. It was published in the OJ on 30 Dec 2025 and entered into force on 19 Jan 2026. Transposition is due by 20 Mar 2028 and application from 20 Sep 2028. It extends ADR to traders in third countries, on a voluntary joint request, adds a 20-working-day duty for traders to reply to ADR bodies, and requires the Commission to build a multilingual digital tool (EAPIL 23 Jan 2026; Bird & Bird 2026; secondary). ECC Poland: active. A notice of 2 Oct 2026 says complaints and queries nearly doubled in two years, so response times are longer. The complaint page gives about 50 days of waiting. Consumer Rights Act: new consolidated text Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1244, announced 4 Sep 2026 and published 23 Sep 2026 (state of law 2 Sep 2026). It supersedes Dz.U. 2024 poz. 1796, which the Sejm ELI record marks as expired on 23 Sep 2026. Allegro: the programme was renamed 'Allegro Ochrona Kupujacych (wczesniej Allegro Protect)'. A cap of 40,000 PLN per buyer per seller over two calendar years applies to purchases from 12 Feb 2024. PayPal: the Polish Buyer Protection terms page showed 'Ostatnia aktualizacja 28 stycznia 2022' on 2026-10-15, and the PayPal user agreement was last updated 6 May 2026 (secondary search summary).

**⚠ cost model**

Free for the buyer on every public route (seen 2026-10-15): ECC Poland complaint (free, per the complaint page), rzecznik konsumentow, e-porady via dlakonsumentow.pl (answer within 5 working days, or 10), and UOKiK and Inspekcja Handlowa reports. The consumer hotline 801 440 220 / 222 66 76 76 (weekdays 10:00-18:00 per gov.pl, updated 13 Jan 2026) is charged at the caller's operator rate. ⚠ *(unverified)* Fees for Inspekcja Handlowa permanent consumer arbitration courts were not verified. Card chargeback: free for the cardholder (bank and consumer-press sources). PayPal Buyer Protection: free, but it does not refund the cost of sending an item back, which matters for bulky goods. Allegro Ochrona Kupujacych: free. It can also reimburse original shipping and return shipping when the order was paid through Allegro's own payment options (annex 9, part I.3). Court route (not free): the European Small Claims Procedure for cross-border claims up to EUR 5,000. ⚠ *(unverified)* Court fees in PL not checked.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **poland domestic seller**: All domestic routes work in Polish: statutory withdrawal and conformity, rzecznik konsumentow, Inspekcja Handlowa mediation and arbitration, UOKiK complaint, chargeback, PayPal, Allegro programme.
- **eu eea seller cross border**: ECC Poland (consumer resident in PL, trader in another EU state, Norway or Iceland). ECC Poland passes the case to the ECC in the trader's country. The consumer must complain to the trader first. Statutory EU minimums apply in every member state: 14-day withdrawal under Directive 2011/83 and 2-year seller liability under Directive 2019/771.
- **uk seller**: Not covered by ECC-Net: the Commission's ECC-Net page says the network only 'cooperates' with the UK International Consumer Centre. konsument.gov.pl lists only EU, NO and IS. gov.pl (13 Jan 2026) lists the UK too; see conflicting_evidence.
- **non eu seller china us**: ECC cannot pursue a trader outside the EU/EEA. The practical routes are the platform's own refund process, card chargeback, and PayPal. Directive 2025/2647 will let third-country traders join EU ADR voluntarily, from 2028 at the earliest. ⚠ *(unverified)* When the platform operator is an EU company (for example, Temu's Whaleco Technology Ltd in Ireland), the ECC route may be open against the platform for its own obligations, but not as the seller of record. This was not confirmed with ECC.
- **us**: N/A. These are EU and Polish consumer-law routes.
- **language**: ECC Poland, the ombudsmen, the hotline and the statutes are all in Polish. The cross-border ECC-to-ECC exchange is handled by the network.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A. This is a redress item, not a comparison tool. One legal link: a delivered item that differs from the ordered variant (size, model year, net height) is a lack of conformity under art. 43b of the Consumer Rights Act, and for PayPal a 'significantly not as described' claim. Keep a snapshot of the exact variant in the offer.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A. These routes do not compare prices.

**price history and omnibus**

N/A for tooling. A fake discount (wrong 30-day lowest price) is a matter for a UOKiK or Inspekcja Handlowa report, not for ECC. The 14-day withdrawal right lets a buyer leave a purchase made on a misleading promotion, but the buyer pays direct return costs if properly informed (art. 34(2)).

**total landed cost**

Directly relevant to bulky goods. Withdrawal route: the consumer bears only the direct cost of return if the trader told them so (art. 34(2)). For goods that 'cannot be returned by ordinary post', the trader must state that return cost before the contract (art. 12(1)(10)). The model withdrawal form asks for a PLN amount or an estimate. The refund covers original delivery only up to the cheapest standard option (art. 33) and is due within 14 days, though the trader may hold it until the goods arrive back or proof of sending is given (art. 32). Conformity route: the trader pays all repair and replacement costs, 'in particular postage, transport, labour and materials', collects the item at its own cost (art. 43d(4)-(5)), and takes back a rejected item at its own cost (art. 43e(6)). So for a defective trampoline, the conformity route is cheaper than withdrawal. PayPal: return shipping is not reimbursed. Allegro: shipping and return shipping can be compensated when paid via Allegro payment options. Cross-border enforceability: the ECC route has no enforcement power and a queue of about 50 days, which is a real cost for EU-shop purchases.

**review and seller verification**

None (grade: none). These routes do not verify sellers, but every one of them depends on knowing who the seller is. ECC requires a trader established in the EU, NO or IS. Consumer-law rights apply only against a trader, not a private seller on Allegro Lokalnie or OLX. Allegro may ask for a copy of the buyer's ID and a police-report confirmation in doubtful cases (annex 9, parts III.2 and IV.1). Check the seller's identity (CEIDG/KRS/VIES) before paying; see the sibling item on seller registers.

**⚠ safety and compliance checks**

N/A. These are redress routes, not safety checks. Related: a dangerous product can be reported to UOKiK or Inspekcja Handlowa. A safety defect that shows within 2 years of delivery is a lack of conformity, presumed to have existed at delivery (art. 43c(1)). ⚠ *(unverified)* Producer liability for damage caused by a dangerous product (Civil Code art. 449^1 and following) is a separate claim, not checked here.

**independent test coverage**

N/A. No lab testing is involved.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

N/A. No alerts are offered. Deadlines worth putting in a calendar from the purchase date: withdrawal statement within 14 days of taking possession (art. 27-28), or 12 months more if the trader did not inform about the right (art. 29); goods sent back within 14 days of withdrawing (art. 34(1)); trader's answer to a complaint within 14 days, or the complaint counts as accepted (art. 7a); non-conformity revealed within 2 years of delivery (art. 43c); PayPal dispute within 180 days of payment, escalated to a claim within 20 days; Allegro claim from day 14 (day 7 for non-delivery) to day 730 after purchase; card chargeback ⚠ *(unverified)* about 120 days from the transaction or expected delivery, depending on scheme and bank.

**⚠ purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A. None of these routes buys anything. Note for agent-made purchases: protection follows the seller, the contract and the payment method, not the tool that placed the order. A purchase made through an AI agent on the buyer's own account is still a distance contract with the same 14-day withdrawal and conformity rights. ⚠ *(unverified)* No Polish or EU guidance specific to agent-initiated purchases was found.

**⚠ after sales and resale**

Two-year conformity liability with a presumption in the buyer's favour (art. 43c). The buyer may choose repair or replacement (art. 43d), then a price reduction or termination (art. 43e). A manufacturer's guarantee (gwarancja) is separate and voluntary; advertised guarantee terms bind the guarantor (art. 43g). Spare parts and resale are not covered by any of these routes. ⚠ *(unverified)* The EU Right to Repair Directive (EU) 2024/1799, with its 31 Jul 2026 transposition deadline, covers listed appliance groups, not trampolines; its Polish transposition status was not checked.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Statute: the official consolidated text from the Sejm ELI API (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1244, state of law 2 Sep 2026, published 23 Sep 2026). ECC: konsument.gov.pl, live, news dated 2 to 5 Oct 2026. gov.pl help page: updated 13 Jan 2026. Allegro: regulation annex 9 PDF, current on 2026-10-15; its clauses cite the 12 Feb 2024 change. PayPal: Buyer Protection page dated 28 Jan 2022, which is older than six months, though it is the live legal text. Chargeback: mBank FAQ (undated, (c) 2026) and Bankier (19 Sep 2025). BLIK disputes: PPRO developer docs (last updated 30 Sep 2025, older than six months).

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. (1) Official API for the law: the Sejm ELI API (api.sejm.gov.pl/eli/acts/DU/{year}/{pos}) returns act metadata as JSON and the consolidated text as PDF, with no authentication. I used it to pull Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1244 and extract it with pdftotext. A Claude Code skill can cite exact article text from it. (2) Filing: ECC Poland accepts one email to ECCNET-PL@ec.europa.eu with the problem described in the body, at most 4 attachments (PDF, Word, JPG, Excel), 10 MB in total, and an unchanged subject line on replies. No API or web form is needed, so Claude Code can draft the email and assemble the attachment pack for the user to send. (3) Allegro, PayPal and the bank: claim forms only inside logged-in accounts; no public API for buyer claims. Allegro pages block plain HTTP fetches (403); I could read them only through a real browser. (4) No MCP server or skill for Polish consumer redress was found. Setup effort: low. A skill template (deadline calculator plus complaint-letter generator plus evidence checklist) is a few hours of work.

**protocol support**

N/A. These are legal and payment-scheme routes, not agent-commerce protocols.

**open source and licence**

N/A, closed public services. Official Polish legal texts are not protected by copyright (Polish Copyright Act art. 4), so the statute text can be stored in the vault verbatim.

**account linking and data access**

ECC: you send personal data, the order, payment proof and all correspondence by email. ECC forwards the case to the ECC in the trader's country, which then contacts the trader. Allegro programme: you need an Allegro account in good standing; Allegro may request an ID photo and proof of a police report; payout goes to the card or account used. PayPal: you need a PayPal account in good standing, and the item must have been paid from that account. You cannot run a PayPal claim and a card dispute at the same time: a card dispute closes the PayPal case, but a PayPal loss can still be taken to the card issuer. Chargeback: through your bank's complaint channel. GDPR applies to every route. Nothing requires giving an AI tool payment credentials.

**automation legal risk**

Low. Drafting complaints and withdrawal statements with an AI tool and sending them yourself carries no ToS risk. Evidence must be genuine: Allegro may refuse a claim when the facts are inconsistent (annex 9, part IV.2). Scraping Allegro to monitor a dispute would conflict with its anti-bot measures; the sibling Allegro item covers this. N/A otherwise.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Public routes: no monetisation and no ranking. Private programmes: Allegro and PayPal are platform retention tools with discretionary decisions. PayPal decides 'at its own discretion'. Allegro can shorten or extend deadlines, require police reports and refuse on 'doubts'. Allegro can also block the seller's account and recover the payout. Chargeback outcomes depend on the merchant's representment and on scheme reason codes, not on consumer law.

**ranking transparency**

N/A. No ranking is involved.

**run to run consistency**

N/A. These are not AI tools.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

N/A for AI. Fraud pattern flagged by ECC Poland (undated warning on konsument.gov.pl): shops with a 'Netherlands address' sell low-quality clothes and shoes, refuse returns, or demand returns to Asia. An EU address on a website does not prove the shop is established in the EU, so check registers before relying on the ECC route.

**known failures**

ECC: about 50 days of waiting, with complaint volume nearly doubled in two years (2 Oct 2026 notice). No enforcement powers. Filing 'does not stop the limitation period' ('nie wstrzymuje biegu przedawnienia', complaint page), so a buyer who waits on ECC can lose a court claim. ECC does not cover sellers outside the EU/EEA. Allegro programme: carrier loss or damage is excluded (annex 9, part II.8), so the buyer is sent to the carrier. 'Not as described' requires a value 'significantly lower' than described (part I.1.b). A decision takes up to 30 working days after a complete file, though the help page says 48 h for Smart! users. Forum complaints about refusals are anecdotal. PayPal: return postage at the buyer's cost; items made to order excluded for 'not as described'; proof of delivery defeats a non-delivery claim even if the buyer disputes it. Chargeback: card payments only. Bank pages and consumer guides say transfers are excluded; BLIK is contested (see conflicting_evidence). Status trap: buying on a company invoice (NIP) can lose consumer protection. A sole trader keeps the chapter 4 and 5a rights only when the purchase is not of a 'professional character' judged against the CEIDG business codes (art. 7aa).

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the public routes. For the private programmes: ⚠ *(unverified)* UOKiK previously ordered PayPal (Europe) to stop applying a unilateral-amendment clause to Polish consumers (secondary search summary; date and decision number not verified). The UOKiK case history for Allegro is in the sibling Allegro item.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

- **1 statutory withdrawal 14 days**: Basis: art. 27-34 of the Consumer Rights Act. Distance or off-premises purchase from a trader. 14 days from taking possession, no reason needed; sending the statement in time is enough (art. 30(2)). Extended by up to 12 months if the trader did not inform you of the right (art. 29). Goods go back within 14 days of the statement. Refund within 14 days, using the same payment method, but it can be held until the goods arrive or proof of sending is given. You pay direct return costs if informed; for goods that cannot go by ordinary post, the trader must state the cost in advance. Exceptions include goods made to your specification (art. 38(1)(3)). A sole trader buying outside their professional field has the same right (art. 7aa).
- **2 lack of conformity successor of rekojmia**: Basis: art. 43a-43g. The seller is liable for non-conformity present at delivery and revealed within 2 years, presumed to have existed at delivery (art. 43c). Order of remedies: repair or replacement at the seller's cost, with pickup and reinstallation (art. 43d); then a price reduction or termination if the seller refuses, fails or the defect is significant; significance is presumed (art. 43e). The seller must answer a complaint within 14 days or it counts as accepted (art. 7a). Rekojmia under the Civil Code still applies to B2B and private sales.
- **3 ecc poland cross border**: For a trader in another EU state, Norway or Iceland, after you have complained to the trader and received a refusal or no answer within the legal deadline. Free. Email ECCNET-PL@ec.europa.eu, phone 22 55 60 600 (weekdays 10:00-13:00). Needs the order, all correspondence, proof of payment and a quantified claim. About 50 days of waiting. No enforcement power. It does NOT pause limitation, so track your own deadlines or use ADR or a court in parallel.
- **4 domestic ombudsmen and adr**: Rzecznik konsumentow (free; drafts complaint and court letters and can sue on your behalf), consumer hotline 801 440 220 / 222 66 76 76, e-porady at dlakonsumentow.pl, Inspekcja Handlowa mediation and permanent consumer arbitration courts (polubowne.uokik.gov.pl). ⚠ *(unverified)* Unlike ECC, starting mediation or an arbitration case interrupts limitation under Civil Code art. 123 §1 (point 3, mediation; point 1, sad polubowny); the text of art. 123 was not re-read for this item.
- **5 card chargeback**: Run by your card issuer under Visa or Mastercard rules, so it is a scheme rule, not a statute. Covers non-delivery, not-as-described and a refund not received after a return or cancellation (mBank FAQ). Free. File as soon as possible. ⚠ *(unverified)* Visa reason code 13.1 allows about 120 days from processing or the expected delivery date, capped at 540 days (secondary). Banks expect you to try the merchant first. Excludes bank transfers. Card or PayPal (with a card behind it) is the strongest choice for a bulky, safety-relevant purchase from an unfamiliar shop.
- **6 paypal buyer protection**: Covers non-delivery and 'significantly not as described', including counterfeit items, missing parts and transit damage. Open a dispute within 180 days of payment and escalate it to a claim within 20 days. PayPal may require the item to be returned at your cost, and return postage is never refunded. Excluded: vehicles, items made to order (for 'not as described'), Friends and Family payments, items for resale, and more. You can file a card dispute after a PayPal loss, but not both at once.
- **7 allegro ochrona kupujacych ex allegro protect**: Covers non-delivery, items not as described with a significantly lower value, incomplete orders, damaged items, and refunds not received after a return or cancellation. Max 20,000 PLN per transaction and 40,000 PLN per buyer per seller over two calendar years (purchases from 12 Feb 2024). Apply from day 14 (day 7 for non-delivery) to day 730 after purchase, after first raising the problem with the seller in an Allegro Discussion. Excluded: carrier loss or damage, pay-on-pickup, voucher-paid amounts, customs or cross-border legal blocks, prohibited goods. Return shipping is reimbursed when paid through Allegro payments. Allegro may require ID and a police report.
- **8 decision order for a problem purchase**: 1) Complain to the seller in writing and note the 14-day answer deadline. 2) Use the platform programme (Allegro or PayPal) within its window. 3) Card chargeback if paid by card. 4) For an EU seller, go to ECC Poland while watching the limitation period. 5) For a domestic seller, go to the rzecznik konsumentow or Inspekcja Handlowa mediation. 6) Court, including the European Small Claims Procedure for cross-border claims up to EUR 5,000.

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

High as a pre-purchase checklist for the reference trampoline (about EUR 200-700, 40-90 kg in boxes, safety-relevant). Choose a Polish or EU trader with a verifiable identity. Pay by card, or by PayPal with a card behind it, not by transfer, so chargeback stays available. Before paying, save the offer's stated return cost for bulky goods (art. 12(1)(10)); if it is missing, the trader bears return costs (art. 34(2)). Damage in transit: this is the seller's problem under consumer law, because risk passes when the consumer receives the goods (⚠ *(unverified)* Civil Code art. 548 §3, not re-read). Allegro's programme excludes carrier damage, so use the statutory route against the seller. A frame crack or net failure within 2 years is presumed to be a conformity defect; the seller collects and repairs at its own cost, which beats withdrawal plus paying for return freight. For an Amazon.de third-party seller in Germany: Amazon A-to-z first, then ECC Poland, which passes the case to ECC Germany (about 50 days, no enforcement). For a seller shipping from China via a marketplace: only the platform programme or a chargeback realistically works.

**workflow role**

Purchase step (choosing seller and payment method) and after-sales (complaint, withdrawal, escalation). Combine with the seller-identity registers item (who is the trader, which country), the shop-reputation item, and the Omnibus item (for fake-discount complaints).

**effort and cost per purchase**

Money: 0 PLN on the public routes. Time: about 10 minutes before purchase (save the offer PDF and seller identity, check the stated return cost, pay by card). About 30-60 minutes per complaint letter with a template. An ECC case means about 50 days of waiting plus follow-ups. No API credits are needed. The ELI API for statute text is free.

**evidence trail**

Strong when you keep it yourself. A vault note per purchase should hold: the offer snapshot (PDF or screenshot with seller name, address, NIP or VAT ID, variant, price, 30-day lowest price, stated return cost); the order confirmation; proof of payment (card or PayPal transaction ID); the delivery date (which starts the 14-day and 2-year clocks); damage photos and the carrier protocol; every message with its date; the complaint letter and the date it was sent, plus 14 days; the platform claim ID; the ECC case number. ECC wants exactly this pack: one chronological file, at most 4 attachments, 10 MB.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Statutory rights are strong and verifiable from the official text: 2-year conformity with a presumption, seller-paid repair and pickup (art. 43c-43d), and complaints deemed accepted after 14 days of silence (art. 7a).
  - The ECC route is free, works in Polish, and reaches traders in 28 other countries.
  - Three payment-layer backstops (chargeback, PayPal, Allegro) cover cases where the seller is unreachable or outside the EU.
  - Allegro's programme reimburses return shipping when Allegro payments were used, which PayPal does not.
  - Sole traders keep consumer rights for non-professional purchases (art. 7aa).
- **weaknesses**:
  - ECC does not pause limitation, has no enforcement power, and has about a 50-day backlog.
  - Non-EU sellers (China, US) are outside ECC and ADR until Directive 2025/2647 applies (2028), and then only voluntarily.
  - Allegro excludes carrier damage; PayPal makes the buyer pay return postage. Both matter for bulky goods.
  - Chargeback deadlines and scope depend on scheme and bank rules that are not public in full.
  - Private programmes decide at their own discretion and can demand an ID copy or police report.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of ECC Poland's success rate or of the Allegro and PayPal programmes' payout rates was found. Official aggregate: ECC-Net assisted over 125,000 consumers in 2023, intermediated 22,500 cases and recovered more than EUR 9 million (Commission ECC-Net page). ECC Poland helped in over 5,500 cross-border cases in 2024, and German traders topped the complaints (press summary of the ECC Poland report). Allegro's page shows a satisfaction share, which is vendor-claimed. Polish consumer press (Bankier, Antyweb, android.com.pl) consistently describes the Feb 2024 Allegro changes as reducing buyer protection.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW. Deciding fact: the statutory conformity route (seller pays pickup and repair, 2-year presumption) plus a card payment is the strongest protection for a bulky, safety-relevant purchase, while ECC is slow and does not pause limitation. Best use: store this cheat-sheet as a vault note and run a pre-purchase check (seller identity, EU or not, stated return cost, pay by card) before every durable-goods order; keep the evidence pack per purchase.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- ECC Poland contact: the complaint page and gov.pl give ECCNET-PL@ec.europa.eu and 22 55 60 600. An older infor.pl summary gives info@konsument.gov.pl and 22 55 60 118. Use the official page.
- UK scope: the gov.pl help page (13 Jan 2026) says ECC helps with businesses in 'the EU, Norway, Iceland or the UK'. konsument.gov.pl says EU, NO and IS, and the Commission says ECC-Net only 'cooperates' with the UK International Consumer Centre. Treat the UK as out of scope.
- BLIK disputes: bank and consumer guides (mBank, rankomat, Bankier) say chargeback covers only card payments and a BLIK payment cannot be reversed. PPRO's developer docs (updated 30 Sep 2025) describe BLIK consumer disputes, including 'goods or services not provided' and 'refund not received', for up to 13 months. Consumer-facing BLIK dispute rules depend on the bank ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- Chargeback window: one bank says the issuer can file within 120 days of the transaction or delivery. Shoper describes 120 days as the length of the whole Mastercard process. Another guide says 120-180 days.
- Allegro cap: some 2024 press says 40,000 PLN per buyer. The regulation text says per buyer per seller over two calendar years, which is the binding version.
- Consumer hotline hours: gov.pl says 10:00-18:00; some older pages say 8:00-18:00.

### Marketplace risk tiers

**Verdict:** USE NOW (platform gate) · **Cost:** N/A, enforcement record · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

A risk-tier reference built from enforcement records, not a tool. It summarises EU Digital Services Act (DSA) decisions, EU consumer-law (CPC network) actions, Polish UOKiK decisions and independent test purchases concerning three non-EU-origin marketplaces: Temu, AliExpress and Shein. The goal is to give the buyer a factual risk tier for safety-critical purchases such as a child trampoline, chargers or baby products. Status on 2026-10-15: Temu was fined EUR 200 million under the DSA (28 May 2026), AliExpress EUR 550 million (20 Jul 2026), and Shein is under formal DSA proceedings opened 17 Feb 2026 with no findings yet. The Digital Markets Act (DMA) does not apply: none of the three is a designated gatekeeper, so 'DMA enforcement' is N/A here. Role type: regulation / enforcement record.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

Temu: owned by PDD Holdings (Chinese-founded). In Poland, the contracting entity for sales is Whaleco Technology Limited, Dublin (UOKiK decision coverage). AliExpress: Alibaba Group (China). ⚠ *(unverified)* The EU contracting entity was not checked. Shein: Shein Group. It is established in Ireland in the EU, which is why Ireland's Digital Services Coordinator, Coimisiun na Mean, is associated with the DSA investigation (IP/26/420). All three are designated Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) under the DSA (Shein since April 2024). All three run marketplaces where most listings come from third-party sellers, many of them outside the EU. Bias note: the three platforms' own trust programmes (refund guarantees, 'verified' badges) are run by the party under investigation.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

Verified 2026-10-15. TEMU: formal DSA proceedings opened 31 Oct 2024. Preliminary findings in July 2025. Non-compliance decision with a EUR 200 million fine on 28 May 2026 for failing to diligently assess the systemic risk of illegal products, based on the 2024 risk assessment (IP/26/1178). An Article 75 action plan was due by 28 Aug 2026; the Digital Services Board then has one month and the Commission another month. No public outcome was found by 2026-10-15. Still open: addictive design, recommender systems and researcher data access (press coverage of the Commission's statements). Temu called the fine 'disproportionate'. ⚠ *(unverified)* No General Court filing was found. ALIEXPRESS: proceedings opened 14 Mar 2024. On 18 Jun 2025 the Commission made commitments binding (notice and action, ad and recommender transparency) and issued preliminary findings on illegal products. Non-compliance decision with a EUR 550 million fine on 20 Jul 2026, the largest DSA fine to date (IP/26/1654). The action plan is due 20 Oct 2026. ⚠ *(unverified)* AliExpress is reported to be challenging the fine at the General Court (MLex via LexisNexis, paywalled). SHEIN: designated VLOP April 2024. Requests for information on 28 Jun 2024, 6 Feb 2025 and 26 Nov 2025. Formal proceedings opened 17 Feb 2026 on illegal products (including child-like sex dolls), addictive design and recommender transparency (IP/26/420). No preliminary findings were found by 2026-10-15. The Paris Court of Appeal refused France's bid to suspend Shein's marketplace on 19 Mar 2026. CPC network (consumer law): Temu was notified of breaches in Nov 2024, Shein in May 2025. ⚠ *(unverified)* No published outcome was found for either. POLAND: UOKiK fined Whaleco Technology Ltd (Temu) PLN 5,910,900 on 12 Jan 2026 over the Omnibus 30-day lowest price; the decision is not final.

**⚠ cost model**

N/A. This is an enforcement record with no tool to pay for. Cost signal for buyers: since 1 Jul 2026 the EU levies a flat EUR 3 customs duty per item type on parcels worth up to EUR 150 from outside the EU, until 1 Jul 2028. The seller or importer declares and pays it, and it may be passed on to the buyer (Retail Gazette Jul 2026, Reuters via cyprus-mail Dec 2025; secondary). A trampoline above EUR 150 pays normal duty and VAT anyway. ⚠ *(unverified)* How each platform prices this for Polish buyers was not verified.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **poland**: All three sell to Poland. Temu sells through Temu.com/pl under Whaleco Technology Ltd (Ireland), with a Polish UOKiK decision. ⚠ *(unverified)* The Polish-language storefronts of AliExpress and Shein were not opened for this item. UOKiK said it monitors all three platforms (price and promotion presentation) and that AliExpress changed some practices after UOKiK intervened (tvp.info, undated, secondary).
- **eu**: DSA decisions and proceedings apply EU-wide. CPC actions are coordinated EU-wide and enforced nationally. France ran a national suspension attempt against Shein, rejected on appeal on 19 Mar 2026.
- **us**: N/A. Out of scope for EU risk tiers.
- **dma**: N/A. None of the three is a DMA gatekeeper.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

N/A. This is an enforcement record. Relevant warning from the AliExpress decision: traders 'easily circumvented' the brand-authorisation system, and products were listed in wrong categories with looser compliance checks (IP/26/1654). Brand names, category labels and variant names on these platforms are therefore weak evidence of what the product actually is.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

N/A. This is an enforcement record.

**price history and omnibus**

Relevant enforcement. UOKiK found that Temu showed untrue 30-day lowest prices, with reference prices that did not track real changes; one example was balloons sold at 10.07-14.38 PLN while the reference stayed at 18.48 PLN (UOKiK charges, 29 May 2025, via Tabletowo). UOKiK fined Temu PLN 5,910,900 on 12 Jan 2026 (not final); the practice reportedly stopped on 22 Oct 2025. The CPC network flagged 'fake discounts' at Temu (Nov 2024) and at Shein (May 2025). So discount claims on these platforms need independent checking.

**total landed cost**

Partly relevant. The EUR 3 duty per item type applies from 1 Jul 2026 on parcels of EUR 150 or less from outside the EU. Return shipping to sellers outside the EU and weak enforcement of returns add hidden cost: the CPC action against Shein cited unclear return and refund information, and ECC Poland warns about shops that demand returns to Asia. For a bulky item, a seller outside the EU makes withdrawal returns impractical.

**review and seller verification**

Grade: none as a tool, but the decisions show which seller-verification controls failed. AliExpress did not enforce its penalty policy against repeat-offending traders; penalised stores stayed active. Brand authorisation was understaffed and easy to bypass (IP/26/1654). The CPC action covered fake reviews and hidden trader contact details at Temu (Nov 2024, trade press) and hard-to-find contact details at Shein (May 2025). UOKiK charged Temu with not telling buyers whether they contract with a business or a private person, and how duties are split between Temu and the seller (press, 2025). What this cannot prove: whether any single listing or seller today is compliant.

**safety and compliance checks**

Core evidence for the risk tier. (1) Commission mystery shopping for the Temu case, by an independent lab: 'a very high percentage' of tested chargers failed basic safety tests, and 'a high percentage' of baby toys posed medium-to-high risks (chemicals above limits, detachable parts that could suffocate). The release gives no counts (IP/26/1178). EU customs and market-surveillance data showed high non-compliance in those categories. (2) AliExpress: illegal products stayed online for weeks after detection, and Commission testing found illegal products being recommended and advertised before removal (IP/26/1654). (3) Stiftung Warentest with Test-Achats/Testaankoop (BE) and Taenk (DK), published 30 Oct 2025 and updated 28 May 2026: 162 items from Temu and Shein (54 necklaces, 54 USB chargers, 54 toys for under-3s); 110 failed EU standards and about a quarter were potentially dangerous; 52 of 54 chargers failed; one Shein pendant had cadmium about 8,500 times the limit. (4) Toy Industries of Europe (an industry body, so self-interested), 17 Oct 2024: over 100 unbranded toys from third-party traders on 10 marketplaces (Allegro, AliExpress, Amazon Marketplace, Bol, Cdiscount, Fruugo, Light In The Box, Shein, Temu, Wish); about 80% failed EU safety rules. No per-platform split, and the study covered unbranded toys only. For a trampoline: none of these tests covered trampolines. Treat any EN 71-14 or TUV claim on these platforms as unverified until checked in Certipedia or with the EU responsible person; see the sibling items.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

Category tests linked to these platforms: Stiftung Warentest et al. (Oct 2025, chargers, jewellery, under-3 toys; access: article on test.de; Shein and Temu sold the items), TIE (Oct 2024, toys, 10 marketplaces), and Testaankoop (70% of Shein and Temu products non-compliant; 53 of 54 toys failed at least one test; secondary, date not verified). The Commission's own mystery shopping was not published as a dataset. ⚠ *(unverified)* No independent trampoline test of products from Temu, AliExpress or Shein was found.

**alerts and monitoring**

N/A as a tool. Watch list: the Commission's decision on Temu's action plan (expected around late Oct 2026), AliExpress's action plan (due 20 Oct 2026), Shein preliminary findings, CPC outcomes, and whether Temu or AliExpress General Court cases (if any) proceed. Sources to monitor: the press-corner API (no key needed) and the DSA enforcement pages on digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

N/A. This is an enforcement record. Relevant design finding: the Temu decision criticised the risk assessment for not covering how recommender systems and affiliated influencer promotion amplify illegal products (IP/26/1178). An AI shopping agent that relies on these platforms' rankings inherits that amplification.

**⚠ after sales and resale**

Brief. Sellers outside the EU make the 2-year conformity claim hard to enforce in practice, and spare parts (nets, pads, springs) for unbranded items are unlikely to be available. Resale value of unbranded trampolines is low. ⚠ *(unverified)* No data was found.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Commission press releases (28 May 2026, 20 Jul 2026, 17 Feb 2026) are primary and current. test.de article updated 28 May 2026. TIE study dated 17 Oct 2024, older than six months. UOKiK Temu decision 12 Jan 2026 (press, primary not opened). CPC actions date from Nov 2024 and May 2025, older than six months, and no outcome was found. Paris appeal ruling 19 Mar 2026 (press).

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial. The Commission press-corner JSON API (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/api/documents?reference=IP/26/1178&language=en) returns the full release text without a key; I used it for IP/26/1178, IP/26/1654, IP/26/420 and IP/26/1772. A Claude Code skill can poll it, or the DSA enforcement page, to refresh a 'marketplace risk' vault note. No official API lists DSA cases per platform. ⚠ *(unverified)* The Commission's DSA transparency database (statements of reasons) has an API, but it was not tested here. No MCP server for DSA enforcement was found. Setup effort: low (a fetch plus a summary step).

**protocol support**

N/A. These are enforcement records.

**⚠ open source and licence**

N/A. Commission press releases may be reused under the Commission's reuse policy (Decision 2011/833/EU). ⚠ *(unverified)* The decision text was not re-read.

**account linking and data access**

N/A for the record itself. When buying on these platforms, the buyer gives an account, address and payment data to a company outside the EU or to its EU subsidiary. Prefer card or PayPal over stored wallets so a chargeback stays available.

**automation legal risk**

N/A for reading Commission releases, which are public. Scraping the marketplaces themselves is outside this item.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

The marketplaces earn from commissions, ads, and affiliate and influencer programmes. The Temu decision names 'affiliated influencers' and recommender systems as amplifiers of illegal products. The CPC actions name pressure tactics (fake deadlines, forced gamification) at Temu and Shein, and the Shein DSA case covers addictive design (points and rewards).

**ranking transparency**

Weak at Temu and AliExpress, according to the decisions: recommender and advertising systems pushed illegal products (AliExpress testing). Recommender transparency and the non-profiling option are under investigation at Shein (IP/26/420).

**run to run consistency**

N/A. These are not AI tools.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

N/A as AI. Marketplace-level manipulation is documented: CPC findings of fake discounts, false deadlines and fake reviews (Temu, Shein); evasion of brand authorisation and category checks (AliExpress).

**known failures**

Documented by regulators: risk assessments built on sector-wide information instead of platform-specific evidence (Temu); overestimated detection performance and understaffed review (AliExpress); illegal products online for weeks after detection (AliExpress); repeat offenders left active (AliExpress); untrue 30-day reference prices (Temu, Poland). Child-like sex dolls, prohibited weapons and banned medicines were found on Shein's marketplace in France (Nov 2025). Shein says it removed the items and stopped selling sex dolls worldwide (press).

**regulatory enforcement history**

DSA: Temu EUR 200 million (28 May 2026, IP/26/1178); AliExpress EUR 550 million (20 Jul 2026, IP/26/1654) plus commitments made binding on 18 Jun 2025; Shein formal proceedings opened 17 Feb 2026 (IP/26/420). For context: X was fined EUR 120 million in Dec 2025 (press), so these are the second and third DSA fines. Consumer law (CPC network): Temu notified of breaches Nov 2024 (CCPC Ireland, Belgium, Germany's UBA leading); Shein notified May 2025 (BE, FR, IE, NL leading). Poland: UOKiK, Whaleco Technology Ltd (Temu), PLN 5,910,900 on 12 Jan 2026 (not final). National: the Paris Court of Appeal refused France's request to suspend Shein's marketplace (19 Mar 2026, n. 25/20957) but upheld the age-verification order for adult products. DMA: N/A.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

Weakest of the purchase routes when the seller is outside the EU. Statutory withdrawal and conformity rights are owed by the trader; when that trader is in China, enforcement is impractical, and ECC cannot pursue traders outside the EU. ⚠ *(unverified)* The EU-established platform operators (Temu: Whaleco Technology Ltd, Ireland; Shein: Irish establishment) are reachable by ECC Ireland for the platform's own obligations, not as the seller. Realistic routes: the platform's own refund programme, then card chargeback or PayPal. See the ECC and buyer-protection item for deadlines.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Useful as a decision rule, not as a shopping tool. Proposed risk tiers for safety-critical durables such as a trampoline: TIER 1 (preferred): an EU retailer or brand store is the seller of record with a verifiable identity, for example a brand's own store, Decathlon or a Media Expert own listing. TIER 2 (check the seller): EU marketplaces with third-party sellers (Allegro, Amazon.de Marketplace). Only buy from an EU-registered business seller that names the manufacturer and EU responsible person; TIE found unsafe toys from third-party traders on Allegro and Amazon too. TIER 3 (avoid for safety-critical items): marketplaces with confirmed DSA non-compliance decisions on illegal or unsafe products (Temu, AliExpress) or open proceedings including illegal products (Shein), when the seller is outside the EU or unbranded. Applied to the trampoline: a cheap unbranded 3 m trampoline shipped from China on Temu, AliExpress or Shein should be ruled out, whatever EN 71-14 claim the listing makes.

**workflow role**

Seller check and safety step: a gate before price comparison. Combine with the Safety Gate and UOKiK register item, the GPSR listing-data checks, the EN 71-14 and Certipedia item, and the seller-identity registers.

**effort and cost per purchase**

About 1 minute per purchase once the tier table is in the vault: classify the platform and seller. Refreshing the table is about 15 minutes per quarter (reading new Commission releases). Cost 0.

**evidence trail**

Good. Each tier assignment can cite a Commission release number (IP/26/1178, IP/26/1654, IP/26/420) and a date, plus the test sources. A saved vault record would be a table with columns platform | decision | date | amount | status | source URL | date checked.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Rests on formal Commission non-compliance decisions with named evidence (mystery shopping, risk-assessment reports), not on opinion.
  - Independent lab tests (Stiftung Warentest with BE and DK partners) agree with the regulator's findings for chargers and baby toys.
  - Easy to refresh from a keyless Commission API.
  - The Polish angle is covered by the UOKiK Temu decision on reference prices.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Decisions judge systemic risk management, not individual products: a specific listing can be safe, and an EU marketplace listing can be unsafe (TIE included Allegro and Amazon).
  - None of the tests covered trampolines.
  - Decisions are under challenge (AliExpress reported at the General Court) and may change.
  - Shein has no findings yet, so its tier rests on the scope of open proceedings and on lab tests.
  - CPC outcomes for Temu and Shein are not public.

**independent review consensus**

Regulators and consumer testers agree that a large share of cheap unbranded electrical and child products sold by third-party sellers on Temu and Shein fail EU rules: Commission mystery shopping, Stiftung Warentest/Testaankoop/Taenk (110 of 162 items failed), and Testaankoop (53 of 54 toys failed, secondary). TIE (an industry body, so self-interested) reports the same for unbranded toys across 10 marketplaces including EU ones. A French court took a narrower view of Shein, finding no ongoing systemic risk after the items were removed (19 Mar 2026).

**verdict for me**

USE NOW, as a seller-and-platform gate. Deciding fact: two final DSA non-compliance decisions (Temu, AliExpress) and corroborating lab tests show unsafe chargers and child products from third-party sellers. Best use: put the three-tier rule in the vault and exclude tier-3 sources for any safety-critical purchase (trampoline, child products, chargers) before comparing prices.

**conflicting evidence**

- AliExpress status: the research brief says AliExpress is 'under DSA proceedings'. The Commission fined it EUR 550 million on 20 Jul 2026 (IP/26/1654). One aggregator headline says EUR 500 million, a typo.
- Shein systemic risk: the Commission opened proceedings over illegal products (17 Feb 2026). The Paris Court of Appeal (19 Mar 2026) found no systemic risk of the illegal goods reappearing, given Shein's removals and new controls.
- Toy failure rates: Commission mystery shopping on Temu gives no numbers ('high percentage'). Stiftung Warentest et al. found almost all toys poorly labelled and some failing chemical or noise limits. TIE gives about 80% across 10 marketplaces including EU ones. Testaankoop gives 53 of 54. Samples and methods differ, so the figures are not comparable.
- Temu proceedings timeline: some coverage dates the preliminary findings to 28 Jul 2025; the Commission release says only 'July 2025'.
- Shein EU user numbers: 108 million (EU figures, press) vs 145 million or more (Shein, press).
