## D. Ready-made AI shopping assistants

### ChatGPT Shopping Research

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY, PILOT for discovery · **Cost:** Included in Free, Go, Plus, Pro · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 12 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

ChatGPT's shopping stack from OpenAI, as of 2026-10-15. It has five parts. (1) Shopping research: a buyer's-guide mode launched 24 Nov 2025. It asks clarifying questions, researches for a few minutes and returns top picks, trade-offs, comparison tables and merchant links. It runs on 'a version of GPT-5 mini trained with reinforcement learning specifically for shopping', post-trained on GPT-5-Thinking-mini. (2) Product discovery UI, 24 Mar 2026: visual browsing, side-by-side comparison of price, reviews and features, image-based lookalike search, and conversational filtering. (3) Instant Checkout: launched 29 Sep 2025 for US users and US Etsy sellers; OpenAI is now 'moving away from a standalone Instant Checkout', and purchases complete on merchant sites or apps. (4) Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP): an open standard by OpenAI and Stripe (Apache-2.0), first for checkout and since 2026 also for merchant product feeds. (5) ChatGPT Ads: a US test from 9 Feb 2026, 31 European markets from 24 Aug 2026, shown only on the Free and Go plans. Lifecycle context: the ChatGPT Atlas browser was retired (sunset announced 9 Jul 2026, target date 9 Aug 2026), and its functions moved into the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in browser. Role type: AI assistant + protocol + ads platform.

**vendor and ownership**

OpenAI (San Francisco, US). Users in the EEA or Switzerland contract with OpenAI Ireland Ltd, Dublin (Europe Terms of Use, updated 16 Jan 2026). ACP is 'currently maintained by OpenAI and Stripe' (GitHub repository description). OpenAI does not own a marketplace or retailer. It earns from subscriptions and ads; Instant Checkout charged merchants a fee, but the merchant page now says 'there are no fees on purchases that start in ChatGPT'. Merchant partners named for ACP discovery: Target, Sephora, Nordstrom, Lowe's, Best Buy, The Home Depot, Wayfair; Shopify merchants through Shopify Catalog; Walmart through its own ChatGPT app. All are US-centric.

**lifecycle status**

Verified 2026-10-15 against OpenAI pages. 28 Apr 2025: ChatGPT shopping product cards. A Polish test (Benchmark.pl, 29 Apr 2025) saw no product cards in Poland. 29 Sep 2025: Instant Checkout plus ACP launched for the US. 24 Nov 2025: shopping research launched on mobile and web for logged-in Free, Go, Plus and Pro users, with 'nearly unlimited usage' through the holidays. Polish press reported global availability, with the Polish UI label 'Analiza zakupow' (Spider's Web, 25 Nov 2025). 9 Feb 2026: ads test starts in the US. 9 Mar 2026: The Information reported OpenAI scaling back in-chat checkout (via Shopifreaks). 24 Mar 2026: 'Powering Product Discovery' post; OpenAI said the first Instant Checkout 'did not offer the level of flexibility that we aspire to provide' and lets merchants use their own checkout. 9 Jul 2026: Atlas sunset announced, target 9 Aug 2026 (9to5mac, Gigazine; no OpenAI post found). 18 Aug 2026: ads announced for 31 European markets, starting 'next week' (24 Aug per press); self-serve Ads Manager live in those markets from 31 Aug 2026. 31 Aug 2026: the Commission designated ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine under the DSA (IP/26/1772). 5 Oct 2026: visual ad format to be tested during image generation (US). The shopping research help article showed 'Updated: 2 months ago' on 2026-10-15. Now launched in it: start research from products already shown in chat via 'Research'. The merchant page (2026-10-15) says 'Shopping is currently live for ChatGPT users in the U.S.'

**⚠ cost model**

Shopping research: included on Free, Go, Plus and Pro; no separate fee (launch post). ⚠ *(unverified)* Current per-plan usage limits for shopping research were not published. ⚠ *(unverified)* Plan prices: the pricing page did not render prices in my session on 2026-10-15, so no PLN or EUR prices were recorded. Free and Go may show ads. A Free 'Ads-Free' option exists with lower limits and no image generation or deep research. Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu are ad-free (Ads help article, updated 2026-10-14). Merchants: product feeds are free, with no fees on purchases that start in ChatGPT (chatgpt.com/merchants, 2026-10-15). Ads: CPM, CPC and conversion bidding; self-serve at ads.openai.com.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **shopping research buyers guide**: US: yes. PL: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed for Poland on 2026-10-15. It launched for logged-in users without a stated region limit, and Polish press (Nov 2025) reported it globally with a Polish UI label. But the current help article starts it from product cards already in chat, and OpenAI's merchant page says shopping 'is currently live for ChatGPT users in the U.S.'.
- **rich product results visual discovery comparison tables**: US: yes (24 Mar 2026). PL and EU: not confirmed. The merchant page says US only and that it 'will expand to additional regions over time'.
- **merchant product feeds acp**: US merchants onboarding, with a waitlist and a self-serve portal promised 'later this year'. The application form accepts Poland as HQ country, but that does not mean live coverage.
- **instant checkout agentic payment**: US only, and deprioritised. Purchases complete on merchant sites or apps. Never available in PL or the EU.
- **chatgpt apps merchant**: Allegro app in ChatGPT is used from Poland since May 2026 (per the sibling Allegro result, not re-verified here). Glovo launched a Polish ChatGPT and Claude extension in Aug 2026 (Wiadomosci Handlowe, secondary). The Walmart app is US only.
- **ads**: US since 9 Feb 2026. 31 European markets since 24 Aug 2026. OpenAI names DE, FR, ES, IT, SE, NO, DK, NL and AT; Digiday names Poland. Free and Go plans only. Personalised ads are not initially available in the EEA or Switzerland.
- **memory personalisation**: Shopping research can use ChatGPT memory. ⚠ *(unverified)* 'Reference chat history' launched in Apr 2025 excluding the EEA, UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein; whether that exclusion still applies in Oct 2026 was not confirmed. The Memory help article (updated about 26 days before 2026-10-15) says only that features 'vary by plan, region'.
- **language**: ChatGPT answers in Polish and has a Polish UI. Polish shop coverage is the limiting factor, not the language.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. The buyer's guide translates specs into practical implications, lists top picks with trade-offs, and builds side-by-side tables (price, size, core features, the user's constraints). It performs best in 'electronics, beauty, home and garden, kitchen and appliances, sports and outdoor' (vendor-claimed). EAN/GTIN mapping is not exposed to the user. The ACP feed schema (spec 2026-04-17) gives each Variant barcodes (type, value), price, list_price, availability, condition, variant_options, seller and marketplace, so feed-fed merchants can be matched by GTIN, but only for US feed merchants today. Independent evidence on variants is weak: Product.ai (22 Sep 2026) found engines presenting superseded models as current (for example Sony WH-1000XM5 vs XM6, mostly Gemini) and conflicts on 97% of head-to-head comparison questions across the four engines tested. No evidence was found on handling white-label OEM rebadges.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

It compares prices across the merchants it finds, but it is not a price index. In the first response, the price shown may be the first merchant's rather than the lowest (secondary report of OpenAI's own wording). Polish coverage checked through robots.txt on 2026-10-15: Amazon.de and Amazon.pl disallow OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User and GPTBot. Media Expert explicitly allows GPTBot and OAI-SearchBot. Allegro, Ceneo, x-kom and Decathlon.pl have no OpenAI-specific rules. ⚠ *(unverified)* Allegro's bot protection may still block crawling in practice. The help article confirms that 'some retailers block automated access', and shopping research then skips those sources. Number of shops indexed: not disclosed. ACP feed partners are all US.

**price history and omnibus**

None. No price history, no Omnibus 30-day lowest price, and no fake-discount detection. The ACP feed has price and list_price but no history field. 'Finding deals' is a marketed use case, but deal claims are not checked against a 30-day reference.

**total landed cost**

None. The help FAQ tells users to 'confirm the final price, taxes, fees, and shipping costs on the retailer's website' and to read return and warranty policies themselves. The ACP feed schema has no shipping-cost or return-fee fields. For a bulky trampoline, shipping and return costs must come from another tool or from the shop.

**⚠ review and seller verification**

Partial at best. It reads reviews and cites sources, avoiding 'low-quality or spammy sites' (vendor-claimed). ⚠ *(unverified)* Review and rating figures shown in summaries are not verified by OpenAI (secondary report). No seller-identity check (CEIDG, KRS, VIES) and no fake-review detection. It cannot prove that a recommended shop is legitimate or that a review is genuine.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No Safety Gate or UOKiK lookup, no GPSR field check, no EN 71-14 version check, no Certipedia verification. It may mention safety standards if a source page does, but the claim is not verified.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

It may cite review sites it finds (for example Wirecutter or RTINGS) when they are crawlable. Wharton's ACES experiments (published 28 Sep 2026) show agents heavily anchor on such sources: one Wirecutter-style review shifted choices by up to 99 percentage points. ⚠ *(unverified)* It does not systematically surface paywalled lab tests such as Stiftung Warentest, VKI or CHOICE.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

None in shopping research. No price-drop or restock alerts. ⚠ *(unverified)* Separately, ChatGPT 'scheduled tasks' (Plus and higher) could re-run a query on a schedule, but that is an unsupported workaround with no price snapshot. Pulse can suggest buyer's guides proactively (Pro, launch post).

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Today: no purchase inside ChatGPT for EU users. The merchant FAQ says users discover and evaluate in ChatGPT, but 'purchases are completed on merchant-owned websites or apps'. Historical (US only, Sep 2025 to Mar 2026): Instant Checkout had single-item orders, with the user confirming order, shipping and payment before any action. It used encrypted payment tokens 'only authorized for specific amounts and specific merchants' (Stripe Shared Payment Token or the ACP Delegated Payments Spec), and the merchant was merchant of record handling fulfilment, returns and support. No spending caps beyond per-order token scoping were described. Merchant apps (for example Walmart) can link accounts and use the merchant's payments.

**after sales and resale**

None. No spare parts, service network, warranty handling or resale data. After-sales goes entirely through the merchant.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Per the help article: merchant product data via ACP, 'publicly available product information' and 'other relevant retail sources'. It reads product pages in real time and cites sources. Freshness: live crawl at query time, plus feeds that merchants sync (US). Every top pick has a merchant link. Reported lags: secondary analyses say mismatches come from copied or stale prices on comparison and deal sites. Core dna (7 Oct 2026, Australia, free account, memory off) found 15 of 24 checkable retailer prices wrong, every one shown lower than the store's real price.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: none for shopping research itself. No API endpoint, MCP server or CLI exposes shopping research or the product-discovery UI. The OpenAI API offers general models with web search, not the shopping-trained model or the buyer's-guide UI. ⚠ *(unverified)* No public shopping-research model ID was found. Browser automation of chatgpt.com is against the Europe Terms of Use, which prohibit 'automatically or programmatically extracting data or Output'. Merchant side: ACP is open (github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol; Apache-2.0; 1,574 stars, 254 forks, 144 open issues; last commit 18 Jul 2026; spec versions 2025-09-29 to 2026-04-17 plus unreleased; OpenAPI and JSON Schema for checkout, delegate_payment and feed). It is useful if he builds a merchant-side or agent-side integration, not for driving ChatGPT from Claude Code. ChatGPT apps (Apps SDK, MCP-based) let merchants such as Allegro run inside ChatGPT, which is the reverse direction. Practical route from Claude Code: none. Use ChatGPT manually and paste or save the guide into the vault. Setup effort: zero manually, not automatable.

**⚠ protocol support**

ACP: the author and maintainer, with Stripe. It covers checkout, delegated payments and, since 2026, product feeds for discovery (feed metadata includes target_country). MCP: used by ChatGPT apps and connectors. ⚠ *(unverified)* No support was found for Google's UCP or AP2, Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, Mastercard Agent Pay or Klarna APP. Future-proofing: ACP is open-sourced and multi-vendor (Salesforce and Stripe as feed providers, Shopify Catalog), but adoption is US-centred.

**open source and licence**

ChatGPT and shopping research: closed. ACP specification: open source, Apache-2.0. Repository created 29 Sep 2025, last commit 18 Jul 2026 (gh API, 2026-10-15).

**account linking and data access**

Shopping research needs a logged-in ChatGPT account. It uses memory if enabled; memory can be turned off, and Temporary Chat avoids it. Chats are 'never shared with retailers' (vendor-claimed). Ads: advertisers get only aggregated reporting. In the EEA and Switzerland, ads are not personalised at launch; contextual ads still use the current chat, general location and language. No payment credentials are needed now that Instant Checkout is US-only and deprioritised. Merchant apps may ask for account linking (for example Allegro, Walmart). GDPR: OpenAI Ireland Ltd is the provider for EEA users. ChatGPT search is a VLOSE under the DSA since 31 Aug 2026, with compliance due by January 2027.

**automation legal risk**

High for automating ChatGPT itself: the Europe Terms of Use prohibit automated or programmatic extraction of data or Output, with a risk of account suspension. For ChatGPT crawling shops: Amazon blocks OpenAI agents in robots.txt (Amazon.de and Amazon.pl). Context: in Amazon v. Perplexity, a district court granted Amazon a preliminary injunction against the Comet agent on 9-10 Mar 2026, but the Ninth Circuit vacated it on 4 Aug 2026 and remanded; contract (ToS) claims remain (secondary coverage).

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Subscriptions and, since 2026, ads on the Free and Go plans. Per OpenAI, ads appear 'below the end of a response', are labelled as sponsored, are kept separate, and do not influence answers. Ads are ranked by relevance and advertiser bids. The shopping research help article says 'Ads are separate from shopping research'. Shopping results are claimed to be 'organic and unsponsored'. Merchant-side bias vectors: (1) feed participants get 'better placement in results' because 'richer data helps your products surface' (merchant page), so feed partners such as big US retailers and Shopify are structurally favoured; (2) the Sep 2025 post listed 'whether Instant Checkout is enabled' among ranking factors when several merchants sell the same item. ⚠ *(unverified)* Whether ads now appear inside or next to shopping research results in Europe was not observed.

**ranking transparency**

Partial. Each top pick comes with a rationale, strengths, trade-offs and merchant links, and sources are cited. You can mark 'Not interested' or 'More like this', exclude brands, and change constraints. There is no visible score, no way to rerun with a specific source excluded other than by asking, and no disclosure of feed versus crawl origin. Ads are labelled 'sponsored' and sit below the answer.

**⚠ run to run consistency**

Low according to independent tests (none tested the shopping research mode specifically). Core dna (7 Oct 2026, ChatGPT free, Australia): 14 of 20 products got a different store or price on a second identical ask. Product.ai (published 22 Sep 2026; 220 questions times 5 runs on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity, free and paid): 86% of scored questions had a confirmed conflict; 85% of 913 verifiable prices were exactly right, but misses were off by a median of USD 300. Product.ai is a vendor with a coupon business. ⚠ *(unverified)* Per-engine ChatGPT price accuracy (85% free, 82% paid) comes only from a search summary and was not seen on the page. SparkToro (Nov-Dec 2025, secondary): less than a 1-in-100 chance that two ChatGPT brand lists match. No own repeat test was run.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Weakly evidenced. OpenAI says it avoids 'low-quality or spammy sites' (vendor-claimed). Research on agents in general: ACES (Allouah et al., arXiv 2508.02630, v3 Dec 2025) found position bias, penalties for sponsored tags, and large market-share gains from seller-side tweaks to product descriptions. Wharton (28 Sep 2026, ACES-based) found that a single review moved choices by up to 99 percentage points, that source order changed outcomes for 4 of 6 models, and that a one-line memory pushed 4 models to a pricier product. ⚠ *(unverified)* Wharton did not name the GPT models, so these results are not specific to ChatGPT. No ChatGPT-specific prompt-injection or fake-shop test of shopping research was found.

**known failures**

OpenAI states that it 'might make mistakes about product details like price and availability'. Independent: wrong prices that are always lower than the store's real price (Core dna); stale or superseded models and conflicting specs (Product.ai, cross-engine); answers changing between runs. In Poland: no product cards seen in the Apr 2025 Polish test (Benchmark.pl), plus unreleased phones recommended. Shops that block crawlers, including Amazon, are skipped. Instant Checkout failed commercially: weak merchant uptake (about 12 Shopify merchants went live per one report, about 30 per Forrester as of Feb 2026), US sales tax collection missing as of Feb 2026, and Walmart said conversion was about 3 times lower in-chat than click-out (Modern Retail, 27 Mar 2026).

**regulatory enforcement history**

DSA: ChatGPT was designated a Very Large Online Search Engine on 31 Aug 2026 (IP/26/1772), with systemic-risk duties due by January 2027. This is a designation, not a finding. GDPR: the Italian Garante's EUR 15 million fine (Nov 2024) was annulled by the Rome tribunal on 18 Mar 2026 on jurisdiction grounds, because Ireland's DPC is the lead authority (secondary). No UOKiK, DMA or consumer-law decision on ChatGPT shopping was found.

**buyer protection path**

ChatGPT is not the seller or merchant of record. It hands the user to the merchant, and all protection comes from the merchant and payment method: statutory 14-day withdrawal and 2-year conformity against an EU trader, ECC for a cross-border EU seller, card chargeback, PayPal, or marketplace programmes such as Allegro's. Historical Instant Checkout (US): the merchant was merchant of record and handled returns and support. See the ECC and buyer-protection item.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Moderate for discovery, poor for the Polish purchase decision. For the trampoline, it can turn 'round 3-3.7 m, safety net inside, frame warranty, budget EUR 200-700, kids 6-10' into a short list with trade-offs (net type, spring count, frame gauge, max user weight) and explain spec jargon. It cannot verify EN 71-14:2018 vs 2025 compliance, check Safety Gate, compute delivered cost to Poland, show Omnibus or historic prices, or reliably list Polish shops: Amazon.de and Amazon.pl block it, Allegro coverage is uncertain, and US-only rich product results do not apply. Its prices must be re-checked on the shop page. Expect models sold in the US or Germany that are not available in Poland.

**workflow role**

Discovery and early spec education, giving an initial shortlist and the trade-offs to care about. Combine with Ceneo or Allegro for Polish prices and offers, with the Omnibus field and price trackers for price history, with Safety Gate and Certipedia for safety, with seller registers for seller checks, and with independent lab tests (Stiftung Warentest, VKI, CHOICE) for quality.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Setup: none (an existing ChatGPT account). One run: about 3-10 minutes of research plus clarifying questions, at no marginal cost on any plan. Cost per comparison: 0 PLN beyond the subscription; Plus avoids ads. Arithmetic: 1 shopping-research run plus about 10 minutes re-checking 3-5 top picks on Polish shop pages is about 20 minutes per product comparison. Not automatable from Claude Code, so it adds manual copy-paste time.

**⚠ evidence trail**

Partial. The buyer's guide includes cited sources and merchant links that can be copied into a vault note. It provides no price snapshots, timestamps per price or screenshots. A saved record would hold: the query and constraints, the date, the top picks with ChatGPT's rationale, the cited URLs, and a column of re-verified shop prices with the date checked. ⚠ *(unverified)* The ChatGPT 'share link' could be stored, but the share format for shopping research was not tested.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Good at turning vague needs into constraints and explaining trade-offs; a shopping-trained model with interactive refinement (launch post).
  - Free on every plan, with a Polish-language interface and answers.
  - Cites sources and links merchants; ads are labelled and claimed to be separate from answers.
  - ACP is open (Apache-2.0) and documented, which is useful if he builds agent or merchant integrations.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Rich shopping is live only in the US (merchant page, 2026-10-15); Polish availability of shopping research is unconfirmed.
  - No price history, Omnibus, landed cost, seller or safety checks.
  - Independent tests show wrong prices (15 of 24 in Core dna) and low run-to-run consistency.
  - Cannot be driven from Claude Code, and the ToS forbid programmatic extraction.
  - Amazon blocks OpenAI crawlers, and Polish shop coverage is unknown.

**independent review consensus**

Independent tests agree that ChatGPT shopping answers are useful for orientation but unreliable on exact prices and stable recommendations. Core dna (10 Oct 2026, small sample, Australia): 14 of 20 answers changed and 15 of 24 prices were wrong. Product.ai (22 Sep 2026, vendor with a commercial interest, US): 86% of questions had conflicts across engines, and price misses had a median error of USD 300. Wharton AI & Analytics (28 Sep 2026): agent choices are highly sensitive to single sources and memory. SparkToro (Dec 2025, secondary): brand lists are almost never identical. None of these tests used shopping research mode specifically, and none covered Poland. Polish press from Nov 2025 only relays OpenAI claims, with no hands-on test.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY, or PILOT for discovery. Deciding fact: OpenAI's own merchant page says shopping is live only in the US, and the tool has no price-history, landed-cost, seller or safety checks and no API. Best use: one manual shopping-research run to learn the trade-offs and get candidate models, saved as cited text in the vault, then verify everything with Polish tools.

**conflicting evidence**

- Ads in Europe: the brief says '30 European countries, Poland not named'. OpenAI's post (18 Aug 2026) says 31 markets and names DE, FR, ES, IT, SE, NO, DK, NL and AT but not Poland. Digiday (19 Aug 2026) names Poland. Indexlab says the 31 are the 27 EU states plus IS, LI, NO and CH.
- Shopping research in Poland: Spider's Web (25 Nov 2025) reports global rollout with the Polish label 'Analiza zakupow'. OpenAI's merchant page (2026-10-15) says 'Shopping is currently live for ChatGPT users in the U.S.'.
- Instant Checkout launch partners: OpenAI says US Etsy sellers first, with Shopify 'coming soon' (29 Sep 2025). Shopifreaks and others say it launched 'in October 2025 with Etsy and Walmart'.
- Instant Checkout uptake: about 12 Shopify merchants went live (one report) vs about 30 Shopify merchants participating by Feb 2026 (Forrester, via eesel).
- Product.ai headline: Tech.co reported 'AI shopping assistants are wrong 86% of the time'. Product.ai's 86% is the share of questions with a confirmed cross-engine conflict, and 85% of verifiable prices were exactly right.
- Atlas shutdown: 9to5mac calls 9 Aug 2026 a 'targeted' date. Others report it as firm. No OpenAI post confirming the final shutdown was found.

### Perplexity Shopping and Comet

**Verdict:** PILOT (research backend only) · **Cost:** Free; Pro USD 20 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Two related Perplexity products. (1) Perplexity Shopping: the shopping layer of the Perplexity answer engine - product cards with images, prices and AI-summarised specs/reviews, plus 'Instant Buy', an in-chat checkout through PayPal launched 25 Nov 2025 (successor of the Nov 2024 Pro-only 'Buy with Pro'). (2) Comet: Perplexity's Chromium-based AI browser with an agentic sidebar assistant that can navigate shops, compare prices, test coupons and fill carts on any website in the user's own session. Role type: AI assistant + agent (Instant Buy = agentic checkout on a payment rail; Comet = browser agent). State on 2026-10-15: Instant Buy and product cards are US-only; Comet and the general Perplexity answer engine (which answers in Polish with citations) work from Poland.

**vendor and ownership**

Perplexity AI, Inc., San Francisco, US (CEO Aravind Srinivas); venture-funded (investors reported in the press include Nvidia, SoftBank and Jeff Bezos). Instant Buy is run with PayPal Holdings (PayPal 'store sync' and 'agent ready' agentic-commerce services). Perplexity owns no marketplace or retailer, so there is no own-inventory bias; merchants reach it through PayPal and commerce platforms (BigCommerce, Shopware, Wix named by secondary sources).

**lifecycle status**

Launched, US-only for commerce; verified 2026-10-15. Timeline: 'Buy with Pro' and product cards launched 18 Nov 2024 for US Pro subscribers (Perplexity blog 'Shop like a Pro'); Comet launched July 2025 for Max subscribers and became free worldwide in early Oct 2025; Comet started asking permission before purchases and logins on 14 Nov 2025 (Perplexity LinkedIn post, reported by createwith.com); free shopping for all US users announced 19 Nov 2025 (Digital Commerce 360, eMarketer); Instant Buy with PayPal launched 25 Nov 2025 (PayPal newsroom); Comet for iOS launched 18 Mar 2026. Litigation: Amazon sued in Nov 2025; N.D. Cal. (Judge Chesney) granted a preliminary injunction barring Comet's agent from password-protected parts of Amazon around 9 Mar 2026 (7-day administrative stay); the Ninth Circuit (No. 26-1444) vacated it on 4 Aug 2026 and denied rehearing on 10 Sep 2026; Amazon filed a 41-page amended complaint on 21 Sep 2026 (CFAA, California CDAFA, tortious interference) targeting Comet for iOS; Perplexity says it temporarily disabled the Comet iOS assistant on Amazon.com around 11 May 2026. Perplexity also wound down its ads programme (FT-reported; reports say ended by Feb 2026). A Perplexity Help Center article on Instant Buy was reportedly last updated 16 Jul 2026 and still describes a US-only flow (seen only via search summary; the page returned 404 when opened). No Polish or EU launch of Instant Buy or product cards found.

**cost model**

Free for the shopper: Perplexity's free tier includes shopping in the US and Comet is free worldwide with query limits. Paid tiers: Perplexity Pro USD 20/month (about EUR 21-22 incl. VAT in the EU, billed in USD or EUR at checkout, per French/Spanish pricing guides July-Aug 2026), Max USD 200/month (Comet Background Assistant), Comet Plus news add-on USD 5/month for non-subscribers. Instant Buy charges no buyer fee and Perplexity has said it does not charge merchants per transaction (launch coverage, Nov 2025). Developer API (docs.perplexity.ai pricing, seen 2026-10-15): Sonar USD 1/1M input + USD 1/1M output tokens + USD 5-12 per 1,000 requests by search-context size; Sonar Pro USD 3/1M input + USD 15/1M output + USD 6-14 per 1,000 requests; Search API USD 5 per 1,000 requests (Fast Search USD 1 per 1,000). No free API tier stated on the page.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **answer engine with citations**: PL: yes, Polish questions and answers. EU: yes. US: yes.
- **shopping product cards**: US: yes (all users since Nov 2025). PL/EU: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed - every launch source says US-only and no international rollout was found; a Polish shopping query returns a normal cited text answer.
- **instant buy paypal checkout**: US only (PayPal newsroom 25 Nov 2025; secondary coverage through Sep 2026 still says US shoppers). PL/EU: not available, no timeline.
- **snap to shop visual search**: US at launch (Nov 2024). PL: not confirmed.
- **shopping memory personalisation**: Memory across chats launched Nov 2025 for all users; US shopping uses it. EU/PL: ⚠ *(unverified)* memory availability and EU-specific limits not confirmed.
- **comet browser and assistant**: PL/EU/US: yes - free worldwide since Oct 2025 on Windows, macOS, Android and iOS (iOS since 18 Mar 2026). The assistant can browse Polish shops in the user's session. Interface language: ⚠ *(unverified)* Polish UI not confirmed; the assistant accepts Polish prompts.
- **comet on amazon com**: US case only: Comet iOS assistant disabled on Amazon.com since about 11 May 2026 (per Amazon's amended complaint); desktop Comet on Amazon.com no longer enjoined after 4 Aug 2026. Amazon.de/Amazon.pl not covered by the US order.
- **price alerts or tracking**: No dedicated Perplexity price-alert feature found in any region.
- **interface language**: Perplexity answers in Polish; shopping cards and checkout English/US only.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. In the US, product cards summarise key features and reviews and Perplexity can build comparison tables on request; from Poland it produces cited text comparisons of specs. No documented EAN/GTIN mapping, no handling of retailer-exclusive variants, regional names or OEM rebadges; variant accuracy depends on the pages it retrieves. Product.ai's Sep 2026 benchmark found direct product-vs-product comparison questions produced factual conflicts 97% of the time across all four assistants tested. Comet can read several open product tabs and tabulate specs, which is useful for comparing two trampoline listings side by side, but the result is an LLM summary that must be checked against the maker's spec sheet.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

US: product cards show prices from merchants reachable via PayPal (vendor-claimed 5,000+ merchants at launch, with about 6,000 more being added via BigCommerce, Shopware and Wix per secondary sources) and Shopify-integrated stores that ship to the US. Poland: no indexed Polish shop feed; the answer engine names prices it finds on web pages (Allegro, Ceneo, shop pages) with citations, but there is no structured multi-shop price table, no coverage count and no test of Polish coverage. Comet can be told to look up the current product in other shops and list prices, which works on any site that does not block it ⚠ *(unverified: for Allegro, which uses DataDome anti-bot)*. Independent evidence on accuracy: Product.ai (Sep 2026, 913 verifiable price answers across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) found only 85% matched the current listed price, median error USD 300 when wrong (vendor study, not Perplexity-specific).

**price history and omnibus**

None. Perplexity shows no price history, does not derive the Omnibus 30-day lowest price and cannot flag fake discounts. It can be asked to find a Keepa/Ceneo price-history page, but that is search, not a feature.

**total landed cost**

None as a feature. In the US Instant Buy checkout shows the merchant's shipping and tax before confirmation (merchant-provided), but nothing adds assembly, return shipping or cross-border warranty. From Poland the cost must be checked in each shop's cart; Comet can be asked to read shipping costs from cart pages, with no guarantee of correctness.

**review and seller verification**

None to partial. Product cards include AI summaries of reviews (US) with no authenticity check; no seller identity checks against CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list or VIES. Instant Buy merchants are PayPal-verified businesses, which is a weak seller-identity signal but only in the US. Comet's own fake-shop resistance is poor (see manipulation field). It cannot prove a Polish shop is real or that its reviews are genuine.

**safety and compliance checks**

None automatic. Perplexity can be asked to search Safety Gate, the UOKiK register or Certipedia and will cite results if it finds them, but it has no structured access to these registers and nothing runs by default; it does not check GPSR listing fields or EN 71-14 edition claims.

**independent test coverage**

Not a test lab. Perplexity's systematic web search makes it relatively good at surfacing test pages when asked (for trampolines: Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 on test.de, paywalled; VKI; CHOICE), with citations, but it does not check whether the tested model is sold in Poland or matches the current model year.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

None. No price-drop or restock alerts, no webhook, cannot watch a Polish shop page. Perplexity 'Tasks'/scheduled searches exist for recurring questions ⚠ *(unverified: not verified for shopping)*, which is not a price monitor.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Two routes. (1) Instant Buy (US only): in-chat checkout with PayPal; the retailer stays merchant of record and receives full customer data; PayPal identity verification, fraud screening and Purchase Protection apply; the user completes checkout 'in a few clicks' (no autonomous purchase). No spending cap or mandate beyond the PayPal checkout itself. (2) Comet assistant (global): can fill carts and checkout forms on any site; since 14 Nov 2025 Perplexity says it asks permission before sensitive actions such as logging in or completing a purchase, shows what it is doing, and can be stopped or taken over at any time. Guardio's Aug 2025 test (before that change) showed Comet completing a purchase on a fake Walmart shop with saved card details without asking in some runs. No BLIK, passkey mandate or hard spending limit. Practical guardrail for this buyer: never store card data in Comet; let it build the cart and stop before payment.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered as a feature. The answer engine can find spare-part pages (nets, pads, springs) or OLX/Allegro Lokalnie listings when asked, with citations; no structured warranty or resale-value view.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Answer engine: Perplexity's own web index plus live web search at query time, with numbered citations on every answer. US shopping cards: merchant catalogs synced through PayPal store sync and platform integrations (Shopify, BigCommerce, Shopware, Wix), described as real-time by PayPal (vendor claim). Comet: live pages in the user's own browser session, so prices are as fresh as the page. No snapshots are stored for the user. Product.ai attributed Perplexity's lowest costly-error rate (14% paid tier, 13% in one French report) to its systematic web search (vendor study, Sep 2026).

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial (answer engine yes, shopping features no). (1) Official API: Perplexity API Platform (Sonar, Sonar Pro, Sonar Reasoning Pro, Sonar Deep Research, Search API, Agent API), API-key auth, docs at docs.perplexity.ai; pricing in cost_model; rate limits documented on a separate page (not read). Works from Poland. (2) Official MCP server: github.com/perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol, 'the official MCP server implementation for the Perplexity API Platform', MIT licence, about 2.6k stars and 381 forks (seen 2026-10-15; last-commit date not shown); tools perplexity_search, perplexity_ask, perplexity_research, perplexity_reason; local stdio via 'claude mcp add perplexity --env PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=... -- npx -y @perplexity-ai/mcp-server', or remote Streamable HTTP at https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp. Setup: about 10 minutes. (3) No API for product cards, Instant Buy or Comet ⚠ *(unverified: none found)*. (4) Comet is a normal Chromium browser for the user, not a scriptable agent endpoint; Claude in Chrome or browser-use is the Claude-Code-side equivalent. (5) No official Claude skill. Net: Perplexity is easy to call from Claude Code as a cited research backend for a trampoline comparison (tests, specs, safety notes), not as a price or checkout engine.

**⚠ protocol support**

⚠ *(unverified)* Instant Buy runs on PayPal's agentic-commerce services (store sync, agent ready); PayPal itself supports agent protocols, and one April 2026 analysis says Perplexity signalled engagement with AP2 in early 2026. Perplexity was named a launch partner of Visa Intelligent Commerce in 2025 (not re-verified). MCP: official server (API side). Comet does not identify itself as an agent: Amazon alleges its user-agent impersonates Chrome, and Cloudflare removed Perplexity from its verified-bots list after an Aug 2025 stealth-crawling report, so no Web Bot Auth-style identification can be assumed.

**open source and licence**

Perplexity answer engine, shopping and Comet: closed. Official MCP server: open source, MIT (github.com/perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol, about 2.6k stars, 178 commits). Comet is built on open-source Chromium.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Answer engine: optional account; memory (Nov 2025) stores preferences across chats and can be turned off; incognito disables memory and history. Instant Buy (US): PayPal account login, and merchants receive full customer information (name, address, order). Comet: browser-level access to everything in the user's logged-in sessions (shops, email, calendar if connected); the agent reads page content and screenshots of what it acts on. Third-party FAQs say card and login data stay in the OS vault and are not sent to Perplexity ⚠ *(unverified: not confirmed in Perplexity docs)*; Amazon's amended complaint alleges Comet for iOS copied Amazon session cookies to Perplexity cloud servers running a virtual browser. GDPR: Perplexity AI, Inc. is a US controller; ⚠ *(unverified)* no EU-specific memory restrictions found. For this buyer: do not store payment credentials in Comet and use a separate browser profile without email/banking sessions.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

High salience. Amazon v. Perplexity (N.D. Cal., Ninth Circuit No. 26-1444): the Ninth Circuit held on 4 Aug 2026 that on that record the user, not Perplexity, 'accesses' Amazon's computers under the CFAA/CDAFA, and vacated the injunction; the panel did not decide contract or tort theories, and Amazon's 21 Sep 2026 amended complaint adds tortious interference and targets Comet's cloud-side iOS browsing. Amazon's Conditions of Use were amended on 30 May 2025 with Agent Terms requiring agents to identify themselves ('Agent/[name]'), and in Sep 2026 Amazon blocked Meta's Muse with a popup saying unauthorized agent access violates the Conditions of Use - users of unidentified agents on Amazon risk account action. EU/PL: no case law on consumer browser agents; using Comet on Allegro may trip DataDome bot detection and Allegro's terms prohibit automated access ⚠ *(unverified: Allegro terms not re-read here)*. Calling the Perplexity API from Claude Code carries no comparable risk.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Subscriptions (Pro, Max, Enterprise, Comet Plus) and API usage. Ads: Perplexity ran sponsored follow-up questions from Nov 2024 and has since phased ads out (FT-reported; executives cited user trust); it says US product cards are not sponsored. Instant Buy: no per-transaction merchant fee announced and Perplexity declined to say how it will monetise shopping (launch coverage) ⚠ *(unverified: affiliate or PayPal revenue share not disclosed)*. Bias vectors: merchants connected through PayPal/platform feeds are buyable in-chat and may be favoured in US cards; source selection in answers is opaque; launch promotions (PayPal 50% back up to USD 50, 25 Nov-1 Dec 2025) can steer users. No marketplace ownership.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

Medium for answers, low for product picks. Every answer shows numbered source citations, and you can rerun with a site excluded only by rewording the prompt or using focus/site filters ⚠ *(unverified)*. Product cards do not explain why an item was chosen; Perplexity states they are not sponsored. Comet shows a step log of what the agent did.

**run to run consistency**

Evidence from Product.ai (vendor study, published 22 Sep 2026; 220 shopping questions x 5 repeats across free/paid ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity; 8,794 responses): 86% of questions produced at least one factual conflict overall; Perplexity paid had the lowest costly-error rate (14%) and Perplexity's systematic web search was named as the structural reason. Inconsistency rates for Perplexity specifically were not reported in the coverage read; no own repeat test run. Treat shortlists as non-reproducible and save citations.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Weak, documented. Brave (Aug 2025) showed indirect prompt injection in Comet: hidden page text could make the assistant exfiltrate a one-time password and post it; Brave said the first fix (13 Aug 2025) was incomplete. Guardio's 'Scamlexity' tests (Aug 2025) showed Comet buying on a Lovable-built fake Walmart shop with saved card data and treating a phishing login as legitimate in some runs. Since Nov 2025 Perplexity adds permission prompts before purchases/logins and says 'no detection system is perfect'. No independent re-test after the Nov 2025 changes found. The answer engine is exposed to SEO spam and persuasive seller pages like any web-grounded assistant.

**known failures**

Early Buy with Pro tests (TechCrunch, late 2024) found purchases taking hours or failing; TechRadar found a product grid ignoring the requested budget; Product.ai (Sep 2026) price mismatches across assistants (15% of verifiable prices wrong, median USD 300 off) and comparison questions 97% conflict rate; Comet prompt-injection and fake-shop failures (Brave, Guardio, Aug 2025); Comet bypassed Amazon's blocks by changing its user-agent (alleged in the amended complaint) and Cloudflare de-listed Perplexity over stealth crawling (Aug 2025). Poland-specific gap: no product cards, no checkout, no Polish shop index.

**regulatory enforcement history**

Amazon.com Services LLC v. Perplexity AI Inc. (N.D. Cal., filed Nov 2025): preliminary injunction around 9 Mar 2026, vacated by the Ninth Circuit 4 Aug 2026, rehearing denied 10 Sep 2026, amended complaint 21 Sep 2026, case continues (no trial date found). Other litigation is copyright/content-related (publishers such as Dow Jones/News Corp) rather than consumer protection. No UOKiK, DSA or DMA decisions against Perplexity found.

**buyer protection path**

Instant Buy (US): retailer is merchant of record (delivery, returns, service); PayPal Purchase Protection and fraud screening apply. Comet on a Polish shop: Perplexity is not a party to the sale - the Polish shop is the seller, so the standard PL path applies: 14-day withdrawal for distance contracts, 2-year statutory conformity liability (rekojmia/niezgodnosc towaru z umowa), plus card chargeback, PayPal or Allegro Protect depending on payment. Cross-border EU seller: ECC Poland. An agent-placed wrong order is still the buyer's contract; the withdrawal right is the practical remedy.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Moderate for research, low for buying. For a 305-366 cm garden trampoline bought in Poland: one Perplexity query ('trampolina ogrodowa 366 cm z siatka - porownanie, testy Stiftung Warentest, EN 71-14') returns a cited overview with links to tests, spec pages and Polish shops, which is a good first pass and easy to log via the API. Comet can open the Allegro/Ceneo listing and the brand page side by side and tabulate spring count, max load, net type and shipping cost, then stop before checkout. It cannot: give price history, check Omnibus, verify the seller, check Safety Gate automatically, or buy through Instant Buy from Poland. Every price and spec must be re-checked on the page.

**workflow role**

Discovery and evidence gathering (specs, independent tests, safety notes) with citations; Comet as an optional assisted-browsing helper for reading several shop pages. Combine with Ceneo/Allegro for prices and history, Keepa for Amazon.de, Safety Gate and the GPSR listing check, and the seller registers.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual: free (or within a Pro subscription), 10-20 minutes. From Claude Code via the official MCP server: setup about 10 minutes; one trampoline comparison = about 5 Sonar Pro calls at roughly 2k input + 1.5k output tokens each -> input 10k x USD 3/1M = USD 0.03, output 7.5k x USD 15/1M = USD 0.11, request fees 5 x USD 10/1,000 (medium context) = USD 0.05, total about USD 0.19; or 10 Search API calls = USD 0.05; plus Claude tokens to read and write the note. Comet: free, but each assisted session takes several minutes of supervision.

**evidence trail**

Good for answers, none for prices. API responses carry the answer text plus a citations/search_results list (URLs, titles, dates) that a vault note can store with the query and timestamp. Perplexity threads can be shared as links. Comet keeps a step log in the UI only; no price snapshots or screenshots are exported. Saved record: query, model, timestamp, answer, cited URLs, plus your own screenshot of each shop price.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Cited, web-grounded answers in Polish, with the lowest costly-error rate (14% paid) among four assistants in Product.ai's Sep 2026 shopping benchmark.
  - Official MIT-licensed MCP server (local or remote) and a simple API, so Claude Code can call it in minutes and store citations.
  - Comet is free worldwide and can work on Polish shop pages in the user's session, with permission prompts before purchases since Nov 2025.
  - No marketplace ownership and ads phased out, so fewer built-in commercial bias vectors than Google or Amazon.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Product cards and PayPal Instant Buy are US-only with no EU/PL timeline.
  - No price history, Omnibus check, alerts, landed-cost view, seller registry or safety-register checks.
  - Comet has documented prompt-injection and fake-shop failures (Brave, Guardio, 2025) and does not identify itself as an agent.
  - Ongoing Amazon litigation and Amazon's agent-blocking policy make Comet a risky tool on Amazon; Allegro anti-bot posture untested.
  - Price facts from any LLM assistant drift (85% price match rate across assistants in Product.ai's test).

**independent review consensus**

Thin and mostly from launch periods. TechCrunch (late 2024) found Buy with Pro unreliable; TechRadar's comparison praised the checkout flow but criticised curation; Tom's Guide compared ChatGPT and Perplexity for deal-finding (not re-opened). Security researchers (Brave, Guardio, Aug 2025) agree Comet was vulnerable to prompt injection and scams. Product.ai's Sep 2026 benchmark ranked Perplexity best of four on costly errors but is vendor research reported via Tech.co, TechRepublic and Ecommerce-Nation. No independent hands-on test of Instant Buy after Nov 2025 and no Polish test found. Many 'best AI shopping assistant' pages are agency or affiliate marketing.

**verdict for me**

PILOT (research backend only) - deciding fact: from Poland only the cited answer engine and the Comet browser work; product cards and Instant Buy are US-only. Best use: add the official Perplexity MCP server to Claude Code and use perplexity_search/ask to gather cited specs, test reports and safety notes into the vault note, then take prices and history from Ceneo/Allegro; use Comet, if at all, in a clean profile with no stored card and stop before payment.

**conflicting evidence**

- Injunction date: the research outline says the district court enjoined Comet on 2026-03-06; GeekWire (10 Mar) and The Register (11 Mar) report the order as issued on Monday, i.e. 9 Mar 2026, and secondary legal summaries call it the 'March 9 preliminary injunction'.
- Free shopping start: Digital Commerce 360 and eMarketer (Nov 2025) say free for all US users from late Nov 2025; one tracker says free agentic shopping for all US users launched in Feb 2026.
- Merchant count: 5,000+ merchants in most coverage; the PayPal press release itself names five merchants plus 'many others to come' and gives no number; one source says merchants will 'eventually' reach 5,000+.
- Payment partners: most sources say PayPal; one April 2026 analysis says Shopify and Stripe.
- Perplexity paid-tier costly-error rate in the Product.ai study: 14% (Tech.co, TechRepublic) vs 13% (Ecommerce-Nation).
- Ads: one report says the programme is being wound down by end of 2026, others say it ended in late 2025 or Feb 2026.
- Comet credential handling: third-party FAQ says credentials and cards never leave the device; Amazon's amended complaint alleges Comet for iOS copied Amazon session cookies to Perplexity cloud servers.

### Amazon Rufus and Alexa for Shopping

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY · **Cost:** Free with an Amazon account · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Amazon's in-store AI shopping layer. Rufus (2024) is the conversational assistant inside the Amazon app and website, trained on Amazon's catalogue, reviews, community Q&A and web data; in the US it was renamed and merged into 'Alexa for Shopping' (powered by Alexa+) on 13 May 2026. Related features: price history (30/90/365 days), price alerts, auto-buy at a target price (Prime, US), Scheduled Actions, and 'Buy for Me', an agent that buys items on third-party brand websites from inside the Amazon app (US beta since April 2025, paired with the 'Shop Direct' off-Amazon listings). Role type: AI assistant + agent inside a marketplace. For a Polish buyer: Rufus exists on Amazon.de (DE/AT), including a Rufus-driven price-history chart since Aug 2026; nothing confirms Rufus or Alexa for Shopping on Amazon.pl; Alexa for Shopping, auto-buy and Buy for Me are US-only.

**vendor and ownership**

Amazon.com, Inc., Seattle, US; EU retail operated by Amazon EU S.a r.l. (Luxembourg), the entity behind Amazon.pl and Amazon.de. Strong bias relevance: the assistant is run by the marketplace operator, which is also a first-party retailer (incl. private labels such as Amazon Basics) and sells ads shown inside the assistant. Buy for Me runs on Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Nova and Anthropic Claude models (Amazon's own Buy for Me page).

**lifecycle status**

Launched and changing; verified 2026-10-15. Rufus: US beta Feb 2024, all US customers Jul 2024; UK Sep 2024; beta in Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Spain on 29 Oct 2024 (TechCrunch); Japan beta 7 Nov 2024; Germany/Austria all customers in the app around Nov 2024 (heise) and on desktop from 21 Jul 2025 (ifun.de); Amazon announced 50+ Rufus upgrades and agentic auto-buy on 18 Nov 2025. Shop Direct + Buy for Me: US beta for a subset of customers from April 2025; expanded on 11 Mar 2026 via Feedonomics, Salsify and CedCommerce feeds (vendor-claimed 100M+ products from 400,000+ merchants); small merchants complained in Jan 2026 of being listed without consent (opt-out by emailing branddirect@amazon.com). Alexa for Shopping: launched 13 May 2026, US only, replacing the Rufus name in the US (Amazon added an editor's note to its Rufus page); 365-day price history from 30 Jun 2026 in US, UK, Canada and India. Amazon.de: 'Preisverlauf' button opening a Rufus chart with 30 days / 3 months / 1 year, reported 19 Aug 2026 (PC-WELT), not shown for all products. Outside the US the assistant is still called Rufus (Amazon's European Prime Big Deal Days copy, Oct 2026, per shopappy); shopappy (8 Oct 2026) forecasts Alexa for Shopping in 3+ non-US marketplaces by 31 Mar 2027 (UK and Canada first), based on job postings - a forecast, not an announcement. Poland: no evidence of Rufus on Amazon.pl in any source found (searched in English and Polish).

**cost model**

Free for signed-in Amazon customers; Alexa for Shopping needs no Prime, Echo device or Alexa+ subscription (PPC Land, May 2026). Auto-buy requires Prime (Amazon's Rufus page). Buy for Me adds no fee beyond the brand's price, tax and shipping shown at checkout. Amazon earns from retail margin, seller fees and ads, including Rufus Sponsored Prompts billed cost-per-click since 25 Mar 2026 (US). No paid developer API for the assistant.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **rufus chat assistant**: US: replaced by Alexa for Shopping 13 May 2026. UK, CA, IN, JP: Rufus. EU: DE/AT (Amazon.de, app since Nov 2024, desktop from Jul 2025), FR, IT, ES (beta from Oct 2024). PL (Amazon.pl): not confirmed - no source found; shopappy counts nine Rufus marketplaces without naming Poland. NL, SE, BE: not confirmed.
- **alexa for shopping brand and scheduled actions**: US only (13 May 2026). Not in EU or PL; forecast only.
- **price history chart**: US/UK/CA/IN: 30/90 days since 2025, 365 days rolling out from 30 Jun 2026. DE (Amazon.de): Preisverlauf via Rufus, 30 days / 3 months / 1 year, reported Aug 2026, partial product coverage. PL: not confirmed.
- **price alerts**: US: yes (set from chat, must be confirmed). EU/DE: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed. PL: no.
- **auto buy at target price**: US Prime members only (Nov 2025). Not in EU or PL.
- **buy for me and shop direct**: US only, beta for a subset of customers. Not in EU or PL; a UK launch was only speculated about.
- **sponsored prompts and ads in assistant**: US: billable CPC since 25 Mar 2026. EU: ⚠ *(unverified)* not confirmed.
- **interface language**: Rufus on Amazon.de works in German (English UI also offered on Amazon.de) ⚠ *(unverified: whether Rufus answers in Polish when Amazon.de is set to Polish)*. No Polish-language Rufus on Amazon.pl found.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial, within Amazon only. Rufus/Alexa for Shopping compares selected search results side by side (features, prices, reviews) and explains differences between similar items, grounded in Amazon catalogue data (ASINs, variations grouped under parent listings). It does not map EAN/GTIN across other retailers, retailer-exclusive variants or OEM rebadges outside Amazon; it will happily compare near-identical white-label trampolines sold under different Amazon brand names without flagging the shared OEM. Accuracy evidence is weak and conflicting (see conflicting_evidence).

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Not a cross-shop price comparator. Prices are Amazon's own offers on the marketplace you are on. In the US, Shop Direct lists external brand-site products (vendor-claimed 100M+ products from 400,000+ merchants) and Buy for Me can buy some of them, so the assistant can show off-Amazon offers - US only. No coverage of Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl. For a Polish buyer the useful comparison is Amazon.de vs Amazon.pl offers of the same ASIN, which Rufus does not do; Histozon/Hagglezon-type tools cover that.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

Partial. Amazon's own price history (Amazon-sourced data, not market-wide) in 30/90/365-day windows in US/UK/CA/IN and 30 days / 3 months / 1 year on Amazon.de via Rufus (Aug 2026, not for all products). Users can ask 'Has this item been on sale in the past 30 days?'. It does not label the Omnibus 30-day lowest price or flag promotions that violate it ⚠ *(unverified: not documented)*; PL: no assistant-side history on Amazon.pl found. Keepa remains the deeper source for Amazon.de history.

**total landed cost**

Partial. Amazon checkout shows price, shipping and tax; Buy for Me shows the brand's tax and shipping on an Amazon checkout page before confirmation. Nothing adds assembly or return shipping for bulky items, and no cross-border warranty view. For a trampoline bought on Amazon.de and shipped to Poland, Amazon's return rules (free returns depend on seller and item) must be read on the offer page.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. Rufus summarises customer reviews and Q&A for an item; Amazon runs its own fake-review enforcement, but the assistant gives no authenticity score and does not identify the seller entity against CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list/VIES. Amazon's seller pages show business name and address (DSA trader information) that you must check yourself. For Buy for Me, the brand site is the seller and Amazon does not vouch for it beyond its program inclusion - and small merchants said they were included without consent.

**safety and compliance checks**

None for the shopper. No Safety Gate or UOKiK register lookup, no GPSR field check (manufacturer, EU responsible person, Polish warnings), no EN 71-14 edition or certificate verification in the assistant. Amazon's marketplace compliance processes run on the seller side and are not exposed to the buyer through Rufus.

**independent test coverage**

None. Rufus draws on reviews, Q&A and some web information; it does not surface Stiftung Warentest, VKI or CHOICE results in a structured way and has no test-date logic.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

US: price alerts set from chat (push), auto-buy at target price for Prime (requests stay active up to six months), Scheduled Actions (time- or condition-based, can notify or add to cart), Echo voice notifications. EU/DE: ⚠ *(unverified)* alerts not confirmed. PL: none. No webhook; cannot watch non-Amazon or Polish shop pages.

**⚠ purchase automation and guardrails**

US only. (1) Auto-buy (Prime): when the price hits the target, Amazon buys with the default payment method and address; the confirmation is after the fact - a notification offers free cancellation within 24 hours; no spending cap other than the target price. (2) Scheduled Actions can add to cart or execute conditional purchases (e.g. price threshold and no recent purchase). (3) Buy for Me: the customer taps Buy for Me and confirms delivery address, taxes, shipping and payment method on an Amazon checkout page; Amazon passes encrypted name, address and payment details to the brand's site; the brand sends the confirmation and handles delivery, returns and service (effectively merchant of record); orders tracked in a 'Buy for Me Orders' tab; one secondary source mentions a USD 10 price-difference tolerance before re-confirmation ⚠ *(unverified)*. No BLIK or passkey mandates; none of this is available to a Polish buyer.

**after sales and resale**

Within Amazon: order tracking, returns and Amazon's A-to-z Guarantee for marketplace sellers. Rufus can answer 'does this model have spare nets?' from listings; no structured spare-parts, Polish service-network or resale (OLX, Allegro Lokalnie) view. Buy for Me after-sales sits with the brand, not Amazon.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Amazon product catalogue, live offers and prices, customer reviews, community Q&A, the customer's shopping history and stated preferences (account memory), and information from the web. Price history uses Amazon's own price data. Shop Direct uses merchant feeds via Feedonomics, Salsify and CedCommerce (from Mar 2026). Answers are not backed by source links outside Amazon. Freshness for Amazon offers is live; external brand data depends on feed sync.

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: none (for the assistant). (1) No public API, MCP server or skill for Rufus, Alexa for Shopping, auto-buy or Buy for Me. (2) Amazon's affiliate Product Advertising API 5.0 was deprecated in Apr-May 2026 and replaced by the Creators API (Amazon docs give 30 Apr and 15 May 2026); third-party guides say Creators API access needs about 10 qualified sales in 30 days ⚠ *(unverified)* - it returns catalogue and offer data, not the assistant. (3) SP-API is seller-side only. (4) Browser-agent route (Claude in Chrome, browser-use) against amazon.de: technically possible but Amazon's Conditions of Use Agent Terms (30 May 2025, per Search Engine Journal) require agents to identify as 'Agent/[name]', and Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent in Sep 2026 with a popup saying unauthorized agent access violates the Conditions of Use - account risk. (5) Practical Claude Code route for Amazon data is Keepa's API (price history) or Apify Amazon scrapers, covered in other items. Setup effort for using Rufus itself: zero, manual only.

**protocol support**

None public. Amazon runs a walled garden: it blocks outside agents (Perplexity Comet litigation, Meta Muse block, Google shopping agents blocked from crawling per 2025 reports) and has not joined UCP or ACP. Buy for Me is Amazon acting as the agent on other sites, with no published protocol; MCP not offered.

**open source and licence**

Closed.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Requires an Amazon account; uses shopping, browsing and order history plus details you tell it (account memory; you can ask what it remembers and correct it; memory of Kindle, Prime Video and Audible activity announced as coming). Auto-buy and Buy for Me use stored default payment method and address; Buy for Me shares encrypted name, address and payment details with third-party brand sites, and Amazon says it cannot see your orders on those sites. In the EU Amazon EU S.a r.l. is the controller under GDPR; no EU-specific memory limits found ⚠ *(unverified)*. For this buyer no new credentials are needed beyond an existing Amazon.de/.pl account.

**automation legal risk**

High for automating Amazon itself: Conditions of Use prohibit robots and data-extraction tools and require agent self-identification (Agent Terms, May 2025); Amazon enforces through litigation (Amazon v. Perplexity: injunction around 9 Mar 2026 vacated 4 Aug 2026, amended complaint 21 Sep 2026 adds tortious interference) and through customer-facing blocks (Meta Muse, 20 Sep 2026). EU/PL: scraping Amazon offers is contractually prohibited; account suspension is the realistic sanction. Using Rufus manually carries no risk.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Strong. Amazon sells ads inside the assistant: Sponsored Products and Sponsored Brands can appear in Rufus answers and comparisons (TechRadar), and Sponsored Prompts (branded suggested questions such as 'Why choose [brand]?') became billable CPC on 25 Mar 2026 in the US. Amazon is also a first-party retailer with private labels; evidence on private-label favouritism conflicts (Amalytix: Amazon Basics 0.6% of 1,300+ recommendations; Stellagent: 41%, unsourced). Shop Direct/Buy for Me steer purchases through Amazon's app. Alexa for Shopping users reportedly spend about 40% more per order (Amazon, Q2 2026 call, vendor claim), which shows the commercial goal.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

Low. Amazon does not disclose how Rufus picks products (Reuters, 2024); answers cite no external sources; you cannot exclude a source. Sponsored placements are labelled as ads in the UI ⚠ *(unverified: how clearly inside chat answers)*. Amalytix found Rufus typically surfaces about 5 products rather than 50 search results, which concentrates visibility.

**run to run consistency**

No published repeat test of Rufus or Alexa for Shopping found and no own test run. Amazon changes the system frequently (50+ upgrades announced 18 Nov 2025; rename May 2026), so older observations age quickly.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

⚠ *(unverified)* No independent study of Rufus against prompt injection in listings or spoofed reviews found. Reported misuse: Telepolis (9 Mar 2026) and posts on X showed Rufus being steered to answer off-topic questions (robotics, coding), with partial refusals - evidence of loose guardrails but not of purchase manipulation. Safeguards: Amazon's catalogue and review-abuse enforcement; for Buy for Me, the Amazon checkout confirmation. Seller-written listing text feeds the assistant, so persuasive or keyword-stuffed listings influence answers by design.

**known failures**

Washington Post testing (2024, via secondary source) found inadequate or missing recommendations for specific questions; Rufus answered off-topic prompts (Telepolis, Mar 2026); Buy for Me listed small merchants' products without consent, with AI images of wrong items and orders for out-of-stock goods (Modern Retail, ConsumerAffairs, TechRadar, Jan 2026); price-history link not shown for all products on Amazon.de (Aug 2026). Poland-specific gap: no assistant on Amazon.pl, no auto-buy, no Buy for Me.

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

Poland: UOKiK fined Amazon EU S.a r.l. PLN 31,850,141 (decision reported 27 Mar 2024) for Amazon.pl practices - misleading availability and delivery information, treating paid orders as non-binding offers, and a countdown-timer dark pattern; Amazon announced an appeal (outcome not found). US: FTC Prime 'dark patterns' case settled for USD 2.5B in Sep 2025 ⚠ *(unverified: not re-opened)*; FTC antitrust case pending. EU: Amazon Store is a designated Very Large Online Platform under the DSA ⚠ *(unverified: on later rulings)*. As plaintiff: Amazon v. Perplexity (ongoing).

**buyer protection path**

Amazon.de/Amazon.pl purchase: Amazon EU or the marketplace seller is the merchant; Amazon A-to-z Guarantee for third-party sellers; EU 14-day withdrawal for distance contracts (Amazon's own return window is typically 30 days); 2-year statutory conformity liability against the seller; card chargeback. Cross-border Amazon.de seller to Poland: ECC Poland. Buy for Me (US): the brand store handles returns and service, not Amazon; protection is the brand's policy plus card chargeback.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low-to-moderate, and only via Amazon.de. For a 305-366 cm trampoline: on Amazon.de, Rufus can compare 3-5 shortlisted listings (spring count, max load, net, reviews) and the Preisverlauf chart shows whether the current Amazon price is low for the year - useful to avoid a fake 'deal'. It cannot compare against Allegro, Ceneo or Decathlon.pl, does not check Safety Gate, GPSR or EN 71-14, gives no landed cost for freight to Poland, and its picks are mixed with ads. Amazon.pl has no assistant. Auto-buy and Buy for Me are irrelevant from Poland.

**workflow role**

Narrow: Amazon-internal shortlist and price-timing check (Amazon.de price history) once Amazon is a candidate shop. Combine with Keepa for full Amazon history, Ceneo/Allegro for Polish prices, Safety Gate and GPSR checks for safety, and seller registers for marketplace sellers.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Manual only: free, about 5-10 minutes in the Amazon.de app or website per product (open listing, ask Rufus, open Preisverlauf). No programmatic route, so no per-run API cost; automating it is a ToS risk. If Amazon data is needed in Claude Code, Keepa API tokens (separate item) are the cost basis.

**evidence trail**

Weak. Rufus chats are not exportable with citations and price-history charts are not downloadable; the saved record would be manual screenshots of the chart and answer plus the ASIN, marketplace, date and price. Keepa provides a better auditable history for the vault.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Rufus works on Amazon.de (DE/AT, app since Nov 2024, desktop since Jul 2025), the EU Amazon store this buyer uses.
  - Amazon.de price history via Rufus (30 days / 3 months / 1 year, Aug 2026) and US 365-day history give a quick fake-discount sanity check from Amazon's own data.
  - Grounded in live Amazon offers, reviews and Q&A, so specs and prices of Amazon listings are current.
  - Buy for Me confirms address, tax, shipping and payment on an Amazon checkout page before buying (US).
- **weaknesses**:
  - Nothing confirms Rufus or Alexa for Shopping on Amazon.pl; Alexa for Shopping, auto-buy and Buy for Me are US-only.
  - Ads inside answers (Sponsored Products/Brands, CPC Sponsored Prompts since Mar 2026) and a marketplace owner with private labels.
  - Amazon-only view: no Allegro/Ceneo/EU price comparison, no safety or seller-registry checks.
  - No API, no MCP, and automating Amazon with a browser agent breaks the Conditions of Use (Agent Terms, Muse block).
  - Auto-buy confirms only after purchase (24-hour free cancellation), with no spending cap.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test of Rufus or Alexa for Shopping with a published method was found for 2026. Reuters (2024) and an OECD AI incident entry raised self-preferencing concerns without documented harm; Amalytix (seller-tools vendor) found little private-label favouritism; Stellagent (vendor blog) claims the opposite without a named study. Trade press (Modern Retail, TechRadar, ConsumerAffairs) documented the Buy for Me consent problems. Most 2026 'Alexa for Shopping guides' are written for sellers (Perpetua, Amalytix, ebrands) and are not buyer evaluations.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY - deciding fact: from Poland only Rufus on Amazon.de is usable (no assistant confirmed on Amazon.pl; Alexa for Shopping, auto-buy and Buy for Me are US-only), and it has no API. Best use: when Amazon.de is a candidate shop, open the listing, ask Rufus to compare the 2-3 shortlisted trampolines and open Preisverlauf to judge the price, then cross-check with Keepa and Ceneo and screenshot the chart into the vault note.

**conflicting evidence**

- Alexa for Shopping outside the US: Perpetua (seller-tools blog) says it is fully available in the UK, DE, FR, IT, ES, CA and IN as of early 2026; ifun.de, PPC Land, resultsense and shopappy (8 Oct 2026) say it is US-only and that other locales still show Rufus.
- Rufus in DE/FR/IT/ES: TechCrunch and FashionNetwork describe an Oct-Nov 2024 beta for select customers; heise reports full availability for German and Austrian customers; shopappy says Rufus spread to these markets over the following fourteen months.
- Private-label bias: Amalytix (1,300+ recommendations) says Amazon Basics was 0.6% of picks; Stellagent says Amazon Basics appears in 41% of recommendations and 83% are Amazon-sold (no study named).
- 365-day price history scope: Amazon (via PYMNTS) lists US, UK, Canada and India; EcomCrew says US, UK and India are still rolling out; PC-WELT reports a one-year view in the German-language store in Aug 2026.
- PA-API 5 retirement date: Amazon's US docs say 15 May 2026; Amazon's Canadian docs say 30 Apr 2026.
- Shop Direct launch date: Modern Retail says Feb 2025; other outlets say Shop Direct and Buy for Me launched as betas in Apr 2025.
