### Gemini in Chrome auto browse

**Verdict:** WATCH · **Cost:** Google AI Pro USD 19.99 a month (US) · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Gemini in Chrome is Google's Gemini assistant built into the Chrome browser as a side panel that reads open tabs (summaries, cross-tab comparison tables, Connected Apps such as Google Shopping and Flights). 'Auto browse' is its agentic mode, powered by Gemini 3: it opens a tab and scrolls, clicks and types on websites to finish multi-step tasks such as researching prices across dates, adding items to a cart within a budget, applying discount codes and filling forms, pausing for confirmation before purchases. Role type: browser agent / AI assistant. State on 2026-10-15: auto browse is a preview for paid Google AI Pro/Ultra subscribers in the US (Google's Chrome page) and, per the Google One plans page, the US and India; Gemini in Chrome itself is not available in the EU, including Poland, although Polish is a supported language.

**vendor and ownership**

Google LLC (Alphabet Inc.), Mountain View, US; in the EEA, Google Ireland Ltd. Bias-relevant: Google also runs Google Shopping and Shopping ads, the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) checkout and Google Pay, and Chrome is a DMA-designated gatekeeper service.

**lifecycle status**

Preview, expanding outside the EU; verified 2026-10-15. Timeline: Gemini in Chrome first launched for US desktop users in Sep 2025; Chrome security architecture for agentic browsing published 8 Dec 2025 (Chrome security blog); new Gemini 3 side panel plus auto browse rolled out from 28 Jan 2026 as a preview for US AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers on Windows, macOS and Chromebook Plus (Google blog, 9to5Google); Gemini in Chrome expanded to Canada, New Zealand and India with 50+ new languages including Polish on 10-11 Mar 2026; seven Asia-Pacific markets in spring 2026; 172 locales from 11 Jun 2026 with the EU omitted (PiunikaWeb, Engadget); UK desktop from 14 Jul 2026 (Google blog via TechBuzz); Android in the US with auto browse for AI Pro/Ultra on 18 Aug 2026 (Google blog). Google One plans page (served in Polish, seen 2026-10-15) lists Chrome auto browse for AI Pro and Ultra subscribers 'in the US and India'. EU/Poland: no launch found as of 2026-10-15; only reports of Gemini in Chrome appearing in German Chrome Canary builds (May 2026). The related Gemini Spark agent (Jul 2026) also excludes the EEA, UK and Switzerland.

**⚠ cost model**

Auto browse requires a paid Google AI plan: Google AI Pro USD 19.99/month (US); Google AI Ultra restructured at I/O on 19 May 2026 into USD 99.99 (5x Pro limits) and USD 199.99 (20x) tiers (secondary sources). Not included in Google AI Plus. Polish price of AI Pro was PLN 97.99/month in 2025 (benchmark.pl), but buying it in Poland does not unlock auto browse. Daily caps on agentic actions apply (number not published). Base Gemini in Chrome (side panel) is free where available. Developer alternative: the Gemini 2.5 Computer Use preview model via the Gemini API/Vertex AI, listed by aggregators at USD 1.25/1M input and USD 10/1M output tokens ⚠ *(unverified: Google's page not opened; aggregators flag possible Gemini 2.5 retirement around 16 Oct 2026)*.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **gemini in chrome side panel**: US (desktop since Sep 2025, Android since Aug 2026), CA, NZ, IN (Mar 2026), seven APAC markets (spring 2026), Latin America, Africa, Middle East (172 locales, Jun 2026), UK (desktop, 14 Jul 2026). EU incl. PL: not available - benchmark.pl (11 Mar 2026) 'available in Polish but not available in Poland'; PiunikaWeb (11 Jun 2026) EU omitted; no later EU launch found. One Polish outlet (android.com.pl, 11 Mar 2026) claimed it launched in Poland, contradicted by the others.
- **auto browse agent**: US only for AI Pro/Ultra subscribers per Google's Chrome AI page; US and India per the Google One plans page. Desktop (Windows, macOS, Chromebook Plus) since 28 Jan 2026; Android (US) since 18 Aug 2026. PL/EU/UK: not available.
- **cross tab spec comparison**: Wherever Gemini in Chrome runs (not EU/PL).
- **connected apps google shopping flights**: US at launch; other countries ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **ucp agentic checkout in chrome**: Announced Jan 2026; UCP checkout is US-only. Not in PL/EU.
- **chrome price tracking and shopping insights**: US feature set; PL ⚠ *(unverified: not confirmed)*.
- **interface language**: Polish supported as a language since Mar 2026, but the feature is not offered to accounts in Poland. Age 18+, signed-in eligible account in a supported country required.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial (where available). The side panel can read several open product tabs and build a pros/cons or spec table (benchmark.pl description, Mar 2026); auto browse can search for visually similar items from a photo. No EAN/GTIN mapping, no detection of retailer-exclusive variants or OEM rebadges. Accuracy concern: Product.ai's Sep 2026 benchmark put Gemini last of four assistants, with costly errors in 56% (free) and 54% (paid) of responses and the free tier contradicting itself 29% of the time (vendor study, Gemini app rather than Chrome agent).

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

Agent-based, not index-based: auto browse visits shop pages and reports prices it sees (Google's example: comparing hotel and flight costs across weekends; Etsy cart under a USD 75 budget). Coverage is whatever sites let the agent in; Bloomberg (Jan 2026) noted websites adding barriers to agentic interaction. No Polish coverage at all because the feature is unavailable in Poland. If it were available, it could in principle open Allegro, Ceneo and Decathlon.pl pages, subject to anti-bot blocking ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**price history and omnibus**

None in auto browse. Chrome's separate US 'shopping insights'/price-tracking features show typical price ranges and history (US); nothing derives the Omnibus 30-day lowest price or flags fake EU promotions.

**total landed cost**

None as a feature. The agent can read shipping costs from a cart page and stop before payment, so a user could ask it to collect price + shipping per shop; no assembly, return-shipping or warranty computation.

**review and seller verification**

None. No review-authenticity analysis and no seller-registry checks. Protection against fake shops comes from Safe Browsing, Gemini Nano scam detection and the prompt-injection classifier, not from identity verification.

**safety and compliance checks**

None automatic. A user could instruct the agent to open Safety Gate or Certipedia and search a model, but nothing is built in; no GPSR field checks.

**independent test coverage**

None. It can open a test page (e.g. test.de) if told to, but paywalls and login requirements stop it or hand control back to the user.

**alerts and monitoring**

Not in auto browse. Chrome/Google Shopping price tracking exists separately in the US and a few other countries (not PL). No webhook; cannot watch a Polish shop page from Poland.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Can prepare purchases, not complete them alone (US preview). Guardrails documented by Google: auto browse pauses and asks for confirmation before sensitive actions such as making a purchase, payments or posting on social media - the user must press the buy button (9to5Google); it asks before visiting sensitive sites such as banking or medical sites and before signing in with Google Password Manager, and the model has no direct access to stored passwords (Chrome security blog, 8 Dec 2025); a work log shows every step and the user can pause, stop or 'Take over task'. Google says the user is responsible for all actions during automated sessions, including purchases and mistakes. No spending cap or mandate beyond the user's prompt budget; UCP/Google Pay agentic checkout is a separate US-only path. Not usable from Poland.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered. Google cites testers using it to manage subscriptions and check bills, which could extend to filing a return form, but there is no warranty, spare-parts or resale feature.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Live web pages rendered in the user's Chrome session (screenshots and page content sent to Gemini 3 in the cloud, with some processing on device), plus Google apps the user connects (Gmail, Calendar, Google Shopping, Flights). Prices are as fresh as the page at run time. Answers cite the pages visited via the step log rather than a structured citation list; no snapshots are stored for the user beyond Gemini Apps Activity and Chrome History (automated sessions are marked).

**⚠ api mcp skill access**

Grade: none for auto browse itself. (1) No public API, MCP server or Claude skill to drive Gemini in Chrome or auto browse; it is a consumer UI feature. (2) Developer analogue: the Gemini 2.5 Computer Use preview model (gemini-2.5-computer-use-preview-10-2025) on the Gemini API and Vertex AI lets you build a browser-control loop yourself ⚠ *(unverified: pricing from aggregators, possible retirement)*. (3) From Claude Code the equivalent capability is already available without Google: Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome tools), the Claude desktop browser pane, Google's Chrome DevTools MCP, or browser-use - all work from Poland. (4) Setup effort to use auto browse from Poland: not possible without a US/India account and subscription; using a VPN or foreign account would breach Google's eligibility terms.

**⚠ protocol support**

Chrome is announced to support Google's Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP, open standard co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target) for agent checkout, and Google's AP2 handles payment mandates in Google's agentic checkout ⚠ *(unverified: whether AP2 is used inside Chrome auto browse)*. No MCP. As a client-side agent in the user's Chrome, it does not need site-side protocols for ordinary browsing.

**open source and licence**

Closed (Gemini models and the agent). Chrome builds on open-source Chromium; UCP specification is open source.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

Requires signing in to Chrome with an eligible Google account (18+, supported country) and, for auto browse, a paid AI Pro/Ultra plan. By default Gemini in Chrome collects the page content and URL of the tab being viewed, and some content not visible to the user; interactions go to Gemini Apps Activity (default retention 18 months, configurable 3/18/36 months) and may be reviewed by human reviewers after disconnection from the account (Gemini Apps privacy notice); automated sessions appear in Chrome History with a dedicated icon. Auto browse can use Google Password Manager credentials only after the user authorises it. Personal Intelligence (cross-app personal data) is opt-in. EU: commentators attribute the EU absence to GDPR, DMA, DSA and AI Act obligations ⚠ *(unverified: Google has given no official reason)*.

**automation legal risk**

For the user: Google's terms make the user responsible for agent actions; sites may block agents (Amazon blocks unauthorised agents under its Conditions of Use Agent Terms and blocked Meta's Muse in Sep 2026; Amazon v. Perplexity shows litigation risk for agent vendors, with the Ninth Circuit holding on 4 Aug 2026 that the user, not the vendor, accesses the site). Using auto browse from Poland via a US account or VPN would breach Google's eligibility rules. Scraping risk is low because it is a human-supervised, single-session agent, but Allegro's DataDome and shop ToS still apply.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Subscription revenue (AI Pro/Ultra) plus Google's commerce stack: auto browse is integrated with Google Shopping connected app, UCP checkout and Google Pay, which favour merchants in Google's ecosystem. No ads inside auto browse documented ⚠ *(unverified)*. Google's broader search self-preferencing was condemned by the EC under the DMA on 23 Jul 2026 (EUR 460M for search self-preferencing) - context for how its agent may route purchases.

**ranking transparency**

Medium for actions, low for picks. The side-panel work log lists each step and site visited, so the user can see where prices came from; there is no explanation of why one product was chosen and no way to exclude a source except by instruction.

**run to run consistency**

No auto-browse-specific repeat test found and no own test possible from Poland. Product.ai (Sep 2026, vendor) found Gemini's free tier contradicted itself on 29% of repeated shopping questions, the worst of four assistants; this concerns the Gemini app, not Chrome's agent.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Best-documented defences of the three agents in this group, but untested independently. Google's layered design (Chrome security blog, 8 Dec 2025): a User Alignment Critic model isolated from untrusted content vets every proposed action and vetoes goal-hijacking; origin sets restrict which sites the agent may read or act on and hide unrelated iframes; a prompt-injection classifier runs in parallel; Safe Browsing and on-device Gemini Nano scam detection; automated red-teaming; up to USD 20,000 bug bounty for breaking the agentic boundaries. Security commentators still warn auto browse remains vulnerable to prompt injection; no published bypass or independent fake-shop test (Guardio-style) found for auto browse.

**known failures**

Few documented because it is a narrow US preview: daily action caps; sites blocking agents (Bloomberg); logins and paywalls force hand-back; Gemini's poor shopping accuracy in Product.ai's benchmark (56%/54% costly-error rates); The Register criticised Google for pushing the Gemini pane on Chrome users (Jan 2026). Only one personal hands-on blog found (Sean Kim, reported 3 of 5 runs useful and the agent refusing to press 'Place Order'; page content not retrievable). Poland-specific gap: entirely unavailable.

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

No decision specific to Gemini in Chrome. Google context: EC Google Shopping decision 2017 (EUR 2.42B, upheld Sep 2024); DMA non-compliance decisions 23 Jul 2026 (EUR 890M total, of which EUR 460M for search self-preferencing); US v. Google search remedies (Sep 2025) did not force a Chrome divestiture ⚠ *(unverified: not re-opened)*. Chrome is a DMA core platform service.

**buyer protection path**

Auto browse is not a party to the sale: the user confirms payment on the merchant's own checkout, so protection is the merchant's and the payment method's (card chargeback, PayPal). For an EU purchase it would be the normal PL path - 14-day withdrawal, 2-year statutory conformity liability, ECC Poland for cross-border - but the feature is not available in Poland. A wrong order placed after the user confirmed is the user's contract (Google disclaims responsibility).

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Not usable for this buyer today. In principle (US): 'Find three 12 ft trampolines with safety nets under USD 400 on these sites, compare spring count and max weight, add the best one to the cart and stop before payment' is exactly its use case, with a step log and a forced confirmation before buying. It still would not check Safety Gate, GPSR, EN 71-14, seller identity or price history. From Poland, the same workflow is achievable now with Claude in Chrome or browser-use driven from Claude Code.

**workflow role**

Would serve assisted multi-shop browsing and cart preparation (price/shipping collection) with a human confirming payment. For this buyer it is a benchmark for designing his own Claude-driven browser agent (confirmation gates, origin restriction, critic model), not a tool to use.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

From Poland: N/A - not available. In the US: USD 19.99/month AI Pro subscription; one trampoline comparison is one or two auto browse tasks of a few minutes each within the daily cap, so marginal cost is zero beyond the subscription. Self-built alternative with the Gemini Computer Use API: about 30 steps x roughly 3k input tokens (screenshot + context) = 90k input tokens x USD 1.25/1M = USD 0.11 plus about 10k output tokens x USD 10/1M = USD 0.10, about USD 0.21 per run ⚠ *(unverified: aggregator pricing, rough token estimate)*.

**evidence trail**

Weak. The work log in the side panel and Chrome History (automated sessions marked) show which pages were visited, and interactions are kept in Gemini Apps Activity; nothing exports a citation list, price snapshot or screenshot set. A vault record would need manual screenshots of the cart and step log.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - The most thorough published agent-safety design of the three (User Alignment Critic, origin sets, prompt-injection classifier, USD 20,000 bounty; Chrome security blog, Dec 2025).
  - Mandatory user confirmation before purchases, payments, sensitive sites and password-manager sign-ins; the user must press buy.
  - Runs in the user's own Chrome session, so it works on any shop that does not block agents, with a visible step log and 'Take over task'.
  - Polish is a supported language since Mar 2026, so an EU launch would work in Polish.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Not available in Poland or the EU: Gemini in Chrome excluded from the EU (Jun 2026 list) and auto browse limited to US (and India per Google One) AI Pro/Ultra subscribers.
  - Requires a paid plan (USD 19.99+/month) and has unpublished daily action caps.
  - No API, MCP or skill; cannot be driven from Claude Code.
  - Gemini had the highest costly-error and inconsistency rates in Product.ai's Sep 2026 shopping benchmark (vendor study).
  - No price history, safety, seller or landed-cost checks; evidence trail limited to an in-UI log.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test with a published method was found. Coverage is launch reporting that repeats Google's claims (9to5Google, The Register, Bloomberg, TechRadar, The New Stack); Bloomberg and The Register add scepticism (site barriers, Gemini pane pushed on users). One personal blog (Sean Kim) reports a positive but partial test. Security commentary (SecurityWeek, Computerworld/CSO) summarises Google's own defence architecture rather than testing it. Product.ai's benchmark (vendor) rates Gemini weakest for shopping facts.

**verdict for me**

WATCH - deciding fact: auto browse is limited to US (and India per Google One) AI Pro/Ultra subscribers and Gemini in Chrome is not offered in the EU, so it cannot run from Poland. Best use now: copy its guardrail design (confirmation before payment, origin allow-list, critic step, step log) into a Claude in Chrome or browser-use shopping skill, and re-check availability when Google announces an EU launch.

**conflicting evidence**

- Gemini in Chrome in Poland: android.com.pl (11 Mar 2026) says it launched in Poland as part of a ~50-country rollout; benchmark.pl the same day says it is available in Polish but not in Poland; PiunikaWeb (11 Jun 2026) says the EU is missing from the 172-locale list.
- Auto browse countries: Google's Chrome AI page says US only; the Google One plans page (seen 2026-10-15) says US and India.
- Gemini in Chrome on Android: Google's Chrome AI page FAQ says it isn't available on Android yet, while the same page's mobile section and Google's 18 Aug 2026 blog say it is available to all Android users in the US.
- Reason for EU absence: commentators cite GDPR (Engadget) or a mix of DSA, DMA and AI Act obligations (pasqualepillitteri.it); Google has given no official reason.
- Auto browse preview start: Google/9to5Google say 28 Jan 2026; one blogger dates his preview access to 19 May 2026 (Google I/O).

### Microsoft Copilot Shopping

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY · **Cost:** Free with a Microsoft account · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 11 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

A set of shopping features inside Microsoft's consumer Copilot (copilot.com, Copilot mobile apps, Copilot in Edge). (1) Copilot Shopping: conversational product research with product cards, comparisons and price tracking. Microsoft announced it at its 50th-anniversary event in April 2025 (secondary coverage). (2) Copilot Checkout, announced 2026-01-08 at NRF: the shopper buys inside the chat and never visits the shop site. Payment runs through PayPal, Shopify or Stripe, and the retailer stays merchant of record. (3) Brand Agents: AI shopping assistants that a Shopify merchant runs on its own store, set up through Microsoft Clarity. (4) Edge shopping tools (price comparison, price history, price tracking, cashback), now moved into Copilot in Edge. Role type: AI assistant + agentic checkout + merchant-side agent.

**vendor and ownership**

Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, USA. Copilot Checkout payment partners: PayPal, Shopify and Stripe, with Etsy inventory. Mastercard Agent Pay and Visa Intelligent Commerce are planned. Microsoft also runs Microsoft Advertising, which sells ads shown in Copilot, and Microsoft Cashback (formerly Bing Rebates). So the assistant's owner earns from ads and affiliate cashback. Microsoft does not own a marketplace or retailer.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

Copilot Shopping announced April 2025 (secondary). Price tracking in Copilot for US users from about March 2025 (secondary). Edge standalone shopping tools retired and folded into Copilot in Edge 'starting in November'. The Microsoft support page does not give the year; most likely November 2025 ⚠ *(unverified)*. It says the features roll out in the US first and 'Other markets will follow later'. Copilot Checkout and Brand Agents launched 2026-01-08 (primary: Microsoft Advertising blog), rolling out in the US on Copilot.com. Later expansion to more than 500,000 merchants and to the Copilot mobile apps, US only (Windows Central / Windows Report; exact date not confirmed, reported around spring 2026 ⚠ *(unverified)*). Expansion to Bing, MSN and Edge was promised, but no source confirms it is live. Tech Insider (2026-09-09) describes Copilot Checkout as 'in active US testing on Copilot.com'. No EU or Polish launch found as of 2026-10-15.

**cost model**

Free for shoppers. It needs a Microsoft account: on 2026-10-15 an anonymous visit to copilot.com from Poland showed a 'Sign into Copilot' wall. No buyer fee for Copilot Checkout is disclosed. Merchants pay their payment processor (PayPal, Stripe, Shopify Payments), and no Microsoft commission is published. Brand Agents need the free Microsoft Clarity and then a waitlist; agent pricing is not published. Microsoft Cashback is free for eligible Microsoft accounts: up to USD 200 per month and USD 1,000 per year, paid out to PayPal, in 36 countries. Poland is not one of them (explore.microsoft.com, seen 2026-10-15).

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **copilot chat product research**: Copilot is offered in 170+ markets and supports Polish for text prompts and answers (Microsoft support page). Whether shopping product cards appear for Polish queries is not confirmed for Poland ⚠ *(unverified: not tested: copilot.com required sign-in)*.
- **copilot checkout buy in chat**: US only (Copilot.com since 2026-01-08; Copilot mobile apps in the US later). Not available in Poland or the EU. No international timeline published.
- **brand agents**: Merchant-side feature for Shopify stores, by waitlist after installing Microsoft Clarity. No market list. Polish shoppers would only meet one on a Shopify store that deployed it.
- **edge price comparison**: Microsoft's Edge shopping page (undated) lists 29 countries, including Poland. The support page says the Copilot-based replacement rolls out in the US first [conflict - see conflicting_evidence].
- **edge price history and tracking**: The Edge shopping page says it is available in 211 countries and territories, including Poland; tracking alerts arrive by email and browser notification. Status of the Copilot-in-Edge version for Poland: not confirmed for Poland ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **proactive deal alerts copilot mode**: US users only (secondary coverage of the Edge holiday update).
- **microsoft cashback**: 36 countries; Poland not included.
- **interface language**: Copilot answers in Polish. Checkout and the merchant base are US English only.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial and unverified. Copilot compares products and summarises reviews when asked ('Copilot supports these scenarios only when explicitly prompted', Edge shopping page). For ranking it uses merchant-supplied titles, descriptions, specifications, pricing, reviews and availability (ChannelEngine). No documented EAN/GTIN mapping, retailer-exclusive variant detection or OEM rebadge detection. No independent test of its spec accuracy found.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

Edge price comparison searches the web for better prices on the product page you are viewing, in 29 listed countries including Poland. Which Polish shops it covers is not documented ⚠ *(unverified)*. Copilot Checkout covers only enrolled US merchants: 500,000+ after the expansion, all Shopify merchants by auto-enrolment with opt-out, plus PayPal and Stripe merchants who apply. No evidence that Allegro, Ceneo-listed shops, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl are indexed for Copilot product cards. Microsoft Advertising does sell shopping ads in Poland (ppc.land, undated), so Polish merchants could appear through ads ⚠ *(unverified)*. All coverage numbers are vendor-claimed.

**price history and omnibus**

Edge price history shows recent price increases, decreases and no-change periods. The history length is not published. No Omnibus 30-day lowest price, and it does not flag promotions that break the Omnibus rule. Edge's 'lowest price available' notification is vendor-claimed and was not tested.

**total landed cost**

Weak. One secondary report says the Copilot Checkout order summary shows the selected product, shipping address and payment details already filled in, so delivery cost appears at confirmation (US only). Return fees, assembly and cross-border warranty are not computed. For a Polish buyer none of this applies.

**review and seller verification**

Partial at most. Copilot summarises user reviews, and Edge 'Product Insights' shows user reviews. No published review-authenticity method. No seller-identity checks against registries. Merchants are vetted only through PayPal, Stripe or Shopify onboarding. Grade: partial (reviews summary only), none for sellers.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No Safety Gate or UOKiK lookups, no GPSR field checks, no EN 71-14 edition check, no certificate verification.

**⚠ independent test coverage**

Not a feature. Copilot web answers can cite web sources, but nothing says it looks for Stiftung Warentest, VKI or CHOICE results or flags paywalled tests ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

Price tracking: you set a drop threshold (for example 20%) and get an email plus a browser notification. It is listed for 211 countries including Poland on the Edge page. View tracked items under 'View tracked products'. Check frequency not published. Watching a specific Polish shop page works only if Edge recognises the product there ⚠ *(unverified)*. No webhook. Copilot chat price tracking was announced for US users.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Yes, but US only (Copilot Checkout). Flow per secondary report: product card with a Buy button, then an order-summary overlay with saved shipping address and payment, then confirm. Payment options: PayPal wallet, PayPal guest checkout, credit cards (PayPal press release), plus Stripe and Shopify Payments. The retailer stays merchant of record and handles fulfilment and customer service. Guardrails: a human confirmation click is described in secondary coverage. No spending caps or mandates are documented. Engadget asked Microsoft what stops erroneous purchases and printed no answer. Not usable from Poland.

**after sales and resale**

Not covered. The merchant handles service and returns. No spare-parts, Polish service-network or resale features.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Merchant catalogues synced through PayPal store sync, Shopify and Stripe. Microsoft Merchant Center feeds help organic Copilot results but are not required. Also the Bing web index, and retailer pages read by Edge. Refresh frequency and lags are not published. Copilot answers usually carry links, but no price snapshot.

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: none. (1) Official API: there is no consumer shopping API. The general Bing Search APIs were retired on 2025-08-11 and replaced by 'Grounding with Bing Search' inside Azure AI Agents. That service returns results to the model, not raw search results, so it cannot serve as a price API. (2) MCP: no official or community MCP server for Copilot Shopping or Checkout found. (3) Claude skill or CLI: none. (4) Browser agent: copilot.com needs a Microsoft sign-in (seen 2026-10-15). Driving one assistant with another adds cost and no data you can export, and Checkout is US only anyway. (5) Merchant side: Brand Agents and Copilot Checkout are configured from the Shopify admin or Microsoft forms, which is irrelevant to a buyer. Setup effort: not applicable.

**protocol support**

Microsoft says it is 'adopting open standards like the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)' (Microsoft Advertising blog, 2026-01-08). PayPal says its store sync supports leading agentic protocols but names none. Mastercard Agent Pay and Visa Intelligent Commerce are planned. No UCP or AP2 statement found. Interoperability matters only to merchants; it gives a Polish buyer nothing now.

**open source and licence**

Closed.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

A Microsoft account is required to use copilot.com (sign-in wall seen 2026-10-15). Copilot Checkout uses a PayPal account or card details and a saved shipping address. Edge shopping data is collected only with the user's permission (Edge FAQ). Copilot conversations and memory follow Microsoft's consumer privacy terms. A secondary report says Microsoft routes some European Copilot traffic outside the EU at peak demand from 2026-04-17 ⚠ *(unverified: single secondary source)*. Retailers receive customer data from Checkout orders ('You own the transaction, the customer data, and the relationship').

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Low relevance. Nothing worth scraping is exposed. Automating copilot.com would breach Microsoft's services terms ⚠ *(unverified: Microsoft Services Agreement not opened)* and risk the Microsoft account. No court cases about automating Copilot found.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Several paid layers. (1) Microsoft Advertising sells placements in Copilot: Showroom ads (2025 pilot, US), 'Offer Highlights' for Copilot conversations (2026), and search ads that can appear in Copilot answers. (2) Microsoft Cashback pays the shopper part of an affiliate commission at participating retailers, so Microsoft earns on the referral. (3) Copilot Checkout is sold to merchants as a conversion tool (vendor claims: 53% more purchases within 30 minutes, 194% more likely to buy). (4) Feed quality from Merchant Center affects organic results. How sponsored units are labelled inside Copilot shopping answers was not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*. A Polish critique (Spidersweb, Jan 2026) says the assistant decides what the shopper sees first and when a purchase is suggested.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

Low. Microsoft's launch post talks about 'organic Copilot results' but does not explain ranking or disclose sponsored ranking. You cannot rerun with a source excluded except by re-prompting. Ad labels inside shopping answers not verified ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**run to run consistency**

No evidence found for Copilot shopping. Expect the same drift as other LLM shopping assistants (see the ACES and Product.ai items); no repeat test was run.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

No Copilot-specific study found. Context only: Microsoft Research's own Magentic Marketplace simulation (Nov 2025) reported first-proposal bias and manipulation risk in LLM shopping agents ⚠ *(unverified: paper not re-opened here)*. Engadget noted Microsoft gave no detail on safeguards against wrong product selection or wrong orders.

**known failures**

No hands-on test of Copilot Checkout found. Coverage is launch reporting plus opinion. Documented gaps: Microsoft did not answer Engadget's question on erroneous-purchase safeguards. Axios says much of the announcement is 'promises and previews'. Promised Bing/MSN/Edge surfaces are not confirmed live after nine months. Poland: no Checkout, no Cashback, and the Copilot-in-Edge shopping features are rolling out US first. General Copilot complaints on Trustpilot are not specific to shopping.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A for the shopping features - no UOKiK, DSA or DMA decision about Copilot Shopping or Checkout found.

**buyer protection path**

US only: the retailer is merchant of record; PayPal Purchase Protection applies on eligible transactions (limits apply); card chargeback applies when paying by card; then the retailer's own US return policy. For a Polish buyer: N/A, because the purchase route is not available. Any purchase from a US merchant would also lose EU 14-day withdrawal and two-year warranty protections in practice.

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

Low. For a ~3 m garden trampoline bought in Poland, Copilot chat can do generic research in Polish: explain what to look for, list brands, summarise reviews it finds. But it cannot buy, does not cover Allegro or Ceneo, and gives no Omnibus, safety or seller checks. Edge price history and tracking might help watch one product on a Polish shop page, if the Copilot-in-Edge version works in Poland ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**workflow role**

Context only. At most, discovery and a secondary price-history or price-drop watch in Edge. Combine with Ceneo or Allegro for prices, Safety Gate and GPSR checks for safety, and a Claude browser agent for evidence.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Free. About 5 minutes per question in Copilot chat, plus signing in with a Microsoft account. No tokens or credits. Arithmetic for one trampoline comparison: about 3-5 prompts, 0 PLN, and nothing exportable except a shared chat link and screenshots.

**evidence trail**

Weak. Copilot answers carry links, and a chat can be shared by link or copied. No timestamped price snapshot or export. An Edge price-history chart can only be screenshotted by hand. A saved vault record would be: date, prompt, Copilot answer text with links, and a screenshot of the Edge price-history chart.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - The only big-tech assistant with in-chat checkout through three payment rails (PayPal, Stripe, Shopify), with the retailer kept as merchant of record (Microsoft blog, 2026-01-08).
  - Copilot answers in Polish, and the Edge shopping page lists Poland for price comparison, history and tracking.
  - Price tracking by drop threshold with email and browser alerts.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Checkout and Brand Agents are US only, with no international timeline nine months after launch.
  - No API, no MCP, no evidence export, so it cannot be driven from Claude Code.
  - Microsoft earns from ads in Copilot and from cashback commissions, and ranking is not explained.
  - No independent hands-on test, and no documented purchase guardrails or spending caps.
  - No Omnibus, safety, seller-registry or landed-cost features.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found. No hands-on test of Copilot Checkout or Copilot Shopping was found as of 2026-10-15. Coverage (Engadget, Axios, GeekWire, Pureinfotech, Windows Central) repeats Microsoft's announcement. Engadget and Axios add scepticism about safeguards and real adoption. Spidersweb (PL, Jan 2026) is a critical opinion piece, not a test. Tech Insider (2026-09-09) compares platforms from announcements, not tests.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY. Deciding fact: Copilot Checkout and Brand Agents are US-only with no EU date as of 2026-10-15, and nothing can be driven from Claude Code. Best use: none for now. At most, try Edge's price-history and price-tracking on one Polish shop page as a free secondary watch, and recheck Checkout availability in six months.

**conflicting evidence**

- Poland and Edge shopping: explore.microsoft.com/edge/shopping (undated) lists Poland for price comparison (29 countries) and for price history and tracking (211 countries). The Microsoft support page 'Changes to Shopping in Edge' says the Copilot-based shopping features roll out in the US and 'Other markets will follow later'.
- Surfaces: several third-party write-ups describe Copilot Checkout as live on Bing, MSN and Edge. Microsoft's launch post and ChannelEngine describe these as future expansion.
- Brand Agents: Microsoft says it 'is now available for Shopify merchants', yet access goes through a waitlist after installing Clarity.
- Merchant enrolment: Pureinfotech says PayPal and Shopify sellers must enrol yet Shopify merchants 'can start immediately'. Microsoft says Shopify merchants are auto-enrolled after an opt-out window and PayPal or Stripe merchants apply.
- Copilot Checkout status in Sept 2026: 'in active US testing' (Tech Insider) vs '500,000+ merchants' and mobile availability (Windows Central / Windows Report).

### Klarna AI shopping

**Verdict:** SKIP (Poland not covered) · **Cost:** Free inside ChatGPT · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 11 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Two linked pieces. (1) Klarna Shopping Search app in ChatGPT (live 2026-05-20). You describe what you want and see product results with current prices, availability and offers from several merchants. The app then redirects you to the merchant's site to buy. It runs on Klarna's Product Search MCP server. (2) Klarna Agentic Product Protocol (APP, announced 2025-12-15). Klarna calls it an open standard. In practice it is a hosted API on api.pricerunner.com with Product Search and Product Listings (offers) endpoints for AI agents and comparison tools. The data comes from PriceRunner, Klarna's price-comparison engine. Role type: AI assistant app (inside ChatGPT) + protocol/data API over a comparison engine.

**vendor and ownership**

Klarna Group plc (NYSE: KLAR); operating company Klarna Bank AB, Stockholm, Sweden. Klarna is a 'global digital bank and flexible payments provider' (BNPL) with 119M+ active users and 1M+ retailers (Klarna press release, 2026-05-20). PriceRunner is Klarna-owned; the APP API base URL is api.pricerunner.com. Not a marketplace, but a payments company that earns merchant fees and runs a comparison engine with affiliate links. Both are bias vectors.

**lifecycle status**

APP announced 2025-12-15 (BusinessWire; The Paypers 2025-12-16): 100M+ products, about 400M prices, '12 markets'. Klarna backed Google's UCP on 2026-02-02 (BusinessWire/PYMNTS). Shopping Search app in ChatGPT live 2026-05-20 (primary press release PDF): 13 markets. The APP spec repository klarna-incubator/agentic-product-protocol was archived (read-only) on 2026-08-05 with the spec still marked draft. The API docs on docs.klarna.com still describe Product Search v2 as current and the API as production-ready in the US and EU. Read: the API is alive, but the 'open standard' repo is frozen. Verified 2026-10-15 from primary pages.

**⚠ cost model**

Shopper: free inside ChatGPT. It needs a ChatGPT account and a one-time 'Connect' to the app; it works on ChatGPT plans that allow apps ⚠ *(unverified: plan gating not checked)*. APP API: only for 'approved partners and developers' (request via agenticproductprotocol@klarna.com); pricing and SLA not published. Merchants: organic listing based on relevance plus paid 'clearly labeled sponsored placements' (price not disclosed). Offer links are Klarna-affiliated links (APP docs), so Klarna earns on referrals.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **app api markets**: AT, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, IE, IT, NL, NO, SE, UK (EU endpoint) and US (US endpoint), per docs.klarna.com, 'currently available'. Poland (PL) is NOT listed.
- **shopping search app in chatgpt**: Klarna says 13 markets but names none. They most likely match the 13 API markets above, so Poland is excluded ⚠ *(unverified: inference)*. Whether the app is offered to ChatGPT accounts in Poland is not confirmed for Poland. Prompting in Polish would at best return offers priced for one of the 13 markets ⚠ *(unverified: not tested)*.
- **checkout**: None anywhere. It always redirects to the merchant.
- **klarna payments in poland**: Klarna payments (Pay in 30 days) launched in Poland in August 2021 (2021 coverage), but that is the payment method, not shopping search. Current Klarna-app shopping features in Poland: not confirmed for Poland ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **interface language**: ChatGPT UI. Product data in the language of each market.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. APP groups offers under unique products and returns gtin14s, attributes, description, rating, numberOfRatings, brand and category. So EAN/GTIN mapping across merchants exists in the data model. Offers can be filtered by condition (NEW, REFURBISHED, USED). No documented detection of retailer-exclusive variants or OEM rebadges, and no lineup 'cheaper near-equivalent' logic. Spec depth depends on PriceRunner's category attributes. No independent test of variant accuracy found.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

Yes, across merchants within each of the 13 markets: 100M+ products and 400M merchant listings (vendor-claimed, not tested). Polish channels: none. No Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl, because PL is not a market. EU channels: the merchant base of PriceRunner's DE, AT, NL, IE and other markets. Whether Amazon.de is listed in the German market is not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*. Each merchant offer carries an 'international' flag.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

APP API: no price history field (docs list none). ChatGPT app: no price-history feature described. PriceRunner's own websites show price history in their markets ⚠ *(unverified: not verified here)*. No Omnibus 30-day lowest price, and it does not flag promotions that break the Omnibus rule.

**total landed cost**

Partial. Each offer returns price, shippingCost, deliveryTime (min/max days), stockStatus and paymentMethods. Shipping is for delivery inside the market country, so not to Poland. No return fees, assembly or cross-border warranty. For a ~30 kg trampoline box shipped to Poland, the landed cost cannot be derived.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. It shows the product rating and rating count, and the merchant name and logo. No published review-authenticity method. No seller-identity checks (CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list/VIES). Merchants are whoever feeds PriceRunner or Klarna. Grade: partial (product ratings only), none for sellers.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No Safety Gate or UOKiK, GPSR, EN 71-14 or certificate checks.

**independent test coverage**

None surfaced. Neither the app nor the API mentions lab tests. Test results would have to come from ChatGPT's own browsing, outside the Klarna app.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

None in the ChatGPT app or the APP API. PriceRunner and the Klarna app have price-drop alerts in their own markets ⚠ *(unverified: not verified here)*. Cannot watch a Polish shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. The app 'seamlessly redirects users to the merchant's site to complete their purchase' (Klarna press release). No agent payment, mandates or caps. Klarna is positioning for agentic payments: it backed Google UCP (2026-02-02) and reportedly AP2 (October 2025, secondary). But no checkout runs through Klarna Shopping Search.

**after sales and resale**

Minimal. The API can filter USED and REFURBISHED offers in its markets. No spare-parts, Polish service-network or resale-value features.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Merchant product feeds connected in existing formats ('without restructuring their data', The Paypers), aggregated in the PriceRunner/Klarna catalogue and served live through the Product Search MCP server (ChatGPT) and the APP API. Klarna says prices are 'up-to-date' and data 'real-time' (vendor claim). The refresh interval is not published, and no lag measurement was found. Each offer carries an offerUrl (Klarna-affiliated) and a Klarna product page URL, so answers are link-backed but carry no snapshot timestamp.

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: partial (approval-gated; no Poland data). (1) Official API: Klarna Agentic Product Protocol API. Auth: a 'tokenId' header issued during onboarding; access only for approved partners via agenticproductprotocol@klarna.com. Base URLs: https://api.pricerunner.com (EU) and https://api-us.pricerunner.com (US). Endpoints: GET /agentic/v2/product/search/{market} (q up to 100 chars, size 1-100, offset) and GET /agentic/v1/product/offers/{market} (up to 50 productIdentifiers, condition and price filters). Rate limits not numeric (HTTP 429 with backoff advice). Swagger at api.pricerunner.com/docs. (2) MCP: Klarna's Product Search MCP server powers the ChatGPT app, but no public endpoint is published for other clients such as Claude. Community 'klarna-mcp' (Walma-Labs, MIT) wraps Klarna's merchant payments APIs (orders, refunds, payouts), not product search. ag2-mcp-servers/open-ai-klarna-product-api wraps the old 2023 Klarna OpenAI plugin spec (0 stars; that older API listed only US, GB, DE, SE, DK). (3) Unofficial: Apify 'm3web' Klarna product-offers and category scrapers (ToS risk). (4) Claude skill or CLI: none. (5) Browser agent: possible on klarna.com or PriceRunner sites, but pointless for Poland. Setup effort: email approval (timeline unknown), then about 1 hour to wrap the two endpoints as an MCP tool.

**protocol support**

Own Agentic Product Protocol (draft spec, Apache-2.0, repo archived 2026-08-05). MCP: the Product Search MCP server is used by ChatGPT through OpenAI's Apps SDK. Klarna publicly backs Google UCP (2026-02-02) and AP2 (secondary). No ACP statement found. For future-proofing it is a data-side standard; in practice it is Klarna's API, since no other provider implementing APP was found.

**open source and licence**

APP specification: Apache-2.0, github.com/klarna-incubator/agentic-product-protocol, 11 stars, 0 forks, 2 commits, archived (read-only) 2026-08-05. The service, catalogue and ChatGPT app are closed.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

A ChatGPT account, and connecting the 'Klarna Shopping Search' app in the Apps sidebar. No Klarna login or payment credentials are needed to search ⚠ *(unverified: connect flow not tested)*. The query context ChatGPT passes to the app reaches Klarna under Klarna's privacy policy. Klarna is a Swedish controller under GDPR. The API needs an approved partner token. No payment credentials are ever needed.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Low for manual ChatGPT use. The API is governed by Klarna's partner terms (general Klarna terms linked, not reproduced). Scraping klarna.com or PriceRunner pages with Apify actors would likely breach their terms ⚠ *(unverified: ToS not opened)*. Irrelevant for Poland anyway.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Three vectors. (1) Sponsored placements in the ChatGPT app: retailers 'appear in organic results based on relevance, with options for clearly labeled sponsored placements to boost visibility' (Klarna press release). How the label looks was not seen; no screenshot or test found. (2) Affiliate economics: offerUrl is a 'Klarna-affiliated link' (APP docs), the PriceRunner click-revenue model. (3) BNPL interest: Klarna earns merchant fees when shoppers pay with Klarna, and offers expose paymentMethods. No evidence that Klarna-accepting merchants rank higher, but nothing excludes it ⚠ *(unverified)*. Note the shift: in December 2025 APP was pitched as surfacing products 'without paid placement', but the May 2026 app sells sponsored placements.

**ranking transparency**

Low to moderate. Organic = 'relevance' (algorithm not published). Sponsored placements are said to be labelled. The API exposes a popularity rank within category and a deprecated v1 sortOrders (POPULARITY, NAME, RATING, TREND, HOT). Inside ChatGPT, nothing explains why offers were picked, and you cannot exclude a source except by re-prompting.

**run to run consistency**

No evidence. The API is deterministic for a given query and time. The ChatGPT layer adds run-to-run variability, and no repeat test was found or run.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Smaller attack surface than a browsing agent. Results come from structured merchant feeds via Klarna, not arbitrary pages. Feed content (titles, descriptions) still reaches ChatGPT unfiltered as far as is documented ⚠ *(unverified)*. No study of prompt injection or persuasive-content resistance for this app found.

**known failures**

No independent hands-on review found as of 2026-10-15. All coverage repeats the press release. Documented gaps: Poland not among the API markets. Market names for the ChatGPT app are not published. 12-market (December 2025) vs 13-market (May 2026) counts. The open-standard repo was archived nine months after launch. The earlier Klarna OpenAI product API (2023 plugin era, 5 countries) was superseded.

**regulatory enforcement history**

As a defendant: Sweden's Finansinspektionen fined Klarna Bank SEK 500M (about USD 46M) with a remark on 2024-12-11 for AML failings (Apr 2021 - Mar 2022). Klarna said it concerned rule interpretation and might appeal (secondary coverage). As a claimant: in PriceRunner (Klarna) v. Google, the Stockholm Patent and Market Court (PMT 1860-22) on 2026-07-01 awarded about EUR 1.3B in damages (about EUR 1.74B with interest) for Google Shopping self-preferencing; Google said it would consider its options (Euronews, secondary). No UOKiK, DSA or DMA decision against Klarna shopping search found.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

The purchase happens on the merchant's site in one of the 13 markets. Protection depends on the payment method: card chargeback, PayPal Purchase Protection, or Klarna's own buyer protection when paying with Klarna ⚠ *(unverified: Klarna buyer-protection terms not opened)*. EU merchants: 14-day withdrawal and two-year legal guarantee cross-border; disputes through ECC Poland. US or UK merchants: weaker practical recourse for a Polish buyer. Klarna Shopping Search itself is not merchant of record.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low for a Polish buyer. For a ~3 m trampoline it could list German or Austrian offers for Berg, Exit, Hudora or Salta with prices, shipping cost (to DE/AT), delivery time and stock, if the app answers for a German market. But it cannot price delivery to Poland, has no Polish shops, gives no Omnibus, safety or seller checks, and shows sponsored placements. At best it is a DE cross-check like idealo, with less transparency.

**workflow role**

Context only. At most a secondary DE/UK price cross-check during discovery. Watch APP and UCP as protocol context. Combine with Ceneo or Allegro for Polish prices and idealo for DE price history.

**effort and cost per purchase**

ChatGPT app: free, about 5 minutes and 3-5 prompts per product, 0 PLN, but results are not for Poland. API route: email approval (unknown wait), then about 1 hour to wrap two endpoints. One comparison of 5 models = 5 search calls + 1 offers call (50 IDs max) = 6 requests, cost unknown (pricing not published), plus about 20-40k Claude tokens to summarise the JSON.

**evidence trail**

ChatGPT app: the conversation can be shared or copied; offers carry Klarna-affiliated merchant links and Klarna product-page URLs; no timestamped snapshot. API (if approved): JSON with productIdentifier, gtin14s, price, shippingCost, stockStatus and merchant, which can be saved with a timestamp into a vault note. Saved record: query, market, date, product name and GTIN, top offers (merchant, price, shipping, stock), and a note on which items were sponsored.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Structured offer data per product: GTIN, price, shipping cost, delivery time, stock and payment methods (APP docs).
  - Documented API with public Swagger and EU/US base URLs, which is more open than most comparison engines (approval needed).
  - Large vendor-claimed catalogue (100M+ products, 400M listings) built on PriceRunner's 13 markets.
  - Sponsored placements are said to be labelled (press release).
- **weaknesses**:
  - Poland is not one of the 13 markets, so there are no Polish shops and no delivery-to-PL pricing.
  - Bias stack: sponsored placements, Klarna-affiliated links and a BNPL owner, with no published ranking method.
  - No price history, Omnibus, safety or seller checks, and no checkout.
  - API access is approval-gated with unpublished pricing. No public MCP for Claude. The APP spec repo was archived 2026-08-05.
  - No independent hands-on review of the ChatGPT app.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found. Coverage of the ChatGPT app (BusinessWire, PYMNTS, The Paypers, Digital Commerce 360, Shopifreaks, Chain Store Age, AI Magazine) repeats Klarna's release. Coverage of APP (The Paypers, Crowdfund Insider, eMarketer) is announcement-based. No test of result quality, sponsored-label visibility or price accuracy was found.

**verdict for me**

SKIP (for Poland). Deciding fact: Poland is not among the 13 markets in Klarna's own API docs, so neither the ChatGPT app nor the API returns Polish shops or delivery-to-Poland prices. Best use: none now. Recheck the market list in six months, and if PL appears, test the API as a structured GTIN/offer feed for a Claude skill.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- Market count: '12 markets' in the APP announcement (2025-12-15/16) vs '13 markets' for the ChatGPT app (2026-05-20). The current APP docs list 13 (12 EU-endpoint markets incl. UK and NO, plus US). The difference may be IE or US being added ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- Neutrality: in December 2025 Klarna pitched APP as surfacing products 'without paid placement or intermediary services' (The Paypers). In May 2026 the ChatGPT app offers merchants paid sponsored placements.
- Status: the APP GitHub repo is archived with the spec still a draft (2026-08-05), while docs.klarna.com calls the API production-ready with Product Search v2 current.
- Older API scope: a mirrored Klarna OpenAI product API spec (2023) lists only US, GB, DE, SE, DK. The current APP lists 13 markets. They are different APIs.

**sources checked**

- Klarna press release 'Klarna launches AI-powered Shopping Search app in ChatGPT', 2026-05-20 - PDF at s205.q4cdn.com/644747736/files/doc_news/Klarna-launches-AI-powered-Shopping-Search-app-in-ChatGPT-2026.pdf - text extracted locally, accessed 2026-10-15 (primary)
- https://docs.klarna.com/acquirer/klarna/other-products/klarna-search/klarna-agentic-product-protocol/ - APP API docs (markets, endpoints, fields, auth) - accessed 2026-10-15 (primary)
- https://github.com/klarna-incubator/agentic-product-protocol - spec repo, Apache-2.0, archived 2026-08-05 - accessed 2026-10-15 (primary)
- https://thepaypers.com/payments/news/klarna-unveils-agentic-product-protocol-for-ai-commerce - APP announcement coverage, 2025-12-16 - accessed 2026-10-15 (secondary)
- https://www.shopifreaks.com/klarna-launches-shopping-search-app-in-chatgpt-with-access-to-100m-products-from-its-merchant-network-across-13-markets/ - 2026-05-21 - accessed 2026-10-15 (secondary)
- https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Walma-Labs/klarna-mcp - community payments MCP - accessed 2026-10-15
- https://github.com/ag2-mcp-servers/open-ai-klarna-product-api - old plugin-spec wrapper - accessed 2026-10-15
- Search-result summaries only (pages blocked, HTTP 403): BusinessWire APP (2025-12-15) and app (2026-05-20) releases, BusinessWire/PYMNTS Klarna backs UCP (2026-02-02), AI Magazine, Finansinspektionen fine coverage (The Local, Fortune, FinTech Futures, 2024-12-11), Euronews/NST on PriceRunner v Google ruling (2026-07-01), 2021 coverage of Klarna's Poland launch.
