## E. Agents, skills and MCP (build it yourself in Claude Code)

### Claude in Chrome browser agent

**Verdict:** USE NOW (research hands, never the payer) · **Cost:** Paid Claude plan; Pro USD 20 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 11 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Anthropic's browser agents that read and act on real web pages for the user. (1) Claude in Chrome: a Chrome extension (side panel) that works in the user's own Chrome profile with existing logins. Generally available on paid plans since 2026-08-26. Claude Code drives it via `claude --chrome` as the 'claude-in-chrome' MCP server, which works with Chrome, Edge and other Chromium browsers. (2) Claude built-in browser: a separate browser inside the Claude desktop app. In Cowork it launched 2026-08-26 with its own profile and per-site cookie import. In Claude Code desktop sessions it shows up as the mcp__Claude_Browser__* tools, which this research used for a live test. Neither is a shopping product: it is a general browser agent that becomes a shopping tool through prompts or a skill. Role type: agent (browser agent) + MCP server for Claude Code.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

Anthropic PBC, San Francisco, USA (public-benefit corporation; large investments from Amazon and Google ⚠ *(unverified: funding not re-verified here)*). Anthropic does not own a marketplace or retailer and does not insert affiliate links. For EU users Claude.ai and Claude Code are offered in Poland (Anthropic supported-countries page).

**lifecycle status**

Claude in Chrome: pilot 2025-08-25 (1,000 Max users). Beta for all Max users 2025-11-24, adding scheduled tasks and multi-tab workflows. Expanded 2025-12-18 to Pro, Team and Enterprise, with the Claude Code integration (all three dates appended to the claude.com pilot post). The side panel became a full Cowork session 2026-08-12. General availability on all paid plans 2026-08-26, adding autonomous actions checked by a safety classifier (claude.com GA post). The help center still labels the side-panel version 'beta'. Built-in browser in Cowork: launched 2026-08-26, rolling out gradually (macOS, Windows, Linux beta). Security fix: the 'ShadowPrompt' flaw, which let any site inject prompts, was reported by Koi Security in late December 2025 and fixed in extension v1.0.41 (January 2026; secondary). Claude Code docs current as of 2026-10-15 require Claude Code 2.0.73+ and extension 1.0.36+. Verified 2026-10-15 from primary Anthropic pages.

**cost model**

Needs a paid Claude plan; no per-action fee, but it consumes the plan's usage limits. Pro: USD 17/month billed annually (USD 200 up front) or USD 20/month billed monthly. Max: from USD 100/month (5x or 20x Pro usage). Free plan: no Claude in Chrome (claude.com/pricing, seen 2026-10-15). The Chrome integration in Claude Code works only with a claude.ai login, not with an API key or setup-token (code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome), so the API token price is only a reference. Reference API prices: Sonnet 5.5 USD 2 input / USD 10 output and Opus 5.5 USD 4 / USD 20 per million tokens (claude.com/pricing, 2026-10-15).

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **claude availability**: Poland: yes, for both Claude.ai/Claude Code/Cowork and the API (anthropic.com/supported-countries, 2026-10-15). No EU-specific limit on Claude in Chrome is stated in the GA post or help pages.
- **claude in chrome side panel**: All paid plans; Google Chrome desktop only. Not other Chromium browsers and not mobile for the side panel.
- **claude code chrome integration**: Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise with a claude.ai login. Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Vivaldi or Opera. Not WSL, and not via Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry.
- **built in browser cowork**: Pro, Max and Team, and Enterprise when enabled. Desktop app on macOS, Windows, Linux (beta). Gradual rollout.
- **polish shops tested**: Allegro listing and product pages and a Ceneo search loaded and read normally in the built-in browser on 2026-10-15. No CAPTCHA or anti-bot wall appeared during the test.
- **amazon and ebay**: Amazon blocks Claude-named agents in robots.txt and has shown 'unauthorized AI agent' pages to other agents. Whether Claude in Chrome itself gets blocked on Amazon.de or Amazon.pl: not confirmed ⚠ *(unverified)*. eBay's User Agreement bans unapproved buy-for-me agents and LLM bots from 2026-02-20 (secondary).
- **language**: Reads Polish pages and takes Polish prompts (tested). Interface in English and other UI languages.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Strong in principle, unverified at scale. It reads spec tables across open product pages and normalises labels (for example 'Memory' vs 'RAM') into a comparison table, an Anthropic use case shown with laptops. On Allegro the product page title carries the EAN (seen: Funfit 312 cm trampoline, EAN 5902759972308), so an agent can map offers by EAN. Live test 2026-10-15: on Ceneo the same 'Funfit 312 cm 10 ft' trampoline appeared in partner listings from 359.00 zl to 1,260.99 zl with near-identical titles. Telling a variant from an overpriced duplicate needs explicit checks: net inside or outside, ladder, max load 120 vs 150 kg. The agent does them only if the prompt or skill demands it. It cannot detect OEM rebadges by itself, and one user report shows it can assert false product facts (it wrongly said a 30-pack of lenses barely existed; libecity, May 2026).

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

Not an index. It compares whatever pages it can open, so Polish coverage is in principle every shop that loads: Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon.pl and brand stores. Tested 2026-10-15: an Allegro search for 'trampolina ogrodowa 305 cm z siatka' returned 1,321 offers. The first listing page's main text (about 28,400 characters) contained 13 'Sponsorowane' and 16 'Promowane' labels, and the first dozen results shown were all sponsored or promoted. Prices were read correctly: 359,00 zl in the text matched the screenshot. Delivery-inclusive prices ('364,98 zl z dostawa') are in the listing text. Ceneo's search page was readable too. Amazon may block Claude agents ⚠ *(unverified)*. Count of shops: unlimited in principle, about 3-5 per run in practice.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

No history of its own. It can read the Omnibus line ('najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka') where a shop shows one, and Allegro's 'Gwarancja najnizszej ceny' badge. It can open Ceneo or Keepa pages for history if they render as text ⚠ *(unverified: charts may need screenshots)*. Telling a real discount from a fake one depends on reading those fields, and the agent has no ground truth. History can be built by re-running the same check on a schedule: scheduled tasks exist in Claude in Chrome since 2025-11-24.

**total landed cost**

Manual-agentic. It can read delivery-inclusive prices on Allegro listings, open delivery and returns pages, and put the item in the cart to see freight (stopping before payment). Nothing is computed automatically. The prompt or skill must ask for shipping, payment surcharges, return freight for a bulky box and cross-border warranty terms.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. It can open the seller profile (seen: 'poleca 98,4%' for the Funfit seller), read 1-2-star reviews, and visit public registers (CEIDG, KRS, the VAT white list 'Biala lista', VIES) to match the NIP or company name. It cannot prove review authenticity and has no fraud database. Financial sites need extra permission.

**safety and compliance checks**

Manual-agentic, all doable on request. Tested 2026-10-15: on the Allegro product page the 'Bezpieczenstwo, zgodnosc i ostrzezenia' (GPSR) section is behind a link. After a click a drawer opened with about 1,800 characters of trampoline warnings citing Regulation (EU) 2023/988. The plain page text did not include it, so the agent must click. It can search the Safety Gate portal and UOKiK register, and check a Certipedia certificate ID if the listing shows one. Nothing runs without being asked.

**independent test coverage**

Can reach paywalled tests through the user's own subscriptions, because it uses the user's logged-in Chrome session (for example a test.de account). It does not surface lab tests unless asked. Built-in browser: logins only if cookies were imported.

**⚠ alerts and monitoring**

Not a price tracker. Claude in Chrome scheduled tasks (since 2025-11-24) can re-run 'check this Allegro or Ceneo page and report the price' on a schedule. Delivery is through Claude's conversation history and notifications ⚠ *(unverified: notification channel not verified)*; no webhook or email documented. It can watch a Polish shop page.

**⚠ purchase automation and guardrails**

Technically yes: it acts in the user's logged-in session and could click 'Kup teraz'. Guardrails: the 2025 pilot listed purchasing as a high-risk action that needs user confirmation. In a Japanese test, Claude still asked explicit permission for the payment step even with 'allow all actions on this site' (libecity summary). The current safety page forbids 'Inputting sensitive data' and 'Bypassing captchas', and asks permission before financial sites. Claude Code pauses at login pages and CAPTCHAs for the user. GA (2026-08-26) introduced autonomous mode, where a classifier blocks actions that don't match the request. The GA post does not list purchases as always needing confirmation ⚠ *(unverified)*. No spending cap or mandate. BLIK still needs confirmation in the banking app, which is a natural human step. Merchant of record is the shop or the Allegro seller. On error, the order is a normal order in the user's account. Practical rule: let it stop at the cart and pay by hand.

**after sales and resale**

Only on request: it can search Allegro, OLX and Allegro Lokalnie for spare nets, pads and springs or used units, and read warranty and service pages. Nothing built in.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Live pages at the moment of the visit, with no index lag. Each finding can be backed by a URL, page text, a screenshot saved to disk (Claude Code v2.1.211+) or a GIF recording. The freshness risk is in the agent: it may reuse an earlier reading in a long session, and pages lazy-load sections it has not opened.

**api mcp skill access**

Grade: full. (1) Claude Code: `claude --chrome`, or `/chrome` and then 'Enabled by default'. It exposes the claude-in-chrome MCP server: navigate, read_page (accessibility tree), get_page_text, find, computer (click, type, screenshot), form_input, javascript_tool, read_console_messages, read_network_requests, gif_creator, file upload, tabs. Requirements: a claude.ai login (not an API key), extension 1.0.36+, Claude Code 2.0.73+, no WSL, not via Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry. Site permissions are inherited from the extension. (2) Claude desktop built-in browser: mcp__Claude_Browser__* tools (same verbs) in desktop Claude Code sessions, with a persistent separate profile. Used for this research on 2026-10-15. (3) Skills: any SKILL.md can orchestrate it, for example the planned custom buying-research skill. (4) No public REST API; this is the agent itself. Setup effort: about 5-10 minutes (install the extension, sign in, run `claude --chrome`). Enabling it by default costs extra context in every session (docs note).

**⚠ protocol support**

None of ACP, UCP, AP2, Visa TAP or Web Bot Auth for shopping. It works through the human web UI. Whether it signs requests with Web Bot Auth is not documented ⚠ *(unverified)*. It is itself delivered as an MCP server to Claude Code. Future-proof in the sense that it needs no merchant cooperation; fragile in the sense that sites can ban agents in their terms (eBay) or block them (Amazon).

**open source and licence**

Closed (proprietary Anthropic extension and desktop app).

**account linking and data access**

Claude in Chrome runs in the user's real Chrome profile and 'shares your browser's login state' (Claude Code docs). It sees every site you are logged into, including Allegro, Gmail and your bank, subject to site permissions. Zenity notes the extension is always logged in and that network and console tools can expose tokens. Admins on Team/Enterprise can set allowlists and blocklists. Built-in browser: a separate profile with per-site cookie import (banking, email and SSO unchecked by default), and logins persist across sessions on that computer. 1Password integration (beta, macOS) fills credentials so Claude never sees them. Conversations are saved in Claude history. Page content goes to Anthropic for processing under the consumer or commercial data terms. GDPR applies (Poland is a supported country). Never give it card numbers; Anthropic's safety page itself forbids inputting sensitive data.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

Moderate and site-dependent. Allegro: the Regulamin in force from 2026-10-13 (opened 2026-10-15) says in art. 10.10 that downloading or using Allegro materials, data included, 'requires Allegro's consent each time'. It bans aggregating data for business use, including scraping. Art. 10.11 bans bots and data-extraction tools, especially ones that raise traffic. Another article lets Allegro deploy bot-blocking tools and restrict accounts. A single consumer reading a few pages for their own purchase is low risk but not explicitly allowed. Bulk extraction is a breach. Ceneo's terms reportedly ban automated access with a contractual penalty ⚠ *(unverified: Ceneo terms not re-opened here)*. eBay bans unapproved buy-for-me agents and LLM bots from 2026-02-20. Amazon blocks Claude-named agents in robots.txt and treats unauthorized agents as violating its Conditions of Use (secondary, Sept 2026); in Amazon v. Perplexity the injunction against Comet was vacated in Aug 2026 but the case continues (outline note, not re-opened ⚠ *(unverified)*). Risk to the user: account restriction on the shop, not criminal exposure.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Anthropic earns subscriptions; no affiliate links or sponsored results come from Claude itself. Bias enters through the pages it reads. Allegro's first results page is dominated by 'Sponsorowane' and 'Promowane' offers (13 + 16 labels on the tested page), so an agent that takes the first results inherits paid ranking unless told to sort by price or to skip sponsored items. A single authoritative source (for example one review site) can swing its pick (Wharton finding, see the H items). Bias also comes from the model's training data on brands.

**ranking transparency**

High if you ask for it: it can cite every URL and the exact text behind each claim, and you can rerun with a source excluded. Low by default: without instructions it does not say which offers were sponsored or why it chose them.

**run to run consistency**

No published shopping consistency test for Claude in Chrome. LLM agents' choices shift with model updates and runs (ACES, Product.ai items). Mitigate with a fixed skill: same sources, sort order and extraction fields, with saved snapshots. Not repeat-tested here.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Anthropic's figures: the 2025 pilot cut attack success from 23.6% to 11.2% (browser-specific set 35.7% to 0%). The GA post (2026-08-26) reports a stronger eval with Opus 5 at 3.8% before extra safeguards, and 0% for Sonnet 5 and Opus 5 and 0.3% for Fable 5 with probes plus classifier. The safety page says under 0.08% on an internal suite (Opus 4.8). All are vendor numbers. Real incidents: ShadowPrompt (Koi Security) let any website inject prompts via a claude.ai subdomain XSS, fixed in v1.0.41 (January 2026). 'ClaudeBleed' (LayerX) let other extensions hijack it, with a partial fix on 2026-05-06 per one aggregator ⚠ *(unverified: single secondary source)*. Zenity (2025-12-29) showed the agent going to a site outside the approved plan in 'ask before acting' mode. Fake shops and persuasive seller copy are only countered by a skill that forces seller-registry checks.

**known failures**

Speed: an early hands-on (2025 preview) took 10-15 minutes for tasks done by hand in 2-3. A May 2026 user report says a 30-minute shopping comparison took 3 minutes. Usage: a GitHub issue (#65927, June 2026) reports one Claude in Chrome prompt on a complex page using about 61% of a session limit, closed as 'not planned'. Errors: it asserted false product facts and defaulted to the smallest size when volume was not specified (libecity). Breakage: a May 2026 extension update broke automation for some users (Japanese report). The service worker goes idle in long sessions and needs a reconnect, and JavaScript modal dialogs block it (docs). Chrome Web Store rating about 2.7-2.8 (secondary). Own test 2026-10-15: get_page_text on an Allegro product page returned one customer review (it picked an <article> element) instead of the offer. Price and GPSR data needed targeted find calls and a click. The raw HTML of the Allegro listing was about 2.37M characters, so anything that feeds the full DOM to the model is very expensive.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - no UOKiK, DSA, DMA or court decision against Anthropic about browser agents or shopping found. Context: courts are weighing third-party shopping agents (Amazon v. Perplexity).

**⚠ buyer protection path**

Same as a manual purchase, because the agent acts in the user's own account: Allegro Protect and the Allegro dispute process, PL statutory warranty (rekojmia), the 14-day withdrawal for distance sales, and card chargeback or PayPal protection (BLIK has no chargeback). Cross-border EU disputes go through ECC Poland. An order placed by the agent in your account is legally your order ⚠ *(unverified: no case law checked)*. Anthropic is not a party to the purchase.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

High for the research half, low for the buying half. For a ~3 m garden trampoline it can: open the Allegro product page and pull the parameters (312 cm, max load 120 vs 150 kg, net inside or outside, ladder, EAN); open Ceneo to see the spread for the same model (359-1,261 zl in the test); open the GPSR drawer and check the manufacturer and EU responsible person; search Safety Gate for the brand; open the user's test.de subscription for the Stiftung Warentest table; and check the seller's NIP on the VAT white list. Output: a table saved to the vault. It cannot give reliable price history, guarantee it picked the right variant without explicit checks, or be trusted to pay.

**workflow role**

The 'hands' across stages: specs and variants, seller check, safety and GPSR check, landed cost (up to the cart), and evidence capture. Combine with Ceneo or Allegro price history and Keepa for history, SerpApi or Shopify Catalog MCP for broad discovery, and a custom skill that fixes sources, fields and the stop-before-payment rule.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup: 5-10 minutes on an existing Pro plan. One comparison run, estimated from the 2026-10-15 measurements: Allegro listing main text about 28,400 chars (about 8-9k tokens for Polish at about 3.3 chars/token); Allegro product page body about 7,700 chars (about 2.3k tokens); GPSR drawer about 1,800 chars (about 0.5k tokens); screenshots about 1-1.5k tokens each. For 5 candidate models: 5 x (Allegro product + GPSR + Ceneo offers + 1 shop or brand page, about 13k tokens) + 1 listing (9k) + 5 Safety Gate lookups (about 10k) is about 85k tokens of unique page text. Over about 40 agent steps the re-sent context adds up to roughly 1-2.5M input tokens, mostly cache reads. At Sonnet 5.5 API list price that is about USD 1-5 per run ⚠ *(unverified: estimate, not metered)*. On a Pro or Max subscription there is no marginal money, but a noticeable share of the 5-hour quota, and much more if a page's full DOM is injected (issue #65927). Time: about 15-30 minutes unattended per 5-model run (estimate; the 2-site test here took about 10 tool calls).

**evidence trail**

Strong. It can save URLs, extracted text, screenshots to disk and GIF recordings, and write a timestamped Markdown table straight into a vault note (Claude Code). Saved record: date and time, query, and per candidate: URL, offer ID or EAN, price, price with delivery, 'najnizsza cena z 30 dni' if shown, sponsored or organic flag, seller name and NIP check result, GPSR fields present or missing, Safety Gate hit or none, plus screenshot file paths.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Already wired into Claude Code (`claude --chrome`, MCP tools) and into the desktop built-in browser, so it fits the vault workflow with no extra vendor.
  - Reads Polish shops live: Allegro listing and product pages and Ceneo search were read normally on 2026-10-15, with no anti-bot wall.
  - Uses the user's own logins, so it can reach paywalled tests, order history and the cart.
  - Produces an auditable trail (URLs, screenshots, GIFs, text) for the vault.
  - Vendor-reported prompt-injection success rate near 0% with the classifier (GA, 2026-08-26), with confirmations before purchases in practice.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No index, history or alerts of its own; quality depends entirely on the prompt or skill.
  - Extraction pitfalls: the wrong page element was read, GPSR data sits behind a click, and sponsored offers dominate the first results.
  - Token and quota heavy on complex pages (61%-of-session issue), and slower than a dedicated API.
  - Shop terms restrict bots (Allegro art. 10.10-10.11 from 2026-10-13, eBay agent ban, Amazon blocks).
  - Security incidents (ShadowPrompt, ClaudeBleed) show the extension itself is attack surface while logged into everything.

**independent review consensus**

Limited and mostly anecdotal. Zenity Labs threat analysis (2025-12-29; security vendor): broad permissions, always-logged-in sessions, and plan deviation in ask mode. Ernest Chiang hands-on (2025 preview): works but slower than manual. libecity user report (May-June 2026, Japanese): large time saving on Rakuten/Amazon comparisons, with factual errors and variant-default mistakes, and the user still made the final purchase. Koi Security / The Hacker News (March 2026): ShadowPrompt, patched. No rigorous independent shopping-accuracy test found; vendor safety numbers are not independently reproduced.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW (as research hands, never as the payer). Deciding fact: it already runs from Claude Code and read Allegro and Ceneo pages live on 2026-10-15 while saving URLs and screenshots for the vault. Best use: a buying-research skill that drives it through fixed sources (Allegro sorted by price with sponsored items flagged, Ceneo, the GPSR drawer, Safety Gate, the VAT white list), writes the evidence table to the vault, and stops at the cart.

**conflicting evidence**

- Purchase confirmations: the 2025 pilot post says Claude asks before purchasing. The GA post (2026-08-26) describes autonomous actions approved by a classifier and does not list purchases as always confirmed. The current safety page lists confirmations for 'downloading a file or entering sensitive information'.
- Attack success rate: GA post 0% for Fable 5 vs 0.3% (Banyan and the GA post's own breakdown) vs 0% for all three models (GIGAZINE). The safety page says 'less than 0.08%' on Opus 4.8. Pre-safeguard Opus 5 rate 3.8%.
- Blocked sites: the 2025 pilot blocked financial-services sites. The current safety page lists only adult and pirated sites as blocked and says financial sites need permission. A third-party summary lists banking, trading and crypto as blocked.
- Beta label: the GA post says generally available on all paid plans, while the help center still marks the side panel as beta.
- Speed: 10-15 minutes vs 2-3 manual (2025 preview hands-on) vs 3 minutes vs 30 manual (May 2026 user report).
- Browser support: help center says Chrome only for the extension side panel, while Claude Code docs say the integration works with Edge and other Chromium browsers.

### browser-use

**Verdict:** PILOT · **Cost:** Free, MIT; agent tokens extra · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 1 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

browser-use is an MIT-licensed browser-automation stack for AI agents (role: agent / browser-automation framework / scraper). It has three parts: (1) the Python library 'browser-use' (latest 0.13.11, 2026-10-07), an Agent loop that turns a page into LLM-readable state and acts on it with any LLM; (2) the CLI / 'browser-harness' (latest 0.1.13, 2026-09-04), which lets a coding agent such as Claude Code drive a real Chromium browser over CDP through Python heredocs with helpers (new_tab, goto_url, js, capture_screenshot, click_at_xy); no LLM key is needed because Claude Code is the brain; (3) Browser Use Cloud: stealth browsers, residential proxies, the hosted 'v4' agent and the BU 2.0 model. On this machine: uv tool browser-use 0.13.7 with browser-harness 0.1.8 (both behind latest), driven via an isolated Microsoft Edge 155 profile over CDP, with a Claude Code skill at C:\Users\pawel\.claude\skills\browser-use\SKILL.md.

**vendor and ownership**

Browser Use (company), San Francisco, USA. Founded 2024 by Magnus Mueller and Gregor Zunic (ETH Zurich origin); Y Combinator W25; USD 17M seed led by Felicis, announced 2025-03-23 (TechCrunch, Seedtable). Open-source maintainer: the browser-use GitHub organisation. Not owned by a marketplace or retailer, so no retail bias. Revenue comes from Browser Use Cloud (browser hours, proxies, LLM gateway with 20% markup).

**lifecycle status**

Active, fast-moving. Library repo created 2024-10-31; 118,064 stars, 549 open issues, last push 2026-10-15; releases 0.13.4 (2026-07-11), 0.13.5/0.13.6 (2026-07-17), 0.13.7 (2026-07-27), 0.13.8 (2026-08-16), 0.13.9/0.13.10 (2026-09-04), 0.13.11 (2026-10-07). browser-harness repo created 2026-04-17; 18,444 stars, 407 open issues, last push 2026-10-15; v0.1.11-0.1.13 all on 2026-09-03/04. The local harness prints 'update available: 0.1.8 -> 0.1.13'. Verified 2026-10-15 via GitHub API, PyPI and a local run. Primary sources: github.com/browser-use/browser-use, github.com/browser-use/browser-harness.

**cost model**

- **library and harness**: Free, MIT. In harness mode the cost is the driving agent's tokens (Claude Code subscription or API).
- **library agent mode**: Bring your own LLM key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama) or use the Browser Use gateway at model cost plus 20%.
- **browser use cloud**: Pay as you go, no subscription, credits never expire (browser-use.com/pricing, seen 2026-10-15, USD): browser USD 0.02 per browser-hour billed per minute with a 1-minute minimum; residential proxy USD 5/GB (on by default); own or direct proxy USD 0.20/GB; BU 2.0 model USD 0.60 input / 0.06 cached / 3.50 output per 1M tokens; Claude Sonnet 5 via gateway USD 2.40 / 0.24 / 12.00 per 1M (20% fee included); minimum top-up USD 5; free credit USD 1 per eligible signup (the README says USD 15, see conflicting_evidence). Concurrency 10 sessions at USD 0 lifetime spend, 50 at USD 200.

**feature geo matrix**

- **local library and harness**: Not geo-gated: works from Poland, the EU and the US on any site that renders in the controlled browser. Language-neutral: the LLM reads Polish pages, and Claude handles Polish. No shopping-specific features, so nothing is US-only.
- **own probe poland 2026-10-15**: Isolated Edge 155 (headful, no logins, Polish residential connection) driven by the installed harness: allegro.pl listing 'trampolina 305 cm' (3,655 offers, prices, 'z dostawa' prices, 'Sponsorowane'/'Promowane' labels, seller badges), ceneo.pl search, mediaexpert.pl search, decathlon.pl search (Cloudflare script present, content loaded) and amazon.pl search all rendered full content with no captcha or DataDome challenge. leroymerlin.pl returned the shop's own 404 for the guessed search URL (wrong URL, not a block). Plain HTTP clients get 403 from allegro.pl, decathlon.pl and mediaexpert.pl (sibling-item probes of the same day). Single low-volume test; not proof of behaviour at volume.
- **browser use cloud**: Residential proxies claimed for 195+ countries, chosen with a proxy country code; the docs sample list (us, gb, de, fr, jp, au, br, in, kr, ca, es, it, nl, se, sg) does not include pl and the default is a US proxy; a Polish exit IP was not tested and is not confirmed for Poland. A US or datacenter exit would likely see different prices or blocks on Polish shops.
- **purchase features**: No agentic-checkout, price-alert or buy-for-me feature of its own; a purchase would be generic clicking through a shop's checkout.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial, do-it-yourself. It reads whatever the page shows: the Allegro listing exposes structured spec snippets per offer (e.g. 'Rozmiar (ft) 10 (304-312 cm), Maks. obciazenie 150 kg, Wysokosc calkowita 250 cm') and product pages carry spec tables and often JSON-LD with gtin/sku. The agent must write the extraction and the cross-shop matching itself; there is no built-in EAN/GTIN mapping, rebadge detection or lineup comparison. Quality of variant mapping depends on the LLM's reasoning and on the shop exposing GTINs.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

No index and no shop discovery: the agent visits each shop and searches it. Coverage is any shop that renders in the browser. Confirmed readable on 2026-10-15: Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, Decathlon.pl, Amazon.pl (own probe). x-kom, brand stores and Amazon.de not tested here but carry no reported block for real browsers. Number of shops: not applicable (no vendor coverage claim). The comparison table is whatever the agent assembles; nothing is pre-computed.

**price history and omnibus**

None stored. It can read and record what the page displays now: Allegro's and other shops' 'najnizsza cena z 30 dni przed obnizka' line, strike-through prices and Ceneo's price-history widget. It cannot judge a fake discount beyond that displayed Omnibus line unless paired with a tracker that has your own history (changedetection.io, Keepa for Amazon).

**total landed cost**

Partial, manual. The Allegro listing already shows a delivery-inclusive price (e.g. '349,99 zl' and '364,98 zl z dostawa' on 2026-10-15); the agent can open a shop's delivery, payment and returns pages and extract return-shipping costs and assembly fees into a table. Nothing computes landed cost automatically, and cross-border warranty enforceability is not assessed.

**review and seller verification**

Partial, do-it-yourself. It can read ratings and review counts (Allegro '4,70 (133)'), seller badges ('Super Sprzedawca', 'Oficjalny sklep'), and open the seller's company-data page to capture NIP/KRS, then query CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list/VIES sites in the browser where they allow it (some registers block automation). No review-authenticity analysis. It cannot prove a review is genuine or that the seller matches the registered company beyond what the pages state.

**safety and compliance checks**

Partial, do-it-yourself. It can read GPSR fields on a listing (manufacturer, EU responsible person, warnings in Polish), search Safety Gate and the UOKiK register, and open TUV Certipedia when a certificate number is known. None of this is built in; each check is a scripted page visit that can be automated once written.

**independent test coverage**

N/A as a feature. It can open Stiftung Warentest, VKI or CHOICE pages, but paywalled results need the user's logged-in subscription, which the isolated profile does not have. It surfaces nothing on its own.

**alerts and monitoring**

None built in. A Claude Code scheduled task or cron could rerun a harness script, but each run costs tokens and a visible browser; a dedicated tracker (changedetection.io) is the better tool for watching a Polish shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Technically yes: it can click 'Dodaj do koszyka' and proceed through any checkout in the browser it controls. No built-in spending caps, mandates, payment confirmation or merchant-of-record logic. Guardrails available: the harness skill tells the agent to stop at login walls, passwords, MFA and consent screens; Claude Code's own permission prompts; the library's allowed_domains and sensitive_data options (allowed_domains had a critical bypass, CVE-2025-47241, fixed in 0.1.45). Recommended setup for this buyer: keep the isolated profile logged out of shops and payment providers, never store card or BLIK data in it, and end every run before the cart. On error the purchase would be the user's own contract with the shop.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: on request it can read spare-part pages (nets, pads, springs), warranty terms and OLX / Allegro Lokalnie listings for used units; nothing is modelled automatically.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Live pages at the moment of the run (DOM text, JS-extracted JSON, screenshots), so price and stock are as fresh as possible; no own index or feed. Every answer can be backed by URL, timestamp and a screenshot file. Freshness caveat from the probe: the first two extraction passes on the Allegro listing returned no prices because content was still rendering; a later pass with a longer wait captured them, so scripts need explicit waits (wait_for_element / wait_for_network_idle).

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full
- **claude code skill and harness**: Installed: skill at C:\Users\pawel\.claude\skills\browser-use\SKILL.md; usage 'browser-use <<PY ... PY' heredocs with pre-imported helpers (new_tab, goto_url, wait_for_load, js, capture_screenshot, click_at_xy, fill_input, http_get, raw cdp()). Claude Code writes the Python; no extra LLM key.
- **mcp server**: Local stdio MCP server built in: 'browser-use --mcp' (module browser_use.mcp.server) and 'browser-use --cli-mcp' (browser_use.mcp.cli_mcp), confirmed in the installed 0.13.7 cli.py. Not tested here.
- **python library**: Agent(task=..., llm=ChatAnthropic(...)) for a self-contained agent loop; Python 3.11+; 'uv add browser-use'.
- **cloud api and sdk**: Browser Use Cloud REST API and SDK (browser_use_sdk 3.4.2 is installed alongside); remote daemons via start_remote_daemon(name) for headless or parallel runs, billed per minute.
- **setup effort on this machine**: Found on 2026-10-15: (1) Smart App Control blocks the uv-generated shims ('An Application Control policy has blocked this file' for browser-use.exe and bu.exe); workaround: run C:\Users\pawel\AppData\Roaming\uv\tools\browser-use\Scripts\python.exe -c "from browser_use.cli import main; ..." with the heredoc on stdin. (2) The launcher C:\Users\pawel\browser-use-edge.ps1 reported 'Edge CDP endpoint not reachable' because another process listens on 127.0.0.1:9222 and answers 404, while Edge listens on [::1]:9222; passing BU_CDP_WS=ws://[::1]:9222/devtools/browser/<id> fixed it. The harness then printed a misleading 'Chrome is asking Allow remote debugging?' message. After these fixes a run took seconds. Estimate: about 20-30 minutes to make the launcher and shim robust (use the IPv6 endpoint and the venv python).
- **fallback**: Claude in Chrome (installed in this environment as mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools) covers the same pages through the user's real Chrome.

**protocol support**

CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) for control; MCP as a server. A Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421) request-signing PR (#4106) was closed on 2026-04-17 and the GitHub API shows no merge; release notes were not checked for a later implementation, so signed-agent identification is not confirmed. No ACP, UCP, AP2 or Visa TAP support; it does not need them, because it acts as a human-like browser rather than through agent-commerce APIs.

**open source and licence**

Open source, MIT. github.com/browser-use/browser-use: 118,064 stars, 13,091 forks, 549 open issues, last push 2026-10-15. github.com/browser-use/browser-harness: MIT, 18,444 stars, 407 open issues, last push 2026-10-15. Browser Use Cloud is closed.

**account linking and data access**

Local mode needs no account. It controls whatever browser profile it is attached to; on this machine an isolated Edge profile (C:\Users\pawel\AppData\Local\browser-use-edge) with no shop or payment logins, which is the right GDPR posture. Telemetry is ON by default: the library (ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY, PostHog EU host eu.i.posthog.com) and the harness (BH_TELEMETRY / BROWSER_HARNESS_TELEMETRY / ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY; it records which coding agent, e.g. 'claude-code', and redacts values containing '://'). Set ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY=false to opt out. Page content goes to whichever LLM drives it (Anthropic in harness mode). Cloud mode sends browsing to Browser Use's US company; profile sync uploads cookies to the cloud.

**automation legal risk**

Moderate. Allegro's Regulamin (effective 2026-10-13) art. 10.10 bans extracting and processing Allegro data for business use 'in particular with bots', and art. 10.11 bans bots that create load; Ceneo's terms 14.7-14.10 forbid automated access and set a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per violation of copying rules (sibling-item findings). Personal, human-paced reading of a few pages for one's own purchase is low practical risk, but it is still automated access and is not covered by any permission. Do not run it logged into an Allegro account (account sanctions are possible). Keep raw snapshots in the unpublished content/_raw area; do not republish offer tables. Anti-bot posture: DataDome on Allegro and Cloudflare on Decathlon did not challenge the headful Edge at probe volume; at higher volume or from cloud IPs blocks are likely (see known_failures).

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

No affiliate links or sponsored ranking in the tool itself. Bias enters from the pages it reads: Allegro's first results are 'Sponsorowane' and 'Promowane' offers (observed 2026-10-15), so an agent that takes the top of a listing inherits paid placement unless told to skip labelled ads. The vendor's commercial interest is in Cloud usage (browser hours, proxies, 20% LLM markup).

**ranking transparency**

Full in harness mode: every step is a visible script and URL in the Claude Code transcript, and the agent can be told to exclude a source or skip sponsored items and rerun. Library agent mode keeps an action history. Sponsored marking depends on the shop's labels, which the agent can read.

**run to run consistency**

No shopping-specific repeat-run data found. Deterministic parts (a fixed extraction script on a fixed URL) repeat well; LLM-chosen navigation and shortlists vary like any LLM agent. Vendor benchmark claims are not comparable across harnesses: Browser Use claims 97% on Online-Mind2Web (own post, March 2026); TinyFish (a competitor) reports Browser Use at 88.3% vs its own 91.1% on WebVoyager; the Online-Mind2Web paper (COLM 2025) shows WebVoyager-style scores overstate live-web success, with most agents far lower under human evaluation.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Weak by design; depends on the driving model. Page text flows straight into the LLM context, so prompt injection on a shop or fake-shop page can steer it. Documented: CVE-2025-47241 (allowed_domains bypass via 'https://allowed.com:pass@evil.com', CVSS 9.3 per GitHub advisory GHSA-x39x-9qw5-ghrf, fixed in 0.1.45) and an arXiv security assessment (2505.13076) rating credential exfiltration via prompt injection High (8.8). The harness has no injection classifier, no blocked site categories and no purchase confirmation of its own, unlike Claude in Chrome (per-site permissions, blocked high-risk categories, confirmation before purchases, Anthropic-reported attack success of about 1% in its current configuration). Safeguards to apply: isolated logged-out profile, no payment data, stop before cart, verify shop identity separately (Scamlexity-style fake shops).

**known failures**

Anti-bot: Kroger (Akamai) unreachable even with Cloud stealth and US proxy (issue #3449, 2025); 'stealth=True but still blocked by Cloudflare' (#2511, 2025); agent silently saw empty pages behind anti-bot challenges in CI (#3845, Carrefour.fr; challenge-detection warnings added 2026); a 2026-08 PR (#5447) documented two CDP detection leaks (Runtime.enable left on, MouseEvent screenX equal to clientX) that Cloudflare Turnstile can detect; the GitHub API shows the PR closed on 2026-10-10 with no merge; whether the fixes landed through another PR was not checked. Local setup on this machine: App Control blocks the exe shims; port 9222 conflict on 127.0.0.1; misleading 'Allow remote debugging' message. Data: extraction before render completes returns empty prices (own probe). Release churn: about two releases a month, so helper names and flags change.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - no UOKiK, DSA, DMA or court action against Browser Use found (searched 2026-10-15).

**buyer protection path**

N/A as a route: any purchase is made on the shop's own checkout, so protection is the shop's or marketplace's - Polish statutory warranty (rekojmia, 2 years), 14-day withdrawal for distance sales (return shipping of a bulky trampoline usually at the buyer's cost unless the shop states otherwise), Allegro Protect on Allegro, card chargeback, ECC-Net for cross-border EU. A purchase an agent clicks through is still the user's contract; a wrong-variant order is handled through withdrawal, not through the tool.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Good as the reader of Polish shop pages that plain fetchers cannot reach. Trampoline example: open the Allegro listing 'trampolina 305 cm' (3,655 offers on 2026-10-15), extract the first 2-3 pages of offers with price, 'z dostawa' price, rating and count, seller badge and spec snippet (max load 150 kg, total height 250 cm), skipping 'Sponsorowane'; open 3-5 shortlisted offers to capture GPSR manufacturer and EU responsible person, the 30-day lowest price line, warranty and the seller's NIP; repeat on Ceneo, Decathlon.pl and Media Expert; save a screenshot per page. It cannot read paywalled lab tests, verify a TUV certificate without its number, watch prices over weeks, or guarantee access at volume.

**workflow role**

Price-and-offer capture plus seller and GPSR field capture on Polish shops (Allegro, Ceneo, Decathlon, Media Expert), after discovery and spec shortlisting. Combine with: Shopify Global Catalog or SerpApi for discovery, independent tests and Safety Gate for product choice, register checks for seller identity, and changedetection.io or Keepa for monitoring. Use Claude in Chrome instead when the step needs the user's own logins.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup: done on this machine, plus about 20-30 minutes to harden the launcher (IPv6 CDP endpoint, venv python instead of blocked shims). One comparison in harness mode: 3 candidate models x 4 shops = 12 product pages + 4 listing pages = 16 page reads. Targeted JS extraction returns about 1-3k tokens per page; a full innerText dump of the Allegro listing was 33,836 characters (about 9-10k tokens); a 1,200 px screenshot is about 1-1.5k image tokens ⚠ *(unverified)*. With reasoning, about 100-200k tokens per run; under a Claude Max subscription no marginal cost, at Sonnet-class API rates (about USD 2-3 per 1M input tokens ⚠ *(unverified)*) roughly USD 0.5-1. Library agent mode with an LLM per step: 30-60 steps x 5-15k tokens = 0.3-0.9M tokens. Cloud variant: 20 browser-minutes = USD 0.007, plus residential proxy for 16 pages x about 3 MB = about 50 MB = USD 0.25 ⚠ *(unverified: page weight)*. Time: about 10-20 minutes.

**evidence trail**

Strong. capture_screenshot(path) saves PNGs (the probe saved a 1121x1200 Allegro listing screenshot with sponsored labels and prices visible), JS extraction returns JSON, and pages can be printed to PDF (print-as-pdf interaction skill). A vault record could read: 'shop, URL, timestamp, offer title, price, price with delivery, 30-day lowest price line, seller name, NIP, rating and count, GPSR responsible person, screenshot path'. Store snapshots under content/_raw (unpublished) because of Allegro and Ceneo terms.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Reads Polish shops that block plain fetchers: Allegro, Ceneo, Decathlon.pl, Media Expert and Amazon.pl rendered fully in the 2026-10-15 probe, where WebFetch-style requests get 403.
  - Already installed with a Claude Code skill; harness mode needs no extra LLM key and every step is a visible script.
  - Strong evidence trail: screenshots, JSON extraction and PDFs saved to files.
  - MIT, very active (118k stars, release roughly every two weeks), with MCP server, Python library and Cloud options.
  - Free locally; Cloud is cheap per browser-hour (USD 0.02) if parallel or headless runs are needed.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No guardrails of its own: no purchase confirmation, spending cap, injection classifier or blocked site categories; past critical allowed_domains bypass (CVE-2025-47241).
  - No shopping intelligence: no index, price history, GTIN mapping or review-authenticity checks; all of it is DIY per run.
  - Anti-bot is not solved: documented blocks (Akamai, Cloudflare Turnstile, CDP leaks) and a Cloud proxy default of US with Poland unconfirmed.
  - Local setup on this machine is brittle (App Control blocks shims, port 9222 conflict, misleading permission message); installed versions lag latest.
  - Automating Allegro and Ceneo conflicts with their terms, even at personal volume.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on test of browser-use on shopping or Polish shops found. Independent evidence is limited to: the Online-Mind2Web paper (COLM 2025), showing that live-web success is much lower than WebVoyager-style vendor numbers; the ARIMLABS security assessment (arXiv 2505.13076) and CVE-2025-47241; and GitHub issue reports of anti-bot blocks. Benchmark numbers come from the vendor (97% Online-Mind2Web) or a competitor (TinyFish: 88.3% WebVoyager). Listicles ('best AI browser agents 2026' from Firecrawl, Olostep, TinyFish) are vendor-written and were not used as evidence. The own probe on 2026-10-15 is the main Poland-specific evidence.

**verdict for me**

PILOT - deciding fact: it is already installed and, in a real Edge on a Polish connection, read Allegro, Ceneo, Decathlon and Media Expert listings that block plain fetchers, while it has no purchase or injection guardrails of its own. Best use: as Claude Code's logged-out reader for the shortlist step - one scripted pass per shop extracting price, delivery price, 30-day lowest price, seller NIP and GPSR fields plus a screenshot into content/_raw, stopping before the cart; switch to Claude in Chrome for anything that needs your account.

**conflicting evidence**

- Free Cloud credit: the GitHub README says new Google, GitHub or Microsoft signups get USD 15; browser-use.com/pricing says USD 1 once per person (both seen 2026-10-15).
- Anti-bot reach: Browser Use's stealth-browser page claims its Chromium fork bypasses Cloudflare, DataDome, Kasada, Akamai and PerimeterX; GitHub issue #3449 reports Kroger (Akamai) unreachable even with Cloud stealth and proxies, and #2511 reports Cloudflare blocks with stealth=True.
- Benchmarks: Browser Use claims 97% on Online-Mind2Web (March 2026); TinyFish reports Browser Use at 88.3% on WebVoyager; the Online-Mind2Web authors show WebVoyager scores overstate live-web performance. Different harnesses and judges, not comparable.
- Local CDP state: the harness reported 'Chrome is asking Allow remote debugging?', but the real cause was another process holding 127.0.0.1:9222 while Edge listened on [::1]:9222.
- Memory note (97 days old) records browser-use 0.13.3; the installed version is 0.13.7 and the latest release is 0.13.11.

#### other info

**comparison with claude in chrome**

- **same brain**: In harness mode Claude Code (Claude) does the reasoning in both cases; the difference is the browser and the safety layer.
- **browser and logins**: browser-use here: an isolated, logged-out Edge profile (no Allegro account, no saved payment data). Claude in Chrome: the user's real Chrome with their logins, which helps when a page needs an account and raises the stakes of a mistake.
- **safety layer**: Claude in Chrome adds per-site permissions, blocked high-risk site categories (banking, trading), confirmation before purchases or sharing personal data, and prompt-injection defences (Anthropic support article: about 1% attack success in its current configuration; 23.6% to 11.2% at the 2025 launch). browser-use adds none of these.
- **automation and evidence**: browser-use is scriptable: arbitrary JS and CDP, batch extraction, screenshots and PDFs saved to files, reruns, cloud parallelism. Claude in Chrome works through read_page / find / get_page_text tools in one visible browser and pauses at CAPTCHAs and logins.
- **anti bot**: Both use a real Chromium on the user's residential IP, which passed Allegro's DataDome and Decathlon's Cloudflare at probe volume. CDP-driven browsers have known detection leaks (PR #5447); a logged-in personal Chrome is the least bot-like.
- **pick**: Use browser-use for repeatable, logged-out extraction with a saved evidence trail; use Claude in Chrome for steps that need the user's account or carry purchase risk.

### Deep-research skills

**Verdict:** USE NOW · **Cost:** Plan quota or API tokens · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 1 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Two research workflows already installed in this Claude Code setup (role: skill / research workflow, not a shopping product), plus claude.ai's Research mode as a non-Claude-Code sibling.
- **anthropic deep research skill**: 'deep-research' skill from Anthropic's skills plugin (synced copy at C:\Users\pawel\.claude\skills\synced\...\deep-research\SKILL.md, file date 2026-10-07). A coordinator asks clarifying questions only when needed, creates research_notes/{title}/ and reports/ in the working directory, splits the question into 1-6+ subtopics and spawns parallel general-purpose research subagents; each must attach an inline [Source](URL) to every claim, flag conflicts and list gaps; at most one extra research round; one report-writer subagent produces a narrative report.
- **vault b research pipeline**: Five vault skills - /b:research (outline from model knowledge plus a web-search-agent screen, confirmation gates), /b:research-add-items, /b:research-add-fields, /b:research-deep (one web-search-agent per batch of items, here 3 items per agent and 4 agents per batch, each writing one JSON per item that must pass validate_json.py) and /b:research-report (a generated Python script turns all JSON into report.md, skipping uncertain-tagged values, then promotes it to content/_raw/inbox for /b:ingest). Output is an N items x M fields matrix. This shopping-decision-support workspace (47 items x 37 fields) is a live run of it.
- **claude ai research**: claude.ai Research mode (web, desktop, mobile; paid plans; needs web search on). Not driven from Claude Code.

**vendor and ownership**

Anthropic PBC (San Francisco, USA) ships the deep-research skill. The b:research suite is adapted from Weizhena/Deep-Research-skills (GitHub user Weizhena; MIT; 2,361 stars, last push 2026-08-23) and maintained by the vault owner; the shared source of truth is github.com/plipowczan/second-brain-template. The web-search-agent and its five strategy modules are vendored from upstream (module files still carry Chinese headings). No commercial or retail interest in any recommendation.

**lifecycle status**

Active. Anthropic skill: synced locally 2026-10-07. b:research: web-search-agent shipped into the vault 2026-07-13 (commit 237da435), date-fetch fix 2026-07-14 (b0de0938), namespaced to /b: on 2026-07-23 (efee0e1b). In use: 11 research workspaces with 290 result JSON files in content/_raw/research-workspaces as of 2026-10-15, including two consumer-purchase runs - 'AI Voice Recorders for Meetings (Polish)' (2026-10-01, 13 devices x 49 fields) and 'Weekend Tent-Camping Hike Candidates' (2026-07-28). Verified 2026-10-15 from local files, git log and the GitHub API.

**cost model**

No separate fee: both run on the Claude Code plan (Pro/Max subscription quota) or on API tokens. The web-search-agent is configured with model: opus, the most expensive tier. Per-run arithmetic is in effort_and_cost_per_purchase.

**feature geo matrix**

- **poland**: Claude Code skills work from Poland; agents search and read Polish sources and write English output (this run cites allegro.pl terms, ceneo.pl terms, UOKiK pages). Claude Code's WebSearch tool is described as 'US-only', yet it returned Polish pages in this run; local ranking may differ from google.pl.
- **live shop access**: Limited in Poland: the default fetcher (WebFetch, a plain HTTP fetch) receives 403 from allegro.pl, decathlon.pl, mediaexpert.pl and kaufland.pl (sibling probes 2026-10-15), and Ceneo's terms ban automated access.
- **claude ai research**: Available on paid plans per the current support article, which lists no countries; an older version listed only the US, Japan and Brazil, so availability in Poland is not confirmed for Poland from Anthropic's own pages.
- **purchase features**: None; research only, no US-only commerce features involved.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Strong when the schema asks for it. In b:research the items can be the candidate models or variants themselves, and fields.yaml can demand a spec table, EAN/GTIN, retailer-exclusive and regional names, OEM rebadges and the cheaper/pricier near-equivalent; every agent fills the same fields, so variants line up in one matrix. Evidence: the voice-recorder run compared 13 devices on 49 fields and overturned 12 claims from the preliminary screen. Limits: there is no product database behind it, so variant mapping is only as good as manufacturer and shop pages, and agents can confuse near-identical model names; the Anthropic skill produces prose, not a matrix.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Weak for live prices. Prices come from search snippets and fetched pages, recorded as dated snapshots (e.g. the voice-recorder note: '699 PLN (x-kom); 589-650 PLN (morele)', seen 2026-10-01). Allegro, Decathlon.pl, Media Expert and Kaufland block WebFetch; Ceneo forbids automation; no shop count applies. Fix: add a browser step (Claude in Chrome or browser-use) or an API (Shopify Global Catalog, SerpApi Google Shopping) for price fields.

**price history and omnibus**

None built in. Agents can research Omnibus rules and cite a shop's displayed 30-day lowest price if a page is readable, but they hold no price history and cannot call a discount fake without a tracker (Keepa for Amazon, own changedetection.io history).

**total landed cost**

Only if the schema demands it: agents can find delivery, return and assembly terms on shop pages and add them up, but blocked shops and missing freight quotes for bulky items leave gaps. Cross-border warranty can be researched as a legal field, not computed.

**review and seller verification**

Partial, as research. Agents can read review summaries, look up company data (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list, VIES) and warning lists, and cite them; sibling items in this workspace show these registers' access limits. They cannot prove review authenticity, and blocked Allegro and Ceneo pages limit review coverage.

**safety and compliance checks**

Strong suit, as research rather than automation: agents can search Safety Gate and UOKiK, establish which EN 71-14 edition applies, check GS/TUV certificates in Certipedia when a number is known, and note GPSR listing duties, with citations. This workspace runs exactly these as separate items (Safety Gate/UOKiK, EN 71-14 and Certipedia, GPSR).

**independent test coverage**

Good at finding and citing tests (this workspace's trampoline-tests item covers Stiftung Warentest 05/2025, VKI 2025 and CHOICE 10/2025) and at checking model-year and Polish availability; paywalled detail is unreadable without the user's subscription, so agents cite summaries.

**alerts and monitoring**

None. A rerun of /b:research-deep on chosen items is the only refresh; scheduled monitoring belongs to a tracker.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No purchase capability, by design. Nothing touches carts, accounts or payment data, which makes it the safest route for the verification phase.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: fields can cover spare parts (nets, pads, springs), warranty handling and service in Poland, and used-market prices on OLX or Allegro Lokalnie; the agents research them like any other field.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Model knowledge (b:research step 1 seeds items from it, then verifies), WebSearch results and WebFetch pages at run time, plus any MCP or CLI tool the agent may call. WebFetch answers through a small summarising model and caches pages for 15 minutes, so numbers can be paraphrased or lost; it keeps no snapshot. Freshness equals the run date; the fields.yaml discipline here asks for a verified-on date per status and a sources_checked list with access dates. Every claim is meant to carry a URL (Anthropic skill: inline per claim; b:research: per item).

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full
- **native**: Both are Claude Code skills: /b:research <topic>, /b:research-add-items, /b:research-add-fields, /b:research-deep, /b:research-report, and the deep-research skill via the Skill tool. Agents: .claude/agents/web-search-agent.md (model opus, all tools) with five strategy modules in .claude/agents/web-search-modules/.
- **tool integration**: Because the deep agents have all tools, a product template can tell them to call the Shopify Global Catalog MCP, SerpApi, Keepa MCP or a browser agent for price fields.
- **setup effort**: Zero to run (installed). Adapting to product research: about 1-2 hours to write a reusable product fields.yaml template (spec table, tests, safety, seller, price snapshot, warranty) and a short instruction for the browser step.
- **fallback**: Manual: run WebSearch and WebFetch directly in a chat.

**protocol support**

MCP only, indirectly (agents can call any MCP server configured in Claude Code). No agent-commerce protocols (ACP, UCP, AP2), which a research-only workflow does not need.

**open source and licence**

b:research: MIT upstream (Weizhena/Deep-Research-skills, 2,361 stars, last push 2026-08-23), vault adaptation in the user's repos. Anthropic deep-research skill: distributed by Anthropic in its skills plugin; licence not stated in the local SKILL.md.

**account linking and data access**

No shop accounts, payment data or browser profile. Queries and fetched pages go to Anthropic as model context and to the search backend. GDPR exposure is limited to what the user writes into the research brief; outputs stay in the local vault (content/_raw is excluded from the published Quartz site, but promoted reports become public notes).

**automation legal risk**

Low at research volume: occasional searches and page fetches. Ceneo's terms (14.7-14.10) ban automated access and copying, with a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty, and Allegro's Regulamin (art. 10.10-10.11, from 2026-10-13) bans scraping, so offer tables from those sites should not be republished in public notes; keep raw extracts in content/_raw. Paywalled test results are copyrighted: cite conclusions, do not paste tables.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

No monetisation. Bias enters through sources: affiliate listicles dominate shopping search results, and this workspace's Step-2 screen reports a Wharton follow-up to ACES finding that one source such as Wirecutter can swing an agent's pick by 90-99 percentage points (secondary, not re-opened for this item). The fields.yaml 'evidence discipline' block (vendor-claimed labels, primary sources first, dates) is the counter-measure, enforced only by instructions.

**ranking transparency**

High. Every value is tied to sources in the JSON or notes, the matrix shows all candidates on the same fields, and a rerun with a source excluded is a matter of editing the brief or fields.yaml. No sponsored items exist.

**run to run consistency**

No repeat-run test of either skill exists in this vault. External evidence: SparkToro/Gumshoe (2,961 prompts across ChatGPT, Claude and Google AI answers) found the same recommendation list in fewer than 1 in 100 repeats, with Claude slightly more consistent on list membership; Product AI (vendor test, 220 shopping questions across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity) reported conflicting or incorrect information in 86% of responses and 97% wrong on comparison questions (Tech.co, via search). Internal evidence of drift between passes: in this workspace the deep phase overturned Step-2 screen claims (Ceneo Apify actors 'not found' vs five found; Keepa community-only vs an official hosted MCP; Shopify 'update_cart' vs a live get_product tool). The schema makes outputs structurally consistent, not factually identical. Mitigation: run the deep phase twice on the final 2-3 candidates and diff the JSON.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Moderate risk. Agents read untrusted pages and affiliate content; the only counter-measures are prompt rules (evidence discipline, vendor-claimed labels) and the researcher instruction to note conflicts. The web-search-agent runs with all tools (Bash, Write), so injected page text could in principle prompt actions; Claude Code's permission system and the agent's instruction-boundary rules are the safeguards. No purchase path exists, so manipulation can distort a verdict but cannot spend money.

**known failures**

validate_json.py checks only that field keys exist (coverage), not values, sources or dates; the vault note's 'anti-fabrication net' framing overstates it. The report generator drops a whole field when any part is uncertain: across 24 result files of this workspace (2026-10-15) 171 field entries sat in uncertain arrays (about 7.1 of 37 fields per item, about 19%), and the voice-recorder run dropped 257 of 637 values (40.3%). The skip rule is a plain substring match, so a field that merely mentions the bracketed uncertain marker in prose (as two drafts of this item did) is also dropped. WebFetch is blocked by key Polish shops and summarises pages through a small model (in this run a search summary of Shopify's docs named a different promoted-placement parameter than the page itself). Deep-research agents in general hallucinate 3-13% of citation URLs and 5-18% do not resolve (Rao, Wong, Callison-Burch, arXiv 2604.03173, April 2026). Runs are long and gated: this workspace's first batch wrote files 15:33-15:48 and a later batch 16:41-16:52 on 2026-10-15. The Anthropic skill writes research_notes/ and reports/ into the working directory, which in this vault is the repo root, outside content/_raw, unless redirected.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - research workflow; no operator or enforcement history applies.

**buyer protection path**

N/A - it never purchases; protection depends on the shop chosen afterwards (rekojmia, 14-day withdrawal, Allegro Protect, chargeback, ECC-Net cross-border).

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Strong for the verify and choose-the-version phases. Trampoline example: items = 6-10 candidate models and variants (e.g. Salta Premium Black Edition 305, BERG Champion 330, Hudora Fabulous 300, Decathlon 360 model, Urbogym 312, VirtuFit 305); fields = diameter, net inside or outside, max user weight, frame tube size and wall thickness, spring count and length, EN 71-14 edition claimed, GS/TUV certificate number and Certipedia check, Safety Gate/UOKiK hits, lab results (Stiftung Warentest 05/2025, VKI 2025, CHOICE 10/2025) with model-year match, Allegro/Ceneo rating and 1-2-star themes, spare parts, warranty, seller identity, and a price snapshot (shop, PLN, delivery, date, 30-day lowest). It cannot reliably fill live Allegro, Decathlon or Media Expert prices and stock through WebFetch, cannot detect a fake discount without history, and needs a browser step for the price row.

**workflow role**

Specs and variants, independent tests, safety and compliance, seller checks and the final verdict with an evidence trail; it is the orchestrator into which price tools plug. Combine with a browser agent (Claude in Chrome or browser-use) for Polish shop prices, Shopify Global Catalog or SerpApi for discovery, Keepa or changedetection.io for price history.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup: none to run; 1-2 hours once for a product fields template. One trampoline run with b:research: 8 candidates x about 30 fields at 3 items per agent = 3 deep agents, about 20-30 minutes of wall time plus confirmation gates. Tokens: the session counter for this 3-item agent (including live probes) dropped by about 0.3M tokens ⚠ *(unverified: counter semantics)*, so about 1M tokens per 3-agent run; this 47-item workspace is about 16 agents, roughly 5M tokens ⚠ *(unverified)*. On a Claude Max subscription that is quota, not cash; at API rates for an Opus-class model most of it is cached input, so a single product run plausibly costs single-digit USD ⚠ *(unverified)*. The Anthropic deep-research skill: 3-5 researchers plus a writer, about 15-30 minutes, similar token order.

**evidence trail**

Strong and already vault-native: one JSON per item with sources_checked (URL plus access date), conflicting_evidence and an uncertain list; report.md promoted to content/_raw/inbox with frontmatter and then ingested as a compiled note (the voice-recorder note is an example). The Anthropic skill leaves research_notes/*.md with an inline source per claim plus the final report. Gap: no page snapshots or screenshots by default, so prices are claims with a URL and date; add browser screenshots for the price row.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Already installed and proven on purchase decisions (voice recorders: 13 devices x 49 fields, 12 screening claims overturned).
  - Schema-first matrix fits 'choose the best version': every candidate is judged on the same spec, safety and test fields.
  - Citations and dates per item, and a direct path into the vault through /b:ingest.
  - No purchase path, no accounts: the safest tool for the verification phase.
  - Agents can call any MCP or browser tool, so price sources can be plugged in.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Live prices and stock on Allegro, Decathlon and Media Expert fail through WebFetch (403), and Ceneo bans automation.
  - Validator checks keys only; wrong values or dead citations pass (3-13% hallucinated URLs in deep-research agents generally).
  - Coarse uncertainty: a whole field is dropped from the report when one sub-claim is uncertain (about 19% of fields here, 40% in the voice-recorder run).
  - No repeat-run test; external studies show AI shopping lists rarely repeat.
  - Slow and token-heavy (opus agents, confirmation gates); 20-30 minutes even for a small product run.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of either skill. General evidence on deep-research agents: more citations but higher URL hallucination (arXiv 2604.03173, 2026); DeepResearch Bench and ReportBench separate citation accuracy from statement accuracy and warn that a resolving link does not prove support. Shopping-answer studies (SparkToro/Gumshoe, Product AI) are by companies selling AI-visibility or shopping products. The vault's own runs are the best evidence: they show deep passes overturning screen claims and a high share of honestly unresolved fields.

**verdict for me**

USE NOW - deciding fact: it is installed, already produced a cited purchase decision in this vault, and its schema fits spec, safety and test comparison, while live Polish shop prices fail through WebFetch. Best use: run /b:research with a product fields template on 6-10 candidate models for specs, tests, safety and seller checks, fill the price row with a browser agent or Shopify Catalog snapshot, and rerun the deep phase on the final 2-3 to check consistency.

**conflicting evidence**

- Product AI study: the outline describes '220 questions x 5 runs, 86% of answers contradicted each other across runs'; Tech.co (via search) describes 86% of responses with conflicting or incorrect information across 220 questions and does not mention five runs. The original study page was not opened (Tech.co URL returned 404 on fetch).
- Validator role: the vault's Deep-Research-skills note calls the uncertain-tag marking plus validate_json.py an 'anti-fabrication net'; the script only checks key coverage and exits 0 for any value.
- Skill naming: the vault note lists '/deep-research (Superpowers)' as the narrative research tool; the deep-research skill present on 2026-10-15 is in Anthropic's skills plugin (anthropic-skills:deep-research).
- claude.ai Research availability: an older support article limited it to the US, Japan and Brazil; the current article lists paid plans without countries; a June 2025 announcement says web search is global.
