### Shopify Global Catalog MCP

**Verdict:** PILOT · **Cost:** Free, keyless · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 2 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

Shopify's public, cross-merchant product-search MCP server (role: MCP server / product index API). Endpoint POST https://catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp (JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP), implementing the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) Catalog capability, version 2026-08-25 (response header x-shopify-ucp-mcp-api-version: 2026-08-25; serverInfo 'universal-ucp-mcp' 0.1.0). Live tools/list on 2026-10-15 returned three tools: search_catalog, lookup_catalog, get_product. Cart, checkout and order tools are separate Shopify MCP servers on merchant endpoints, not part of this one.

**vendor and ownership**

Shopify Inc., Ottawa, Canada (listed on NYSE and TSX). The catalog indexes products of Shopify merchants; Shopify is the commerce platform, not the seller. UCP is co-developed with Google (launched January 2026), with listed industry support from Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, Stripe, Etsy, Target and Wayfair (Shopify Spring '26 Edition). Bias note: Shopify earns from its merchants (subscriptions, payments) and plans paid promoted placements in catalog results; it is not owned by Allegro, Ceneo or any Polish marketplace.

**lifecycle status**

Live. Shopify Catalog announced 2025-05-21 for select apps and agents (shopify.dev changelog). Spring '26 Edition (2026-06-17): 'Building on Shopify's agentic commerce layer used to require approval. That requirement is gone.' The Catalog REST API is deprecated in favour of the Global Catalog MCP tools; secondary sources (daily.dev, ecommerceparadise) say it stops serving traffic on 2026-11-02. A community thread dates the old per-store Storefront MCP catalog tools' sunset to 2026-08-31. Promoted placements: Developer Preview, invite-led. Own live test 2026-10-15 from Poland: endpoint answered keyless with the hosted example agent profile. Primary sources: shopify.dev/docs/agents/catalog, /catalog/catalog-mcp, /profiles/auth-and-rate-limiting, /catalog/promoted-placement; shopify.com/news/spring-26-edition-dev.

**cost model**

Free to query. Keyless access works with only an agent profile URL in each tool call (tested 2026-10-15). An optional Dev Dashboard API key (client credentials exchanged for a JWT with a 60-minute TTL, scope read_global_api_catalog_search) is also free and gives the per-client limit of 5 requests per second shared by the three tools; anonymous traffic shares one pool across all callers and Shopify says 'Don't use unauthenticated requests for production traffic'. Keyless access cannot get rate-limit increases. The real cost in Claude Code is tokens: one 20-result search returned about 200 KB of JSON (see effort_and_cost_per_purchase).

**feature geo matrix**

- **poland catalog search**: Works. With ships_to PL and context address_country PL, a trampoline search on 2026-10-15 returned Polish Shopify stores (bieznie.pl: VirtuFit trampoline 305 cm with net, PLN 1,299.00; Weep Sports PLN 549.00; Abiko PLN 1,049.95; Jungle Jumparoo PLN 1,777.00) and EU stores, some showing PLN-converted prices (Tormino NL, Fietsenwinkel.be, Shopyourproduct).
- **language**: Polish queries match Polish titles ('trampolina ogrodowa 305 cm z siatka' returned Polish-titled offers). Descriptions come in each merchant's language (Danish, Dutch, German, Lithuanian seen); Shopify-inferred metadata is in English.
- **eu**: Works across EU shops (DK, NL, BE, DE, IE, LT seen). Currency is the merchant's presentment currency, not the requested PLN: of 75 variants seen, 25 EUR, 22 PLN, 21 DKK, 3 AUD, 2 GBP, 2 USD.
- **checkout and agentic features**: Not usable from Poland as seen: eligible.native_checkout was false for all 75 variants observed; Global Catalog returns only a merchant cart link. Shopify's direct/agentic checkout (Agentic Storefronts) is reported to have gone live by default for eligible US merchants selling to US shoppers on 2026-03-24 (secondary sources), so not confirmed for Poland. Complete-checkout via Checkout MCP needs a Token-tier permission.
- **us**: Same endpoint; US merchants are the largest share and agentic checkout is US-first.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial and error-prone. Each product carries the merchant's HTML description (often a full spec list) plus Shopify-inferred metadata (tech_specs, top_features, unique_selling_points) that Shopify labels as inferred and possibly inaccurate. Observed errors on 2026-10-15: for the Salta Cosmos 305 cm the inferred spec says 'Net Material: Polyethylene, 0.35 mm thick', but the merchant text gives 0.35 mm for the PVC edge cover; for the round Salta Premium Black Edition the inferred spec says 'Shape: Rectangular' and lists '305 x 214 cm, 396 x 244 cm' sizes. Variant handling: get_product on the UPID of a 'Premium Black Edition 305 cm, EUR 499' search hit returned the 366 cm variant at EUR 629 because no 'selected' option was passed. Filters cover only Color, Size and Target gender attributes, a relative price_tier (low/medium/high within a category) and minimum rating. No EAN/GTIN field appeared in the responses (variant keys seen: id, title, url, price, list_price, availability, media, seller, checkout_url, condition, eligible), so cross-shop mapping by barcode, rebadge detection and lineup comparison are left to the agent.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Cross-merchant price listing, but only within Shopify. Not covered: Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon.pl, Leroy Merlin, Amazon.de or idealo shops (none run on Shopify). Covered: Shopify-based Polish brand and niche stores (e.g. bieznie.pl) and EU brand stores (BERG, Salta and North resellers; Acon EU). Size: total_count estimates of 381-408 matches for trampoline queries (results stop at 1,000). The docs say global results are clustered by Universal Product ID with offers from multiple merchants, but in the tests every product had exactly one variant from one seller: the same Salta Premium Black Edition 305 appeared under two different UPIDs (Azzura Pool NL, EUR 499; Bolig og Haven DK, DKK 3,677), and 'Sonos Era 100' returned 10 separate one-seller products. ships_to is not a hard filter in practice: with ships_to PL the results included Australian shops (JB Hi-Fi in AUD, Everfit resellers) and a Danish shop whose shipping policy names no destination countries; ships_to US returned the same Danish and Dutch shops as no filter. Vendor claim: 'AI searches powered by Catalog convert at 2x the rate of those using scraped data' (vendor-claimed, Spring '26).

**price history and omnibus**

None. Each variant may carry list_price (the merchant's compare-at price; present in 27 of 75 variants seen), which is a strike-through price set by the merchant, not the Omnibus 30-day lowest price. Shopify's usage guidelines say search results cannot be cached, so building your own price history from repeated queries conflicts with the terms.

**total landed cost**

None in Global Catalog. No shipping cost or delivery estimate appeared in the 2026-10-15 responses (Spring '26 mentions delivery estimates as richer metadata, not observed here). Each seller object links to shipping_policy and refund_policy pages; Cart MCP / the UCP CLI 'cart update' can request shipping estimates where the merchant supports it. For a bulky cross-border item the freight and return cost must be checked on the merchant's site.

**review and seller verification**

Partial for the product, none for seller identity. Products may carry a rating (value, scale, count; 26 of the products seen had one, e.g. Acon EU 4.9 from 337), with no stated source or authenticity check. The seller object gives shop name, shop GID, the myshopify domain, the public URL and policy links (privacy, terms, refund, shipping) but no company name, address, VAT or registry number. Example: 'Shopyourproduct' (mbbb9j-ch.myshopify.com) lists the Salta First Class 305 at PLN 3,777.28 (Fietsenwinkel.be lists the same model at PLN 3,733.00), and its shipping policy gives no company name or destination countries. Grade: partial (domain and policies) / none (CEIDG, KRS, VIES, blocklists).

**safety and compliance checks**

None. Safety claims appear only as merchant text (the Salta Cosmos description lists 'TUV, CE, EN 71' without a certificate number or standard edition). No GPSR fields (manufacturer, EU responsible person), no Safety Gate or UOKiK checks, no certificate verification.

**independent test coverage**

None; it does not surface lab tests.

**alerts and monitoring**

None. No watch, webhook or alert feature for buyers, and caching results for later comparison is not allowed by the usage guidelines.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

Global Catalog itself cannot buy: it returns checkout_url, a merchant cart permalink with the variant and quantity (e.g. https://boligoghaven.dk/cart/50309872157002:1?...utm_source=shopify&utm_medium=catalog), which the buyer opens and pays on the merchant's own Shopify checkout. Separate Cart and Checkout MCP servers (UCP) exist with trust tiers: anonymous and signed agents can build and edit carts and checkouts, but complete_checkout requires a Token-tier credential with permission to complete purchases; non-trusted agents 'refer them to the merchant storefront to complete payment'. The UCP CLI adds a requires_escalation hook that opens the buyer's browser and a --dry-run flag. No spending caps or mandates are documented. Merchant of record: the individual merchant.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: the condition filter includes 'secondhand', so used items from Shopify resale shops can be found; spare parts appear in searches (Hudora ground-anchor sets came up in a trampoline query); refund policy links are provided. No service-network or resale-value data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Shopify's own index of merchant product data, which Shopify describes as real-time pricing, options and availability; plus Shopify AI-inferred fields marked as such. Each result links to the merchant product page with a _gsid and utm tags. total_count is an estimate and varied between 381 and 387 on identical queries minutes apart. Answers are backed by product and variant GIDs and merchant URLs, but snapshots cannot be cached under the usage guidelines.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full
- **official mcp server**: Remote, official: https://catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp. Every tool call must include meta.ucp-agent.profile (a URL to a UCP agent profile JSON); Shopify's hosted example https://shopify.dev/ucp/agent-profiles/examples/2026-08-25/valid-with-capabilities.json worked on 2026-10-15. Tools: search_catalog (query, context, filters: categories, price in minor units, available, shops up to 1,000, condition, ships_to, ships_from, attributes, rating, price_tier; pagination; view 'compact'; catalog_id; like for image or item similarity), lookup_catalog (1-50 IDs or Shopify product URLs), get_product (id, selected, preferences).
- **claude code wiring**: Expected: 'claude mcp add --transport http shopify-catalog https://catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp' and let Claude pass the profile URL as an argument. Not tested here, because adding an MCP server changes persistent configuration. Caveat: the server returns only structuredContent (no content array); Claude Code issue reports describe Claude Code reading structuredContent, so it should work, but this was not verified.
- **cli and skill**: Shopify UCP CLI @shopify/ucp-cli 0.9.1 (npm, 2026-10-12; MIT; github.com/Shopify/ucp-cli, 79 stars, last push 2026-10-12): 'npm install -g @shopify/ucp-cli' then 'ucp skills add' installs a SKILL.md; 'ucp catalog search' hits the global catalog by default; also cart, checkout and order commands. Shopify AI Toolkit (github.com/Shopify/Shopify-AI-Toolkit, MIT, 597 stars, last push 2026-10-14) is a Claude Code / Cursor / Codex plugin that ships the UCP skill.
- **raw http**: curl with a JSON-RPC body works (used for every test here), which allows jq filtering before anything enters Claude's context.
- **setup effort**: About 5-10 minutes: no account or key needed for testing; a free Dev Dashboard key for production-grade rate limits.

**protocol support**

UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) Catalog capability 2026-08-25 with its MCP binding; UCP Cart, Checkout and Order on merchant endpoints; HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421, ECDSA P-256) for the Signed tier; Shop sign-in for buyer identity linking. UCP spec repo github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp is Apache-2.0 (3,428 stars, last push 2026-10-15). Interoperability: any MCP client can call it; UCP is backed by Google and Shopify, which makes it the most future-proof discovery API in this group. No ACP endpoint here.

**open source and licence**

Service closed (Shopify-hosted). Open parts: UCP specification (Apache-2.0), @shopify/ucp-cli (MIT), Shopify AI Toolkit (MIT).

**account linking and data access**

Keyless use needs no account and no personal data; the agent profile is a public URL describing the agent, and profiles are unsigned ('whoever controls the advertised URL controls the agent's identity', ucp-cli README). Optional signals fields (dev.ucp.buyer_ip, dev.ucp.user_agent) should be left empty. Personalised search requires a buyer-linked token via Shop sign-in, which shares the buyer's identity with Shopify; Token-tier calls to merchant endpoints must send the buyer's IP in a Shopify-Buyer-IP header. Usage rules: images may only be shown with the merchant's listing and rendered in real time (not downloaded), and search results cannot be cached.

**automation legal risk**

Low. It is an official API for agents, used within its rules: respect the rate limit (5 requests per second per client; anonymous pool shared), do not cache results or images, and expect URLs to change ('API URLs are subject to change'). Keeping a dated personal audit note with a few fields (GID, seller, price, date) sits in a grey zone against the no-caching rule; storing raw responses or images would breach it. No anti-bot friction and no account-ban risk for keyless reads.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Ranking is Shopify's organic relevance ranking, unexplained. Paid placement: promoted placements (Developer Preview, invite-led) pay the integrating developer a base commission of 0.3% (30 bps) of attributed orders (last click, 7-day window), with optional extra merchant commission; promoted variants carry a placement object (type 'affiliate', commission percentage). They are returned only to approved callers using an affiliate-enabled saved catalog; keyless organic calls return only organic results. Structural bias: the universe is Shopify merchants only (DTC brand stores and resellers), excluding Allegro, Ceneo shops, Amazon and big-box retailers. Merchants are in the catalog by default if eligible and can opt out of catalog access (secondary sources), so coverage reflects merchant choices. Result URLs carry utm_source=shopify tracking.

**ranking transparency**

Low. No reason is given for an order; the profile, context and ships_to change both order and currency. Promoted items are machine-marked (placement object) and Shopify tells developers to label them, but organic results have no explanation. You can restrict to an allowlist of shops (filters.shops) but not exclude a shop; exclusion has to be done client-side.

**run to run consistency**

Own repeat test 2026-10-15: four identical searches ('garden trampoline 305 cm with safety net', ships_to PL, limit 20) within minutes returned the same 20 product IDs in the same order; total_count varied (384, 387, 381, 381) and one response was 197 KB versus 218 KB for the others, so contents can change slightly. It is a search index, not an LLM ranking, so shortlists are stable; changing country context changes the result set and currencies.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

No visible safeguards for buyers. Merchant-authored HTML descriptions flow into the agent's context, which is a prompt-injection channel; Shopify-inferred fields can be wrong (observed). Sellers of unclear identity appear beside brand stores with no trust signal: 'Shopyourproduct' (no company name or address in its shipping policy) listing several Salta models in PLN; 'obihirofurniture.com' selling a SONGMICS trampoline with a Polish title, priced in USD, from a furniture-named store. Agent profiles are unsigned in the keyless tier, so identity is weak. Safeguards to add: verify each seller (company data, registers, reviews) and the merchant page before trusting a price.

**known failures**

Observed 2026-10-15: inferred specs wrong (net thickness, rectangular vs round, wrong size list); UPID clustering did not merge the same model across merchants; ships_to PL let through Australian and other shops whose shipping to Poland is not stated; requested currency PLN ignored for many merchants; get_product returned a different size than the search hit; response is structuredContent only; payloads are large (about 200 KB per 20 results; the 'compact' view still 111 KB). Documentation drift: one Shopify page shows the endpoint as /api/mcp; the forum reports no UCP successor for the Storefront MCP 'search_shop_policies_and_faqs' tool before its 2026-08-31 sunset. Coverage gap: none of the main Polish retail channels are on Shopify.

**⚠ regulatory enforcement history**

No UOKiK, DSA or DMA action concerning Shopify Catalog found (searched 2026-10-15). Shopify faces a US privacy class action (Briskin v. Shopify) about tracking on merchant checkouts, unrelated to the catalog ⚠ *(unverified)* (not re-opened for this item).

**buyer protection path**

The purchase happens on the merchant's own Shopify checkout, and the merchant is the seller. For an EU merchant: EU 14-day withdrawal and 2-year legal guarantee under the merchant's national law, card chargeback, PayPal buyer protection if paid with PayPal; cross-border disputes via ECC-Net (Polish ECK). For non-EU merchants that slip through ships_to (Australia, US): customs duties, weaker enforcement and costly returns of bulky goods. Global Catalog adds no protection of its own.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Useful for one slice of the trampoline purchase: finding EU brand-store and reseller prices for premium models that Polish marketplaces stock thinly. Example from 2026-10-15 with ships_to PL: VirtuFit 305 cm with net at bieznie.pl PLN 1,299; Salta Premium Black Edition 305 at Azzura Pool EUR 499; BERG Champion InGround 330 at Intersport Elverys (Ireland) EUR 779; Hudora Fabulous 300 at Insplay.net EUR 331.90; Acon EU listing rated 4.9 from 337. It cannot cover the mainstream Polish market (Allegro, Decathlon, Media Expert, Leroy Merlin, Ceneo shops), give landed cost for a 50-80 kg parcel to Poland, confirm a shop actually ships to Poland, verify safety certificates, or rank offers by quality. Every candidate offer must be checked on the merchant page.

**workflow role**

Discovery and EU brand-store price points, plus raw spec text from merchant descriptions. Combine with: a browser agent (Claude in Chrome or browser-use) for Allegro, Ceneo and Polish retailers; independent tests and Safety Gate for product choice; seller registers for identity; the merchant's own shipping page for landed cost.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup: 5-10 minutes (curl or ucp CLI; optional free API key). Queries are free. Token arithmetic: a 20-result search returned about 200 KB of JSON (mostly HTML descriptions), roughly 50-60k tokens if passed raw into Claude ⚠ *(unverified: bytes-per-token ratio for mixed HTML)*. A trampoline comparison with 4 searches (generic Polish query, generic English query, two brand queries) at limit 10 would be about 400 KB, about 100k tokens raw, or a few thousand tokens if filtered with jq to title, seller, price, currency and URL first. Time: about 5 minutes. Under a Claude subscription no marginal cost; at API rates under USD 0.50 even unfiltered ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**evidence trail**

Machine-readable: product GID, variant GID, seller name and domain, price with currency, list price, merchant URL and checkout link. A vault record could read: 'query, ships_to, date, product GID, seller, price, currency, merchant URL, verified-on-merchant-page yes/no'. Constraint: the usage guidelines forbid caching search results and images, so keep only a minimal dated audit line, not raw responses or pictures.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Official, free and keyless: worked from Poland on 2026-10-15 with only Shopify's example agent profile; no anti-bot friction.
  - Covers Shopify-based Polish brand stores and EU brand stores that comparison sites and Allegro miss (bieznie.pl, Salta, BERG and North resellers).
  - Structured output with stable, repeatable rankings (same top 20 across four identical runs).
  - Clean Claude Code routes: remote MCP, official UCP CLI with a SKILL.md, Shopify AI Toolkit plugin.
  - Built on UCP, the Google-backed protocol that is the most future-proof agent-commerce discovery API.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, Decathlon, Leroy Merlin or Amazon: the core Polish channels are absent.
  - ships_to PL and UPID clustering did not work as documented in tests (Australian shops returned; same model under separate UPIDs).
  - Shopify-inferred specs contained clear errors (shape, sizes, material thickness).
  - No seller identity, safety, landed cost or price history; caching results is prohibited.
  - Large payloads (about 200 KB per 20 results) make raw MCP use token-expensive in Claude Code.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evaluation of Global Catalog result quality found. Coverage is Shopify's own documentation and announcements plus agency and vendor blogs (Weaverse, Digital Applied, eSEOspace, Remio, Tenten) that restate Shopify's claims; these are not evidence of quality. The main evidence here is the own probe of 2026-10-15 (about 14 search_catalog calls, 2 get_product calls and 1 lookup_catalog call).

**verdict for me**

PILOT - deciding fact: it works keyless from Poland and finds Shopify-based PL and EU brand-store offers, but ships_to PL and cross-merchant clustering did not hold in tests and the main Polish channels are not on Shopify. Best use: in a buying-research skill, one jq-filtered search per shortlisted model with ships_to PL to collect EU brand-store prices, then confirm shipping to Poland, freight cost and seller identity on each merchant page.

**conflicting evidence**

- Tools: the research outline lists search_catalog, lookup_catalog and update_cart; the live tools/list on 2026-10-15 returned search_catalog, lookup_catalog and get_product. Cart tools belong to the separate Cart MCP.
- Authentication: shopify.dev Catalog docs say 'Agent profile (no API key needed)'; the Spring '26 Edition says 'Catalog access takes just an API key, no approval needed'; the auth page says not to use unauthenticated requests for production. Live test: keyless calls work.
- Clustering: docs say global results are clustered by UPID with offers from multiple merchants; live tests returned one seller per product and the same model under different UPIDs.
- ships_to: the schema describes a shipping-destination filter; live results with ships_to PL included Australian shops and shops with no stated Polish shipping.
- Endpoint path: most Shopify pages use /api/ucp/mcp; one Shopify page shows https://catalog.shopify.com/api/mcp.
- Promoted placements request: a search summary of the docs mentions a catalog.placements ['affiliate'] parameter; the promoted-placement page describes an affiliate-enabled saved catalog passed via catalog_id.
- Approval gate: a third-party source in the outline says it was removed in June 2026; Shopify's own Spring '26 Edition post (2026-06-17) confirms it.

### SerpApi MCP

**Verdict:** PILOT · **Cost:** Free 250 searches a month; Starter USD 25 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

SerpApi is a commercial search-results scraping API (role: data API + official MCP server + official agent skill). Two engines matter for shopping: google_shopping (one request returns the first page of the Google Shopping vertical, about 40 products, with title, price, source shop, rating, reviews, delivery, product_id and an immersive_product_page_token; the start parameter is ignored, so there is no deeper pagination) and google_immersive_product (the product pop-up: up to 13 stores with more_stores=true, each with price, original price, discount, shipping, total, tag, stock and payment methods, plus price_range, about_the_product features, top_insights, star breakdown, user_reviews, videos, forum threads and more_options). The hosted MCP server at https://mcp.serpapi.com/mcp (serpapi/serpapi-mcp v2.0.0, 2026-09-22) exposes one 'search' tool that can call every SerpApi engine, plus two opt-in UI tools. The older google_product engine is dead: Google removed the product page in 2025 and SerpApi now returns an error for it.

**vendor and ownership**

SerpApi, LLC, Austin, Texas, US; founder and CEO Julien Khaleghy; founded 2017; bootstrapped and profitable with about 35 staff (Sacra estimate, not audited). Terms governed by Texas law. Independent of Google (Google is suing it) and of any retailer or marketplace, so ownership adds no shop bias; the bias it carries is Google's.

**lifecycle status**

Active; verified 2026-10-15. API in service since 2017. MCP repo created 2025-03-04; v1.0.3 on 2026-09-09; v2.0.0 on 2026-09-22 (FastMCP upgrade, guided search inputs, MCP Bundle for Claude Desktop, directory readiness); last commit 2026-10-12; OAuth support is an open PR (#73, 2026-09-18). Engine changes: Google discontinued the Google Product endpoint (SerpApi changelog, September 2025), replaced by the Immersive Product API; more_stores added 2025-10-03. Google Shopping API release notes for 2026 are mostly fixes: intermittent empty results (2026-03-06, 03-16, 08-17), wrong rating (03-17), min_price bug (03-13), inconsistent results on repeated tries (06-04), localisation discrepancies (08-17), performance degradation (09-22), intermittent zero results (09-25), safe=off support (09-28). Immersive Product API notes: timeouts (2026-01-27), no results (05-14), downtime (05-16), malformed product_results (10-01), missing tax (10-13). Context: in mid-September 2026 Google removed free product carousels and the Shopping tab link from EEA search under the DMA, but the Shopping vertical itself (udm=28) still returned a full Polish product grid in this research's browser on 2026-10-15. Primary sources: serpapi.com pricing, docs, release notes, GitHub repo.

**⚠ cost model**

Subscription with a free tier, billed per successful search (USD, serpapi.com/pricing, seen 2026-10-15): Free USD 0 = 250 searches/month at 50/hour; Starter USD 25 = 1,000 (200/hour); Developer USD 75 = 5,000 (1,000/hour); Production USD 150 = 15,000 (3,000/hour, adds U.S. Legal Shield); Big Data USD 275 = 30,000; Searcher USD 725 = 100,000; larger Cloud plans from USD 3,750 for 1,000,000. Only successful searches count; cached (1-hour cache, identical parameters), errored and failed searches are free; empty results still count as one search. Every engine call is one search: a google_shopping query, each immersive product page, and each next page of stores. Monthly plans, no pay-as-you-go; full refund within 7 days unless more than 20% of searches are used. Optional speed modes cost 2x or 4x. The MCP server and skill are free; MCP searches use the same account quota ⚠ *(unverified: the MCP page says searches use your subscription but does not state per-call billing explicitly)*.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **poland google shopping via api**: Supported: 'pl' is on SerpApi's list of 74 Google Shopping countries (google-shopping-countries.json downloaded 2026-10-15). Use gl=pl, hl=pl and a Polish location; the docs warn that without 'location' the search may take the proxy's location. SerpApi's own output for Poland was not tested here (no API key).
- **poland google shopping vertical live**: Yes on 2026-10-15: google.pl/search?udm=28&hl=pl&gl=pl for 'trampolina ogrodowa 305 cm z siatką' showed a 'Produkty Sponsorowane' block and an organic grid of Polish shops in PLN with Polish labels, in this research's browser.
- **eea dma change**: EEA (incl. PL): free product carousels in general search and the Shopping tab link were removed in mid-September 2026; secondary sources and the browser test agree the Shopping vertical stays reachable by URL, which is what the google_shopping engine queries ⚠ *(unverified: SerpApi has published nothing on EEA behaviour)*.
- **price insights in poland**: Google UI in PL shows 'Statystyki dotyczące cen' with a typical price range and a 'Historia cen' table of daily prices for about 12 months in the immersive panel (observed 2026-10-15). Not in SerpApi's documented Immersive Product response ⚠ *(unverified: whether it is returned)*.
- **google track price alerts**: US, CA, AU, JP, IN only (Google help page, per earlier batch); not available in PL and not exposed by SerpApi.
- **agentic checkout**: None. Google's 'Buy for me' is US-only and SerpApi only reads results.
- **eu other countries**: de, fr, it, es, nl, at, cz, sk and more are supported as separate gl values; results are not merged across countries.
- **language**: Docs and MCP in English; result text follows hl (Polish titles, 'zł' prices, 'Dni na zwrot' labels).
- **legal shield scope**: U.S. Legal Shield covers only claims under US law in US courts; no EU equivalent.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. Google clusters offers for the same product across shops, and the immersive page returns that cluster (observed: one Virtufit Premium 305 cm trampoline grouped across Decathlon at 985 PLN and Allegro, Sk-Sport and bieznie.pl at 1,599-1,699 PLN). about_the_product.features gives a key-value spec list and more_options lists near-equivalent products with prices, which helps with the cheaper/pricier sibling question; release notes show variation handling (variant titles, serpapi_link for variations). It does not normalise specs across makers, does not return EAN/GTIN in the documented fields, and does not detect white-label rebadges (the PL grid showed the same 'Ø305 cm, TUV SUD' trampoline under several shop titles and brands). Shop titles mix 305 and 312 cm sizes for 10 ft models, so variant matching still needs a human or a spec-normalising prompt.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Yes, across every shop that feeds Google Merchant Center. Observed in the PL Shopping vertical on 2026-10-15 for the trampoline query: Allegro (several offers), Decathlon, Media Expert, Castorama, Empik, ERLI, Kaufland.pl, Lidl Sklep Online, Sportano, Jula, Ceneo.pl as a listed source, the BERG brand store, 4fizjo, meteor.pl, inSPORTline, Makstor, Mamabrum, Tantis, Trampoliny.pl and others - over 20 Polish sellers on one page. Shops without a Merchant Center feed are missing, and only the first ~40 results per query are returned, so several query variants are needed. Immersive pages cap at 13 stores per product. No published shop count for Poland; vendor numbers are Google's (Shopping Graph 50B+ listings, vendor-claimed). EU shops such as Amazon.de or idealo-listed stores need separate gl=de queries.

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

Partial and mostly indirect. The PL Shopping grid shows 'WYPRZEDAŻ' with a strikethrough price, a 'Najtaniej (30 dni)' badge (lowest price in 30 days) and 'NISKA CENA ... Zwykle X zł' (typical price); SerpApi's release notes include 'Scrape 30-day low label' (2024-03-21) and old_price/second-hand fields (2023), and immersive stores carry original_price, extracted_original_price and discount. The 12-month 'Historia cen' table visible in the Polish immersive panel is not among the documented response keys (price_insights/price_history absent from the sample) ⚠ *(unverified)*. So the API can flag 'on sale vs Google's 30-day low' where Google shows it, but cannot by itself prove an Omnibus breach; for history use Ceneo, or store your own dated SerpApi snapshots (SerpApi keeps searches only 31 days).

**total landed cost**

Partial. Each immersive store row has shipping, total/extracted_total and (since 2026-10-13) tax, plus payment methods and stock; the PL grid also shows return windows ('Dni na zwrot: 14' or 30) and shipping surcharges, which matter for bulky goods (observed: one Decathlon trampoline offer +250 PLN shipping, Makstor +180 PLN, Najtanszy-SPORT +199 PLN). Not covered: return shipping cost, assembly, payment fees, cross-border warranty enforceability.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. Product rating, review count, star breakdown and review text (user_reviews with source and date), store rating and review counts per store, and an 'incentivized review' label (added 2025-10-22). No review-authenticity analysis and no seller identity check (CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list, VIES). It cannot prove that a shop is a registered business or that its ratings are genuine.

**safety and compliance checks**

None automatic. The same MCP 'search' tool can run plain Google web queries (e.g. Safety Gate or Certipedia look-ups by brand and model), but nothing checks GPSR fields, EN 71-14 edition or certificates. Shop titles carrying claims such as 'Certyfikat TUV SUD' come through unverified.

**independent test coverage**

Not a test source. Immersive top_insights (snippets from third-party articles) and discussions_and_forums may surface test or forum pages, and a separate Google web query can find test.de or Which? pages, but nothing is systematic or dated against the model year.

**alerts and monitoring**

None built in. Monitoring means re-running queries on a schedule (cron or a Claude Code scheduled task), each run costing searches; responses can be diffed for price drops. Google's own 'Track price' alerts are unavailable in Poland. No webhook; cannot watch an arbitrary Polish shop page except as it appears in Google Shopping.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. It only reads results; product and store links send the buyer to the merchant, who handles checkout.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: used offers appear with a condition label ('Używany', second_hand_condition field), and spare parts (nets, pads, springs) can be priced with separate queries. No service network, warranty handling or OLX/Allegro Lokalnie resale data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

SerpApi fetches Google results live through its own proxy and browser fleet at request time, unless an identical query in the last hour is served from cache (no_cache=true forces a fresh fetch). Google Shopping data come from merchant feeds (Merchant Center) and crawled product markup; freshness is Google's. Each response carries search_metadata (id, created_at, json_endpoint, raw_html_file, the Google URL) and every result links to the merchant offer, so each answer is backed by a link and an archived raw HTML copy kept 31 days. Reported lags and glitches are the empty-result and localisation fixes listed in the release notes.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full (paid, with a 250-search free tier)
- **official api**: REST: https://serpapi.com/search?engine=google_shopping&q=...&gl=pl&hl=pl&location=Poland&api_key=KEY, then engine=google_immersive_product&page_token=TOKEN&more_stores=true (next_page_token for more stores). Filters: min_price, max_price, sort_by (1 price ascending, 2 descending), on_sale, free_shipping, small_business, shoprs filter tokens. output=json|html|md, json_restrictor to trim fields, async plus Searches Archive API. Rate limit = plan throughput per hour. Docs: https://serpapi.com/google-shopping-api and https://serpapi.com/google-immersive-product-api. Official SDKs for Python, JavaScript, Ruby and others.
- **official mcp server**: Hosted Streamable-HTTP server https://mcp.serpapi.com/mcp (also self-hostable with uv or Docker, or as a local .mcpb bundle). Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http serpapi https://mcp.serpapi.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SERPAPI_API_KEY" (a key-in-path URL also works but leaks into logs). Tools: 'search' (any engine via params.engine, mode complete/compact, output md said to cut tokens by about 50% on average), 'search_table' and 'search_dashboard' (MCP Apps UI, ignored by hosts without MCP Apps). Resources serpapi://engines/<engine> expose parameter schemas, including google_shopping, google_shopping_filters, google_shopping_light, google_immersive_product, amazon, ebay, walmart and bing_shopping. Missing required parameters trigger a form in MCP 2026-07-28 clients or an error listing them. Repo github.com/serpapi/serpapi-mcp: MIT, 180 stars, 43 forks, 8 open issues and PRs, last commit 2026-10-12. Remote; no local install needed.
- **official skill**: github.com/serpapi/skills (MIT, 10 stars, last push 2026-07-09): 'serpapi-web-search' SKILL.md with engine, parameter and response rules for coding agents.
- **browser agent and fallback**: Not needed: the Google Shopping vertical can also be read manually (google.pl/search?udm=28) or by a browser agent in the user's own session, but Google's anti-bot checks make that brittle; SerpApi is the robust route.
- **setup effort**: About 10 minutes: create an account, copy the key, run one claude mcp add command. Keep the key out of the repository (it sits in the user-level Claude config).

**protocol support**

MCP only (official hosted server, MCP 2026-07-28 form elicitation supported). No ACP, UCP, AP2 or Web Bot Auth, which is expected for a read-only data API.

**open source and licence**

API: closed SaaS. MCP server: open source, MIT (github.com/serpapi/serpapi-mcp, 180 stars, active, releases v1.0.3 and v2.0.0 in September 2026). Skill: MIT (github.com/serpapi/skills, 10 stars).

**account linking and data access**

Needs only a SerpApi account and API key (card for paid plans). No Google account, shop account or payment credentials. Queries, parameters and results are retained 31 days after each search (privacy policy); ZeroTrace (no retention) only on enterprise/cloud plans. International transfers rely on adequacy decisions or EU Standard Contractual Clauses; a DPA is available on request; Texas law governs. Shopping queries carry no personal data, so GDPR exposure is low.

**automation legal risk**

Google's terms forbid automated querying; SerpApi carries the scraping and says it 'assumes liability for the lawful collection of public search data' (terms, updated 2026-08-27). Google LLC sued SerpApi under the DMCA on 2025-12-19; Judge Gonzalez Rogers dismissed it on 2026-07-20 (public search results are not copyrighted); Google filed an amended complaint on 2026-08-10 that drops the Google Shopping and Maps theories and narrows the case to licensed Knowledge Panel images; SerpApi moved to dismiss on 2026-08-25 (pending as of 2026-10-15). Reddit also sued SerpApi in October 2025. For an end user the realistic risk is service disruption if Google tightens SearchGuard, not an account ban (no Google account is used). The Legal Shield covers only US claims. Personal, low-volume research use in Poland carries low risk.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

SerpApi earns only subscriptions: no affiliate links, ads or paid placement of its own. Bias is inherited from Google: a 'Produkty Sponsorowane' block of paid Shopping ads sits above the organic grid on google.pl (observed), Google decides organic order, shops without Merchant Center feeds are invisible, and Google has two EU self-preferencing findings (2017 Shopping decision, 2026 DMA decision). Whether SerpApi's JSON keeps sponsored items in a separate key or marks them was not confirmed from the docs ⚠ *(unverified)*; check for an ads/inline block before ranking.

**⚠ ranking transparency**

Low for 'why', good for reproducibility. Results come with Google's position but no explanation. You can rerun with filters (price range, on sale, free shipping, sort by price) and drop sources client-side, which gives full control over exclusions. Sponsored marking depends on how SerpApi parses the ad block ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**run to run consistency**

Not an LLM, so no sampling variance; a repeat within one hour is served from cache and is identical. SerpApi's own release notes record 'The same search is returning many or no results on repeated tries' (fixed 2026-06-04) and several intermittent empty-result fixes in 2026, so a run that returns nothing should be retried with no_cache. No own repeat test was possible without a key.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Returns raw merchant and user text (titles, descriptions, review text, forum snippets) into the agent's context, so prompt injection via product data is possible; the MCP server does not document marking output as untrusted ⚠ *(unverified)*. Google Merchant Center policies remove some scam merchants, but fake shops can still buy Shopping ads. Seller claims in titles (certificates, load limits) are not verified.

**known failures**

Only the first ~40 results per query (start ignored, num has no effect); immersive page tokens expire (scrape.do, 2026-08-03); immersive stores default to 3-5, up to 13; google_product engine shut down; 2026 incidents listed under lifecycle (empty results, timeouts, downtime, localisation discrepancies, wrong ratings, min_price bug). Users on Capterra and GetApp mainly complain about price per search and monthly plans with no pay-as-you-go; one aggregator notes confusion about empty results counting. In Parallel.ai's July 2026 agent web-search benchmark (a competitor's test, different task) SerpApi had the slowest p50 latency (999 ms) and 23.3% accuracy. No Poland-specific failure reports found.

**regulatory enforcement history**

No regulator action found. Litigation: Google LLC v. SerpApi LLC (N.D. Cal., filed 2025-12-19, dismissed 2026-07-20, amended 2026-08-10, motion to dismiss filed 2026-08-25); Reddit v. SerpApi (filed October 2025, motion to dismiss filed). No UOKiK, DSA or DMA decisions against SerpApi.

**buyer protection path**

None from SerpApi or Google. The purchase happens at the merchant: Polish statutory rights (14-day withdrawal for distance purchases, 2-year conformity liability), Allegro Protect when the offer is on Allegro, card chargeback or PayPal protection by payment method, and ECC Poland for cross-border EU shops found via other gl values.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Good for the 'where to buy and at what spread' step. For the trampoline: one google_shopping call with gl=pl, hl=pl, location=Poland for 'trampolina ogrodowa 305 cm z siatką' returns about 40 offers from 20+ Polish shops including Allegro, Decathlon, Media Expert, Castorama and Lidl, with price, shipping surcharge, return window and 30-day-low badges; immersive calls for 3-6 shortlisted models then give up to 13 stores each with totals, ratings and review text, exposing spreads such as 985 vs 1,699 PLN for the same model. It cannot check Safety Gate, EN 71-14 claims, spare-part availability or seller identity, and the documented API gives no price history even though Google shows it in Poland.

**workflow role**

Price and place-to-buy scan (plus a first candidate list from the Shopping grid). Combine with Ceneo for price history and Omnibus checks, Keepa for Amazon.de history, Safety Gate and the GPSR listing check for safety, seller registers for identity, and Stiftung Warentest/VKI for lab results.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Setup about 10 minutes. One trampoline run = 3 google_shopping queries (generic plus two model-specific) + 6 immersive product calls with more_stores + 2 next-page store calls = 11 searches. Free tier: 250/month covers about 22 such runs (USD 0). Starter: 11 x USD 0.025 = USD 0.28. Developer: 11 x USD 0.015 = USD 0.17. Plus Claude tokens to read the JSON, roughly 30-80k per run ⚠ *(unverified)*; output=md or json_restrictor reduces this. Repeats within an hour are free (cache).

**evidence trail**

Good. Every response has a search id, timestamp, the exact parameters, the Google URL and an archived raw HTML file (kept 31 days, so save it locally). A vault note can hold a table per run: query, gl/hl/location, timestamp, product, store, price, shipping, total, return window, 30-day-low or sale badge, link, SerpApi search id, with the raw JSON saved next to the note.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Poland supported (gl=pl on the 74-country list) and the Google Shopping vertical still lists 20+ Polish shops, Allegro included, on 2026-10-15.
  - Official hosted MCP server (one claude mcp add command, MIT source, active September-October 2026) plus an official skill.
  - Immersive product data: up to 13 stores with shipping, totals, return windows, ratings and review text per product.
  - Free 250 searches/month covers about 20 product comparisons; cached repeats are free.
  - Timestamped, archived responses give a clean audit trail for vault notes.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Only the first ~40 results per query and 13 stores per product; shops without Merchant Center feeds are invisible.
  - Price history visible in the Polish Google UI is not in the documented API response.
  - Inherits Google's sponsored block and ranking; sponsored marking in the JSON not confirmed.
  - Frequent upstream glitches in 2026 (empty results, timeouts, localisation discrepancies).
  - Legal dependency on an ongoing Google lawsuit, and no safety, seller-identity or landed-cost checks.

**independent review consensus**

No independent test of SerpApi with Polish Google Shopping exists. Scrape.do's 2026-08-03 comparison (a competitor; disclosed authorship) found 100% success, 0.7 s average response (helped by caching) and correct filters across 15 passes, and confirmed the google_product shutdown and the 13-store cap. GetApp and Capterra user reviews (unverified testimonials) say Shopping results match what users see on desktop and mobile, and criticise price. AIMultiple's July 2026 SERP API benchmark (18,000 requests) exists but its SerpApi figures could not be read. Parallel.ai's benchmark is a competitor test of a different task.

**verdict for me**

PILOT - deciding fact: the Google Shopping vertical still lists 20+ Polish shops (Allegro, Decathlon, Media Expert, Castorama, Lidl) on 2026-10-15 and SerpApi's free 250 searches/month cover about 20 runs. Best use: add the hosted MCP to Claude Code, run google_shopping plus google_immersive_product with gl=pl, hl=pl, location=Poland for the shortlisted models, and save the timestamped JSON and a price table to the vault; take history and Omnibus checks from Ceneo.

**conflicting evidence**

- EEA Shopping after the DMA change: several outlets describe all organic Shopping results as removed from EEA search in September 2026, while Productrise (citing Paul Schreiner) and this research's browser test on 2026-10-15 show the Shopping vertical (udm=28) still returns a full grid in Poland.
- Price insights in Poland: the earlier Google Shopping item in this workspace recorded price history as 'not confirmed for PL'; on 2026-10-15 the Polish immersive panel showed 'Statystyki dotyczące cen' and a 12-month 'Historia cen' table.
- Number of stores: SerpApi's Immersive Product docs say 3-5 by default and up to 13 with more_stores; SerpApi's October 2025 tutorial says more_stores collects all available online sellers.
- Enterprise pricing: Sacra says enterprise packages start at USD 3,750/month for 100,000 searches; serpapi.com/pricing lists USD 3,750 for 1,000,000 searches (Cloud 1M) and USD 725 for 100,000 (Searcher).
- Status of Google v. SerpApi: some coverage reports the suit as 'tossed' (July 2026); SerpApi's own blog and Search Engine Journal report an amended complaint (2026-08-10) and a second motion to dismiss (2026-08-25), so the case is still open.

### Keepa MCP servers

**Verdict:** SKIP the community servers · **Cost:** Servers free; Keepa API from EUR 49 a month · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Three unofficial, open-source MCP servers that wrap the paid Keepa API so an agent can read decoded Amazon price and sales-rank histories (role: MCP server for a price tracker's data). Compared against Keepa's own hosted MCP server at https://keepa.com/mcp, which uses the same API plan.
- **purahmanian keepa mcp**: npm package keepa-mcp 0.1.2 (TypeScript, stdio via npx). Six tools: get_product, get_price_history, get_sales_rank_history, search_products, get_best_sellers, get_deals.
- **bwb03 keepa adapter**: keepa-adapter (TypeScript, stdio, built from source or installed as a Claude Desktop .mcpb bundle; also an 'OpenClaw skill' library). 33 tools: product, price history, buy box, variations, token check, local SQLite snapshots with change detection, BSR trends, sales history, deals/coupons, seller stats, best sellers, categories, Product Finder, seller finder, lightning deals, graph images, Keepa-hosted trackings and webhooks, promo-impact analysis.
- **cosjef keepa mcp**: keepa_MCP (TypeScript, stdio, built from source). Eleven tools aimed at Amazon sellers: product lookup, batch lookup, price history, product finder, category analysis, deal search, best sellers, sales velocity, inventory analysis, seller lookup, token status.
- **official baseline**: Keepa GmbH's hosted Streamable-HTTP MCP server https://keepa.com/mcp: product lookups with stats and Buy Box, decoded price histories, charts, Amazon search, Product Finder, price drops and Lightning Deals, best sellers, seller and storefront inspection, trackings with notifications.

**vendor and ownership**

All three community servers are individual side projects with no funding and no affiliation with Keepa GmbH: keepa-mcp by Puya Rahmanian (GitHub purahmanian; the README states it is unofficial and not endorsed by Keepa), keepa-adapter by Brett Bohannon (GitHub BWB03, Bend, Oregon), keepa_MCP by Jeffrey Costa (GitHub cosjef, Atlanta; works at Entrust). The data owner is Keepa GmbH, Kemnath, Germany, which also runs the official MCP server. None is owned by Amazon or a retailer.

**⚠ lifecycle status**

- **keepa mcp**: Created 2026-06-05; last commit 2026-08-09 (fixes reading current data from stats/csv and stops forcing a live offer fetch); npm 0.1.2 published 2026-08-09; 269 downloads in the 30 days to 2026-10-12; 0 stars; listed in the MCP registry. Early but maintained.
- **keepa adapter**: Created 2026-03-20; last commit 2026-09-14 (configurable seller-stats window); 16 stars, 3 forks, 0 open issues; GitHub releases v1.0.1 (2026-05-05) to v1.1.1 (2026-05-08), while the README already refers to a v1.2.0 bundle. Active.
- **keepa MCP cosjef**: Created 2025-08-02; last code commit 2025-08-08; 36 stars, 10 forks; 5 open dependabot PRs left unmerged (MCP SDK 0.5.0 to 1.25.2, axios 1.11.0 to 1.13.5, js-yaml). Unmaintained.
- **official**: Live on 2026-10-15 (keepa.com/api-docs/mcp.html and the API landing page); launch date not published and the API changelog has no MCP entry ⚠ *(unverified)*. Keepa API changelog latest entry 2026-10-08; breaking changes on 2026-02-23 (Offer isScam and Seller isScammer removed; NEW/USED series switched to landed price) and fields scheduled for removal from 2026-04-20, which community servers must track - cosjef's code still references isScammer.
- **verified**: 2026-10-15 via GitHub API, npm registry and keepa.com.

**cost model**

The servers are free (MIT). Every route needs a paid Keepa API plan: 'Monthly, from EUR 49. Every plan has every endpoint', 'For commercial and professional use' (keepa.com/#!api, seen 2026-10-15); the entry plan gives 20 tokens per minute (earlier batch, same page). The official MCP connector is included in the same plan ('One API plan runs both') and tool calls cost the same tokens as API calls. Token use per call: keepa-mcp README estimates 2-4 tokens per product or history lookup, 50-100 for best-seller lists, 5-25 per deals page; live offers add 10+ tokens. Prepaid monthly by card, no free API tier on keepa.com.

**feature geo matrix**

- **marketplaces keepa**: 11 Amazon marketplaces: US, UK, DE, FR, JP, CA, IT, ES, IN, MX, BR (keepa.com, 2026-10-15). Amazon.pl, .nl, .se and .be are not covered.
- **keepa mcp**: Domain ids 1-10 documented in the tool schema (US, UK, DE, FR, JP, CA, IT, ES, IN); default amazon.com; no MX or BR.
- **keepa adapter**: com, uk, de, fr, jp, ca, it, es, in, mx, br (BR on a subset of endpoints); default com, configurable via KEEPA_DEFAULT_DOMAIN.
- **keepa MCP cosjef**: Enum US, UK, DE, FR, JP, CA, CN (a marketplace Keepa no longer lists), IT, ES, IN, MX.
- **poland**: Usable from Poland only for Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es purchases; nothing for Amazon.pl, Allegro or Polish shops.
- **language**: English tool descriptions and output; product titles in the marketplace language.
- **us only features**: None of the servers has US-only features; Keepa features are the same across its marketplaces.

#### capabilities

**⚠ spec and variant comparison**

Partial, Amazon only. keepa-adapter has keepa_get_variations and keepa_check_variations (parent/child family, attribute drift) and returns features and variations per ASIN; keepa-mcp returns title, brand and category only; cosjef returns basic product attributes (model, colour, size). No cross-maker spec comparison. The Keepa API can resolve an EAN/UPC to ASINs (cosjef types include a 'code' parameter) ⚠ *(unverified: whether each server exposes it)*, but nothing maps one product across other shops or regional names.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Amazon only, one marketplace per call; you can query DE, FR, IT and ES separately for the same ASIN. No Polish shops, no Allegro, no Ceneo shops, no Amazon.pl. Keepa's vendor-claimed counter shows 7,913,357,013 products tracked (keepa.com, 2026-10-15).

**⚠ price history and omnibus**

This is their core use. All three decode Keepa's price series (Amazon, new, used, buy box; keepa-adapter adds list price, lightning deal, FBA/FBM and coupon/deal history). keepa-mcp downsamples each series to at most 60 points and defaults to a 90-day stats window, which can hide short dips. None documents Keepa's 'savingBasis' strikethrough reference price (added 2026-08-25) ⚠ *(unverified)*, so the Omnibus test (was the 'was' price the 30-day low?) must be derived from the history by the agent. The official server 'walks decoded price histories' with Keepa's stats and is the most likely to expose new fields first.

**total landed cost**

Partial: since 2026-02-23 Keepa's NEW/USED series are landed prices (item plus shipping) within the marketplace's country, and the buy-box series carries shipping. Nothing on delivery to Poland, return shipping, assembly or warranty.

**review and seller verification**

Partial for Amazon sellers only: rating and review-count history (all three), buy-box ownership and seller stats (keepa-adapter), seller lookup (cosjef, official). No review-authenticity analysis (Keepa removed its isScam/isScammer flags on 2026-02-23) and no CEIDG/KRS/VIES checks.

**safety and compliance checks**

N/A - none of them checks Safety Gate, GPSR fields, standards or certificates.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - no lab-test data.

**alerts and monitoring**

keepa-adapter: Keepa-hosted trackings with webhook configuration (keepa_add_api_trackings, keepa_set_tracking_webhook, keepa_get_tracking_notifications) plus local snapshots compared on a cron schedule with severity levels. Official server: trackings with notifications. keepa-mcp: deals lookup only, no alerts. cosjef: none. Keepa refreshes tracked items about hourly. None can watch a Polish shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. None of them can buy; links lead to Amazon.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: the used and warehouse price lines are a weak proxy for resale value on Amazon; no spare parts, service or OLX/Allegro Lokalnie data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

All three call api.keepa.com with the user's key; Keepa's data come from its own crawl of Amazon with timestamped history back to 2011 and roughly hourly refresh for tracked items. Outputs are JSON with timestamps; keepa-mcp caps responses at 25,000 characters; keepa-adapter stores snapshots in a local SQLite file and can export raw JSON/CSV. No snapshots of the Amazon page itself; Keepa's graph-image endpoint (official server and keepa-adapter) can render a chart.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full (paid Keepa API required for every route)
- **official keepa mcp**: Remote Streamable HTTP, no install. Claude Code with OAuth: claude mcp add --transport http keepa https://keepa.com/mcp, then /mcp and Authenticate (no key in config); or add --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY". Each tool description states its token cost and each response returns the token balance. Connected apps can be revoked on the API page. Maintained by Keepa. Docs: https://keepa.com/api-docs/mcp.html.
- **keepa mcp purahmanian**: Local stdio: claude mcp add keepa -e KEEPA_API_KEY=your_key -- npx -y keepa-mcp. Six tools; unit tests use mocked HTTP; published to npm and the MCP registry via GitHub OIDC. Repo github.com/purahmanian/keepa-mcp, MIT, 0 stars, last commit 2026-08-09.
- **keepa adapter bwb03**: Local stdio from a source build (git clone, npm install, node dist/index.js with KEEPA_API_KEY) or a .mcpb bundle for Claude Desktop; 33 tools including writes to the Keepa account (trackings, webhook). Repo github.com/BWB03/keepa-adapter, MIT, 16 stars, last commit 2026-09-14.
- **keepa MCP cosjef**: Local stdio from a source build; 11 seller-analytics tools; outdated dependencies. Repo github.com/cosjef/keepa_MCP, MIT, 36 stars, last code commit 2025-08-08.
- **skill cli browser**: No Claude skill found for any of them; keepa-adapter ships an 'OpenClaw skill' TypeScript class. Keepa's official Java client and the community Python 'keepa' package are alternatives. Browser fallback: the free Keepa extension on Amazon pages.
- **setup effort**: Official: 2-5 minutes plus subscription. keepa-mcp: 2 minutes. keepa-adapter: 10-15 minutes (build). cosjef: 15 minutes plus a dependency audit.

**protocol support**

MCP only (stdio for the community servers, Streamable HTTP with OAuth for the official one). No ACP, UCP or AP2.

**open source and licence**

keepa-mcp: MIT, 0 stars, 1 open issue, maintained (Aug 2026). keepa-adapter: MIT, 16 stars, 0 open issues, maintained (Sep 2026). keepa_MCP (cosjef): MIT, 36 stars, 5 open dependabot PRs, unmaintained since Aug 2025. The official Keepa MCP server is closed (hosted); the Keepa API is proprietary.

**account linking and data access**

All routes need a Keepa API key tied to a paid account (card via Stripe). Community servers keep the key as a plain environment variable in the local MCP config, and 'npx -y keepa-mcp' pulls the latest unpinned package at each start (supply-chain exposure; pin a version). keepa-adapter writes a local SQLite database (~/.keepa-adapter/keepa.db) and its tracking tools change the Keepa account. The official server supports OAuth, so no key sits in config, and access can be revoked. Data sent: ASINs and search terms only; Keepa GmbH is a German company under GDPR. No Amazon login or payment data.

**automation legal risk**

Low. All servers use the official API, which Keepa sells for this purpose; Keepa's T&C (version 2026-10-07, earlier batch) forbid scraping keepa.com and reselling data, not API clients. Keepa offers the API 'for commercial and professional use', so purely private shopping use is a grey zone; a sole trader buying for business qualifies. Keepa warns that keys must not be committed to shared repositories. Amazon is not involved because no Amazon pages are scraped.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Community servers earn nothing directly; keepa-mcp's README wraps the Keepa sign-up link in an 'AFFILIATE' comment marker, though the link is currently plain ⚠ *(unverified: whether an affiliate link is planned)*. Keepa earns subscriptions. The data are observational price series, so bias is minimal; cosjef adds opaque seller-oriented 'opportunity scores'.

**ranking transparency**

N/A for keepa-mcp and keepa-adapter (raw series and stats). cosjef's opportunity and profit scores are heuristics that are not explained in the output.

**run to run consistency**

N/A - deterministic data tools; repeated calls return the same history, while current prices move with Amazon.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Not agents, but they pass merchant-written titles and feature bullets into the model's context, which is an injection surface; none of the community servers marks output as untrusted ⚠ *(unverified)*. Price history is itself a defence against inflated 'was' prices.

**⚠ known failures**

keepa-mcp: versions before 0.1.2 always requested 20 live offers, so calls cost 10+ tokens and could fail on small token buckets, and current prices were read from the wrong place until the 2026-08-09 fix; its README claims a free 100 tokens/min tier that Keepa does not offer (issue #1, 2026-07-28: a user could not find it). keepa-adapter: README clone URL points to a placeholder org, it assumes a 5 tokens/min plan by default, and it labels prices as dollars whatever the marketplace currency ⚠ *(unverified)*. cosjef: unmerged security bumps, a CN domain, removed Keepa fields (isScammer) still in its types, and an open issue that some ASINs cannot be retrieved. All: no Amazon.pl.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - no regulator or court action involving these projects or Keepa GmbH found (searched 2026-10-15).

**buyer protection path**

Purchases happen on Amazon: Amazon as merchant of record for 'sold by Amazon', A-to-z Guarantee for marketplace sellers, 2-year statutory warranty, 14-day EU withdrawal, card chargeback, ECC Poland for cross-border disputes with Amazon.de/.fr/.it/.es. The servers carry no liability.

#### fit for user

**⚠ fit for big ticket durables**

Narrow. For the trampoline, only useful if a shortlisted model (e.g. a Berg or Hudora 305) is sold on Amazon.de and ships to Poland; then a call such as get_price_history for its ASIN on domain 3 shows whether today's price is near the 90-day or 365-day low. Bulky 3 m trampolines often do not ship from Amazon.de to Poland ⚠ *(unverified)*, and none of the servers helps with Allegro, Polish shops or Amazon.pl.

**workflow role**

Price-history check for Amazon EU marketplaces only. Combine with SerpApi Google Shopping or Ceneo for Polish shops, and with safety and seller checks.

**effort and cost per purchase**

Fixed cost dominates: EUR 49 for a month of the Keepa API (cancellable). Arithmetic for 10 candidate ASINs on Amazon.de with keepa-mcp: 10 x get_product (~3 tokens) + 10 x get_price_history (~3 tokens) = ~60 tokens; the 20 tokens/min plan refills that in 3 minutes, so the marginal cost is near zero and the whole run costs the EUR 49 month. Free alternative: the Keepa browser extension, about 2 minutes per ASIN, EUR 0.

**evidence trail**

Good: timestamped JSON series and stats per ASIN; keepa-adapter adds local SQLite snapshots and raw JSON/CSV exports, and it and the official server can render Keepa chart images. A vault note can store ASIN, marketplace, date, current price, 30-day and 90-day minimum, average, and the chart image.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Decoded Amazon price histories back to 2011 inside Claude Code (all three).
  - keepa-adapter covers the whole Keepa endpoint index, with local snapshots, change detection and webhook trackings.
  - keepa-mcp installs in one command and is maintained (fix released 2026-08-09).
  - All MIT-licensed and use the official API, so legal risk is low.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Each needs the same EUR 49/month Keepa API plan that already includes the official hosted MCP server with OAuth.
  - No Amazon.pl, no Polish shops (Keepa covers 11 marketplaces).
  - Community servers store the key in plain config; cosjef's is unmaintained with stale dependencies and removed API fields.
  - keepa-mcp downsamples history to 60 points and misstates Keepa's free tier.
  - Tiny user bases (0-36 stars) and no independent reviews.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found. Only directory listings (Glama, LobeHub, claudemarketplaces.com, getdrio, socket.dev) that repeat the READMEs; no hands-on reviews or tests of any of the three servers or of the official Keepa MCP.

**verdict for me**

SKIP the community servers (WATCH keepa-adapter only if you build Amazon-seller tooling) - deciding fact: they need the same paid Keepa API plan (from EUR 49/month) that already includes Keepa's official hosted MCP server with OAuth, and none adds Amazon.pl. Best use: if Amazon.de becomes a regular channel, connect the official server with claude mcp add --transport http keepa https://keepa.com/mcp for a one-month pilot; otherwise use the free Keepa extension.

**conflicting evidence**

- Free API tier: keepa-mcp's README (and socket.dev's listing of it) says the free tier gives 100 tokens/min; keepa.com says plans start at EUR 49/month, and keepa-mcp issue #1 (2026-07-28) reports no free tier on the sign-up page.
- Token cost per lookup: keepa-mcp's table once claimed 1 token per get_product; its own 0.1.2 notes say earlier versions always cost 10+ tokens because live offers were requested, and current estimates are 2-4 tokens.
- Supported marketplaces: keepa.com lists 11 (incl. MX, BR); keepa-mcp documents 9 domain ids; cosjef lists CN, which Keepa no longer covers; keepa-adapter's README example mentions 'au' while its supported list omits it.
- keepa-adapter version: README references a v1.2.0 bundle while the latest GitHub release is v1.1.1 (2026-05-08).
- Default token budget: keepa-adapter assumes 5 tokens/min 'default plan', while keepa.com's entry plan in the earlier batch is 20 tokens/min.

**sources checked**

- https://registry.npmjs.org/keepa-mcp and https://api.npmjs.org/downloads/point/last-month/keepa-mcp (2026-10-15)
- https://github.com/BWB03/keepa-adapter (README, releases, commits via GitHub API; 2026-10-15)

- https://keepa.com/api-docs/changelog.html (2026-10-15)
- https://keepa.com/#!api (rendered in the built-in browser; 'from EUR 49', 11 marketplaces, 'For commercial and professional use'; 2026-10-15)
- GitHub user profiles purahmanian, BWB03, cosjef (GitHub API, 2026-10-15)
