### Apify, Bright Data and Firecrawl scrapers

**Verdict:** SKIP for Allegro and Ceneo · **Cost:** Apify about USD 2-5 per 1,000 rows · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 9 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Paid scraping infrastructure that an agent in Claude Code can call through MCP to pull marketplace data (role: scraper + MCP server). Apify is a marketplace of third-party 'Actors'; about 30 of them target Allegro (plus 7 for Ceneo). Bright Data MCP and Firecrawl MCP are general scraping MCP servers with built-in unblocking.
- **apify allegro actors**: Most used on 2026-10-15 (Apify Store API): memo23/allegro-scraper (398 users, 31,959 successful runs in 30 days; keyword, category, seller or offer URL; pure HTTP behind a managed proxy), e-commerce/allegro-fast-product-scraper (672 users, oldest, created 2024-04-22), unfenced-group/allegro-scraper (38 users; EAN/GTIN to Allegro product to every seller offering it; also .cz/.sk), maximedupre/allegro-scraper (49 users), studio-amba/allegro-scraper (14 users), karamelo/allegro-pl-scraper (2 users, created 2026-09-15). Apify's official MCP server (https://mcp.apify.com) lets Claude search, run and read any of them.
- **bright data mcp**: brightdata/brightdata-mcp v3.1.0 (2026-10-15): 32 tools - search_engine, scrape_as_markdown, batch tools, 14 remote-browser tools, and a scraper flow (search_scrapers, get_scraper_details, run_scraper) over 1,200+ pre-built Web Scraper API scrapers, including an Allegro scraper (URL input). The 'Pro mode' and web_data_* extractor tools in the brief were replaced by tool groups and the scraper flow in v3.0.0 (2026-10-11).
- **firecrawl mcp**: firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server (release 3.30.0, 2026-10-13): 27 tools - scrape (markdown or JSON by schema), map, crawl, search, interact (browser actions), monitor (scheduled re-checks with diffs), credit usage; hosted endpoints at mcp.firecrawl.dev with a keyless rate-limited tier for scrape/search/parse.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

Apify Technologies s.r.o., Prague, Czech Republic (EU); founded 2015-2016 by Jan Čurn and Jakub Balada (Y Combinator Fellowship); about EUR 2.8M raised from J&T Ventures and Reflex Capital in April 2024, otherwise bootstrapped (2023 turnover EUR 6.7M per tech.eu). Allegro actors are written by independent developers (memo23, unfenced-group, maximedupre, karamelo, studio-amba) whose identity is not disclosed; none is linked to Allegro. Bright Data Ltd. (formerly Luminati Networks, spun out of Hola VPN), Netanya, Israel; sold to London fund EMK Capital in 2017 for about USD 200M ⚠ *(unverified: whether EMK still owns it)*. Firecrawl (grew out of Mendable), San Francisco; Y Combinator; USD 14.5M Series A led by Nexus Venture Partners (August 2025); a later Series B and a USD 82M Form D are reported by single outlets ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**lifecycle status**

- **apify actors**: Volatile: most Allegro actors were created in 2026 (karamelo 2026-09-15, memo23 2026-06-27, unfenced-group 2026-06-21, maximedupre 2026-05-31, studio-amba 2026-04-06). 30-day run stats on 2026-10-15: memo23 31,959 of 32,211 runs succeeded (99.2%); unfenced-group 634 of 765 (128 failed); maximedupre 307 of 391 (74 timed out); e-commerce fast scraper 266 of 340; studio-amba and karamelo 26 of 26. Several were modified on 2026-10-15 itself, a sign of constant repair against Allegro's anti-bot changes.
- **apify mcp**: apify/apify-mcp-server v0.18.3 (2026-10-15), MIT, 11,366 stars, 195 open issues; very active.
- **bright data mcp**: v3.0.0 (2026-10-11) removed 46 web_data_* tools; v3.1.0 (2026-10-15) enabled all tools by default and marks results as untrusted web content; MIT, 2,677 stars.
- **firecrawl mcp**: Release 3.30.0 on 2026-10-13, commits on 2026-10-15; MIT, 7,609 stars, 168 open issues.
- **rules**: Allegro Regulamin version effective 2026-10-13 contains art. 10.10-10.11 (read 2026-10-15); Allegro REST API terms changed 2025-09-23 and again 2026-09-01; Ceneo terms effective 2026-08-01 contain art. 14.7-14.10.
- **verified**: 2026-10-15 via Apify Store API, GitHub API, vendor pricing pages and the two marketplaces' terms.

**⚠ cost model**

- **apify platform**: Free plan USD 0 with USD 5 of monthly usage; Starter USD 19/month (USD 19 usage); Scale USD 199; Business USD 999; compute USD 0.20 per CU (Free/Starter); residential proxy USD 8/GB (apify.com/pricing, seen 2026-10-15) ⚠ *(unverified: older sources quote different Starter prices)*.
- **allegro actor prices**: Pay per event, USD, seen 2026-10-15: memo23 USD 3.00 per 1,000 products + USD 0.005 per start (seller phone USD 0.03, seller email USD 0.05 per seller when lead data is on); unfenced-group USD 2.49 per 1,000 listings, USD 10 per 1,000 EAN products resolved, USD 1.50 per 1,000 seller offers; maximedupre USD 2.25 per 1,000; studio-amba USD 2.00 per 1,000 + USD 0.005 start; karamelo USD 2.00 per 1,000 + USD 0.003 start; e-commerce fast scraper USD 5.00 per 1,000 on the free tier falling to USD 0.75 at the top tier. The brief's 'USD 1.5-5 per 1,000' range holds. Proxy cost is bundled in these per-event prices.
- **ceneo actors**: bovi/ceneo-price-scraper from USD 4.75 per 1,000 and studio-amba/ceneo-scraper from USD 2.00 per 1,000 (batch-1 finding; not re-priced here).
- **bright data**: MCP: 5,000 free requests per month (renewing, no card needed); then pay as you go USD 1.50 per 1,000 results for search/scrape/extract and USD 8/GB for browser navigation; spend cap settable. Allegro scraper: USD 1.5 per 1,000 records pay-as-you-go, 5,000 free records per month, Scale USD 499/month for 384,000 records.
- **firecrawl**: Free 1,000 credits per month (renewing); Hobby USD 19 monthly or USD 16 billed yearly for 5,000 credits; Standard USD 83/month yearly for 100,000. Scrape 1 credit per page (+4 for JSON extraction), search 2 credits per 10 results, monitor 1 credit per page per check. Keyless hosted endpoint for scrape/search/parse, rate-limited.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **allegro actors**: allegro.pl (some also allegro.cz, .sk, .hu); output in Polish with PLN prices; Allegro Lokalnie supported by at least one actor (lentic_clockss). No Polish UI on Apify.
- **bright data**: Global; geo-targeting and unblocking vendor-claimed; Allegro scraper takes product URLs, not keywords.
- **firecrawl**: Global fetcher; whether it gets past Allegro's DataDome was not tested (testing would itself breach Allegro's terms) ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **poland legal availability**: Technically available from Poland; contractually barred for Allegro and Ceneo (see automation_legal_risk).
- **us only features**: None; no checkout or buy-for-me features.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Partial. Allegro actors return the offer 'parameters' (Allegro's structured spec fields), condition, and in deep mode GTIN/EAN, SKU, warranty and returns; unfenced-group maps an EAN to the Allegro catalogue product and then lists every seller of that product, which is the cleanest same-product mapping on Allegro. Bright Data's Allegro scraper returns item ID, variant ID and category tree. Nothing compares specs across makers or detects white-label rebadges; that is left to the agent.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Allegro only (and Ceneo shops if a Ceneo actor is used, which Ceneo's terms forbid). Within Allegro: all sellers of one product with priceStats.lowest and cheapestOffer (unfenced-group), or keyword result pages capped at about 6,000 products per query (memo23). Nothing for Media Expert, x-kom, Decathlon or Amazon.de unless other actors are added. Shop counts: N/A.

**price history and omnibus**

No history; each run is a snapshot. unfenced-group's originalPrice is the price Allegro displays as 'the lowest price of the last 30 days before the reduction' under the Omnibus rule, filled only when Allegro shows a discount badge; memo23 returns the pre-discount original price. History requires scheduled runs stored over time (Apify schedules) or Firecrawl monitor checks. A fake-discount check is possible only by comparing your own stored snapshots with Allegro's displayed 30-day price.

**total landed cost**

Partial: delivery price and date (lowest delivery cost in memo23), plus warranty and returns text in maximedupre and memo23 deep mode; allegro.cz/.sk results lack delivery prices. No assembly, payment fees or return shipping cost.

**review and seller verification**

Partial. Seller login, Super Seller status and feedback score (unfenced-group); memo23 adds sellerCompany (legal name, NIP/tax ID, REGON, KRS, address, verification status), which an agent could check against KRS, CEIDG or the VAT white list. Product reviews: unfenced-group skips them because robots.txt disallows /opinie-produktowe/, while separate review actors (e-commerce/allegro-reviews-scraper) collect them anyway. No authenticity analysis. Collecting sole-trader seller names, phones and emails creates GDPR controller duties.

**⚠ safety and compliance checks**

None from the Allegro actors ⚠ *(unverified: whether any captures Allegro's GPSR product-safety section)*. Bright Data and Firecrawl can legitimately fetch public pages that allow automated access, such as Safety Gate entries, manufacturers' spec sheets or Certipedia certificate pages, but nothing runs automatically.

**independent test coverage**

N/A - scrapers do not hold test data; Firecrawl or Bright Data could fetch test.de or Which? pages, which are mostly paywalled.

**alerts and monitoring**

Apify: schedules plus webhooks on run completion, so a price drop can trigger a notification; Firecrawl: monitor tools re-check a page on a schedule and report diffs and change alerts; Bright Data MCP: no alerting. Pointing any of these at Allegro or Ceneo pages breaches those sites' terms.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No. None of these tools buys; Bright Data's and Firecrawl's browser tools could click through a checkout in principle, but nothing provides spending caps or confirmation steps, and the buyer should not give them payment credentials.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: actors can collect used offers and Allegro Lokalnie listings (lentic_clockss), and spare parts by keyword; robots.txt disallows Allegro's /z-drugiej-reki path. No service network or warranty-handling data.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Live scraping at run time. memo23 routes requests through a scrape.do-managed proxy with a Polish exit by default and 'clears the DataDome challenge'; unfenced-group says DataDome clearance takes about 30-60 seconds per page and retries blocked pages; Bright Data and Firecrawl use their own unblocking. Freshness equals the run time; each dataset row has the source URL, and run IDs and timestamps are stored on Apify. No screenshots unless Firecrawl's screenshot format or Bright Data's browser is used.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full technically (official MCP servers for all three platforms), but legally unusable against Allegro and Ceneo
- **apify mcp**: Hosted https://mcp.apify.com (Streamable HTTP; OAuth recommended so no token in config, or Bearer token); local npx @apify/actors-mcp-server with APIFY_TOKEN. Tools: search-actors, fetch-actor-details, call-actor, get-dataset-items, get-dataset, plus the rag-web-browser actor; preload actors with ?tools=, e.g. https://mcp.apify.com?tools=actors,memo23/allegro-scraper. An Apify plugin for Claude Code installs the server and agent skills together. Repo github.com/apify/apify-mcp-server (MIT, 11,366 stars, v0.18.3 2026-10-15). Apify REST API and JS/Python clients also available.
- **bright data mcp**: claude mcp add --transport http brightdata "https://mcp.brightdata.com/mcp?token=YOUR_API_TOKEN" (the token travels in the URL query string); &groups=scrapers,browser or &tools=... limits the tool set. Local npx option. Repo github.com/brightdata/brightdata-mcp (MIT, 2,677 stars, v3.1.0 2026-10-15). Bright Data also published price-comparison and competitive-intel skills that its v3.0.0 notes say must be updated.
- **firecrawl mcp**: Hosted https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp (keyless tier for scrape/search/parse; Bearer key for everything else), OAuth surface /v2/mcp-oauth, search-only surface /v2/mcp-search; local: env FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=fc-KEY npx -y firecrawl-mcp, or Docker. Repo github.com/firecrawl/firecrawl-mcp-server (MIT, 7,609 stars).
- **official allegro route**: Allegro REST API: GET /offers/listing (offer search) has been limited to verified applications since 2021-06-01, with popularity shown only in ranges and search capped at 10 pages; there is no Allegro MCP server. Allegro's own AI assistant and ChatGPT app are covered in a separate item.
- **setup effort**: Apify MCP 5-10 minutes (OAuth); Bright Data 5 minutes; Firecrawl 2-5 minutes; plus actor selection and input tuning for Allegro, 20-40 minutes the first time.

**protocol support**

MCP only (all three platforms run official MCP servers; Apify and Firecrawl offer OAuth). No ACP, UCP, AP2 or Web Bot Auth.

**⚠ open source and licence**

Apify MCP server, Bright Data MCP server and Firecrawl MCP server: MIT, all very active (releases on 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-15). The Allegro actors are Store actors whose source is generally not public ⚠ *(unverified)*. Apify's Crawlee library is Apache-2.0; Firecrawl's core engine is open source and self-hostable ⚠ *(unverified: on its exact licence)*.

**account linking and data access**

Needs an Apify, Bright Data or Firecrawl account and token (card for paid use; Bright Data asks for a card only as verification). No Allegro or Ceneo login: the actors state they do not log in. Third-party actor code runs with your Apify token and input, so pick widely used actors. GDPR: scraped seller data (names, NIP, phones, emails of sole traders) is personal data that makes the user a controller; memo23 sells phone and email 'lead data' per seller. Bright Data is based in Israel (EU adequacy decision); Apify in the EU; Firecrawl in the US. Bright Data's MCP token sits in the URL.

**⚠ automation legal risk**

High for Allegro and Ceneo; this is the deciding factor. Allegro Regulamin (version effective 2026-10-13, read 2026-10-15): art. 10.9 claims database rights; art. 10.10 says downloading or using any Allegro materials, including data, requires Allegro's consent every time, and prohibits aggregating and processing Allegro data for further use in business activity, including extraction ('skrapowania, ang. scraping'), especially with bots; art. 10.11 prohibits bots and data-extraction tools that generate extra traffic or load. Allegro uses DataDome: the actors themselves describe bypassing it, and this research's plain HTTP fetch of allegro.pl/regulamin got HTTP 403. robots.txt disallows /offer/, /produkt/warianty/, /opinie-produktowe/ and /z-drugiej-reki but robots.txt is not consent. Allegro's REST API terms (from 2025-09-23) allow a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per breach (xyz.pl). Ceneo terms (effective 2026-08-01, PDF read 2026-10-15): art. 14.7 forbids automated access including bots and crawlers, 14.8 allows it only with Ceneo's written consent, and 14.10 sets a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty for each breach of 14.9 (copying, distributing or sharing Ceneo content including data), cumulative, plus further damages. EU law: in Ryanair v PR Aviation (CJEU C-30/14, 2015) website terms can contractually bar scraping of databases the Database Directive does not protect; where a sui generis database right exists (as Allegro claims), extracting substantial parts is barred by statute (Polish Act on the protection of databases, 2001). US rulings favouring public-data scraping (Meta v. Bright Data, January 2024; X Corp v. Bright Data, dismissed May 2024) do not apply in Poland. Practical exposure for a one-off personal run is small but real: Allegro account suspension if linked, contractual claims, and GDPR duties for seller data. Not legal advice ⚠ *(unverified: on how Polish courts treat terms against non-logged-in visitors)*.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

Pay-per-use platforms: Apify takes a share of each actor's event fees, actor authors earn per row, and some Allegro actors earn extra from seller 'lead data' (aimed at sales prospecting, not buyers). Bright Data sells proxies and data; Firecrawl sells credits. No affiliate bias in results; the data reflect Allegro's own ordering, including sponsored offers, which memo23 flags (Smart!/sponsored flags) - useful for transparency.

**ranking transparency**

N/A - scrapers return raw rows in the marketplace's order; the agent does the ranking, so you control exclusions completely. Sponsored flags are available in memo23's output.

**run to run consistency**

N/A for AI variance. Reliability varies by actor: 30-day failure or timeout rates on 2026-10-15 were 0.8% (memo23), 17% (unfenced-group), 19% (maximedupre) and 22% (e-commerce fast scraper); Allegro's anti-bot changes break actors without notice.

**⚠ manipulation and injection resistance**

Fetching arbitrary pages puts seller-written text into the agent's context. Bright Data MCP v3.1.0 (2026-10-15) marks all scraped results and error bodies as untrusted web content; Firecrawl and Apify do not document equivalent marking ⚠ *(unverified)*. Third-party actor code is a trust risk of its own. None checks for fake shops or spoofed reviews.

**known failures**

Actor churn and breakage (most created in 2026; several patched on 2026-10-15); DataDome slows pages to 30-60 s and blocks some; memo23 caps search at ~6,000 products per query and needs deep mode for rating, stock and GTIN; unfenced-group returns no reviews by design and no delivery price on .cz/.sk; Bright Data's 2026-10-11 removal of 46 web_data_* tools broke older configs and skills (old group IDs still map); Firecrawl success on Allegro untested. The memo23 Store page claims '100.0% runs succeeded' while the API's 30-day stats show 99.2%.

**regulatory enforcement history**

No UOKiK, DSA or DMA action found for Apify, Bright Data or Firecrawl. Court history: Meta v. Bright Data (N.D. Cal., summary judgment for Bright Data on the contract claim, January 2024; Meta later dropped the case) and X Corp v. Bright Data (dismissed 2024-05-10). Nothing found for the individual actor authors.

**buyer protection path**

N/A - scrapers sell nothing. Buying on Allegro after research gives Allegro Protect, Polish statutory rights (14-day withdrawal, 2-year conformity) and payment-method protections; a scraping breach linked to your account could put that account at risk.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low for a one-off trampoline purchase. What it could do: one memo23 run for 'trampolina ogrodowa 305 z siatką' returns ~120 Allegro offers with price, delivery, seller rating, sponsored flag and (deep mode) GTIN and warranty; an unfenced-group EAN run lists every Allegro seller of a chosen model with the Omnibus 30-day price when discounted. Why not: Allegro's own product page already shows all sellers of a catalogue product for free, Allegro offers also appear in Google Shopping (see the SerpApi item), and the Allegro and Ceneo terms forbid the automated route. Bright Data and Firecrawl remain useful for permitted pages such as manufacturer spec sheets or Safety Gate entries.

**workflow role**

Price and place-to-buy (Allegro sellers) and seller-identity hints - but in practice replaced by SerpApi Google Shopping, Ceneo in the browser and manual Allegro checks. Generic Firecrawl/Bright Data: fetching permitted spec, safety and test pages into the vault.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Arithmetic (USD, 2026-10-15 prices): memo23 keyword run of 120 listings = 120 x 0.003 + 0.005 = 0.365, plus 10 deep rows at the same rate = 0.03, about USD 0.40; unfenced-group for 5 EANs = 5 x 0.01 + 75 seller offers x 0.0015 = USD 0.16; both fit inside Apify's free USD 5 monthly credit. Bright Data: about 30 requests, inside the 5,000 free monthly requests (else 30 x 0.0015 = USD 0.05). Firecrawl: 30 pages with JSON extraction = 150 credits of the 1,000 free monthly. Add roughly 50-150k Claude tokens to read the rows ⚠ *(unverified)* and 20-40 minutes of first-time setup. The hidden cost is legal: Ceneo's PLN 50,000 per-breach penalty clause and Allegro's terms.

**evidence trail**

Technically good: Apify datasets (JSON/CSV) with run ID, timestamps and source URLs; Firecrawl markdown, JSON and screenshots; Bright Data snapshots. A vault note could store run ID, date, query, rows (seller, price, delivery, original 30-day price, URL). But a record that documents a terms breach is not something to keep for Allegro or Ceneo data.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Cheap: USD 1.5-5 per 1,000 Allegro rows, with free monthly credits on Apify (USD 5), Bright Data (5,000 requests) and Firecrawl (1,000 credits).
  - Official, actively maintained MCP servers for all three platforms, with OAuth on Apify and Firecrawl.
  - unfenced-group's EAN-to-all-sellers mapping and Omnibus 30-day price field are the most structured Allegro data available.
  - Bright Data v3.1.0 marks scraped content as untrusted, a useful injection safeguard.
  - Firecrawl and Bright Data are legitimate tools for pages that allow automated access (spec sheets, Safety Gate, test pages).
- **weaknesses**:
  - Allegro Regulamin art. 10.10-10.11 and Ceneo art. 14.7-14.10 (PLN 50,000 per breach) forbid the automated route.
  - Actors work by bypassing DataDome, which undercuts any 'public data' defence and makes them break often (up to 22% failed or timed-out runs).
  - Allegro-only coverage; no history without scheduled snapshots.
  - Seller lead-data features pull personal data of sole traders into GDPR scope.
  - Small, anonymous actor authors with no independent reviews.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found for the Allegro actors: only Apify Store ratings (memo23 5.0 from 3 reviews, e-commerce fast scraper 4.86 from 5) and run statistics. Bright Data and Firecrawl appear in vendor-run or competitor benchmarks (e.g. Hackernoon's SERP benchmark naming Bright Data the winner, vendor-influenced) and in many affiliate listicles, which were not used.

**verdict for me**

SKIP for Allegro and Ceneo (CONTEXT ONLY for Firecrawl or Bright Data on sites that permit automated access) - deciding fact: Allegro's Regulamin (version of 2026-10-13, art. 10.10-10.11) and Ceneo's terms (art. 14.7, PLN 50,000 per breach under 14.10) forbid automated extraction, and Allegro offers already reach you through Google Shopping. Best use: keep Firecrawl's keyless MCP for fetching manufacturer spec sheets, Safety Gate entries and test pages into the vault; check Allegro and Ceneo manually or in your own browser session at human pace.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- Whether Allegro's scraping ban is new: the brief records it as applying from 2026-10-13 (the current Regulamin version date), while a search summary of earlier versions says the art. 10.10-10.11 wording existed before; no version diff was found ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- Allegro API penalty: xyz.pl (2025-09-15) reports a PLN 50,000 per-violation penalty in the REST API terms from 2025-09-23; the article also says the change does not directly target AI or scraping.
- memo23 reliability: its Store page says '100.0% runs succeeded'; the Apify API's 30-day stats show 31,959 of 32,211 (99.2%).
- Bright Data free tier: the MCP README says 5,000 free requests per month; the Allegro scraper page says 5,000 free records (about USD 7.50 of credit); the brief's 'Pro mode' was replaced by tool groups in v3.0.0.
- Apify Starter price: apify.com/pricing shows USD 19/month on 2026-10-15; older third-party pages cite higher Starter prices.
- robots.txt etiquette: unfenced-group skips Allegro reviews because robots.txt disallows them; other actors (e-commerce/allegro-reviews-scraper) sell review scraping.

### Community shopping skills

**Verdict:** PILOT (as design templates) · **Cost:** Free; licences vary · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 7 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Three community SKILL.md files that turn Claude into a shopping researcher. Each is a prompt-level workflow, not a data service: none ships its own price, safety or seller data. All three were opened and read in full on 2026-10-15 (GitHub API). Role type: Claude skill.
- **infranodus skill shopping**: Folder skill-shopping in github.com/infranodus/skills; installs as 'shopping-assistant'. One SKILL.md (24,643 bytes). A 10-phase workflow: DISCOVER, DEFINE, SURVEY (8-12 candidates plus a 'disruptor scan' for brands launched in the last 12-18 months), COMPARE ('A vs B' articles; any competitor named in 2+ independent reviews joins the list), OPTIMIZE (cheaper or pricier near-equivalents in the same brand's lineup), EXPAND, NARROW (3-4 finalists), REVIEW (5-star and 1-2-star extremes), STRETCH (options 20-30% pricier or cheaper), DECIDE (resale value via eBay completed auctions, delivery, returns, warranty, support). Optional InfraNodus MCP calls in phases 2, 3, 4 and 6. Web search is the only required tool.
- **emptor**: Orchestrator skill in github.com/npbuilds/skill-library (skills/consumer-research/emptor). SKILL.md 6,499 bytes plus a brief exemplar. It routes to six child skills (needs-elicitor, source-trust-atlas, product-verifier, review-forensics, recommendation-brief, decision-journal) and reuses general skills (agentic-researcher, source-triangulator, paywall-strategist, bias-and-funding-tracer, vault-writer). Phases 0-8: Recall, Elicit (no WebSearch or WebFetch before the requirements spec is signed off, budget locked before any price is seen), Source plan (four trust tiers), Scan (15-50 candidates from Tier 1-2 sources only), Eliminate (elimination-by-aspects to 3-6 finalists), Verify (claims, availability, recalls, merchant trust, review authenticity), Evaluate (weighted matrix plus a +-20% weight-sensitivity check), Brief (cited 'EMPTOR BRIEF' with a CRS- ID and confidence tags), Journal (JSONL plus a markdown brief plus an optional vault mirror). Commands /emptor, /purchase-log and /purchase-review close a 30-day satisfaction loop.
- **firecrawl shop**: Workflow skill in github.com/firecrawl/skills (skills/workflows/firecrawl-shop), synced from firecrawl/firecrawl-workflows. SKILL.md 2,290 bytes, version 0.1.0. It requires FIRECRAWL_API_KEY and uses Firecrawl search, scrape and a hosted browser: research options, compare price, specs, reviews, seller quality and shipping, pick one, and optionally add the item to a cart in an authenticated browser profile, stopping 'before checkout unless explicitly instructed'. Output: a markdown report with Recommendation, Products Compared, Review Signals, Cart Status, Sources and Rerun Inputs.
- **other skills found in search**: Seen while searching on 2026-10-15, not evaluated in depth: Shopify/shop-cli with the bundled 'Shop skill' (MIT, 18 stars; Shop catalog search, Sign in with Shop, UCP checkout with a pre-authorised Shop Pay budget; personal use only); Shopify/ucp-cli ('a shopping skill for AI agents', MIT, 79 stars); filtalgo/Filtmall-Shopping-Skill (Apache-2.0, 997 stars, a Chinese beauty catalogue, irrelevant for Poland); nexscope-ai/eCommerce-Skills (seller-side). The Shopify ones are covered under the Shopify Global Catalog and protocol items.

**⚠ vendor and ownership**

- **infranodus skill shopping**: Nodus Labs / InfraNodus. Author Dmitry Paranyushkin (commits under his name and 'deemeetree'). InfraNodus sells a paid knowledge-graph SaaS, and the skill steers the agent to call its MCP tools first at four checkpoints, so the skill doubles as a funnel for the paid product. HQ country not verified ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **emptor**: Individual developer: GitHub user npbuilds (account created 2026-01-26, 3 public repos), skill metadata author 'nirav'. Part of a personal 535-skill library. No company, funding or monetisation; the skill states 'zero monetization'.
- **firecrawl shop**: Firecrawl (the web-scraping API company; firecrawl.dev). The skill exists to consume Firecrawl credits. US-based company ⚠ *(unverified: HQ not re-verified here)*.

**lifecycle status**

- **infranodus skill shopping**: Active, low churn. Added 2026-02-23 (commit 'add the shopping skill'); changes 2026-02-23 (tool use), 2026-02-26 (underlying-needs analysis), 2026-03-10, 2026-09-01 (description fix for Claude requirements). Repo: 120 stars, 31 forks, 0 open issues, last push 2026-09-20. skills.sh first seen 2026-04-04, 26 installs. Verified 2026-10-15 via GitHub API and skills.sh.
- **emptor**: Early, single drop. The whole consumer-research suite arrived in one commit on 2026-07-27 ('salvage Emptor research suite (#222)'), with no later change to the emptor folder. The host repo is active (automated score recalibration commits daily; last push 2026-10-15) but has 1 star and 0 forks. Not listed on skills.sh (404 on 2026-10-15). Listed on claudskills.com (last updated 2026-07-31; static scan 2026-09-28). Verified 2026-10-15.
- **firecrawl shop**: Young. firecrawl-workflows repo created 2026-05-14 (ISC, 193 stars, last push 2026-08-21); the skill landed in firecrawl/skills by a bot sync on 2026-08-21 (one commit). firecrawl/skills: 126 stars, 5 open issues, last push 2026-10-08. skills.sh first seen 2026-08-21, 2.7K installs. Version 0.1.0. Verified 2026-10-15.

**⚠ cost model**

- **skills themselves**: Free to install and read. Licences: infranodus none stated; emptor MIT; firecrawl-shop ISC.
- **infranodus**: Required: only web search plus model tokens. Optional InfraNodus MCP: 'free access for the first few iterations' (repo README), then an API key. InfraNodus pricing page seen 2026-10-15: Basic EUR 12/month and Advanced EUR 32/month (Advanced adds API access; both list the MCP server), 14-day free trial, VAT excluded for EU private customers. The page showed the annual-plan view ('saving 35%'), so monthly billing may cost more ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **emptor**: Free (MIT). Costs are model tokens and any paywalled tests the user buys. The optional local MCP server is free and, per its SETUP.md, runs locally with nothing sent to the internet.
- **firecrawl shop**: Needs a Firecrawl account. firecrawl.dev/pricing on 2026-10-15: Free 1,000 credits (whether one-off or monthly not stated ⚠ *(unverified)*); Hobby USD 16/month billed yearly or USD 19 billed monthly for 5,000 credits; Standard USD 83/month billed yearly for 100,000 credits. Search 2 credits per 10 results; scrape 1 credit per page (+4 for JSON extraction); browser 'Interact' 2 credits per browser minute. No general pay-as-you-go beyond the free allowance (secondary: tinyfish.ai).

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **general**: All three are region-neutral prompts that run wherever Claude Code runs, so they 'work' from Poland. What changes per country is the quality of the sources they search. None was written for Poland, and all three skew to US or UK sources.
- **infranodus**: PL: works; Phase 1 asks for the buyer's country and city, and the InfraNodus calls take language and country parameters. Whether InfraNodus search-intent data covers Polish queries was not tested ⚠ *(unverified)*. Source hints are US-centric (Wirecutter, RTINGS, Tom's Hardware, Consumer Reports, eBay completed auctions) and price thresholds are in USD (under ~50, over ~500).
- **emptor**: PL: runs, but its source atlas and checks are US/UK: Tier 1 = Consumer Reports, Rtings, Which?, America's Test Kitchen, Project Farm; recalls = CPSC, NHTSA, FDA; regulation = FTC fake-review rule. No Stiftung Warentest, VKI, Pro-Test, Safety Gate, UOKiK, Omnibus or Polish registers. Budget defaults to USD in the schema.
- **firecrawl shop**: PL: runs via Firecrawl's cloud. Firecrawl search accepts location settings ⚠ *(unverified: not tested with gl=pl)*. Fetching Allegro or Ceneo through Firecrawl is the automated access their terms forbid (see automation_legal_risk). Cart actions need an authenticated browser profile hosted by Firecrawl.
- **checkout and buy for me**: None of the three buys. firecrawl-shop can add to cart and could continue to checkout on explicit instruction; the other two stop at a recommendation.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

infranodus: strongest on 'choosing the best version'. Phase 5 OPTIMIZE asks for a slightly cheaper model in the same lineup that keeps almost all features, and a slightly pricier one that adds a wanted feature; Phase 9 STRETCH checks options 20-30% above and below the shortlist; Phase 4 adds any competitor named in 2+ independent reviews. No EAN/GTIN mapping, no retailer-exclusive or OEM-rebadge detection. emptor: product-verifier step 1 'Pin the exact SKU' records which model-year and regional variant each piece of evidence applies to, and the brief names the SKU. No EAN/GTIN or rebadge logic either. firecrawl-shop: one line, 'be specific with model numbers'. None maps a Polish listing to the tested variant (for example a 305 cm Berg model sold under two names on Allegro); that has to be added.

**⚠ price comparison and pl coverage**

None indexes shops. infranodus says 'track prices across retailers' and runs web searches; emptor collects 'where to buy' prices with dates for the finalists; firecrawl-shop scrapes product pages. Polish coverage depends on what the search engine or scraper reaches. Sibling items found that plain HTTP gets 403 from most Polish shops (Allegro, Decathlon, Media Expert), so WebFetch-based skills (infranodus, emptor) will mostly miss live Polish prices, while Firecrawl's proxies may reach them against the shops' terms ⚠ *(unverified: not tested)*. Coverage figures: none claimed, none tested.

**price history and omnibus**

None. No skill reads price history or the Omnibus 30-day lowest price, or flags fake discounts. emptor's scope section says it does not track prices continuously; firecrawl-shop's catalogue listing on skillselion.com says 'Skip if Real-time pricing or inventory tracking' (catalogue guidance, not a test). infranodus mentions waiting for sales only as a timeline question.

**total landed cost**

Partial at best. infranodus Phase 10 checks delivery speed, return policy, warranty and support, but not shipping cost or return fees as numbers. firecrawl-shop compares 'shipping' as one criterion. emptor records the return window per merchant. None adds price + shipping + return shipping for a bulky item, assembly, or cross-border warranty enforceability.

**review and seller verification**

- **grade**: partial (emptor), weak (infranodus, firecrawl-shop)
- **emptor**: review-forensics scores five signals per product (velocity spikes, verified-purchase ratio, rating-distribution shape, reviewer-account patterns, cross-product repetition), marks unobservable signals 'unchecked' instead of passing them, and returns clean / mixed / suspect / unverifiable (<3 signals or <25 reviews). product-verifier rates each merchant verified / caution / avoid from domain age, marketplace vs first-party seller, return policy, price plausibility (40% below market on a fresh domain = scam signal) and consumer-protection history. It cannot prove seller identity: no CEIDG, KRS, VAT white list or VIES lookup.
- **infranodus**: Review analysis is qualitative: read 5-star and 1-2-star extremes, decide whether complaints are relevant, recurring or about service. Volume rule: 2,000 reviews at 4.2 beat 15 at 4.8. No authenticity method and no seller checks.
- **firecrawl shop**: Compares 'seller quality' and asks to 'note affiliate, sponsored, or unreliable sources when visible'. No method.

**safety and compliance checks**

emptor only, and US-only: product-verifier step 4 checks recalls in CPSC, NHTSA or FDA plus Tier-1 failure modes and warranty terms. No Safety Gate, UOKiK, GPSR listing fields, EN 71-14 edition or Certipedia checks in any of the three. For a trampoline sold in Poland the safety gate has to be added from sibling items (Safety Gate JSON API, GPSR Art. 19 fields, EN 71-14 and GS/Certipedia).

**independent test coverage**

emptor is the only one with a rule: Tier-1 independent testers are primary evidence, Tier-2 affiliate-funded editorial is corroboration, crowd sources are hypotheses, affiliate listicles and merchant copy are never evidence; freshness horizons of ~12 months for Tier 1 and ~6 months for Tier 2; paywalled Tier-1 evidence routes to paywall-strategist before 'unverifiable'. Its roster misses the European labs that matter here (Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 and VKI 2025 trampoline tests). infranodus lists Wirecutter, RTINGS, Tom's Hardware and Consumer Reports as places to check. firecrawl-shop says 'trusted review sites' without naming any.

**alerts and monitoring**

None. emptor explicitly runs no daemons; its follow-up is a pull-based /purchase-review after 30 days. No skill watches a Polish shop page.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

infranodus: no purchase. emptor: no purchase ('does not complete purchases'). firecrawl-shop: can add to cart through Firecrawl's hosted browser when the user asks and has an authenticated browser profile, and says to stop before checkout 'unless explicitly instructed' and not to 'purchase or check out without explicit approval'. That is a prompt-level rule with no spending cap, no confirmation UI and no allow-list; the skills.sh Gen Agent Trust Hub audit notes the browser cart capability next to the prompt-injection surface. For this buyer: do not give firecrawl-shop a logged-in shop profile.

**after sales and resale**

infranodus covers resale value (search '[product] resale value', eBay completed auctions), warranty length and support reputation; it does not know OLX, Allegro Lokalnie or Vinted. emptor logs the purchase and a 30-day satisfaction check-in that recalibrates future confidence. firecrawl-shop: none. None covers spare parts (nets, pads, springs) or a Polish service network.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

infranodus and emptor: WebSearch and WebFetch (emptor site-scopes queries such as 'site:rtings.com <product>' and bans generic 'best X' queries); optional InfraNodus graph tools. emptor date-stamps every price and availability fact and re-checks prices at brief time. firecrawl-shop: Firecrawl search and scrape (live at fetch time) plus Firecrawl browser. No skill keeps snapshots; firecrawl-shop and emptor require a source list, infranodus does not require URLs in its final presentation.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full (they are Claude Code skills), with different setup effort
- **infranodus**: Install: '/plugin marketplace add infranodus/skills' then '/plugin install shopping-assistant@infranodus-skills', or 'npx skills add infranodus/skills --skill shopping-assistant -g -a claude-code -y'. Optional InfraNodus MCP server (official repo infranodus/mcp-server-infranodus, last push 2026-10-12) with tools analyze_related_search_queries, search_queries_vs_search_results, generate_content_gaps, generate_research_ideas. Setup: 2 minutes without MCP, about 10 minutes with an InfraNodus account and key.
- **emptor**: Three routes. (a) Copy the folder skills/consumer-research/* plus the reused general skills into ~/.claude/skills; (b) run the library's local read-only MCP server (Python, stdio; tools search_skills, get_skill) and the /emptor command fetches the skill through it; (c) claudskills.com one-file install of emptor/SKILL.md, which silently drops the six child skills it routes to. Telemetry: the server mirrors usage events to the author's Firestore only in remote Cloud Run mode with TELEMETRY_FIRESTORE=1; local stdio installs are a no-op (firestore_telemetry.py, read 2026-10-15). Setup: 30-60 minutes to copy and adapt; the vault mirror expects a different vault layout (Raw/, Notes/, _meta/frontmatter-schema.md) and would fall back to JSONL only here.
- **firecrawl shop**: Install via 'npx skills add' from firecrawl/skills or firecrawl-workflows; needs FIRECRAWL_API_KEY and the Firecrawl CLI or MCP server. Setup: about 10 minutes plus a paid plan for real use.
- **fallback**: All three are readable markdown, so the useful parts can be re-implemented inside this vault's own skill (see the custom buying-research skill item).

**protocol support**

None. No ACP, UCP, AP2 or Klarna APP. They act through web search, scraping or a browser. MCP only as an optional tool source (InfraNodus MCP, Firecrawl MCP, the skill-library MCP).

**open source and licence**

- **infranodus**: Public repo, but no LICENSE file: the GitHub API returns license null and the README states none. Default copyright applies, so copying or redistributing the SKILL.md text is not licensed; reading it and re-implementing the ideas is the safe route. 120 stars, 31 forks, 0 open issues, last push 2026-09-20.
- **emptor**: MIT (repo licence). 1 star, 0 forks, 0 open issues, last push 2026-10-15; emptor folder unchanged since 2026-07-27. Safe to fork and adapt with attribution.
- **firecrawl shop**: ISC (frontmatter and repo). firecrawl/skills 126 stars, firecrawl-workflows 193 stars; last skill change 2026-08-21. The service it depends on is closed and paid.

**⚠ account linking and data access**

infranodus: optional InfraNodus account and API key; queries sent to InfraNodus are processed by its SaaS (privacy terms not reviewed ⚠ *(unverified)*). emptor: no account; it writes data/decision-journal.jsonl, data/purchases.jsonl and data/consumer-preferences.json (budget style, liked brands, trusted merchants) in the repo where it runs, so purchase history stays local. firecrawl-shop: a Firecrawl API key; every searched query and scraped page passes through Firecrawl's cloud; cart actions require storing a logged-in shop session in Firecrawl's browser profile, which for this buyer is a no-go under the GDPR and credential rules in the brief. None asks for payment credentials.

**automation legal risk**

infranodus and emptor: low; they read pages through ordinary search and fetch at human volume. firecrawl-shop: medium to high on Polish sites. A cloud scraper with rotating infrastructure fetching Allegro or Ceneo is exactly what Allegro's Regulamin art. 10.10-10.11 (from 2026-10-13) and Ceneo terms art. 14.7 (PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per copying violation, 14.10) forbid (sibling findings). Logged-in cart automation also risks account restriction. Amazon blocks unidentified agents under its Conditions of Use (sibling).

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

infranodus: no affiliate links, but the skill pushes InfraNodus tool calls ('start with the InfraNodus tool call first', four checkpoints), which is a product funnel; its 'disruptor scan' and Kickstarter suggestions can favour newer, less-proven brands. emptor: no monetisation; explicitly treats affiliate listicles and merchant copy as non-evidence, and downgrades a source one tier for hidden affiliate relationships. firecrawl-shop: none in the skill; the bias comes from whatever Firecrawl search ranks first, which for 'best trampoline 2026' style queries is affiliate SEO content unless the agent filters it.

**ranking transparency**

emptor: high. The brief shows requirements, weights, a per-finalist weighted matrix scored 'before brand/price reveal', +-20% sensitivity, sources with tier and date, and a mandatory satisficing note when two options clear every must-have. infranodus: medium; tables of options against the user's priorities and a stated recommendation, but no required citations. firecrawl-shop: medium; a Sources section and 'Rerun Inputs' so the same run can be repeated. None lets you exclude a source and rerun automatically.

**run to run consistency**

No repeat tests found for any of the three. emptor partly designs for it: frozen requirements spec, fixed source chain per category, a sensitivity check, and confidence capped at 'Likely' when the ranking flips within +-20% weights. infranodus and firecrawl-shop leave source choice to the model, so shortlists will drift between runs (ACES and Wharton findings in sibling items). Not repeat-tested here.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

- **audits**: skills.sh (2026-10-15): firecrawl-shop: Gen Agent Trust Hub 'Pass' (risk level SAFE; notes no delimiters between retrieved content and instructions, no sanitisation, browser cart capability), Socket 'Pass', Snyk 'Warn' with risk level MEDIUM, finding W011 'third-party content exposure' score 0.30, audited 2026-08-21. infranodus shopping-assistant: Gen Agent Trust Hub 'Pass', Socket 'Pass', Snyk 'Warn' (risk level MEDIUM label, W011 score 0.10, audited 2026-10-05). emptor: not on skills.sh; claudskills.com shows 'Grade A' from a free static OWASP Agentic Skills Top-10 scan on 2026-09-28 while also flagging the filesystem category.
- **design**: emptor is the only one with an adversarial stance: merchant copy is a claim, not evidence; Reddit threads get an astroturf protocol (account age, posting history, cross-thread repetition); a 40%-below-market price on a new domain is a scam signal. None of the three wraps fetched text as untrusted data or blocks instructions inside pages. firecrawl-shop combines untrusted page text with cart actions, the riskiest mix here (Scamlexity pattern in the sibling studies item).

**known failures**

No user reports or issues about shopping results for any of the three (infranodus/skills 0 open issues; firecrawl/skills 5 open issues, none about shop; skill-library 0). Documented weaknesses from reading the files: infranodus does not require source URLs in its final answer, uses USD thresholds and US sources, and its checkpoints push paid-tool calls. emptor's evidence base cites a 'zombie products in 18-34% of AI recommendations' figure tagged 'Confirmed' but sourced to an Alibaba product-insights page (vendor content); its single-file install on claudskills.com drops the child skills; its vault mirror targets a different vault schema. firecrawl-shop is a 2,290-byte outline with no method for reviews, sellers or variants; install counts disagree across catalogues (2.7K on skills.sh, 14K and 29.5K elsewhere per secondary search).

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - community skills; no decisions against the authors found.

**buyer protection path**

N/A for infranodus and emptor (research only; the buyer purchases normally and keeps the payment method's protection). firecrawl-shop: if it adds to cart on a merchant site, the merchant is the seller and statutory rights (rekojmia, 14-day withdrawal for distance sales) apply as usual; the skill adds no protection and an agent-placed order would complicate proof of what the buyer agreed to.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Moderate as templates, low as-is. For a ~3 m garden trampoline (EUR 200-700, safety-relevant): infranodus would elicit needs, list 8-12 models, compare Berg vs Exit vs Hudora articles, check whether a cheaper model in the same Berg line (or the 330 cm step) is the better value, and read 1-2-star reviews about rust and net tears, but it would not find the Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 grades unless the search surfaces them, would not check Safety Gate, GPSR fields or the EN 71-14 edition, and would not price delivery to Poland. emptor would route to 'deep' mode because the purchase is safety-relevant and over ~500, lock the budget in advance, and demand verified finalists, but its sources (Consumer Reports, Project Farm, CPSC) barely cover EU trampoline brands. firecrawl-shop would scrape product pages and summarise, with the ToS problem on Allegro and Ceneo and no safety step.

**workflow role**

Templates for the custom buying-research skill rather than tools to run. emptor = architecture (bias gate before prices, trust tiers, verify-before-rank, cited brief, journal). infranodus = 'choosing the best version' tactics (lineup near-equivalents, +-20-30% stretch, reviewer cross-reference, 1-2-star review reading, resale and warranty). firecrawl-shop = short report format with Rerun Inputs; skip as a runtime. Combine with sibling tools for Polish data: Ceneo/Skapiec/Allegro via a browser agent, Safety Gate API, registers, Omnibus capture.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

infranodus (full 10 phases, no MCP): about 25-40 web searches and 10-20 page fetches; at roughly 10-30k tokens per fetched page the run is about 0.3-1M tokens including re-sent context, quota on a Max plan or a few USD at API rates ⚠ *(unverified: estimate, not metered)*; 30-60 minutes with the user answering questions. With InfraNodus: 4 tool calls within the 14-day trial, then EUR 12-32/month. emptor (deep mode): 15-50 scanned candidates plus verification of 3-6 finalists, comparable or higher, roughly 0.5-2M tokens ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*. firecrawl-shop: e.g. 5 searches x 10 results = 10 credits, 25 page scrapes = 25 credits (125 with JSON extraction), 10 browser minutes = 20 credits, so 55-155 credits per run, inside the free 1,000 credits or about USD 0.21-0.59 at the Hobby monthly rate (USD 19 / 5,000 credits), plus Claude tokens.

**evidence trail**

emptor: best. EMPTOR BRIEF with Brief ID, numbered sources with tier and date, 'checked <date>' on prices, a GAPS & FRESHNESS section with a stale-after date; JSONL journal line with sources_used, forensics flags and availability checks; markdown copy in research/consumer-briefs/. No screenshots or page snapshots. firecrawl-shop: a Sources list of URLs plus Rerun Inputs (query, budget, sites); no snapshots. infranodus: tables in chat; nothing saved and no URL requirement. For this vault the record should be: brief markdown in content/_raw with source URLs, access dates and raw JSON from registers, plus a compiled note with conclusions only.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - emptor puts requirements and a locked budget before any search (anchoring defence), which no commercial assistant in the sibling items does.
  - emptor's verify-before-rank rule and review-forensics rubric mark unobservable signals 'unchecked' instead of passing them.
  - emptor's brief is auditable: weights, matrix, +-20% sensitivity, tiered and dated sources, confidence caps; MIT licence allows reuse.
  - infranodus adds the 'best version' tactics: same-brand cheaper or pricier near-equivalents, +-20-30% stretch, competitors named in 2+ independent reviews.
  - firecrawl-shop's Rerun Inputs block makes a run repeatable, and its rule to stop before checkout is explicit.
- **weaknesses**:
  - All three are US/UK-centric: no Polish shops, Omnibus, Safety Gate, GPSR, EN 71-14, CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list or European labs.
  - None captures price history or snapshots; live Polish prices fail through plain fetch (403) while the one cloud scraper (Firecrawl) collides with Allegro and Ceneo terms.
  - infranodus has no licence, so its text cannot be copied, and it nudges toward the paid InfraNodus tools.
  - firecrawl-shop combines untrusted page content with logged-in cart actions; Snyk rates it MEDIUM risk (W011, 0.30).
  - No independent test of output quality exists for any of them; emptor has 1 star and a single commit.

**independent review consensus**

No independent evidence found of output quality. What exists: automated catalogue audits (skills.sh: Gen Agent Trust Hub and Socket 'Pass', Snyk 'Warn' for firecrawl-shop and infranodus; claudskills.com static scan Grade A for emptor), catalogue scores (one catalogue gave firecrawl-shop 74/100, grade B, per secondary search) and install counts. No blog, forum thread or test that ran these skills on real purchases and checked the picks was found on 2026-10-15.

**verdict for me**

PILOT as design templates, not as runtimes - deciding fact: none covers Polish shops, EU safety checks, Omnibus or seller registers, but emptor (MIT) supplies a sound auditable architecture and infranodus the best-version tactics. Best use: fork emptor's needs-elicitor, trust-tier and brief/journal structure into the vault's own buying skill, re-implement (not copy) infranodus phases 5 and 9, swap in PL/EU sources from the sibling items, and skip firecrawl-shop.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- firecrawl-shop risk: the outline note says 'skills.sh audit rates it MEDIUM risk'; the skills.sh summary shows Gen Agent Trust Hub 'Pass' (risk level SAFE), Socket 'Pass' and Snyk 'Warn'. Only Snyk's detail page uses the MEDIUM label (W011, score 0.30). Both are true depending on which auditor is quoted.
- infranodus Snyk finding: labelled risk level MEDIUM on the page while the finding title says '(low risk: 0.10)'.
- emptor scan: claudskills.com shows 'Static scan found no risk patterns' and 'Grade A' while stating the scan 'flagged 1 of 10 categories (filesystem)'.
- firecrawl-shop install counts: 2.7K (skills.sh, 2026-10-15) vs 14K and 29.5K on other catalogues (secondary search summary); likely different counting methods and dates ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- emptor's '18-34% zombie products' figure is tagged 'Confirmed' in its research file, but the listed source is an Alibaba product-insights page; no independent study was found.
