### Custom buying-research skill

**Verdict:** PILOT (build it) · **Cost:** Build about 12-18 h (estimate) · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 5 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Proposed vault skill 'brain-buy' (command /b:buy): a Claude Code orchestrator that turns a purchase need into a verified shortlist of 2-3 offers with an evidence trail in the vault, then stops. A human buys. Role type: Claude skill (orchestrator) over browser agents, official registers, free public APIs and the existing /b:research pipeline.
- **pipeline**:
  - S0 Recall - read vault-map and catalog for earlier purchase notes in the category and any pending 30-day check-ins.
  - S1 Elicit (no web access) - job to be done, must-haves, won't-haves, weighted soft criteria, budget in PLN including delivery locked before any price is seen, delivery postcode, buying as a consumer (not on a NIP invoice), timing, risk class. Output requirements.yaml with signed_off: true. Safety-relevant or over ~PLN 2,000 switches to deep mode.
  - S2 Source plan - pick sources per category from a PL/EU trust atlas (Tier 1 labs, Tier 2 editorial and spec databases, Tier 3 verified reviews and forums, Tier 4 claims only).
  - S3 Shortlist and variant map - 8-12 candidates from Tier 1 test lists, web search, Perplexity MCP and Shopify Global Catalog MCP; eliminate on must-haves to 3-5 finalists; build a variant/SKU table with EAN/GTIN, regional names, retailer-exclusive variants, OEM rebadge flags, same-lineup near-equivalents and options 20-30% above and below budget.
  - S4 Tests and safety gate (hard gate, before prices) - map tested model codes to Polish listings; Safety Gate API and UOKiK Hermes; EN 71-14 edition and GS/Certipedia check where relevant; GPSR Art. 19 listing fields; marketplace risk tier. A fail removes the finalist.
  - S5 Price and total landed cost - per shop at human pace: price, delivery to the postcode, return shipping, assembly, Omnibus 30-day lowest price with the discount recomputed, price history cross-check (Ceneo, Skapiec, Keepa/PriceRoo for Amazon, idealo for DE), second capture on a later day.
  - S6 Seller identity and buyer-protection path - lista.cert.pl and RDAP domain age; VAT white list (status and bank account), KRS or CEIDG, VIES; shop-review profiles; choose the payment and protection route (card chargeback, Allegro Protect, Trusted Shops, statutory warranty, 14-day withdrawal and its return cost).
  - S7 Evaluate - weighted matrix on quality criteria first, landed cost added as its own criterion; +-20% weight sensitivity; source-robustness rerun (reverse source order, drop the strongest single source); confidence tags; satisficing note.
  - S8 Brief, evidence trail, stop - write the brief and evidence files to content/_raw, compile a public note with conclusions only, update the three indexes, then stop at links to the verified offers. After purchase: log price paid, set a 30-day review and a recall watch.

**vendor and ownership**

N/A - own build by the buyer, lives in this vault repo. Reuses MIT-licensed structure from npbuilds/skill-library emptor (attribution required) and re-implements ideas from infranodus skill-shopping (no licence, so no text copied). External services are public bodies (European Commission Safety Gate, Polish Ministry of Finance white list, Ministry of Justice KRS, CERT Polska, NASK), private sites read at human pace (Allegro, Ceneo, Skapiec, brand stores) and optional paid APIs (Perplexity, SerpApi, Keepa).

**lifecycle status**

Proposed design, 2026-10-15; not built. Every reused component was verified live on 2026-10-15 by sibling items (Claude in Chrome and browser-use read Allegro and Ceneo; Safety Gate JSON API, VAT white list, KRS and VIES answered without keys; Shopify Global Catalog MCP answered keyless from Poland). Time-bound dependencies: the VAT white list host wl-api.mf.gov.pl must be replaced by wykazpodatnikowvat.mf.gov.pl before 2026-12-01; the Safety Gate search API is undocumented and can change; Shopify's Catalog REST API is reported to stop on 2026-11-02 (MCP route unaffected); EN 71-14 national standards withdrawal deadline 2026-10-31.

**⚠ cost model**

- **build**: One-off about 12-18 hours ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*: SKILL.md and references 3-4 h; product fields.yaml template for /b:research 1-2 h (sibling estimate); Safety Gate plus Hermes script 1-2 h (sibling); seller-check script for white list, KRS, VIES, CERT list and RDAP about 1-1.5 h (siblings); GPSR extraction step 2-4 h (sibling); Omnibus capture and parser 1-2 h (sibling); one end-to-end trial on the trampoline 2-3 h.
- **per run cash**: Usually EUR 0-10: registers, Safety Gate, CERT list, RDAP and Certipedia are free; one paid test unlock when it decides the category (test.de trampoline 05/2025: EUR 4.90); optional Perplexity MCP about USD 0.19 and SerpApi about USD 0.12 per comparison (or the 250-search free tier); Keepa MCP only if Amazon.de is a regular channel (EUR 49/month).
- **per run tokens**: Deep agents for S3-S4 about 1M tokens (sibling estimate for a 3-agent /b:research run) plus the browser pass for S5-S6 about 1-2.5M input tokens including cache reads (Claude in Chrome sibling estimate for 5 models). On a Max subscription this is quota, not cash; at API list prices roughly USD 3-10 per run ⚠ *(unverified: estimate, not metered)*.
- **date seen**: Prices from sibling items, all seen 2026-10-15.

**feature geo matrix**

- **works from poland verified**: Claude in Chrome and the built-in browser (Allegro, Ceneo read live), browser-use in Edge (Allegro, Ceneo, Decathlon, Media Expert), Safety Gate JSON API, UOKiK Hermes (HTML), VAT white list, KRS, VIES, CEIDG (token), lista.cert.pl, RDAP (rdap.dns.pl), Certipedia ID pages, Shopify Global Catalog MCP with ships_to PL (results need checking), Perplexity MCP (answers, not shopping cards), SerpApi with gl=pl, Keepa for Amazon.de, PriceRoo for Amazon.pl delivered totals, test.de purchases.
- **excluded because us only or not pl**: Agent checkout of every kind (Google UCP Buy for me, Copilot Checkout, Perplexity Instant Buy, Alexa for Shopping), Google price tracking, ChatGPT merchant shopping ('currently live for ChatGPT users in the U.S.'), Klarna Shopping Search and APP (Poland not among 13 markets), Gemini in Chrome auto browse, Reddit Answers in Polish.
- **manual only in poland**: Ceneo and Skapiec (terms ban automated access; read by the human or a browser agent on the human's screen at human pace), Asystent Ceneo and Allegro AI Assistant (no API; outputs may not be republished), uokik.gov.pl pages (robots.txt blocks ClaudeBot).
- **language**: Elicitation and brief in Polish or English; Polish queries for shops and Allegro reviews; Safety Gate queries in English and Polish; German for test.de and idealo.

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Design core. For each finalist the skill fills a variant table: brand, product line, model code, size, enclosure type, key specs that drive safety (max user weight, frame tube thickness, spring count, net position), EAN/GTIN, regional or retailer-specific names, and the source of each value. EAN sources in order: Allegro product card (Allegro groups offers by EAN), the brand's own page, the GPSR product-safety panel, the box label photo; Shopify catalog barcodes when present. Rebadge check: same EAN, or same GPSR manufacturer name and address plus identical spec sheet under a different brand, flags a white-label OEM product. Tested-model mapping: a lab result counts only if the model code and size match the Polish listing; otherwise it is recorded as 'same line, different variant'. Best-version tactics re-implemented from infranodus: one cheaper and one pricier model in the same lineup, plus options 20-30% above and below budget, kept only if they change the value equation. Geizhals spec filters for technical durables (electronics, tools, appliances).

**price comparison and pl coverage**

The skill does not index shops; it reads them. Channels and route: Allegro (browser agent, sort by price, sponsored items flagged, GPSR panel opened), Ceneo with the 'ceny z dostawa: najnizszej' sort and duplicate cards checked (human or browser agent on the human's session, no scraping), Skapiec as a second sweep including marketplace offers and 1-year history, brand stores and Shopify-based EU stores via Shopify Global Catalog MCP, Decathlon.pl, Media Expert, x-kom and similar by browser agent, Amazon.de/Amazon.pl via Keepa and PriceRoo. Coverage target: at least 3 independent shops per finalist plus one marketplace. Evidence from siblings: Skapiec showed a trampoline PLN 180 cheaper than Ceneo for the same model, so one comparison engine is not enough.

**price history and omnibus**

For every shortlisted offer: capture the Omnibus label text verbatim and amount (regex for 'najnizsza cena z ostatnich 30 dni' and German equivalents), the strikethrough price and the advertised percentage; recompute the real discount from the 30-day reference; flag a missing, vague or shifting reference as a red flag (UOKiK fined Zalando and Temu for this, January 2026). Independent history: Ceneo 6-month trend (needs login, human session), Skapiec 1 year without login, Keepa for Amazon EU, idealo for DE. Repeat the capture on a second day before deciding. A correct-looking Omnibus field is still self-declared, never proof of a good deal.

**total landed cost**

Computed per offer: item price + delivery to the buyer's postcode (read from the shop's delivery table or cart, stopping before login or payment) + payment fee + assembly if paid + expected return cost (who pays return shipping for a ~30 kg box, from the shop's terms) + a flag for cross-border sellers (EU: 2-year legal guarantee and ECC route; non-EU: weak recourse). For bulky goods the return cost often decides between two near-equal offers.

**review and seller verification**

- **grade**: full for seller identity (official registers), partial for review authenticity
- **seller**: Order of checks, all scriptable and free: (1) lista.cert.pl daily domains.txt grep plus RDAP domain age (young domain = escalate); (2) NIP from the shop's terms page -> VAT white list (name, VAT status, KRS number, requestId) and, before any transfer, the NIP-to-bank-account check; (3) KRS by number or CEIDG by NIP (CEIDG needs a token); (4) VIES for EU sellers and for the GPSR EU responsible person; (5) TrustMate, Opineo and Trusted Shops profiles read manually (rating, 12-month count, verified share, recent negatives). 'Not listed' on a blocklist is never a pass.
- **reviews**: Adapted from emptor review-forensics: velocity, verified-purchase share, rating distribution, account patterns and repeated text, each marked ok / flag / unchecked; Allegro and Ceneo verified-purchase reviews clustered by the LLM for durability complaints (rust, net tears, spring failures). Cannot prove authenticity; it only lowers the weight of suspect corpora.

**safety and compliance checks**

Hard gate in S4, all automatable except UOKiK web pages: Safety Gate search via POST /safety-gate-alerts/public/api/search (brand, model and product type, English and Polish) with hits filtered on the brand field and alert URLs saved; UOKiK Hermes query by EAN; GPSR Art. 19 fields on each listing (manufacturer, EU responsible person with electronic contact, model or batch identifier, warnings in Polish) extracted to JSON with a screenshot, responsible person checked in VIES or KRS; EN 71-14 edition claimed (2018 vs 2025) noted; GS mark or certificate ID checked on the Certipedia ID page (no search crawling; 10 s crawl delay); marketplace tier rule excludes third-party sellers on Temu, AliExpress and Shein for safety-critical goods. A clean result is recorded as 'no known alert for queries X on date D', not 'safe'.

**independent test coverage**

S2 and S4 look up the newest test in the ICRT family first (Pro-Test for Poland, then Stiftung Warentest and VKI Konsument, then Which?, Consumentenbond and CHOICE), then RTINGS for electronics. Each lab is shown separately with test date versus model year and market. Paid results are bought by the human (one-off unlocks are cheap: test.de EUR 4.90) and stored only in content/_raw. Rule from the Wharton findings: a verdict-driving claim needs two independent sources, and no single 'pick' from one publisher decides the shortlist.

**alerts and monitoring**

Not part of the research run. Optional after S5: put 5-12 product URLs that answer plain HTTP under changedetection.io (REST API, Polish decimal parsing fixed in 0.60.9) or set a Pepper.pl keyword alert; Allegro and Ceneo pages are not watched automatically because of their terms. After purchase: a weekly Safety Gate query for the bought model and a 30-day review reminder.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

No purchase by design. The skill stops at a verified shortlist with offer links. Hard rules in SKILL.md: never click 'Kup teraz', 'Do koszyka' on a logged-in account, 'Zaplac' or any payment control; never type card numbers, BLIK codes or passwords; no stored payment methods in any browser profile the agent uses; browser-use runs logged out in an isolated profile, Claude in Chrome is used only where the human's session is needed (Ceneo history) and with its confirmation prompts on. Rationale: agent checkout is US-only, Comet bought from a fake shop and autofilled a card in the Scamlexity test (outline note), and the buyer requires a hard limit plus confirmation. Future hook: if a protocol such as AP2 closed mandates reaches Poland, the only acceptable form is a per-purchase amount cap with a human confirmation.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: the brief records warranty length and who handles claims in Poland, availability of spare parts (for a trampoline: net, padding, springs, mat; checked on the brand's Polish spare-parts page or Allegro), and a resale check on OLX and Allegro Lokalnie for used prices of the finalists. The post-purchase log keeps the invoice reference, the complaint route (statutory warranty first) and the 30-day review.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Live reads at run time; nothing cached beyond the run. Freshness handling: every price, stock and delivery fact carries a capture timestamp and URL; prices are re-captured on a second day; Safety Gate and registers return their own request IDs or dates (white list requestId, KRS 'stan z dnia', VIES requestDate); tests carry publication date and model year; Tier 1 evidence is trusted for about 12 months and Tier 2 for about 6 months (emptor atlas rule). Every answer row links to a URL plus a screenshot or raw JSON in content/_raw.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: full - designed for Claude Code
- **form**: Skill folder .claude/skills/brain-buy/ with SKILL.md (orchestrator), references/source-atlas-pl.md (trust tiers per category), references/fields-product.yaml (a /b:research fields template for S3-S4), references/extraction-schema.json (browser step fields), scripts/safety_gate.py, scripts/seller_check.py (white list, KRS, VIES, CERT list, RDAP), scripts/omnibus_parse.py; command .claude/commands/b/buy.md. brain-only: scripts/check-kb-template-drift.sh compares only its hard-coded SHARED list, so a skill outside that list is not flagged (read 2026-10-15). Follow the DOX rule: add it to .claude/skills/AGENTS.md and root AGENTS.md Workflows.
- **reused routes**:
  - /b:research pipeline and web-search-agent for S3-S4 (installed; one JSON per candidate, validated by validate_json.py).
  - Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser (Claude Code MCP) for pages needing the human's session.
  - browser-use (installed, isolated Edge CDP via C:\Users\pawel\browser-use-edge.ps1) as the logged-out reader for shop pages.
  - Safety Gate public JSON API (no key), UOKiK Hermes Rejestr.ashx (HTML).
  - VAT white list REST (no key; 100 search queries a day, up to 30 NIPs each), KRS OdpisAktualny (no key), VIES REST (no key), CEIDG v3 (free token via Profil Zaufany); community MCP servers (honest-nip-krs-mcp, krs-mcp) only after a code review.
  - lista.cert.pl domains.txt download, rdap.dns.pl.
  - Shopify Global Catalog MCP (keyless) for EU brand stores; optional Perplexity MCP, SerpApi MCP, Keepa MCP.
- **not used**: Apify or Firecrawl actors for Allegro, Ceneo or Skapiec (terms breach; Ceneo PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per copying violation), firecrawl-shop (cloud scraper plus cart actions), any ChatGPT or Asystent Ceneo automation.

**protocol support**

None needed for research. UCP is used indirectly through Shopify Global Catalog MCP for discovery. ACP, UCP checkout and AP2 are not used because no consumer-facing agent checkout exists in Poland; the stop-before-payment rule stays even if one arrives.

**open source and licence**

Own code in the brain repository; licence follows that repo. Attribution note required for structure adapted from emptor (MIT, npbuilds/skill-library). No text from infranodus skill-shopping (no licence); ideas re-implemented only. Keep any CEIDG token out of the repo (a third-party note says its payload contains the account holder's PESEL).

**account linking and data access**

Needs: a Ceneo login only for the 6-month history (human's session through Claude in Chrome, optional); a CEIDG API token (optional; NIP lookups also work through the white list and KRS); optional API keys for Perplexity, SerpApi and Keepa. Never: Allegro account in the automated browser, payment credentials, saved cards, BLIK. GDPR: the run stays on the buyer's machine and vault; the published vault note must not contain the delivery address, postcode, order numbers or reviewers' names; raw review text, Ceneo offer tables and paid test grades stay in content/_raw, which is not built into the public site.

**automation legal risk**

Designed to stay low. Allegro Regulamin art. 10.10-10.11 (from 2026-10-13) bans scraping and bots that raise traffic, and Ceneo terms 14.7-14.10 ban automated access with a PLN 50,000 contractual penalty per copying violation; Skapiec terms Art. 5.3 ban automated access too. The skill therefore reads only shortlisted pages at human pace in a real browser for one personal purchase, never bulk, never logged into Allegro, and never republishes offer tables. Residual risk: a browser agent reading pages is still automated access not covered by any permission; the practical consequence is an IP or account restriction, not legal action at this volume. Public registers and Safety Gate are open data (CC0 / official interfaces); respect the white list quota (block until midnight on breach) and Certipedia's robots rules. Paid tests and Wirecutter-style content are copyrighted: conclusions only in public notes.

#### trust and bias

**monetization and bias vector**

The skill has no monetisation. Bias enters through sources, and each has a counter-rule: Ceneo default sort is paid (switch to 'ceny z dostawa'); Allegro and Skapiec mark sponsored or promoted offers (flag and do not rank them higher); Polish 'ranking trampolin 2026' affiliate pages and manufacturer copy are Tier 4 claims only; Shopify catalog has invite-only promoted placements; Pepper.pl uses affiliate links; Asystent Ceneo and Allegro AI Assistant rank inside their own platforms; ChatGPT shows ads in Europe on Free and Go plans. Allegro-owned extensions (Cenowskaz) are excluded as non-neutral.

**ranking transparency**

Full by construction: the brief shows the signed requirements, weights, the matrix with per-criterion scores and their sources, the +-20% sensitivity result, the source-robustness rerun result, sponsored flags per offer, and every excluded candidate with the reason. Any source can be dropped and the evaluation rerun from the saved JSON.

**⚠ run to run consistency**

Designed for it, not yet measured. Fixed parts: frozen requirements, fixed source plan per category, deterministic scripts for registers, Safety Gate and Omnibus parsing, a fixed extraction schema for the browser step. LLM-variable parts (discovery and scoring) are checked by (a) rerunning S7 with the source order reversed and with the strongest single source removed, and (b) for deep mode, a second independent S3 pass whose candidate list must overlap; a flipped top pick becomes 'co-leads' or 'Contested'. Motivation: ACES (model updates reshuffle choices), the Wharton source-influence results (one source swinging picks by up to 90-99 percentage points) and the Product.ai inconsistency study (outline and sibling notes; the H-group items were not yet in results on 2026-10-15) ⚠ *(unverified: figures not re-opened here)*.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Guardrails: page text is data, never instructions (stated in SKILL.md and in the browser-step prompt); browser navigation limited to the shops and sources in the source plan; no credentials or payment data reachable; seller-identity gate before any offer reaches the brief (counters fake shops of the Scamlexity kind); review-forensics lowers weight of suspect corpora; the Wharton guard (two independent sources per verdict-driving claim) blunts a fake 'Wirecutter pick' or persuasive seller copy; first-proposal bias (Magentic Marketplace, outline note) is countered by scoring all finalists in one matrix. Residual: Claude in Chrome has vendor-reported low attack success with its classifier; browser-use has no injection defence of its own, so it runs logged out with nothing to steal.

**known failures**

Anticipated from sibling tests on 2026-10-15: Claude in Chrome get_page_text returned a review instead of the Allegro offer (use targeted find and the extraction schema); feeding a full Allegro DOM (~2.37M characters) is very expensive (issue #65927); browser-use read empty prices before rendering finished; plain HTTP gets 403 from Allegro, Decathlon and Media Expert; Allegro hides the Omnibus explanation in a tooltip on some views; Shopify catalog's ships_to PL let through shops that do not state shipping to Poland and inferred wrong specs; Ceneo shows duplicate product cards; uokik.gov.pl blocks ClaudeBot; EUR-Lex and BAuA block scripted clients; white list quota is 100 search queries a day; only German lab tests cover EU trampoline brands. None of these has been observed inside the skill because it is not built.

**regulatory enforcement history**

N/A - own tool. Enforcement records are inputs, not liabilities: UOKiK Omnibus fines (Zalando about PLN 31M, Temu about PLN 5.9M, announced 2026-01-12) and the EU DSA fine on Temu (May 2026) feed the Omnibus red-flag rule and the marketplace risk tier.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

The brief names the path for the chosen offer: pay by card for chargeback rights; on Allegro use Allegro Protect (up to PLN 20,000) and buy as a consumer, not on a NIP invoice (a company purchase weakens consumer rights; a sole trader keeps some only when the purchase is not professional in character ⚠ *(unverified: not re-checked here)*); prefer Trusted Shops-certified shops (buyer protection up to PLN 10,000) when the shop is unfamiliar; statutory warranty (rekojmia) first for defects, seller pays pickup and repair, 2-year presumption; 14-day withdrawal with the return cost known in advance; EU cross-border disputes through ECC Poland (slow, does not pause limitation); never a bank transfer to an account that fails the white list check. Merchant of record is always the shop; the skill adds no protection of its own.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

High by design. Trampoline walk-through: S1 locks e.g. 'round 305-366 cm, net inside the springs, max user weight at least 100 kg, ground anchors, under PLN 2,000 delivered to my postcode'. S3 starts from the Stiftung Warentest 05/2025 list (11 models, EUR 219-695) and VKI 2025, adds Allegro and Shopify candidates, and maps e.g. one Berg model sold under two Allegro names to a single EAN. S4 drops any model with a Safety Gate hit, a listing without an EU responsible person or Polish warnings, or a GS claim that Certipedia does not confirm. S5 compares the same EAN on Allegro, Ceneo shops, Skapiec, Decathlon.pl and the brand store with delivery and return cost for a ~30 kg box and the Omnibus reference. S6 verifies the 2-3 shops. S8 writes 'Model X at shop Y, PLN Z delivered, pay by card; runner-up W if the net position matters more'. The same pattern fits tools, appliances (add EPREL for the energy label) and electronics (add RTINGS and Geizhals).

**workflow role**

All stages from requirements to a verified shortlist: discovery, specs and variants, independent tests, safety, price and history, seller check, buyer-protection choice and evidence capture. It does not do the purchase or long-term price monitoring. Combine with a human checkout, changedetection.io or Pepper alerts for timing, and the ECC cheat-sheet note for after-sales.

**⚠ effort and cost per purchase**

Arithmetic for one trampoline comparison with 5 finalists and 4 shops each: page reads 5 x (Allegro product + GPSR panel + Ceneo offers + Skapiec + brand page) + 2 listings = 27 browser page reads; Safety Gate 5 models x 2 query terms x 2 languages = 20 API calls; white list 1 batched call (up to 30 NIPs) + up to 3 account checks; KRS or CEIDG 3 calls; VIES 1-3 calls; CERT list 1 download; RDAP 4 calls; all PLN 0. Paid: test.de unlock EUR 4.90. Tokens: about 1M (deep agents) + 1-2.5M input incl. cache (browser pass) = quota on Max, or roughly USD 3-10 at API prices ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*. Time: human about 30-45 minutes (elicitation, buying the test, approving gates, reading the brief), agent about 40-70 minutes ⚠ *(unverified: estimate)*. Build once: about 12-18 hours ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**evidence trail**

Saved per purchase under content/_raw/research-workspaces/purchase-<slug>/ (not built into the public site): requirements.yaml (signed, with budget lock), fields.yaml and results/<model>.json from /b:research, evidence/ with Safety Gate query log and alert JSON, white list JSON with requestId and requestDateTime, KRS or CEIDG JSON, VIES result, CERT grep result with download time, RDAP JSON, GPSR extraction JSON plus screenshot per listing, Omnibus captures from two days with screenshots, offer tables per shop, test reference (paid grades only here), and brief.md (requirements snapshot, matrix, sensitivity, verification, where to buy, protection path, gaps and stale-after date, numbered sources with access dates). Public part: one compiled note in the topic folder that matches the product (as with AI/KNOWLEDGE/INFO/AI Voice Recorders for Meetings (Polish)), type compiled-note, tag purchase-decision, conclusions and links only, plus the three index updates.

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Covers the gaps no existing tool or community skill covers in Poland: Omnibus, Safety Gate and GPSR, EU labs, CEIDG/KRS/VAT white list and landed cost for bulky goods.
  - Built only from components verified to work from Poland on 2026-10-15, most of them free official interfaces with citable request IDs.
  - Keeps the human as the payer, matching the buyer's hard-limit and confirmation rule and avoiding US-only agent checkout.
  - Auditable output that fits the vault: raw evidence in content/_raw, a public conclusion note, indexes updated.
  - Robustness rules taken from the evidence (Wharton, ACES): several independent sources, source-order and leave-one-out reruns.
- **weaknesses**:
  - Not built; effort and token costs are estimates.
  - Ceneo, Skapiec and Allegro can only be read at human pace in a real browser, so the price step stays slow and partly manual.
  - Depends on undocumented or changing endpoints (Safety Gate search API, white list host migration, Shopify catalog) and on browser-agent extraction that failed in places in sibling tests.
  - Lab coverage is thin for many categories (only German tests for EU trampoline brands), so many verdicts will rest on Tier 2-3 evidence.
  - Maintenance: shop layouts, Omnibus label wording and terms change; the source atlas needs a yearly refresh.

**⚠ independent review consensus**

N/A - not built, so no hands-on reviews exist. Evidence behind the design choices comes from sibling items: the Wharton source-influence study and ACES (one source or a model update can flip an agent's pick), Product.ai's vendor consistency study, Guardio's Scamlexity and Microsoft's Magentic Marketplace (manipulation and fake shops). The H-group items holding these studies were not yet in results on 2026-10-15, so their figures are taken from the outline and sibling notes without re-opening the papers ⚠ *(unverified)*.

**verdict for me**

PILOT (build it and test it on the trampoline) - deciding fact: no existing system, assistant or community skill covers Polish shops, EU safety checks, Omnibus and seller registers together, while every needed component works from Poland for free or a few euros. Best use: build brain-buy as an orchestrator over /b:research plus a browser pass and three small scripts, run it once on the trampoline, and stop at a verified shortlist the human buys from.

**conflicting evidence**

- Browser agent choice: the Claude in Chrome item says USE NOW as the 'hands' with built-in purchase confirmations; the browser-use item says PILOT, logged out, because it lacks injection and purchase guardrails. The design uses browser-use for logged-out reading and Claude in Chrome only where the human's session is needed.
- Allegro automation: the Allegro item reads art. 10.10-10.11 as a high risk for scraping but low for personal browser-agent use; the Claude in Chrome item notes that a few page reads are low risk yet not explicitly allowed. Both agree bulk extraction is a breach.
- Shopify Global Catalog: stable, identical result sets on repeat searches, but wrong inferred specs and unreliable ships_to PL (same sibling item). Use it for discovery only.
- Omnibus field: legally defined and mandatory, yet self-declared, and about half of 3,026 businesses checked by Inspekcja Handlowa in 2025 mislabelled prices (Omnibus item), so it is a red-flag reader, not proof.
- ChatGPT shopping research in Poland: Polish press (Nov 2025) reported a global rollout while OpenAI's merchant page (2026-10-15) says shopping is live only in the US (ChatGPT item). The design does not depend on it.

## F. Protocols and payment rails

### Agentic commerce protocols

**Verdict:** CONTEXT ONLY (watch UCP and AP2) · **Cost:** Free, open specs · **Verified:** 2026-10-15 · 4 field(s) flagged ⚠

#### identity

**basics**

- **summary**: Four open specifications that let AI agents discover products, build carts, check out and pay on a buyer's behalf. None is a tool a buyer runs; they are plumbing between agent platforms, merchants and payment providers. Role type: protocol (AP2: payment-authorisation protocol). Context item: what they change for a buyer in Poland.
- **acp**: Agentic Commerce Protocol, by OpenAI and Stripe, status 'beta'. Covers agentic checkout (checkout sessions, delegated payment via scoped tokens, delegated 3DS authentication), and since spec 2026-04-17 also cart, product feeds (merchants push catalogues to agent-hosted feeds), orders, authentication and an MCP binding. Latest stable spec 2026-04-17.
- **ucp**: Universal Commerce Protocol, co-developed by Google and Shopify with Etsy, Target, Wayfair and others. A modular standard for discovery and transaction: Catalog (search, lookup), Cart, Checkout, Order, Identity linking, Location and Permalink capabilities plus extensions (fulfillment, discounts, buyer consent, loyalty, AP2 mandates, payment terms, split payments, 3DS2). Merchants publish a profile at /.well-known/ucp; transports REST, MCP, A2A and embedded. Latest release v2026-08-25.
- **ap2**: Agent Payments Protocol, created by Google, donated to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28 with v0.2. Defines verifiable digital credentials ('mandates') that prove what the user authorised: Checkout Mandate and Payment Mandate, each 'open' (constraints such as budget and allowed instruments, before a cart exists) or 'closed' (a specific finalised checkout and amount). Chained mandates form an audit trail for human-present and human-not-present purchases. Works as an extension to A2A, UCP and MCP.
- **klarna app**: Klarna Agentic Product Protocol, announced 2025-12-15: in practice Klarna's approval-gated product-search and offers API on api.pricerunner.com over the PriceRunner catalogue, plus a draft spec in an archived repo. Discovery only, no checkout. Covered in depth in the Klarna sibling item; summarised here.

**vendor and ownership**

- **acp**: Maintained by OpenAI (US) and Stripe (US/Ireland); contributions need a CLA; governance through a SEP (specification enhancement proposal) process. No neutral foundation as of 2026-10-15.
- **ucp**: UCP Tech Council. Founding members Google, Shopify, Etsy, Target, Wayfair; Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and Stripe joined on 2026-04-24 (UCP press release via Newsfile), making ten. Walmart is named as a co-developer in launch coverage but not as a council member in the release. All US-headquartered except Shopify (Canada).
- **ap2**: Created by Google (US); donated to the FIDO Alliance on 2026-04-28 (Google blog). Standardisation continues in FIDO's Agentic Authentication and Payments technical working groups; the payments group is reported to be chaired by Mastercard and Visa (secondary). Verifiable Intent, a related standard co-developed by Google and Mastercard, is also going to FIDO.
- **klarna app**: Klarna Group plc / Klarna Bank AB (Sweden), a BNPL bank that also owns PriceRunner. Bias-relevant: payments revenue plus affiliate links (sibling item).

**lifecycle status**

- **acp**: Launched 2025-09-29 with ChatGPT Instant Checkout (US). Spec versions 2025-09-29, 2025-12-12 (fulfillment), 2026-01-16 (capability negotiation), 2026-01-30 (extensions, discounts, payment handlers), 2026-04-17 (cart, feed, orders, authentication, MCP; 2026-01-30 deprecated). Last commit 2026-07-18; 1,574 stars, 254 forks, 144 open issues (GitHub API, 2026-10-15). OpenAI scaled back Instant Checkout in March 2026 and now sends buyers to merchant sites; its merchant page says shopping is 'currently live for ChatGPT users in the U.S.' (ChatGPT sibling, 2026-10-15). Microsoft said it is adopting ACP for Copilot Checkout (2026-01-08, sibling). Status: live spec, flagship consumer use reduced.
- **ucp**: Launched 2026-01-11 at NRF (Google). Releases v2026-01-11 and v2026-01-23 (both published 2026-01-23), v2026-04-08, v2026-08-25 (3DS2, Web Bot Auth interop, policies snapshot, attribution, loyalty, payment schedules, grocery and lodging groundwork). Last commit 2026-10-14; 3,428 stars, 478 forks, 249 open issues (GitHub API, 2026-10-15). Tech Council doubled 2026-04-24. Shopify removed the approval requirement for its agentic layer in June 2026 (Shopify sibling). Status: most active of the four.
- **ap2**: v0.1.0 on 2025-09-16 (announcement); v0.2.0 on 2026-04-28 with the FIDO donation and 'Human Not Present' payments. Last push 2026-06-17; 3,230 stars, 511 forks, 179 open issues (GitHub API, 2026-10-15). Google's Buy for me flow in the US uses AP2 mandates (Google sibling). The donation post does not say whether AP2 is in production elsewhere. Status: spec plus samples and SDK, moving into FIDO.
- **klarna app**: Announced 2025-12-15; spec repo klarna-incubator/agentic-product-protocol created and last committed 2025-10-13, archived read-only (sibling dates the archiving to 2026-08-05), spec still 'draft'; the API on docs.klarna.com is described as production-ready in the US and EU; Klarna Shopping Search app in ChatGPT live 2026-05-20 (sibling). Status: API alive, open-standard effort frozen.
- **verified**: All four checked 2026-10-15 against the GitHub repositories (API), ucp.dev, ap2-protocol.org, the Google blog and the UCP press release; Klarna and ChatGPT details from sibling items verified the same day.

**cost model**

For a buyer: free. The specs are Apache-2.0 and cost nothing to read or implement; buyers meet them only inside an agent product (ChatGPT, Gemini/AI Mode, Copilot, Shop app). Fees fall on merchants: payment processing through the PSP (e.g. Stripe for ACP Shared Payment Tokens) and any platform fee (OpenAI's merchant page said 'no fees' on 2026-10-15 per the ChatGPT sibling). Klarna's APP API is approval-gated with unpublished pricing. Compliance cost for a buyer: none.

**⚠ feature geo matrix**

- **acp consumer checkout in chatgpt**: US only, and scaled back since March 2026. PL: no. EU: no.
- **acp payment layer stripe spt and acs**: Stripe's docs (read 2026-10-15) list 34 countries for Shared Payment Tokens (public preview) and the Agentic Commerce Suite, including PL: US, CA, AT, BE, BG, HR, CY, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, GI, GR, HU, IE, IT, LV, LI, LT, LU, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SK, SI, ES, SE, CH, GB. So a Polish Stripe merchant could accept agent payments technically, but no consumer agent offering ACP checkout to Polish buyers was found ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **ucp catalog discovery**: Works from PL today through Shopify Global Catalog MCP (keyless; Polish and EU Shopify stores returned with ships_to PL, results need checking; Shopify sibling, tested 2026-10-15).
- **ucp checkout google ai mode buy for me**: US only; Canada and Australia moved to 2027 per Merchant Center help (2026-10-06), UK 'later'; no EU or PL date (Google sibling). Secondary guides agree no EU launch is confirmed.
- **ucp checkout shop app and shop cli**: Shop CLI examples default to --country US; Shop Pay availability for Polish buyers not checked ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- **ap2 mandates**: Used in Google's US Buy for me flow. No deployment in PL or the EU found. Payment methods: cards first; roadmap names e-wallets, real-time bank transfers (UPI, PIX) and digital currencies; BLIK is not mentioned.
- **klarna app**: 13 markets (AT, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, IE, IT, NL, NO, SE, UK, US); Poland not included (sibling).
- **language**: Protocols are language-neutral; product data is in the merchant's language. Polish content works wherever a Polish merchant implements a protocol.
- **big polish channels**: Allegro, Ceneo, Media Expert, x-kom and Decathlon.pl implement none of the four (sibling items). Allegro's only agent surface is its ChatGPT app built on OpenAI's Apps SDK (MCP-based).

#### capabilities

**spec and variant comparison**

Data model supports it, behaviour depends on the agent. ACP feed schema (2026-04-17): variants carry machine-readable identifiers with type GTIN, UPC or EAN, plus price, list_price and unit_price. UCP variant schema: barcodes with 'UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, JAN', list_price 'before discounts (for strikethrough display)', product price ranges. Klarna APP returns gtin14s per product. So EAN/GTIN mapping across merchants is possible in principle; Shopify's live UCP catalog did not merge the same trampoline across merchants in the sibling test. No protocol handles OEM rebadges, retailer-exclusive variants or lineup near-equivalents; that stays with the agent or skill.

**price comparison and pl coverage**

Protocols do not compare prices; they let one agent query many merchants in one format. Polish coverage today: only Polish Shopify stores via UCP catalog (e.g. bieznie.pl trampolines in PLN in the sibling test). No Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom or Decathlon.pl. EU: Shopify-based EU stores via UCP; Klarna APP for its 12 EU-endpoint markets (not PL).

**price history and omnibus**

None. Neither ACP nor UCP has a prior-price or 'lowest price in the last 30 days' field; both have only a list_price for strikethrough display (schemas grepped 2026-10-15). An agent that shows a strikethrough list_price to an EU buyer is displaying a price reduction, which under Omnibus must refer to the 30-day lowest price; the protocols give no way to check that. Klarna APP has no price history field either.

**total landed cost**

Partly built in at checkout time. ACP checkout sessions return line items, fulfillment options and totals; UCP checkout returns totals and fulfillment methods (shipping vs pickup), and v2026-08-25 adds a policies snapshot on Cart, Checkout, Catalog and Order to carry return, refund and warranty terms. Klarna APP offers carry shippingCost and delivery time for its markets. None models return shipping cost for a bulky item or cross-border warranty enforceability as numbers.

**review and seller verification**

Technical identity only. UCP: business profile at /.well-known/ucp, namespace authority bound to DNS/host, signed requests (RFC 9421) and Web Bot Auth interop for agent identity. ACP: the merchant is onboarded with its PSP (e.g. Stripe KYC) and remains merchant of record. Neither verifies legal seller identity for the buyer (no NIP, KRS, VAT white list or VIES), reviews or ratings authenticity. Grade: partial for merchant authentication, none for reviews.

**safety and compliance checks**

None. No GPSR fields (manufacturer, EU responsible person, warnings), no Safety Gate or certificate data in ACP or UCP schemas (grepped 2026-10-15). Future: the EU Digital Product Passport is the likelier carrier of verifiable product data (regulatory-horizon item).

**independent test coverage**

N/A - protocols carry merchant data, not lab tests.

**alerts and monitoring**

No price or restock alerts in the protocols. UCP and ACP Order capabilities cover post-purchase order status. AP2 v0.2 'Human Not Present' mandates enable buy-when-condition-met flows (Google's example: limited-run tickets; Google's US Buy for me buys when a tracked price is hit), which is the protocol basis for future price-triggered purchases.

**purchase automation and guardrails**

- **summary**: This is what the protocols are for, and their guardrails are better than browser-agent checkout, but none is usable for buying from Poland as of 2026-10-15.
- **acp**: Delegated payment: the agent passes a Shared Payment Token that is a scoped grant with usage and expiration limits (Stripe docs: currency, maximum amount, expiration window), tied to one merchant; the merchant stays merchant of record and handles fulfilment, returns and support. Delegated 3DS authentication flows with outcomes such as denied or frictionless (2026-04-17 examples), which matters for EU strong customer authentication. In ChatGPT's former Instant Checkout the user confirmed order, shipping and payment before any action (sibling).
- **ucp**: complete_checkout requires a Token-tier credential with purchase permission; otherwise the agent hands over continue_url so the buyer finishes on the merchant site (Shopify sibling, ucp.dev). 3DS2 via the Actions primitive (v2026-08-25); extensible buyer consent; identity linking via OAuth or delegated IdP; AP2 mandates extension. Shopify's Shop CLI adds a buyer-set 'payment budget' (delegated spending, revocable in Shop settings) and never prints the wallet token.
- **ap2**: Open mandates carry constraints (budget, allowed instruments, user goals); closed mandates bind a specific amount and checkout; mandates are signed credentials chained into an audit trail; Verifiable Intent adds a tamper-resistant log of what the user authorised. The 2026-04-28 post does not describe expiry or merchant restrictions in detail.
- **blik and passkeys**: No protocol supports BLIK (about 71% of Polish e-commerce transactions in Q4 2025, outline note). FIDO stewardship of AP2 points toward passkey-based authorisation; the BLIK agent pilot and Mastercard Agent Pay tests in Poland are covered in the payment-rails item.
- **on error**: ACP defines error responses (invalid item, out of stock, payment declined) and version-mismatch errors; UCP falls back to continue_url. Refunds and disputes follow the merchant and the card scheme, not the protocol.

**after sales and resale**

Brief: Order capabilities in ACP (2026-04-17) and UCP give order status and, in UCP, the policies snapshot with return, refund and warranty terms. Shop CLI supports tracking, returns and reorders for Shop purchases. No spare-parts, service-network or resale features.

#### data and integration

**data sources and freshness**

Merchant-supplied data: ACP feeds pushed by merchants to agent-hosted feed services (full file replacement or partial PATCH); UCP catalog served from merchant or platform endpoints (Shopify's Global Catalog for Shopify stores); Klarna APP from PriceRunner feeds. Freshness is the merchant's: catalogue data may lag, while checkout-session prices are authoritative at the moment of checkout. Every object carries merchant URLs; nothing is snapshotted by the protocol unless the agent saves it.

**api mcp skill access**

- **grade**: partial - only UCP catalog search is usable from Claude Code in Poland today
- **ucp**: Shopify Global Catalog MCP at https://catalog.shopify.com/api/ucp/mcp (keyless with an agent profile; tools search_catalog, lookup_catalog, get_product; sibling-verified from Poland). Shopify/ucp-cli ('a shopping skill for AI agents', MIT, 79 stars, last push 2026-10-12) and Shopify/shop-cli with the bundled Shop skill (MIT, 18 stars, last push 2026-09-16; catalog search signed out, Sign in with Shop via OAuth device flow, UCP checkout with Shop Pay; personal-use only). Any merchant's /.well-known/ucp profile can be read by an MCP client. Setup: 5-10 minutes for catalog search.
- **acp**: No public endpoint for an individual buyer: checkout endpoints live at merchants and are called by approved agent platforms; the Feed API is hosted by agents for merchants. The spec repo provides OpenAPI, JSON Schema and (since 2026-04-17) MCP/OpenRPC definitions. Useful to a builder, not to a buyer.
- **ap2**: Python SDK and samples (ADK, Gemini; Go and Android scenarios; x402 sample) in google-agentic-commerce/AP2. No consumer endpoint.
- **klarna app**: Approval-gated REST API (tokenId header; api.pricerunner.com); no public MCP for Claude (sibling).
- **fallback**: For Polish shops: browser agent plus registers (see the custom buying-research skill item).

**protocol support**

How they fit together: UCP is the broadest (discovery to order) and can carry AP2 mandates as an extension and run over MCP or A2A; AP2 is payment authorisation that plugs into UCP, A2A or MCP; ACP is OpenAI and Stripe's checkout-plus-feeds stack, now with an MCP binding; Klarna APP is a discovery API that Klarna positions next to UCP (Klarna backed UCP on 2026-02-02, sibling). Stripe sits on both sides (ACP co-owner, UCP Tech Council member since April 2026; its Agentic Commerce Suite supports both). UCP v2026-08-25 adds Web Bot Auth interop; Visa Trusted Agent Protocol and Mastercard Agent Pay are separate rails (payment-rails item). For future-proofing, UCP plus AP2 has the widest backing (Google, Shopify, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, Stripe, FIDO); ACP's flagship consumer use shrank in 2026.

**open source and licence**

- **acp**: Apache-2.0; github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol; 1,574 stars; last commit 2026-07-18; 144 open issues; CLA required.
- **ucp**: Apache-2.0; github.com/Universal-Commerce-Protocol/ucp; 3,428 stars; last commit 2026-10-14; 249 open issues; docs at ucp.dev.
- **ap2**: Apache-2.0; github.com/google-agentic-commerce/AP2; 3,230 stars; v0.2.0 2026-04-28; last push 2026-06-17; 179 open issues; docs at ap2-protocol.org.
- **klarna app**: Apache-2.0 spec at github.com/klarna-incubator/agentic-product-protocol, 11 stars, archived; the API and catalogue are closed.
- **verified**: GitHub API, 2026-10-15.

**account linking and data access**

When used, the agent platform shares buyer data with the merchant at checkout (contact, shipping address, consent choices) and the payment credential stays tokenised with the PSP or credential provider (Stripe SPT, Shop Pay wallet token, AP2 payment mandate). UCP identity linking uses OAuth or a delegated identity provider (e.g. Sign in with Shop); buyer consent is a per-purpose map since v2026-08-25. GDPR: merchant and agent platform are separate controllers; the protocols do not define retention. For this buyer: nothing to link today; if it arrives, the acceptable setup is a capped, revocable budget plus per-purchase confirmation, never a stored card in an agent.

**automation legal risk**

Low - these are the sanctioned routes for agents, the opposite of scraping. Terms still bind the caller: Shopify's catalog and Shop CLI are for personal use (no aggregators or resale; no caching of catalogue results), Klarna's API is partner-only. Context: Amazon joined the UCP Tech Council in April 2026 while still blocking unidentified agents on its own site and suing Perplexity over Comet (siblings), so protocol membership does not mean a shop accepts every agent.

#### trust and bias

**⚠ monetization and bias vector**

Protocols define no ranking, but they add paid hooks: UCP v2026-08-25 'Attribution' carries platform-driven referral and ad attribution context; Shopify catalog has invite-only promoted placements (sibling); ChatGPT ads run in Europe on Free and Go plans (sibling); Klarna's ChatGPT app sells labelled sponsored placements and uses Klarna-affiliated links (sibling). The council members are platform, marketplace, ads and payments companies, so the agent that ranks offers will usually earn from the outcome ⚠ *(unverified: inference from membership, not a documented ranking rule)*.

**ranking transparency**

Not addressed by any of the four. Ranking and explanation are left to the agent platform; the protocols neither require a reason for a recommendation nor a 'sponsored' flag on catalogue results (UCP's attribution field records ad context but is not a buyer-facing label).

**run to run consistency**

N/A for the protocols. Structured catalogues behind them are deterministic per query (Shopify catalog returned the same 20 product IDs on four identical searches in the sibling test); variability comes from the LLM agent on top.

**manipulation and injection resistance**

Better than browser agents on identity and payment: signed requests, DNS-bound merchant namespaces, scoped or mandate-bound payments limit the damage of a hijacked agent (a closed AP2 mandate or an SPT capped to one merchant and amount cannot be redirected). Weak on content: merchant-authored descriptions still flow into the agent's context as a prompt-injection channel, and a fraudulent business can implement UCP or ACP like any other; no protocol checks seller legitimacy or product safety. The fake-shop risk in the Scamlexity study is not removed, only moved to merchant onboarding.

**known failures**

ACP's flagship consumer deployment (ChatGPT Instant Checkout) was scaled back in March 2026; one secondary source says only about a dozen Shopify merchants ever went live (single source, not confirmed). Klarna's open-standard repo was archived with the spec still a draft. UCP checkout remains US-only nine months after launch, with Canada and Australia slipping to 2027. Shopify's live UCP catalog showed wrong inferred specs, unreliable ships_to filtering and no cross-merchant merge (sibling). Large open issue counts (ACP 144, UCP 249, AP2 179). Documentation drift: one Shopify page lists a different MCP endpoint path (sibling); a mid-2026 blog claimed neither ACP nor UCP had cut a release in four months, which UCP v2026-08-25 disproved.

**regulatory enforcement history**

None against the protocols. Related: the European Commission's DMA decisions on Google Shopping self-preferencing (sibling: EUR 890M fine 2026-07-23) and Google's September 2026 EEA search redesign shape how Google can surface UCP shopping in the EU; ChatGPT was designated a Very Large Online Search Engine under the DSA on 2026-08-31 (sibling). Amazon v. Perplexity (US) concerns agents acting without protocols.

**⚠ buyer protection path**

In ACP and UCP the merchant is merchant of record, so for an EU merchant the buyer keeps the 14-day withdrawal right, the 2-year legal guarantee (rekojmia in Poland) and ECC for cross-border disputes; card chargeback applies when the token wraps a card. AP2 mandates and Verifiable Intent create signed evidence of what was authorised, which should help in a dispute over an agent purchase ⚠ *(unverified: no dispute rules published)*. The agent platform itself is not liable for the goods. For a US merchant reached through an agent, practical recourse from Poland is weak.

#### fit for user

**fit for big ticket durables**

Low today. For the trampoline: UCP catalog search via Shopify MCP can list Polish and EU Shopify stores selling 305-366 cm trampolines with prices and cart links, which is useful for discovery; everything else (Allegro, Ceneo shops, Decathlon.pl, safety, seller identity, Omnibus, delivery of a ~30 kg box) happens outside the protocols, and no agent can check out for a Polish buyer. If UCP checkout reaches Poland, a closed AP2 mandate with a PLN cap and a confirmation step would be the acceptable way to let an agent pay, and the policies snapshot would document return and warranty terms.

**workflow role**

Context only. Discovery step via UCP catalog (Shopify Global Catalog MCP) now; watch UCP and AP2 for EU checkout. Combine with the browser-agent research skill for Polish shops, registers for seller identity and a human checkout.

**effort and cost per purchase**

UCP catalog via Shopify MCP: 5-10 minutes setup, queries free; one trampoline discovery pass of 4 searches is about 400 KB of JSON raw (about 100k tokens) or a few thousand tokens when filtered to title, seller, price and URL (Shopify sibling arithmetic). ACP, AP2 and Klarna APP: no cost and no use for a Polish buyer today.

**evidence trail**

Strong in principle: checkout sessions, totals, the UCP policies snapshot, order objects, signed AP2 mandates and Verifiable Intent logs are structured, timestamped records that could be saved into a vault note as proof of what was offered and authorised. Today, for a Polish buyer, only UCP catalog JSON (product ID, merchant, price, currency, URL, query date) can be saved; Shopify's no-caching rule means storing a few fields in a dated personal note, not raw responses (Shopify sibling).

#### assessment

**strengths weaknesses**

- **strengths**:
  - Structured, merchant-of-record purchases with scoped payment credentials (ACP SPT limits, AP2 closed mandates, Shop budgets) are safer than browser agents typing card details.
  - UCP has the widest backing (Google, Shopify, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, Stripe) and the most active development (v2026-08-25, commits to 2026-10-14).
  - Both ACP and UCP support 3DS authentication, so they can satisfy EU strong customer authentication.
  - GTIN/EAN barcodes and a policies snapshot (return, refund, warranty) in the data model help variant matching and evidence.
  - UCP catalog search already works keyless from Poland through Shopify MCP.
- **weaknesses**:
  - No consumer agent checkout in Poland or the EU under any of the four as of 2026-10-15.
  - The main Polish channels (Allegro, Ceneo shops, Media Expert, x-kom) implement none of them.
  - No Omnibus prior-price, GPSR, safety or seller-legitimacy fields; ranking and sponsored labelling left to the platforms, with ad attribution now in UCP.
  - No BLIK support, while BLIK dominates Polish e-commerce payments.
  - Churn: ACP's flagship checkout scaled back, Klarna's spec repo archived, UCP country rollouts slipping.

**independent review consensus**

No independent hands-on evidence for buyers. Coverage is vendor announcements (Google, Shopify, OpenAI, Stripe, Klarna), trade press repeating them, and agency or vendor explainers (UCP rollout guides, protocol comparisons) that often sell implementation services. They agree on three points: UCP checkout is US-first with no confirmed EU date, ACP's consumer checkout shrank in 2026, and the standards race is consolidating around UCP plus AP2 (opinion pieces, not tests). No test of agent purchase accuracy, price correctness or dispute outcomes under these protocols was found.

**verdict for me**

CONTEXT ONLY (WATCH UCP and AP2) - deciding fact: no consumer agent can check out for a Polish buyer under any of the four, and Allegro and Ceneo implement none, while UCP catalog search already works from Poland via Shopify MCP. Best use: use UCP catalog search for discovery inside the buying-research skill, recheck EU checkout availability in six months, and accept agent payment only as a capped, confirmed mandate.

**⚠ conflicting evidence**

- UCP in the EU: one guide claims a 'Phase Two' EU and UK activation in March 2026, while Google's Merchant Center help (2026-10-06, per sibling), other guides and the same site's other page say UCP checkout is US-only with the UK later. Google's own documentation is more credible ⚠ *(unverified)*.
- Stripe Shared Payment Tokens: an August 2026 explainer calls SPTs generally available in US states only; Stripe's docs (2026-10-15) list 34 countries including PL and label SPTs public preview.
- ACP direction: OpenAI scaled back Instant Checkout (March 2026) while the ACP spec kept growing (cart, feeds, orders, MCP in 2026-04-17) and Microsoft adopted it for Copilot Checkout; 'ACP is fading' and 'ACP extended to discovery' are both partly true.
- Release cadence: a mid-2026 blog said neither ACP nor UCP had cut a release in four months; UCP shipped v2026-08-25, ACP's last stable spec is 2026-04-17.
- UCP founding members: some coverage lists Walmart; the 2026-04-24 UCP press release lists Google, Shopify, Etsy, Target and Wayfair as founding Tech Council members.
- AP2 v0.2 content: some coverage says v0.2 added Verifiable Intent; Google's post presents Verifiable Intent as a separate, AP2-compatible standard.
- Klarna APP market count: '12 markets' at launch vs 13 in current docs (sibling).
